passages.name: 2018年12月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，男士向女士推荐一本物理书，女士说自己读过，称赞作者西尔维娅·门德斯写得清楚有趣、书中有很多动手实验，还提到不少鲜为人知的女科学家。第二段长对话里，一名学生请教授指点学位论文怎样开头，教授建议他缩小“美学”这一题目，从哲学家休谟的传记入手，并严格按作业要求来写。第一篇短文讲今年北极冬天气温异常偏高，海冰加速融化，北极夏季可能在二十年内就不再有冰。第二篇短文介绍一项研究：意志力的关键在于你相信自己有多少意志力，相信它取之不尽的人反而越干越有劲。第一段录音讲机器学习会让许多工作实现自动化，但机器很难应对从没见过的新情况，这正是人类的长处。第二段录音介绍用太阳能产生的蒸汽开动火车的设想，以及日本研究团队探索的几种储热材料。第三段录音分析英格兰老年人照护危机的成因和历史，以及六十年来批评不断却改变甚少的原因。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Six, Part Two: Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with the single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hey, I just read a great book about physics.
paras.zh: 嘿，我刚读了一本很棒的物理书。

paras.en: I think you’d like it.
paras.zh: 我觉得你会喜欢的。

paras.en: It’s called The Physics of the World.
paras.zh: 书名叫《世界的物理》。

paras.en: It’s written by a scientist named Sylvia Mendez.
paras.zh: 作者是一位名叫西尔维娅·门德斯的科学家。

paras.en: Oh, I read that book.
paras.zh: 哦，那本书我读过。

paras.en: It was great.
paras.zh: 写得很棒。

paras.en: The writer is a warm and competent guide to the mysteries of physics.
paras.zh: 作者是一位亲切又能干的向导，带你探索物理学的种种奥秘。

paras.en: I think it promises enrichment for any reader, from those who know little about science to the career physicist, and it’s refreshing to see a strong, curious, clever woman adding her voice to the scientific discourse in a field that has been traditionally dominated by men.
paras.zh: 我觉得这本书能让每位读者都有所收获，不论是对科学所知甚少的人，还是专业的物理学家；而且在一向由男性主导的领域里，能看到一位坚强、好奇又聪明的女性在科学界发出自己的声音，真让人耳目一新。

paras.en: I think she is to be commended for making an effort to include anecdotes about little-known female scientists.
paras.zh: 我觉得她特意收进了一些鲜为人知的女科学家的轶事，这一点值得称赞。

paras.en: You know, they were often victims of a generation firmly convinced that the woman’s place was in the home.
paras.zh: 你知道，那一代人坚信女人就该待在家里，她们常常成了这种观念的受害者。

paras.en: I like how the book is clearly written, with each chapter brought to life by pieces of fascinating knowledge.
paras.zh: 我喜欢这本书写得清楚明白，每一章都穿插着有趣的知识，读起来生动鲜活。

paras.en: For example, in one chapter, she exposes a myth that I’ve heard taught by university physics professors.
paras.zh: 比如，有一章里她揭穿了一个说法，我听大学物理教授就这么讲过。

paras.en: I’ve often heard that medieval glass windows are thicker at the bottom because glass flows like a fluid.
paras.zh: 我常听人说，中世纪的玻璃窗下面比上面厚，是因为玻璃会像液体一样流动。

paras.en: This she shows is not true.
paras.zh: 她证明了这种说法不对。

paras.en: The distortion is actually thanks to a peculiarity of the glass maker’s process.
paras.zh: 玻璃变形其实是因为玻璃工匠的制作工艺有个特点。

paras.en: Yeah, I like how she cultivates scientific engagement by providing a host of do-it-yourself experiments that bring the same foundational principles of classical physics that govern everything from the solar system to your kitchen table.
paras.zh: 是啊，我喜欢她提供了大量自己动手的实验来激发读者对科学的投入，这些实验展示的经典物理学基本原理是一样的，从太阳系到你家的餐桌，万事万物都受它们支配。

paras.en: From using complex laws of physics to test whether a spinning egg is cooked to measuring atmospheric pressure by lifting a piece of cardboard, her hands-on examples make her book a truly interactive read.
paras.zh: 从运用复杂的物理定律检验转动的鸡蛋熟没熟，到掀起一块硬纸板测量气压，她举的这些动手实例让这本书真正成了一本能互动的读物。

paras.en: Yes, I must say this equation-free book is an ideal read for scientists of all stripes, anyone teaching science, and even people who dislike physics.
paras.zh: 是啊，我得说，这本不含公式的书非常适合各种各样的科学家、所有教科学的人来读，甚至连讨厌物理的人也适合。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the woman say about the book the man recommended?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于男士推荐的那本书，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question two: What can we find in the book the man recommended?
paras.zh: 第二题：在男士推荐的那本书里，我们能看到什么？

paras.en: Question three: How does the author bring her book to life?
paras.zh: 第三题：作者是怎样让她的书生动起来的？

paras.en: Question four: How does the book cultivate readers’ interest in physics?
paras.zh: 第四题：这本书是怎样培养读者对物理的兴趣的？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi, Professor.
paras.zh: 您好，教授。

paras.en: was hoping I could have a moment of your time if you’re not too busy.
paras.zh: 如果您不太忙的话，我想占用您一点时间。

paras.en: I’m having some problems getting started on my dissertation, and I was hoping you could give me some advice on how to begin.
paras.zh: 我的学位论文一直开不了头，想请您给我出出主意，看该怎么开始。

paras.en: Sure, I have quite a few students though, so can you remind me what your topic is?
paras.zh: 好啊，不过我带的学生挺多的，你能提醒我一下你的题目是什么吗？

paras.en: The general topic I chose is aesthetics, but that’s as far as I’ve got.
paras.zh: 我选的大方向是美学，可我也就只想到这一步。

paras.en: I don’t really know where to go from there.
paras.zh: 我真不知道接下来该往哪儿走。

paras.en: Yeah, that’s much too large a topic.
paras.zh: 是啊，这个题目太大了。

paras.en: You really need to narrow it down in order to make it more accessible.
paras.zh: 你真得把它缩小一些，好让它更容易着手。

w.m: adj. 易处理的；易理解的

paras.en: Otherwise, you’ll be writing a book.
paras.zh: 不然的话，你就要写成一本书了。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 一点没错。

paras.en: That’s what I wanted to ask you about.
paras.zh: 我想问您的就是这个。

paras.en: I was hoping it would be possible for me to change topics.
paras.zh: 我本来希望能换个题目。

paras.en: I’m really more interested in nature than beauty.
paras.zh: 比起美，我其实对自然更感兴趣。

paras.en: I’m afraid you have to adhere to the assigned topic.
paras.zh: 恐怕你得按指定的题目来写。

paras.en: Still, if you’re interested in nature, then that certainly can be worked into your dissertation.
paras.zh: 不过，既然你对自然感兴趣，当然可以把它融进你的论文里。

paras.en: We’ve talked about Hume before in class, right?
paras.zh: 我们以前在课上讲过休谟，对吧？

paras.en: Oh yeah, he’s the philosopher who wrote about where our ideas of beauty come from.
paras.zh: 哦，对，他就是那位写过我们对美的观念从何而来的哲学家。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 一点没错。

paras.en: I suggest you go to the library and get a copy of his biography.
paras.zh: 我建议你去图书馆借一本他的传记。

paras.en: Start from there, but remember to stick to the parameters of the assignment.
paras.zh: 从这里着手，不过别忘了，要严格按照作业的要求来写。

paras.en: This paper is a large part of your cumulative grade, so make sure to follow the instructions.
paras.zh: 这篇论文在你的总成绩里占很大比重，所以一定要按要求做。

paras.en: If you take a look at his biography, you can get a good idea of how his life experiences manifest themselves in his theories of beauty, specifically the way he looked towards nature as the origin of what we find beautiful.
paras.zh: 你看看他的传记，就能很好地了解他的人生经历在他关于美的理论中是怎样体现出来的，特别是他怎样把自然看作我们觉得美的东西的根源。

paras.en: Great, thanks for taking the time to answer my questions, Professor.
paras.zh: 太好了，谢谢您抽时间回答我的问题，教授。

paras.en: I’ll let you get back to class now.
paras.zh: 那我不耽误您回去上课了。

paras.en: If there’s anything else you need, please come see me in my office any time.
paras.zh: 要是还需要别的什么，随时来办公室找我。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is the man’s problem?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士遇到了什么问题？

paras.en: Question six: What does the professor think of the man’s topic?
paras.zh: 第六题：教授觉得男士的题目怎么样？

paras.en: Question seven: What is the man really more interested in?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士其实更感兴趣的是什么？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the professor say the man has to do?
paras.zh: 第八题：教授说男士必须做什么？

paras.en: Section B: Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: During the Arctic winter, from October to March, the average temperature in the frozen north typically hovers around minus 20 degrees Celsius, but this year the Arctic is experiencing much higher temperatures.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文：北极的冬天从十月持续到三月，冰封的北方平均气温通常在零下二十摄氏度上下，可今年北极的气温却高得多。

w.m: v. 徘徊；（数值）在……上下浮动

paras.en: On February 20th, the temperature in Greenland climbed above freezing or zero degrees Celsius, and it stayed there for over 24 hours.
paras.zh: 二月二十日，格陵兰的气温升到冰点以上，也就是零摄氏度以上，而且持续了二十四个多小时。

paras.en: Then, on February 24th, the temperature on Greenland’s northern tip reached six degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 接着到了二月二十四日，格陵兰北端的气温达到了六摄氏度。

paras.en: Climate scientists describe the phenomenon as stunning.
paras.zh: 气候科学家称这一现象令人震惊。

paras.en: Weather conditions that drive this bizarre temperature surge have visited the Arctic before.
paras.zh: 造成这种气温异常飙升的天气状况以前在北极也出现过。

w.m: adj. 异乎寻常的；怪异的

paras.en: They typically appear about once in a decade.
paras.zh: 这种情况通常大约十年出现一次。

paras.en: However, the last such increase in temperature took place two years ago, this is troubling as climbing Arctic temperatures combined with rapid sea ice loss are creating a new type of climate feedback loop, which could accelerate Arctic warming.
paras.zh: 可是，上一次这样的升温就发生在两年前，这让人忧心，因为北极气温不断上升，再加上海冰迅速减少，正在形成一种新的气候反馈循环，可能会让北极变暖得更快。

paras.en: Indeed, sea ice cover in the Arctic is melting faster than expected.
paras.zh: 事实上，北极的海冰融化得比预想的还要快。

paras.en: Without those masses of cooling sea ice, warm air brought to the Arctic can penetrate further inland than it ever did before.
paras.zh: 没有了那一大片起降温作用的海冰，被带到北极的暖空气就能比以往任何时候都更深入内陆。

paras.en: The air can stay warmer longer too.
paras.zh: 暖空气停留的时间也会更长。

paras.en: This drives additional melting.
paras.zh: 这又会加剧融化。

paras.en: Overall, Earth is warming at a rapid pace.
paras.zh: 总的来说，地球正在迅速变暖。

paras.en: 2014 through 2017 rank as the hottest years on record, and the Arctic is warming twice as fast as any place else on Earth.
paras.zh: 二零一四年到二零一七年是有记录以来最热的几年，而北极变暖的速度是地球上其他任何地方的两倍。

paras.en: This raises unique challenges for Arctic wildlife and Indigenous people, who depend on Arctic ecosystems to survive.
paras.zh: 这给北极的野生动物和依靠北极生态系统生存的原住民带来了特有的挑战。

paras.en: Previously, climate forecasts predicted that Arctic summer ice would disappear entirely by around 2060, but based on what scientists are seeing now, the Arctic may be facing summers without ice within 20 years.
paras.zh: 以前的气候预测认为，北极夏季的冰大约到二零六零年才会完全消失，可根据科学家现在看到的情况，北极也许二十年内就会迎来没有冰的夏天。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What did climate scientists describe as stunning?
paras.zh: 第九题：气候科学家称什么令人震惊？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the passage say about the temperature surge in the Arctic?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于北极的气温飙升，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What may occur in 20 years, according to scientists’ recent observations?
paras.zh: 第十一题：根据科学家最近的观察，二十年内可能会发生什么？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: A good dose of willpower is often necessary to see any task through, whether it’s sticking to a spending plan or finishing a great novel, and if you want to increase that willpower, a new study suggests you just simply have to believe you have it.
paras.zh: 无论是严格执行开支计划，还是读完一部长篇巨著，要把任何事坚持做完，往往都需要相当的意志力；一项新研究表明，要想增强这种意志力，你只要相信自己有意志力就行了。

paras.en: According to this study, what matters most is what we think about our willpower.
paras.zh: 这项研究认为，最重要的是我们怎么看待自己的意志力。

paras.en: If we believe it’s a finite resource, we act that way; we feel exhausted and need breaks between demanding mental tasks.
paras.zh: 如果我们认为它是有限的资源，我们就会照这个想法行事：觉得精疲力竭，在两项费脑子的任务之间需要休息。

paras.en: However, people who view their willpower as a limitless resource get energized instead.
paras.zh: 然而，把自己的意志力看作无限资源的人，反而会越干越有劲。

paras.en: The researchers used a psychological assessment tool to test the validity of the study.
paras.zh: 研究人员用一种心理评估工具来检验这项研究的有效性。

paras.en: They asked 1,100 Americans and 1,600 Europeans to grade different statements, such as, “After a challenging mental activity, my energy is depleted, and I must rest to get it refueled again,” or, “I can focus on a mental task for long periods without feeling tired.”
paras.zh: 他们请一千一百名美国人和一千六百名欧洲人给不同的说法打分，比如“做完一项费脑子的活动后，我的精力就耗尽了，必须休息才能重新充满电”，或是“我能长时间专注于一项脑力任务而不觉得累”。

w.m: v. 补充燃料；恢复精力

paras.en: Although there was little difference between men and women overall, Americans were more likely to admit to needing breaks after completing mentally challenging tasks.
paras.zh: 虽然总体上男性和女性差别不大，但美国人更愿意承认做完费脑子的任务后需要休息。

paras.en: European participants, on the other hand, claimed they were able to keep going.
paras.zh: 而欧洲的参与者则说自己能一直干下去。

paras.en: Based on the findings, the researchers suggest that the key to boosting your willpower is to believe that you have an abundant supply of it.
paras.zh: 研究人员根据这些发现指出，增强意志力的关键在于相信自己的意志力很充足。

paras.en: Your feelings about your willpower affect the way you behave, but these feelings are changeable, they said.
paras.zh: 你怎么看自己的意志力，会影响你的行为方式，但这些看法是可以改变的，研究人员这样说。

paras.en: Changing your beliefs about the nature of your self-control can have positive effects on character development.
paras.zh: 改变你对自控力本质的看法，会对品格的培养产生积极影响。

paras.en: This leads to healthier behaviors and perceptions of other people.
paras.zh: 这会让人的行为更健康，对他人的看法也更健康。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What is often necessary for carrying through a task?
paras.zh: 第十二题：要把一项任务坚持到底，往往需要什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What is the finding of the new study?
paras.zh: 第十三题：这项新研究的发现是什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What do we learn about European participants as compared with their American counterparts?
paras.zh: 第十四题：与美国参与者相比，欧洲参与者有什么特点？

paras.en: Question 15: What do the researchers say concerning people’s feelings about willpower?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于人们对意志力的看法，研究人员说了什么？

paras.en: Section C Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Here is my baby niece, Sarah.
paras.zh: 这是我的小侄女萨拉。

paras.en: Her mum is a doctor and her dad is a lawyer.
paras.zh: 她妈妈是医生，爸爸是律师。

paras.en: By the time Sarah goes to college, the jobs her parents do are going to look dramatically different.
paras.zh: 等萨拉上大学的时候，她父母现在做的工作会变得面目全非。

paras.en: In 2013, researchers at Oxford University did a study on the future of work.
paras.zh: 二零一三年，牛津大学的研究人员做了一项关于未来工作的研究。

paras.en: They concluded that almost one in every two jobs has a high risk of being automated by machines.
paras.zh: 他们得出结论：差不多每两份工作里就有一份很可能被机器自动化取代。

paras.en: Machine learning is the technology that’s responsible for most of this disruption.
paras.zh: 造成这种颠覆的主要是机器学习这项技术。

paras.en: It’s the most powerful branch of artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 它是人工智能中最强大的分支。

paras.en: It allows machines to learn from data and copy some of the things that humans can do.
paras.zh: 它让机器能从数据中学习，并模仿人类能做的一些事情。

paras.en: My company, Kaggle, operates on the cutting edge of machine learning.
paras.zh: 我的公司Kaggle走在机器学习的最前沿。

paras.en: We bring together hundreds of thousands of experts to solve important problems for industry and academia.
paras.zh: 我们把几十万名专家聚到一起，为产业界和学术界解决重要的问题。

paras.en: This gives us a unique perspective on what machines can do, what they can’t do, and what jobs they might automate or threaten, machine learning started making its way into industry in the early 90s.
paras.zh: 这让我们有独特的视角，能看清机器能做什么、不能做什么，以及它们可能让哪些工作自动化、威胁到哪些工作。机器学习从九十年代初开始进入产业界。

paras.en: It started with relatively simple tasks.
paras.zh: 一开始做的是相对简单的任务。

paras.en: It started with things like assessing credit risk from loan applications, sorting the mail by reading handwritten zip codes.
paras.zh: 一开始做的是评估贷款申请中的信用风险、识别手写的邮政编码来分拣邮件之类的事情。

paras.en: Over the past few years, we have made dramatic breakthroughs.
paras.zh: 过去几年里，我们取得了巨大的突破。

paras.en: Machine learning is now capable of far, far more complex tasks.
paras.zh: 机器学习现在能完成复杂得多得多的任务。

paras.en: In 2012, Kaggle challenged its community to build a program that could grade high school essays.
paras.zh: 二零一二年，Kaggle向它的社区发起挑战，要大家编一个能给高中作文打分的程序。

paras.en: The winning programs were able to match the grades given by human teachers.
paras.zh: 获胜的程序打的分能和人类老师给的分一致。

paras.en: Now, given the right data, machines are going to outperform humans at tasks like this.
paras.zh: 现在，只要有合适的数据，机器在这类任务上就会超过人类。

paras.en: A teacher might read 10,000 essays over a 40-year career.
paras.zh: 一位老师在四十年的职业生涯里也许要读一万篇作文。

paras.en: A machine can read millions of essays within minutes, we have no chance of competing against machines on frequent, high-volume tasks.
paras.zh: 机器几分钟之内就能读几百万篇作文。在频繁、大量的任务上，我们根本没有机会和机器竞争。

paras.en: But there are things we can do that machines cannot.
paras.zh: 但有些事情我们能做，机器却做不了。

paras.en: Where machines have made very little progress is in tackling novel situations.
paras.zh: 机器进展甚微的地方，是应对新情况。

paras.en: Machines can’t handle things they haven’t seen many times before, the fundamental limitation of machine learning is that it needs to learn from large volumes of past data, but humans don’t.
paras.zh: 机器处理不了之前没见过很多次的事情。机器学习的根本局限在于它需要从大量的过去数据中学习，而人类不需要。

paras.en: We have the ability to connect seemingly different threads to solve problems we’ve never seen before.
paras.zh: 我们有能力把看似不相关的线索联系起来，去解决从没遇到过的问题。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What did the researchers at Oxford University conclude?
paras.zh: 第十六题：牛津大学的研究人员得出了什么结论？

paras.en: Question 17: What do we learn about Kaggle company’s winning programs?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于Kaggle公司那些获胜的程序，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What is the fundamental limitation of machine learning?
paras.zh: 第十八题：机器学习的根本局限是什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: We’ve talked recently about the importance of sustainable energy.
paras.zh: 我们最近讲过可持续能源的重要性。

paras.en: We’ve also talked about the different theories on how that can be done.
paras.zh: 我们还讲过实现它的各种理论。

paras.en: So far, our discussions have all been theoretical.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，我们的讨论都停留在理论上。

paras.en: Now I have a practical question for you all: Can you run a 140,000 kilogram train on just the steam generated by solar power?
paras.zh: 现在我要问大家一个实际问题：一列十四万公斤重的火车，能只靠太阳能产生的蒸汽开起来吗？

paras.en: Well, one engineer, Tim Castleman, believes it’s possible, and his home city of Sacramento, California, should see the technology’s first test as part of the upgrading of its rail yard, Castleman, who is an inventor and self-proclaimed steam visionary, is campaigning for a new steam train that runs without any fire and could run on an existing 10-kilometer line, drawing tourists and perhaps offering city commuters a green alternative to their cars, Castleman wants to build an array of solar magnifying mirrors at one end of the line to collect and focus heat onto water-filled tubes.
paras.zh: 嗯，有一位工程师蒂姆·卡斯尔曼认为这是可能的，他的家乡加利福尼亚州萨克拉门托在升级铁路车场时，这项技术应该会迎来首次试验。卡斯尔曼是一位发明家，自称蒸汽梦想家，他正在为一种新型蒸汽火车奔走呼吁：这种火车不用烧火，可以在现有的一条十公里长的线路上运行，既能吸引游客，也许还能为城里通勤的人提供一种代替汽车的绿色出行方式。卡斯尔曼想在线路的一端建一组太阳能聚光镜，把热量收集起来，聚焦到装满水的管子上。

w.m: n. 有远见的人；梦想家
v. 奔走呼吁；开展运动

paras.en: This would generate steam that could be used to fill tanks on a small steam train without the use of fire.
paras.zh: 这样产生的蒸汽可以灌进一列小型蒸汽火车的罐子里，用不着烧火。

paras.en: Supplying power to trains in this way would offer the shortest distance from well to wheels, he says, with the least amount of energy lost.
paras.zh: 他说，用这种方式给火车供能，从能源源头到车轮的距离最短，损失的能量也最少。

paras.en: According to Harry Valentine, a Canadian engineer who is researching modern steam technology, a special tank measuring two by 10 meters could store over 750 kilowatt hours of energy as high-pressure steam, enough to pull a two-car train for an hour or so.
paras.zh: 加拿大工程师哈里·瓦伦丁正在研究现代蒸汽技术，据他说，一个长十米、宽两米的特制罐子能以高压蒸汽的形式储存七百五十多千瓦时的能量，足够拉动一列两节车厢的火车跑一个小时左右。

paras.en: Energy to drive a steam locomotive can be stored in other materials besides water.
paras.zh: 驱动蒸汽机车的能量，除了用水，还可以储存在别的材料里。

paras.en: For example, a team at Tohoku University in Japan has studied materials that can store large amounts of heat.
paras.zh: 比如，日本东北大学的一个团队就研究过能储存大量热量的材料。

paras.en: When heated, these materials turn from a solid into a liquid, absorbing energy as they change phase.
paras.zh: 这些材料受热后会从固体变成液体，改变物态时吸收能量。

paras.en: The liquid is maintained above its melting point until steam is required, at which point the liquid is allowed to turn back into a solid, releasing its stored energy.
paras.zh: 液体一直保持在熔点以上，直到需要蒸汽的时候，再让它变回固体，释放出储存的能量。

paras.en: Another team at Nagoya University in Japan has tested calcium compound as an energy storage material.
paras.zh: 日本名古屋大学的另一个团队试验了用钙化合物作储能材料。

paras.en: Heating this chemical compound drives off carbon dioxide gas, leaving calcium oxide.
paras.zh: 给这种化合物加热会释放出二氧化碳气体，留下氧化钙。

paras.en: The gas can be stored under pressure in a tank.
paras.zh: 这些气体可以加压储存在罐子里。

paras.en: To recover the energy, the gas is fed back over the calcium oxide.
paras.zh: 要把能量取回来，就把气体重新送回氧化钙上。

paras.en: In theory, says Valentine, this can create a high enough temperature to generate superheated steam.
paras.zh: 瓦伦丁说，理论上，这样能产生足够高的温度，生成过热蒸汽。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What has the speaker previously talked about?
paras.zh: 第十九题：说话人之前讲过什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What is Tim Castleman trying to do in Sacramento?
paras.zh: 第二十题：蒂姆·卡斯尔曼想在萨克拉门托做什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What has a Japanese research team tried to do?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：日本的一个研究团队尝试做什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Today’s crisis in care for older people in England has two main causes.
paras.zh: 如今英格兰老年人照护出现危机，主要有两个原因。

paras.en: First, people are living longer with a lot more complex needs.
paras.zh: 第一，人们活得更久了，需求也复杂得多。

paras.en: Second, they rely on a system that has long been marked by a poor relation between national health and social care services.
paras.zh: 第二，他们依赖的这套体系长期以来一直有个问题：国家医疗服务和社会照护服务彼此衔接得很差。

paras.en: Current services originate in two key measures; they are the National Health Service and the 1948 National Assistance Act.
paras.zh: 现有的服务源于两项关键措施，那就是国民医疗服务体系和一九四八年的《国民救助法》。

paras.en: This required local governments to provide residential accommodation for older people and supervise care homes run by independent organizations.
paras.zh: 这部法律要求地方政府为老年人提供养老住所，并监管由独立机构开办的养老院。

paras.en: They also provided home and community services, including meals, day centres, and home helpers, and other subsidized services.
paras.zh: 地方政府还提供上门和社区服务，包括送餐、日间照料中心、居家护工以及其他有补贴的服务。

paras.en: The National Health Service was free and wholly publicly provided.
paras.zh: 国民医疗服务体系是免费的，完全由公共部门提供。

paras.en: It delivered the best healthcare for all.
paras.zh: 它为所有人提供最好的医疗服务。

paras.en: No such vision guided residential and community care, though.
paras.zh: 不过，养老住所和社区照护却没有这样的理念来指导。

paras.en: The care was substantially provided by voluntary services, which worked together with local authorities as they long had with eligibility based on income.
paras.zh: 照护主要由志愿服务机构提供，它们和地方政府合作，一直以来都是这样，而能否享受服务要看收入。

paras.en: Today, life expectancy has risen from 66 for a male at birth in 1948 to around 80 now.
paras.zh: 如今，男性的出生时预期寿命已经从一九四八年的六十六岁提高到现在的八十岁左右。

paras.en: In addition, there is better overall health and improved medical knowledge and care.
paras.zh: 此外，人们的整体健康状况更好了，医学知识和医疗护理也有了进步。

paras.en: This means an unprecedented number of people are surviving longer in conditions requiring expert support.
paras.zh: 这意味着，身体状况需要专业照护、却活得更久的人，数量之多前所未有。

paras.en: Families provide at least as much care as they ever did.
paras.zh: 家庭提供的照护至少和以往一样多。

paras.en: Even so, they can really, without subsidized support, address serious personal needs.
paras.zh: 即便如此，没有补贴支持，他们也很难照顾好那些严重的个人需求。

paras.en: Care for older people faced persistent criticism as these trends became apparent.
paras.zh: 随着这些趋势越来越明显，老年人照护不断受到批评。

paras.en: From the early 1960s, local authorities were required to plan health and welfare services.
paras.zh: 从二十世纪六十年代初起，地方政府就被要求规划医疗和福利服务。

paras.en: The aim was to enable older people to remain in their own homes for as long as possible, but this increased concern about the lack of coordination between free health and paid-for social care.
paras.zh: 目的是让老年人尽可能长时间地住在自己家里，但这加重了人们的担忧：免费的医疗和自费的社会照护之间缺乏协调。

paras.en: Through the 1970s, a number of measures sought to improve matters.
paras.zh: 整个七十年代，政府出台了一系列措施，想改善状况。

paras.en: However, at a time of financial crisis, funding diminished and little changed.
paras.zh: 然而，正值金融危机，资金减少了，状况几乎没有改变。

paras.en: In the 1980s, the government cut spending.
paras.zh: 八十年代，政府削减了开支。

paras.en: Meanwhile, preference for private over public services made management even more difficult.
paras.zh: 与此同时，相对于公共服务，人们更偏爱私营服务，这让管理更加困难。

paras.en: Simultaneously, the number of sick older people grew.
paras.zh: 同时，生病的老年人越来越多。

paras.en: Governments emphasized the need to improve services.
paras.zh: 历届政府都强调需要改善服务。

paras.en: They did so, though, while doing little to stop the erosion of available aid.
paras.zh: 可它们一边这么说，一边几乎没采取什么措施来阻止可用援助一点点减少。

paras.en: Services were irregular across authorities, unless you were prepared to pay they were increasingly difficult to obtain for any but the most severely disabled.
paras.zh: 各地方政府的服务参差不齐，除非你愿意自掏腰包，否则除了重度残疾的人，谁都越来越难获得这些服务。

w.m: adj. 不规则的；参差不齐的

paras.en: Why has 60 years of criticism produced so little change?
paras.zh: 为什么六十年的批评带来的改变这么少？

paras.en: Discrimination against older people has a long history.
paras.zh: 对老年人的歧视由来已久。

paras.en: Additionally, those affected by inadequate health and social care are too vulnerable to launch the protests that have addressed other forms of discrimination.
paras.zh: 此外，受医疗和社会照护不足影响的人太脆弱了，没法像别的歧视问题那样发起抗议，引起重视。

w.m: adj. 脆弱的；易受伤害的

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What is one cause of the current crisis in care for the elderly in England?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：英格兰当前老年人照护危机的原因之一是什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the speaker say about residential and community care?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于养老住所和社区照护，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What made management of care for the elderly more difficult in the 1980s?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：二十世纪八十年代，是什么让老年人照护的管理更加困难？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker say about older people in England?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于英格兰的老年人，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2018年12月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2018年12月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，男士请女士帮他和雕像合影，说自己梦想成为网红，最近花大量时间修图、发帖、研究热门话题，女士则自嘲只有妈妈爱看她的照片。第二段长对话里，主持人在节目《今日物理》中采访理论物理学教授梅丽莎·菲利普斯，她讲到宇宙大爆炸时物质和反物质同时产生，正因为物质略多一点，宇宙才得以形成。第一篇短文讲美国女子米歇尔·迈尔斯患上“外国口音综合征”，一觉醒来就说起了英国口音。第二篇短文讲在英国野外游泳越来越受欢迎，尤其受女性青睐，并介绍女性游泳的历史和英吉利海峡第一位女性横渡者。第一段录音讨论用脑部扫描测谎的技术，说话人认为它还没有经过严格检验，不可轻信。第二段录音讲世界上语言分布极不均匀，研究人员发现以往有关语言多样性的研究很少，也没得出清晰的规律。第三段录音讲美国贫富差距越来越大，低收入者只盼有一份全职工作，以及造成这种局面的原因。

paras.en: College English Test, Band Six, Part Two: Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with the single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Do you mind taking my photo with the statue over there?
paras.zh: 你能帮我跟那边的雕像拍张照吗？

paras.en: I think it will make a great shot.
paras.zh: 我觉得会拍出一张很棒的照片。

paras.en: Sure, no worries.
paras.zh: 当然，没问题。

paras.en: You’re always taking photos.
paras.zh: 你总是在拍照。

paras.en: What do you do with all the photos you take?
paras.zh: 你拍的那么多照片都拿来干什么呀？

paras.en: Well, don’t laugh.
paras.zh: 嗯，你可别笑啊。

paras.en: My dream is to become an online celebrity of sorts.
paras.zh: 我的梦想是当个网红什么的。

paras.en: You’re not serious, are you?
paras.zh: 你不是认真的吧？

paras.en: I am completely.
paras.zh: 我完全是认真的。

paras.en: I just got the idea a few months ago after posting some holiday photos on my social media accounts, a lot of people liked my photos and started asking me for travel tips.
paras.zh: 几个月前，我在社交媒体账号上发了一些度假照片，很多人都喜欢，还开始向我讨要旅行攻略，我这才有了这个想法。

paras.en: So I figured I’d give it a go.
paras.zh: 所以我想不如试一试。

paras.en: I post a lot on social media anyway, so I’ve got nothing to lose.
paras.zh: 反正我在社交媒体上发的东西就很多，所以也没什么可损失的。

paras.en: I guess that’s true.
paras.zh: 我想也是。

paras.en: So what do you have to do to become Internet famous, surprisingly, a lot more than I did as a hobby.
paras.zh: 那要想在网上走红得做些什么呢？说出来你可能不信，要做的比我以前当爱好的时候多多了。

paras.en: Recently, I’ve been spending a lot more time editing photos, posting online, and clearing storage on my phone.
paras.zh: 最近我花在修图、上网发帖和清理手机存储空间上的时间多了很多。

paras.en: It’s always full now.
paras.zh: 现在手机总是满的。

paras.en: That doesn’t sound like too much work.
paras.zh: 听起来工作量也不算太大嘛。

paras.en: Well, there’s more to it.
paras.zh: 嗯，还不止这些呢。

paras.en: I spent all last weekend researching what topics are popular, what words to use in captions, and similar accounts to follow, it really was a lot to take in, and I was up well past midnight.
paras.zh: 上周末我一整个周末都在研究什么话题受欢迎、配文用什么词，还有哪些同类账号值得关注，要消化的东西真多，我一直熬到半夜过后很久才睡。

paras.en: I’d say it’s paying off, though.
paras.zh: 不过我觉得这些努力没白费。

paras.en: I increased the number of people following my accounts by 15% already.
paras.zh: 关注我账号的人已经增加了百分之十五。

paras.en: That is impressive.
paras.zh: 真了不起。

w.m: adj. 令人钦佩的；了不起的

paras.en: I guess I never thought much about all the effort behind the scene.
paras.zh: 我从没怎么想过背后要花这么多工夫。

paras.en: Now that I think about it, there’s always something wrong with my photos as it is: half smiles, closed eyes, messy hair.
paras.zh: 现在想想，我的照片本来就总有毛病：笑得不自然、闭着眼、头发乱糟糟。

paras.en: I hope you have better luck than I do.
paras.zh: 希望你运气比我好。

paras.en: Then again, I think the only person interested in my photos is my mum.
paras.zh: 不过话说回来，我觉得对我的照片感兴趣的只有我妈妈。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the man ask the woman to do?
paras.zh: 第一题：男士请女士做什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man dream of?
paras.zh: 第二题：男士的梦想是什么？

paras.en: Question three: What has the man been busy doing recently?
paras.zh: 第三题：男士最近一直在忙什么？

paras.en: Question four: What does the woman say about her photos?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于自己的照片，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Good evening and welcome to Physics Today.
paras.zh: 晚上好，欢迎收看《今日物理》。

paras.en: Here we interview some of the greatest minds in physics as they help us to understand some of the most complicated theories.
paras.zh: 在这里我们会采访物理学界一些最杰出的头脑，请他们帮我们理解一些最复杂的理论。

paras.en: Today, I’m very pleased to welcome Dr. Melissa Phillips, professor of theoretical physics.
paras.zh: 今天，我很高兴请到梅丽莎·菲利普斯博士，她是理论物理学教授。

paras.en: She’s here to tell us a little about what it is she studies.
paras.zh: 她来给我们简单讲讲她研究的究竟是什么。

paras.en: Dr. Phillips, you seem to study everything.
paras.zh: 菲利普斯博士，您好像什么都研究。

paras.en: I guess that would be fair to say.
paras.zh: 这么说也算公道吧。

paras.en: I spend most of my time studying the Big Bang theory and where our universe came from.
paras.zh: 我大部分时间都在研究宇宙大爆炸理论，研究我们的宇宙是从哪里来的。

paras.en: Can you tell us a little about that?
paras.zh: 您能给我们简单讲讲吗？

paras.en: Well, I’m very interested in why the universe exists at all.
paras.zh: 嗯，我很想知道宇宙究竟为什么会存在。

paras.en: That may sound odd, but the fact is, at the moment of the Big Bang, both matter and antimatter were created.
paras.zh: 这听起来可能有点怪，但事实是，在大爆炸的那一刻，物质和反物质都产生了。

paras.en: For a short time, and I mean just a fraction of a second, the whole universe was a super hot soup of radiation filled with these particles.
paras.zh: 在很短的时间里，我是说只有一瞬间，整个宇宙是一锅超高温的辐射“汤”，里面充满了这些粒子。

paras.en: So, what’s baffled scientists for so long is why is there a universe at all?
paras.zh: 所以，长期以来让科学家困惑不解的，就是宇宙究竟为什么会存在。

paras.en: That’s because matter and antimatter are basically opposites of each other; they are exactly alike, except that they have opposite electrical charges.
paras.zh: 这是因为物质和反物质基本上是彼此对立的，它们一模一样，只是电荷相反。

w.m: n. 对立面；adj. 相反的

paras.en: So when they collide, they destroy each other.
paras.zh: 所以它们一相撞，就会把对方毁掉。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 正是这样。

paras.en: So during the first few moments of the Big Bang, the universe was extremely hot and very small.
paras.zh: 所以在大爆炸最初的那一小段时间里，宇宙温度极高，而且非常小。

paras.en: Matter and the now more exotic antimatter would have had little space to avoid each other.
paras.zh: 物质和如今更罕见的反物质几乎没有空间避开对方。

paras.en: This means that they should have totally wiped each other out, leaving the universe completely barren.
paras.zh: 这就意味着，它们本该把对方彻底消灭，让宇宙变得一片荒芜。

paras.en: But a recent study seems to point to the fact that when matter and antimatter were first created, there were slightly more particles of matter, which allowed the universe we all live in to form.
paras.zh: 可最近的一项研究似乎表明，物质和反物质刚产生时，物质粒子稍微多一点，正是这一点让我们生活的宇宙得以形成。

paras.en: Exactly, because there was slightly more matter, the collisions quickly depleted all the antimatter and left just enough matter to create stars, planets, and eventually us.
paras.zh: 没错，因为物质稍微多一点，碰撞很快就耗尽了所有反物质，剩下的物质刚好够形成恒星、行星，最终还有我们人类。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the man say is physics today?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士说《今日物理》是什么？

paras.en: Question six: What is the woman physicist’s main research area?
paras.zh: 第六题：这位女物理学家主要研究什么领域？

paras.en: Question seven: What is the woman interested in?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士对什么感兴趣？

paras.en: Question eight: What seems to be the finding of the recent study?
paras.zh: 第八题：最近那项研究的发现似乎是什么？

paras.en: Section B Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: In this week’s edition of special series on bizarre medical conditions, there’s a report of the case of Michelle Myers.
paras.zh: 在本周的离奇病症系列特别节目中，有一篇关于米歇尔·迈尔斯病例的报道。

paras.en: Myers is an American woman who woke up one day speaking with a British accent, even though she’s lived in the United States all her life.
paras.zh: 迈尔斯是一位美国女性，她一辈子都住在美国，可有一天醒来却说起了英国口音。

paras.en: In 2015, Myers went to bed with a terrible headache.
paras.zh: 二零一五年，迈尔斯头痛得厉害，上床睡觉了。

paras.en: She woke up sounding like someone from England.
paras.zh: 她醒来时，说话听起来就像英国人。

paras.en: Her British accent has remained for the past two years.
paras.zh: 她的英国口音已经持续了两年。

paras.en: Previously, Myers had woken up speaking in Irish and Australian accents.
paras.zh: 此前，迈尔斯就曾经一觉醒来说起了爱尔兰口音和澳大利亚口音。

paras.en: However, on both of those occasions, the accents lasted for only a week.
paras.zh: 不过那两次口音都只持续了一周。

paras.en: Myers has been diagnosed with foreign accent syndrome.
paras.zh: 迈尔斯被诊断出患有外国口音综合征。

paras.en: It’s a disorder in which a person experiences a sudden change to their speech so that they sound like they are speaking in a foreign accent, the condition is most often caused by a stroke or traumatic brain injury.
paras.zh: 这是一种疾病，患者说话会突然改变，听起来像在用外国口音说话。这种病最常见的病因是中风或外伤性脑损伤。

paras.en: Although people with the syndrome have intelligible speech, their manner of speaking is altered in terms of timing and tongue placement, which may distort their pronunciation.
paras.zh: 虽然这种综合征的患者说话别人能听懂，但他们的说话方式在节奏和舌头位置上发生了变化，这可能会让他们的发音走样。

w.m: adj. 可理解的；听得懂的

paras.en: The result is that they may sound foreign when speaking their native language, it’s not clear whether Myers has experienced a stroke or other brain damage, but she also has a separate medical condition, which can result in loose joints, easily bruised skin, and other problems.
paras.zh: 结果就是，他们说自己的母语时，听起来可能像外国人。目前还不清楚迈尔斯是否经历过中风或其他脑损伤，不过她还另外患有一种病，可能导致关节松弛、皮肤容易淤青等问题。

paras.en: Foreign accent syndrome is rare, with only about 60 cases reported within the past century.
paras.zh: 外国口音综合征很罕见，过去一百年里报告的病例只有六十例左右。

paras.en: However, a different American woman reportedly spoke with a Russian accent in 2010 after she fell down the stairs and hit her head.
paras.zh: 不过，据报道，二零一零年另一位美国女性从楼梯上摔下来撞到头后，说起了俄罗斯口音。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What happened to Michelle Myers one day?
paras.zh: 第九题：有一天米歇尔·迈尔斯身上发生了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the passage say about foreign accent syndrome?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于外国口音综合征，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What accent did another American woman speak with after a head injury?
paras.zh: 第十一题：另一位美国女性头部受伤后说的是什么口音？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: There is something about water that makes it a good metaphor for life.
paras.zh: 水有某种特质，很适合用来比喻人生。

paras.en: That may be one reason why so many people find relief in swimming when life’s seas get rough, and it goes some way towards explaining why books about swimming, in which people tackle icy lakes, race in rivers, and overcome oceans while reflecting on their lives, have recently become so popular.
paras.zh: 这也许就是为什么生活中风浪来袭时，那么多人能从游泳中得到解脱；这也在一定程度上解释了，为什么那些讲游泳的书最近这么受欢迎——书里的人挑战冰冷的湖泊、在河里比赛、征服大海，同时回顾自己的人生。

w.m: adj. 波涛汹涌的；艰难的

paras.en: These books reflect a trend, particularly strong in Britain, where swimming in pools is declining, but more and more folks are opting for open water.
paras.zh: 这些书反映出一种趋势，这种趋势在英国尤其明显：在泳池游泳的人越来越少，而选择去开阔水域游泳的人越来越多。

paras.en: Wild swimming seems to be especially popular among women.
paras.zh: 野外游泳似乎在女性中尤其受欢迎。

paras.en: Jenny Landreth recently published a guide to the best swimming spots in London, her new book Swell interweaves her own story with a history of female pioneers who accomplished remarkable feats and paved the way for future generations.
paras.zh: 珍妮·兰德雷思最近出版了一本伦敦最佳游泳地点指南，她的新书《涌浪》把她自己的故事和一段女性先驱的历史交织在一起，这些先驱完成了了不起的壮举，为后人铺平了道路。

paras.en: Notions of modesty restricted women in the Victorian era, but they still swam.
paras.zh: 维多利亚时代，端庄矜持的观念束缚着女性，但她们照样游泳。

paras.en: A bathing machine was rolled down to the seashore so women would not be seen in swimwear.
paras.zh: 人们会把一种更衣车推到海边，这样女性穿着泳衣就不会被人看见。

paras.en: In 1892, the Gentlewoman’s Book of Sport described a woman swimming in a heavy dress, boots, hat, gloves, and carrying an umbrella.
paras.zh: 一八九二年，《淑女运动之书》描述了一位女性游泳时穿着厚重的连衣裙、靴子，戴着帽子和手套，还打着一把伞。

w.m: n. 淑女；有教养的女子

paras.en: Eventually, swimming became freer.
paras.zh: 后来，游泳慢慢变得自由了。

paras.en: Mixed bathing was permitted on British beaches in 1901.
paras.zh: 一九零一年，英国的海滩允许男女同浴了。

paras.en: Women won the right to swim in public pools, learned to swim properly, created appropriate swimwear, and in time even competed against men.
paras.zh: 女性赢得了在公共泳池游泳的权利，学会了正规的游泳方法，设计出合适的泳衣，后来甚至还和男性同场竞技。

paras.en: The first woman to cross the English Channel was Gertrude Ederle in 1926.
paras.zh: 第一位横渡英吉利海峡的女性是格特鲁德·埃德尔，那是一九二六年。

paras.en: She beat the record by almost two hours, and her father rewarded her with a red sports car.
paras.zh: 她把原纪录缩短了将近两个小时，她父亲奖励了她一辆红色跑车。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What has become so popular recently?
paras.zh: 第十二题：最近什么变得这么受欢迎？

paras.en: Question 13: What did Jenny Landreth do recently?
paras.zh: 第十三题：珍妮·兰德雷思最近做了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What do we learn about women in the Victorian era?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于维多利亚时代的女性，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the passage say about Gertrude Ederle?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于格特鲁德·埃德尔，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Section C: Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Today I’m going to talk about a very special kind of person.
paras.zh: 今天我要讲的是一种非常特别的人。

paras.en: Psychologists call them masters of deception; those rare individuals with a natural ability to tell with complete confidence when someone is telling a lie.
paras.zh: 心理学家称他们为识谎大师：这些人极为少见，天生就能十拿九稳地看出别人是不是在撒谎。

paras.en: For decades, researchers and law enforcement agencies have tried to build a machine that will do the same thing.
paras.zh: 几十年来，研究人员和执法机构一直想造出一台能做到同样事情的机器。

paras.en: Now, a company in Massachusetts says that by using magnetic brain scans, they can determine with 97% accuracy whether someone is telling the truth.
paras.zh: 现在，马萨诸塞州的一家公司说，他们利用脑磁扫描，能以百分之九十七的准确率判断一个人说的是不是真话。

paras.en: They hope that the technology will be cleared for use in American courts by early next year.
paras.zh: 他们希望这项技术到明年初能获准在美国法庭上使用。

paras.en: But is this really the ultimate tool for you, the lawyers of tomorrow.
paras.zh: 可是，对你们这些未来的律师来说，这真是终极利器吗？

paras.en: You will not find many brain scientists celebrating this breakthrough.
paras.zh: 你不会看到多少脑科学家为这项突破欢呼。

paras.en: The company might be very optimistic, but the ability of their machine to detect deception has not provided credible proof.
paras.zh: 这家公司也许很乐观，但他们的机器能识破谎言，这一点并没有拿出可信的证据。

paras.en: That’s because the technology has not been properly tested in real-world situations.
paras.zh: 这是因为这项技术还没在真实情境中好好测试过。

paras.en: In life, there are different kinds of lies and diverse context in which they’re told.
paras.zh: 生活中，谎言多种多样，说谎的情境也各不相同。

w.m: adj. 不同的；多种多样的

paras.en: These differences may elicit different brain responses.
paras.zh: 这些差别可能会引起不同的大脑反应。

paras.en: Does their hypothesis behind the test apply in every case?
paras.zh: 这项测试背后的假设是否适用于所有情况呢？

paras.en: We don’t know the answer because studies done on how reliable this machine is have not yet been duplicated.
paras.zh: 我们不知道答案，因为关于这台机器有多可靠的研究，至今还没有人重复验证过。

paras.en: Much more research is badly needed.
paras.zh: 还急需做更多的研究。

paras.en: Whether the technology is eventually deemed reliable enough for the courts will ultimately be decided by the judges.
paras.zh: 这项技术最终是否被认为可靠到能用于法庭，最后将由法官来决定。

paras.en: Let’s hope they’re wise enough not to be fooled by a machine that claims to determine truthfulness at the flip of a switch, they should also be skeptical of the growing tendency to try to reduce all human traits and actions to the level of brain activity.
paras.zh: 但愿他们足够明智，不会被一台号称一按开关就能判断真假的机器骗了。他们也应该对一种越来越普遍的倾向保持怀疑：试图把人的一切特点和行为都归结为大脑活动。

w.h: at the flip of a switch

w.m: adj. 越来越多的；增长的

paras.en: Often, they do not map that easily.
paras.zh: 很多时候，它们并不能那么简单地一一对应。

paras.en: Moreover, understanding the brain is not the same as understanding the mind.
paras.zh: 而且，了解大脑并不等于了解心智。

paras.en: Some researchers have suggested that thoughts cannot properly be seen as purely internal.
paras.zh: 一些研究人员提出，思想不能被看作纯粹是内在的东西。

paras.en: Instead, thoughts make sense only in reference to the individual’s external world.
paras.zh: 相反，思想只有联系个人的外部世界才有意义。

paras.en: So, while there may be insights to be gained from matching behavior to brain activity, those insights will not necessarily lead to justice in a court of law.
paras.zh: 所以，虽然把行为和大脑活动对应起来也许能带来一些见解，但这些见解不一定能让法庭作出公正的判决。

paras.en: Problems surround the use of machines to spot deception, at least until it has been rigorously tested.
paras.zh: 用机器识破谎言存在种种问题，至少在它经过严格测试之前是这样。

paras.en: A high-tech test that can tell when a person is not telling the truth sounds too good to be true, and when something sounds too good to be true, it usually is.
paras.zh: 一种能看出别人没说真话的高科技测试听起来好得不像真的，而当一件事听起来好得不像真的，它通常就不是真的。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What have researchers and law enforcement agencies tried to do?
paras.zh: 第十六题：研究人员和执法机构一直想做什么？

paras.en: Question 17: How do many brain scientists respond to the Massachusetts company’s so-called technological breakthrough?
paras.zh: 第十七题：对于马萨诸塞州那家公司所谓的技术突破，许多脑科学家是什么反应？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker think of using a high-tech test to determine whether a person is telling the truth?
paras.zh: 第十八题：用高科技测试来判断一个人是否在说真话，说话人怎么看？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Last week, I attended a research workshop on an island in the South Pacific.
paras.zh: 上周，我在南太平洋的一个岛上参加了一个研究研讨会。

paras.en: 30 people were present, and all except me came from the island, called Malakula in the nation of Vanuatu.
paras.zh: 到场的有三十人，除了我，都来自这个岛，它叫马勒库拉，属于瓦努阿图这个国家。

paras.en: They live in 16 different communities and speak 16 distinct languages.
paras.zh: 他们住在十六个不同的社区，说十六种截然不同的语言。

w.m: adj. 截然不同的；独特的

paras.en: In many cases, you could stand at the edge of one village and see the outskirts of the next community, yet the residents of each village speak a completely different language.
paras.zh: 很多时候，你站在一个村子的边上，就能看到下一个社区的边缘，可每个村子的居民说的却是完全不同的语言。

paras.en: According to recent work by my colleagues at the Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History, this island, just 100 kilometers long and 20 kilometers wide is home to speakers of perhaps 40 different indigenous languages.
paras.zh: 根据我在马克斯·普朗克人类历史科学研究所的同事最近的研究，这个岛只有一百公里长、二十公里宽，却生活着说大约四十种不同本土语言的人。

paras.en: Why so many?
paras.zh: 怎么会有这么多呢？

paras.en: We could ask this same question of the entire globe.
paras.zh: 我们可以对整个地球提出同样的问题。

paras.en: People don’t speak one universal language or even a handful.
paras.zh: 人类并不说一种通用的语言，甚至也不只说少数几种。

paras.en: Instead, today our species collectively speaks over 7000 distinct languages, and these languages are not spread randomly across the planet.
paras.zh: 相反，如今我们人类总共说七千多种不同的语言，而且这些语言在地球上的分布并不是随机的。

paras.en: For example, far more languages are found in tropical regions than in the mild zones.
paras.zh: 比如，热带地区的语言就比温带地区多得多。

paras.en: The tropical island of New Guinea is home to over 900 languages.
paras.zh: 热带岛屿新几内亚就有九百多种语言。

paras.en: Russia, 20 times larger, has 105 indigenous languages.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯比它大二十倍，却只有一百零五种本土语言。

paras.en: Even within the tropics, language diversity varies widely.
paras.zh: 即便在热带地区，语言的多样性也相差很大。

w.m: adv. 很大程度上；广泛地

paras.en: For example, the 250,000 people who live on Vanuatu’s 80 islands speak 110 different languages.
paras.zh: 比如，生活在瓦努阿图八十个岛上的二十五万人说一百一十种不同的语言。

paras.en: But in Bangladesh, a population 600 times greater speaks only 41 languages.
paras.zh: 可是在孟加拉国，人口是它的六百倍，却只说四十一种语言。

paras.en: How come humans speak so many languages, and why are they so unevenly spread across the planet?
paras.zh: 人类怎么会说这么多种语言，又为什么在地球上分布得这么不均匀呢？

paras.en: As it turns out, we have few clear answers to these fundamental questions about how humanity communicates.
paras.zh: 结果发现，对于人类如何交流的这些根本问题，我们几乎都没有清楚的答案。

paras.en: Most people can easily brainstorm possible answers to these intriguing questions.
paras.zh: 对这些有趣的问题，大多数人都能随口想出几种可能的答案。

w.m: v. 集思广益；头脑风暴
adj. 有趣的；引人入胜的

paras.en: They hypothesize that language diversity must be about history, cultural differences, mountains or oceans dividing populations.
paras.zh: 他们推测，语言多样性一定跟历史、文化差异，或者把人群隔开的高山、海洋有关。

paras.en: But when our diverse team of researchers from six different disciplines and eight different countries began to review what was known, we were shocked that only a dozen previous studies had been done, including one we ourselves completed on language diversity in the Pacific.
paras.zh: 可是，当我们这个由来自六个学科、八个国家的研究人员组成的多元团队开始梳理已有的研究成果时，我们震惊地发现，以前只做过十来项研究，其中包括我们自己完成的一项关于太平洋地区语言多样性的研究。

paras.en: These prior efforts all examined the degree to which different environmental, social, and geographic variables correlated with a number of languages found in a given location.
paras.zh: 之前的这些研究都考察了各种环境、社会和地理变量与某个地方的语言数量有多大程度的相关。

paras.en: The results varied a lot from one study to another, and no clear patterns emerged.
paras.zh: 不同研究的结果差别很大，没有出现清晰的规律。

paras.en: The studies also ran up against many methodological challenges; the biggest of which centered on the old statistical saying, “Correlation does not equal causation.”
paras.zh: 这些研究在方法上也遇到了很多难题，其中最大的难题就围绕着那句统计学老话：“相关不等于因果。”

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about the island of Malakula?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于马勒库拉岛，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What do we learn from the talk about languages in the world?
paras.zh: 第二十题：从讲话中，我们对世界上的语言了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What have the diverse team of researchers found about the previous studies on language diversity?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于以前那些语言多样性的研究，这个多元研究团队发现了什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: We often hear people say that America is a land of opportunity, a country built on hope to aspire to greatness, on the American dream.
paras.zh: 我们常听人说，美国是一片充满机遇的土地，是一个建立在希望之上的国家——希望追求卓越，希望实现美国梦。

paras.en: But is the dream as we once knew it dying?
paras.zh: 可是，我们曾经熟悉的那个梦想正在消亡吗？

paras.en: Today’s demographics show that the middle class is disappearing, and now the richest 1% of the population has amassed more wealth than the bottom 90%.
paras.zh: 如今的人口统计数据表明，中产阶级正在消失；现在，最富有的百分之一人口积累的财富，已经超过了底层百分之九十人口的财富。

paras.en: Once upon a time, Americans thought that if they worked hard enough, even in the face of adversity, they would be rewarded with success.
paras.zh: 从前，美国人认为只要足够努力，即便身处逆境，也会得到成功的回报。

paras.en: These days, though, the divide between rich and poor is greater than it has ever been.
paras.zh: 可如今，贫富之间的差距比以往任何时候都大。

paras.en: The question is, what is it going to take to change things.
paras.zh: 问题是，要怎样才能改变这种状况？

paras.en: Maybe one day soon, real change will actually be made in our nation, and the gap will be eradicated.
paras.zh: 也许不久的将来，我们国家会真正有所改变，差距也会被消除。

paras.en: But what happens in the meantime?
paras.zh: 可在那之前，又会怎么样呢？

paras.en: Is there something that we can do to help close the gap?
paras.zh: 我们能做点什么来帮助缩小差距吗？

paras.en: Is there something that we can do to prove that a little compassion goes a long way?
paras.zh: 我们能做点什么来证明一点点同情心就能起很大作用吗？

paras.en: If we want to fix the problem of the income gap, first we have to understand it.
paras.zh: 如果我们想解决收入差距问题，首先得了解它。

paras.en: It is a grim reality that you can have one person who only makes around $13,000 a year, while across town another is making millions.
paras.zh: 残酷的现实是，一个人一年只挣一万三千美元左右，而城里另一头的人却在挣几百万。

paras.en: For me, it is kind of astonishing, and if you ask low-income people what’s the one thing that would change their life?
paras.zh: 对我来说，这有点令人吃惊；如果你问低收入的人，什么事能改变他们的生活？

paras.en: They’ll say a full-time job.
paras.zh: 他们会说，一份全职工作。

paras.en: That’s all they aspire to.
paras.zh: 他们盼望的就只有这个。

paras.en: So why is it so difficult for so many people to find employment?
paras.zh: 那为什么这么多人找工作都这么难？

paras.en: It partly comes down to profit-driven business models that are built around low-wage work and part-time jobs that don’t provide benefits, businesses in order to bolster profits, hire employees as part-time workers only.
paras.zh: 部分原因在于以利润为导向的商业模式，这些模式建立在低薪工作和不提供福利的兼职工作之上；企业为了增加利润，只把员工当作兼职工人来雇用。

paras.en: This means they are paid the lowest legal wage and receive no health care or other benefits provided to full-time employees.
paras.zh: 这就意味着，他们拿的是法定最低工资，也享受不到全职员工的医疗保险或其他福利。

paras.en: Simultaneously, technological advancement and a global economy has reduced the demand for well-paying blue-collar jobs here in the United States.
paras.zh: 与此同时，技术进步和全球经济让美国本土收入不错的蓝领工作需求减少了。

paras.en: The cumulative effect of these two factors is that many Americans are forced to take two or more part-time jobs just to make ends meet.
paras.zh: 这两个因素累积起来，结果就是很多美国人被迫同时打两份甚至更多兼职，才能勉强维持生计。

w.m: 收支相抵；勉强维持生计

paras.en: What has become obvious to me when it comes to the income gap is that there needs to be an opportunity for the people at the bottom to push them back up and push them into the middle class to give them hope in their lives.
paras.zh: 说到收入差距，我越来越明白一点：必须给底层的人一个机会，把他们推上去，推进中产阶级，让他们的生活有希望。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do the surveys show about America according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人说，调查显示美国怎么样了？

paras.en: Question 23: What did Americans use to believe?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：美国人过去相信什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What do low-income people aspire to?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：低收入的人渴望什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What do businesses do to increase their revenues?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：企业是怎样增加收入的？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2019年6月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2019年6月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，凯茜和约翰在婚礼前的聚会上相识：凯茜是新娘布伦达的同事，要给婚礼做蛋糕，约翰是摄影师，要给婚礼拍照当贺礼。第二段长对话里，男士告诉快要上大学的女生，大学里要自己对自己负责，管好时间，交对朋友，别在社团活动上花太多时间。第一篇短文讲滑雪运动员让·克洛德·基利敢于挑战传统技术，创出新滑法，赢得多项大奖。第二篇短文讲负面情绪会产生有毒物质，身体健康反映心理健康。第一段录音讲初学者和行家的区别：行家不必操心基本动作，能把心思放在比赛或音乐本身上。第二段录音里，在亚洲生活多年的作者谈各种减肥方法和不同文化里的审美观，认为合理饮食加适量运动才是最好的办法。第三段录音里，一位动物学家讲人类为什么失去体毛、肤色为什么深浅不一，以及肤色至今还在变化。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解。

paras.en: Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hi, my name’s Cathy.
paras.zh: 你好，我叫凯茜。

paras.en: Nice to meet you.
paras.zh: 很高兴认识你。

paras.en: Nice to meet you too, Cathy.
paras.zh: 我也很高兴认识你，凯茜。

paras.en: My name’s John.
paras.zh: 我叫约翰。

paras.en: I’m a university friend of the bride.
paras.zh: 我是新娘的大学同学。

paras.en: What about you?
paras.zh: 你呢？

paras.en: Who do you know at this party?
paras.zh: 这次聚会上你认识谁呀？

paras.en: I’m a colleague of Brenda.
paras.zh: 我是布伦达的同事。

paras.en: I was a little surprised to be invited.
paras.zh: 她请我来，我还有点意外呢。

paras.en: To be honest, we’ve only been working together the last six months, but we quickly became good friends.
paras.zh: 说实话，我们才一起共事了半年，不过很快就成了好朋友。

paras.en: We just wrapped up a project with a difficult client last week.
paras.zh: 上周我们刚做完一个项目，那个客户很难缠。

w.m: adj. 难对付的；难相处的

paras.en: I bet Brenda is glad it’s done with, and she can focus on wedding preparations.
paras.zh: 我猜布伦达一定很高兴那件事结束了，这下她可以专心准备婚礼了。

paras.en: Oh yes, so you’re Cathy from the office.
paras.zh: 哦，对，原来你就是办公室里那位凯茜啊。

paras.en: Actually, I’ve heard a lot about you and that project.
paras.zh: 其实我早就听说过你和那个项目的不少事了。

paras.en: The client sounded like a real nightmare.
paras.zh: 听起来那个客户真是个噩梦。

w.m: n. 噩梦；可怕的人或事

paras.en: Oh, he was.
paras.zh: 哦，可不是嘛。

paras.en: I mean, we deal with all kinds of people on a regular basis.
paras.zh: 我是说，我们平时要跟各种各样的人打交道。

paras.en: It’s part of the job, but he was especially particular.
paras.zh: 这是工作的一部分，可他特别挑剔。

paras.en: Enough about that.
paras.zh: 不说这个了。

paras.en: What line of work are you in?
paras.zh: 你是做哪一行的？

paras.en: Well, right out of college, I worked in advertising for a while.
paras.zh: 嗯，我大学一毕业就做了一段时间的广告。

paras.en: Recently, though, I turned my photography hobby into a small business.
paras.zh: 不过最近，我把摄影这个爱好变成了一门小生意。

paras.en: I’ll actually be taking photos during the big event as a wedding gift.
paras.zh: 其实这次婚礼上我会负责拍照，就当是送给他们的结婚礼物。

paras.en: That sounds wonderful and very thoughtful of you.
paras.zh: 听起来太棒了，你真是有心。

w.m: adj. 体贴的；考虑周到的

paras.en: I bake just as a hobby, but Brenda has asked me to do the cake for the wedding.
paras.zh: 我烤东西只是爱好，可布伦达让我给婚礼做蛋糕。

paras.en: I was a bit nervous saying yes because I’m far from a professional.
paras.zh: 我答应的时候有点紧张，因为我根本算不上专业的。

paras.en: Did you bake the cookies here at the party tonight?
paras.zh: 今晚聚会上的饼干是你烤的吗？

paras.en: Yes, I got the idea from a magazine.
paras.zh: 是的，我是从一本杂志上学来的。

paras.en: They’re delicious.
paras.zh: 太好吃了。

paras.en: You’ve got nothing to worry about.
paras.zh: 你完全不用担心。

paras.en: You’re a natural.
paras.zh: 你真有天分。

w.m: n. 天生的好手；有天赋的人

paras.en: You really think so?
paras.zh: 你真这么觉得？

paras.en: If you hadn’t told me that, I would have guessed they were baked by the restaurant, you know.
paras.zh: 你要是不说，我还以为是餐厅烤的呢。

paras.en: With your event planning experience, you could very well open your own shop.
paras.zh: 你有策划活动的经验，完全可以自己开一家店。

paras.en: One step at a time.
paras.zh: 一步一步来吧。

paras.en: First, I’ll see how baking the wedding cake goes.
paras.zh: 先看看婚礼蛋糕做得怎么样吧。

paras.en: If it’s not a disaster, maybe I’ll give it some more thought.
paras.zh: 要是没搞砸，我也许会再考虑考虑。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What did Cathy and Brenda finish doing last week?
paras.zh: 第一题：凯茜和布伦达上周做完了什么事？

paras.en: Question two: What is John going to do for Brenda?
paras.zh: 第二题：约翰要为布伦达做什么？

paras.en: Question three: How did Cathy feel when asked to bake the cake?
paras.zh: 第三题：被请去做蛋糕时，凯茜感觉怎么样？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man suggest the woman do?
paras.zh: 第四题：男士建议女士做什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: You’re heading for a completely different world now that you’re about to graduate from high school.
paras.zh: 你马上就要高中毕业了，前面是一个完全不同的世界。

paras.en: I know it’s the end of high school, but many of my classmates are going on to the same university, and we are still required to study hard.
paras.zh: 我知道高中结束了，可我好多同学都要上同一所大学，我们还是得努力学习。

paras.en: So, what’s the difference?
paras.zh: 那有什么不一样呢？

paras.en: Many aspects are different here at university.
paras.zh: 大学里很多方面都不一样。

paras.en: The most important one is that you have to take more individual responsibility for your actions.
paras.zh: 最重要的一点是，你得更多地为自己的行为负责。

paras.en: It’s up to your own self-discipline how much effort you put into study.
paras.zh: 你在学习上花多少力气，全靠你自己自觉。

paras.en: Living in college dormitories, there are no parents to tell you to study harder or stop wasting time.
paras.zh: 住在大学宿舍里，没有父母叫你用功一点、别浪费时间。

paras.en: Lecturers have hundreds of students, and they’re not going to follow you up or question you if you miss their lectures, nobody cares.
paras.zh: 讲师有几百个学生，你逃了他们的课，他们不会追着你、也不会来问你，没人管。

paras.en: You mean?
paras.zh: 你是说……？

paras.en: It’s not that nobody’s concerned about you.
paras.zh: 倒不是说没人关心你。

paras.en: It’s just that suddenly at university you are expected to behave like an adult.
paras.zh: 只是一到大学，大家突然就要求你像个成年人一样行事了。

paras.en: That means concentrating on the direction of your life in general, and your own academic performance specifically, for example.
paras.zh: 比如说，这就意味着你要总体上把握好自己人生的方向，具体来说，就是要关注自己的学业成绩。

paras.en: Well, like you need to manage your daily, weekly, and monthly schedules so that you’ll study regularly.
paras.zh: 嗯，比如你得安排好每天、每周、每月的日程，这样才能有规律地学习。

paras.en: Be sure to attend all classes and leave enough time to finish assignments and prepare well for examinations.
paras.zh: 一定要每节课都去上，留出足够的时间完成作业，好好准备考试。

paras.en: Okay, and what else is different?
paras.zh: 好的，还有什么不一样的？

paras.en: Well, in college, there are lots of distractions, and you need to control yourself.
paras.zh: 嗯，大学里让人分心的东西很多，你得管住自己。

paras.en: You will make interesting friends, but you need only keep the friends who respect your student commitments.
paras.zh: 你会交到有意思的朋友，但只需要留下那些尊重你学业的朋友。

paras.en: Also, there are a lot of wonderful clubs, but you shouldn’t allocate too much time to club activities unless they’re directly related to your study.
paras.zh: 另外，大学里有很多很棒的社团，可除非跟你的学习直接相关，否则别在社团活动上花太多时间。

paras.en: It’s also your choice if you want to go out at night, but you would be foolish to let that affect your class performance during the day.
paras.zh: 晚上要不要出去玩也由你自己定，可要是因此影响了白天的课，那就太傻了。

paras.en: Well, I’m determined to do well at university, and I guess I’m going to have to grow up fast.
paras.zh: 嗯，我下定决心要在大学里好好表现，看来我得快点长大了。

w.m: adj. 下定决心的；坚决的

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the man say about college students as compared with high schoolers?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士说大学生和高中生相比怎么样？

paras.en: Question six: What are college students expected to do according to the man?
paras.zh: 第六题：男士认为大学生应该做什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What kind of friends does the man suggest the woman make as a college student?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士建议女士上大学后交什么样的朋友？

paras.en: Question eight: What kind of club activities should college students engage in, according to the man?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士认为大学生应该参加什么样的社团活动？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Most successful people are unorthodox persons whose minds wander outside traditional ways of thinking.
paras.zh: 大多数成功人士都不循规蹈矩，他们的思维会跳出传统的思维方式。

w.m: adj. 非传统的；不循常规的

paras.en: Instead of trying to refine old formulas, they invent new ones.
paras.zh: 他们不去改进老办法，而是发明新办法。

paras.en: When Jean Claude Killy made the French national ski team in the early 1960s, he was prepared to work harder than anyone else to be the best.
paras.zh: 二十世纪六十年代初，让·克洛德·基利入选法国国家滑雪队时，他准备比谁都刻苦，争取成为最好的选手。

paras.en: At the crack of dawn, he would run up the slopes with his skis on, an unbelievably back-breaking activity.
paras.zh: 天刚亮，他就穿着滑雪板往山坡上跑，这项训练苦得难以置信。

w.m: adj. 累死人的；极其繁重的

paras.en: In the evening, he would do weightlifting and running, but the other team members were working as hard and long as he was.
paras.zh: 晚上他还要练举重、跑步，可队里其他人也跟他一样刻苦，练得一样久。

paras.en: He realized instinctively that simply training harder would never be enough.
paras.zh: 他凭直觉意识到，光是更刻苦地训练永远不够。

paras.en: Killy then began challenging the basic theories of racing technique.
paras.zh: 于是基利开始挑战滑雪比赛技术的基本理论。

paras.en: Each week he would try something different to see if he could find a better, faster way down the mountain.
paras.zh: 他每周都会尝试一些不同的做法，看能不能找到一种更好、更快的下山方法。

paras.en: His experiments resulted in a new style that was almost exactly opposite the accepted technique of the time.
paras.zh: 他的种种尝试带来了一种新滑法，跟当时公认的技术几乎完全相反。

w.m: adj. 公认的；普遍接受的

paras.en: It involved skiing with his legs apart for better balance, and sitting back on the skis when he came to a turn, he also used ski poles in an unorthodox way, to propel himself as he skied.
paras.zh: 这种滑法是两腿分开滑，保持更好的平衡，转弯时身体在滑雪板上往后坐；他还不按常规用雪杖，滑的时候用雪杖推着自己前进。

w.m: adj. 非传统的；不循常规的

paras.en: The explosive new style helped cut Killy’s racing time dramatically.
paras.zh: 这种爆发力十足的新滑法让基利的比赛用时大大缩短。

paras.en: In 1966 and 1967, he captured virtually every major skiing trophy.
paras.zh: 1966年和1967年，几乎每一项重大滑雪奖杯都被他收入囊中。

paras.en: The next year, he won three gold medals in the Winter Olympics, a record in ski racing that has never been topped.
paras.zh: 第二年，他在冬季奥运会上拿了三枚金牌，创下了滑雪比赛中至今无人超越的纪录。

paras.en: Killy learned an important secret shared by many creative people: innovations don’t require genius, just a willingness to question the way things have always been done.
paras.zh: 基利悟出了许多富有创造力的人都知道的一个重要秘诀：创新不需要天才，只需要愿意质疑一直以来的做事方式。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does the speaker say about most successful people?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于大多数成功人士，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the speaker say about Killy’s experiments?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于基利的尝试，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What is said to be Killy’s biggest honor in his skiing career?
paras.zh: 第十一题：基利滑雪生涯中最大的荣誉是什么？

paras.en: Passage two: Scientific experiments have demonstrated incredible ways to kill a guinea pig, a small furry animal.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文：科学实验证明，有一些让人难以置信的方式能杀死豚鼠这种毛茸茸的小动物。

paras.en: Emotional upsets generate powerful and deadly toxic substances.
paras.zh: 情绪波动会产生强烈的致命毒素。

paras.en: Blood samples taken from persons experiencing intense fear or anger when injected into guinea pigs have killed them in less than two minutes.
paras.zh: 从处于极度恐惧或愤怒中的人身上采集的血样，注射到豚鼠体内，不到两分钟就能把它们毒死。

paras.en: Imagine what these poisonous substances can do to your own body.
paras.zh: 想想这些有毒物质会对你自己的身体造成什么样的伤害吧。

paras.en: Every thought that you have affects your body chemistry within a split second.
paras.zh: 你的每一个念头都会在一瞬间影响你身体的化学反应。

paras.en: Remember how you feel when you are speeding down the highway and a big truck suddenly brakes 20 meters in front of you.
paras.zh: 回想一下，你在高速公路上飞驰，一辆大卡车突然在你前方20米处急刹车，那时你是什么感觉。

paras.en: A shock wave shoots through your whole system.
paras.zh: 一股冲击波瞬间传遍你的全身。

w.m: v. 迅速穿过；飞速移动

paras.en: Your mind produces instant reactions in your body.
paras.zh: 你的大脑会让身体立刻产生反应。

paras.en: The toxic substances that fear, anger, frustration, and stress produce, not only kill guinea pigs but kill us off in a similar manner.
paras.zh: 恐惧、愤怒、挫败感和压力产生的有毒物质，不光能杀死豚鼠，也会以类似的方式要了我们的命。

paras.en: It is impossible to be fearful, anxious, irritated, and healthy at the same time, it is not just difficult; it is impossible.
paras.zh: 一个人不可能既害怕、焦虑、烦躁，同时又很健康，这不只是难，而是根本不可能。

paras.en: Simply put, your body’s health is a reflection of your mental health.
paras.zh: 简单地说，身体健康反映的是心理健康。

paras.en: Sickness will often then be a result of unresolved inner conflicts, which in time show up in the body.
paras.zh: 所以，疾病往往是内心冲突没有解决的结果，这些冲突迟早会在身体上表现出来。

paras.en: It is also fascinating how our subconscious mind shapes our health.
paras.zh: 我们的潜意识如何影响健康，这一点也很有意思。

paras.en: Do you recall falling sick on a day when you didn’t want to go to school?
paras.zh: 你还记得吗？不想上学的那天，你偏偏就病了。

paras.en: Headaches brought on by fear.
paras.zh: 那是害怕引起的头痛。

paras.en: The mind-body connection is such that if, for example, we want to avoid something, very often our subconscious mind will arrange it.
paras.zh: 身心之间的联系就是这样：比如说，我们想逃避某件事，潜意识往往就会替我们安排好。

paras.en: Once we recognize that these things happen to us, we are halfway to doing something about them.
paras.zh: 一旦我们认识到这些事会发生在自己身上，解决问题就已经成功了一半。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What happens to guinea pigs when blood samples of angry people are injected into them?
paras.zh: 第十二题：把愤怒的人的血样注射到豚鼠体内，豚鼠会怎么样？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the speaker say about every thought you have?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于你的每一个念头，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the speaker say is impossible?
paras.zh: 第十四题：说话人说什么是不可能的？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the passage say about our mind and body?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于我们的大脑和身体，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Teachers and students alike have experienced the curious paradox that beginners, as a rule, tend to think too little about what they are doing because they think too much about what they are doing.
paras.zh: 老师和学生都体会过这样一个奇怪的矛盾：初学者通常对自己在做的事想得太少，恰恰是因为他们对自己在做的事想得太多。

paras.en: Take, for example, people who are learning to play basketball or the piano, they have to give so much thought and attention to the low-level mechanics of handling the ball, or fingering the keys, or reading the music, that they are unable to give any thought to the thing that matters, the game, or the music, respectively.
paras.zh: 就拿学打篮球或学弹钢琴的人来说，他们要花大量心思去顾及运球、按键或看谱这些最基础的动作，结果对真正要紧的东西——比赛本身或音乐本身——反倒一点心思都腾不出来。

paras.en: With experts, it’s just the other way around.
paras.zh: 行家则正好相反。

paras.en: They’re open to the tactical possibilities and the musical challenges precisely because they’re freed through skill from the need to pay attention to the low-level details of how to play.
paras.zh: 他们能把心思放在战术上的种种可能、音乐上的种种难点上，正是因为技艺纯熟，他们不用再去顾及怎样弹、怎样打这些基础细节。

paras.en: Indeed, when the expert pays attention to the mechanics, this is liable to disrupt performance.
paras.zh: 其实，行家一旦去注意基本动作，反倒容易影响发挥。

paras.en: This has led some to say that the expert operates in a zone beyond thought, in a state of flow.
paras.zh: 于是有人说，行家是在一种超越思考的境界里、在一种心流状态中发挥的。

paras.en: But this is misleading.
paras.zh: 但这种说法有误导性。

w.m: adj. 误导的；引人误解的

paras.en: Expert performance is not beyond thought.
paras.zh: 行家的发挥并没有超越思考。

paras.en: Smart basketball players or skilled musicians need to pay close attention to the demands of high performance, to the challenges to be overcome.
paras.zh: 聪明的篮球运动员或技艺精湛的音乐家，需要密切关注高水平发挥的要求，关注要攻克的难关。

w.m: adj. 熟练的；技艺精湛的

paras.en: What they don’t need to do, what would be a distraction, is to have to think about where their fingers are or how to control the ball while running.
paras.zh: 他们不需要做的、会让他们分心的，是不得不去想手指放在哪儿，或者跑动时怎么控球。

paras.en: It’s not mechanics, but the play itself that absorbs the expert’s intelligence.
paras.zh: 占据行家头脑的不是基本动作，而是比赛本身。

w.m: v. 吸引（注意）；使全神贯注

paras.en: A nice video published online last month sheds light on expertise and the conscious mind.
paras.zh: 上个月网上发布的一段很好的视频，让人对专业技能和意识有了更多了解。

paras.en: The video reports a new study using an eye tracking device.
paras.zh: 这段视频报道了一项用眼动仪做的新研究。

paras.en: It turns out that the less skilled pianist spends more time looking at her fingers than does the expert, who, in contrast, is more likely to be looking at the sheet music, or looking ahead at keys he’s not yet playing.
paras.zh: 结果发现，技术较差的钢琴手看手指的时间比行家多；而行家则更多地看乐谱，或者往前看那些还没弹到的琴键。

paras.en: In general, the expert’s gaze was calmer and more stable.
paras.zh: 总的来说，行家的目光更平静、更稳定。

paras.en: This is not a surprising finding; it supports what we might almost think of as conventional wisdom.
paras.zh: 这个发现并不出人意料，它印证了我们差不多可以看作常识的观点。

paras.en: But it’s remarkable for all that, none the less.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，它仍然很了不起。

w.m: adj. 非凡的；值得注意的

paras.en: The eye tracker gives expert and learning performers a glimpse into what they do without thinking about it.
paras.zh: 眼动仪让行家和学习中的表演者得以一窥自己不假思索时做了些什么。

paras.en: The topic of the nature of skill and the differences between beginners and experts has been one of considerable discussion in cognitive science and philosophy.
paras.zh: 技能的本质、初学者与行家的差异，一直是认知科学和哲学里讨论颇多的话题。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about beginners and expert pianists?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于初学者和钢琴行家，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What do smart basketball players do, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十七题：说话人认为，聪明的篮球运动员会做什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What do we learn about the new study published in an online video?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于网络视频里发布的那项新研究，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Every summer, when I top up my selection of summer outfits from the department stores, my eyes would nearly pop out of my head.
paras.zh: 每年夏天，我去百货商店添置夏装的时候，眼珠子都快瞪出来了。

w.m: n. 可供选择的东西；一批

paras.en: I’m overwhelmed with a wide range of different slimming products each year, and more shockingly, these products are often advocated by very slim models.
paras.zh: 每年各种各样的减肥产品都让我眼花缭乱，更让人吃惊的是，给这些产品做宣传的往往是很瘦的模特。

w.m: v. 使不知所措；使应接不暇

paras.en: Having lived in Asia for almost 10 years now, I’ve seen various dieting tips come and go.
paras.zh: 我在亚洲生活了快十年，见过各种减肥妙招来了又去。

paras.en: I remember in Japan, people heading directly to the fruit section in the supermarket when the banana diet was at its peak.
paras.zh: 我记得在日本，香蕉减肥法最流行的时候，人们一进超市就直奔水果区。

paras.en: Then there was the black tea and oolong tea diet, followed by the soybean diet and the tomato juice diet.
paras.zh: 接着又有了红茶和乌龙茶减肥法，后来又出了黄豆减肥法和番茄汁减肥法。

paras.en: The list goes on and on.
paras.zh: 这样的例子数都数不完。

paras.en: Apart from what people eat, I’ve also seen many interesting slimming products.
paras.zh: 除了吃什么，我还见过很多有意思的减肥产品。

paras.en: In Hong Kong, I’ve seen girls wrapping their whole body or both legs up with a special type of slimming tape, which is supposed to help make them thinner, but it just reminded me of the roasted ham my mother usually puts on the dinner table at Christmas.
paras.zh: 在香港，我见过女孩子们用一种特殊的减肥胶带缠住全身或两条腿，据说能让人变瘦，可我看了只会想起我妈妈圣诞节常端上餐桌的烤火腿。

paras.en: Then there were the face slimming rollers that were said to improve your blood circulation and make your face smaller.
paras.zh: 后来又出了瘦脸滚轮，据说能促进血液循环，让脸变小。

paras.en: Personally, I do not believe in any of these slimming gadgets, and I think I have a very different perspective when it comes to the definition of what is beautiful.
paras.zh: 我个人一点也不相信这些减肥小玩意儿，而且我觉得，说到什么是美，我的看法很不一样。

paras.en: Asian women prefer to avoid the sun because being pale or white is considered beautiful, whereas a tanned complexion is considered much more beautiful and sexy in the West.
paras.zh: 亚洲女性喜欢躲着太阳，因为皮肤白才被认为是美；而在西方，晒成小麦色的肤色要美得多、性感得多。

paras.en: It is most certainly shaped by a person’s culture, as well as how they were raised in their childhood, as each summer season approaches, there’s no escape from it.
paras.zh: 审美观肯定是由一个人的文化以及童年时的成长方式塑造的；每到夏天临近，这种压力就躲也躲不掉。

paras.en: But it’s not only women who are affected by this pressure to look good.
paras.zh: 不过，受这种要好看的压力影响的不只是女性。

paras.en: Men aspire to be able to show off their six packs, or their V-shaped backs, and there’s a growing market of slimming pills aimed at men too.
paras.zh: 男性也想秀出六块腹肌或者倒三角的后背，而且专门针对男性的减肥药市场也越来越大。

paras.en: I think no matter what diets we follow or what slimming products we obsess ourselves with, at the end of the day there’s no magic trick to shape up for the summer.
paras.zh: 我觉得，不管我们采用什么减肥方法，迷上什么减肥产品，说到底，夏天之前要变好身材是没有什么灵丹妙药的。

w.h: at the end of the day

paras.en: Eat in a balanced way and incorporate the right level of physical activity.
paras.zh: 饮食要均衡，再加上适量的运动。

paras.en: For me, this still seems to be the best plan.
paras.zh: 对我来说，这似乎仍然是最好的办法。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What overwhelms the speaker when she buys her summer outfits each year?
paras.zh: 第十九题：每年买夏装时，什么让说话人应接不暇？

w.m: v. 使不知所措；使应接不暇

paras.en: Question 20: What does the speaker think of girls wrapping their legs up with slimming tape?
paras.zh: 第二十题：说话人怎么看女孩子用减肥胶带缠腿？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker think affects people’s interpretation of beauty?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人认为什么影响人们对美的理解？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Skin may seem like a superficial human attribute, but it’s the first thing we notice about anyone we meet.
paras.zh: 皮肤看上去也许是人身上很表面的一个特征，可我们遇见任何人，最先注意到的就是皮肤。

paras.en: As a zoologist focusing on the studies of apes and monkeys, I’ve been studying why humans evolved to become the naked ape, and why skin comes in so many different shades around the world.
paras.zh: 我是一名动物学家，专门研究猿和猴子；我一直在研究人类为什么会进化成“裸猿”，世界各地的人肤色为什么会深浅不一。

paras.en: We can make a very good estimate from the fossil record that humans probably evolved naked skin around a million and a half years ago, and meanwhile, they mostly lost their coat of fur.
paras.zh: 根据化石记录，我们可以相当有把握地推断，人类大概在一百五十万年前进化出了裸露的皮肤，同时也基本失去了身上的皮毛。

paras.en: Today we have a few patches of hair remaining on various parts of our bodies, but compared with apes and monkeys, we have very little.
paras.zh: 今天，我们身上各个部位还留着几片毛发，但跟猿和猴子比起来，就少得可怜了。

paras.en: Basically, we turned our skin darker to serve as a natural sun protector in the place of the hair we lost.
paras.zh: 简单来说，我们让皮肤变深，作为天然的防晒层，来代替失去的毛发。

paras.en: We think we lost this hair because of the need to keep ourselves cool when we were moving around vigorously in a hot environment.
paras.zh: 我们认为，之所以失去这些毛发，是因为在炎热的环境里剧烈活动时需要让身体保持凉爽。

paras.en: We can’t really lose heat by breathing quickly and loudly like dogs.
paras.zh: 我们没办法像狗那样靠呼哧呼哧地快速喘气来散热。

paras.en: We have to do it by sweating, so we evolved the ability to sweat plentifully and lost most of our fur.
paras.zh: 我们只能靠出汗来散热，所以进化出了大量出汗的能力，也失去了大部分皮毛。

paras.en: Most animals protect themselves from the sun with fur.
paras.zh: 大多数动物都靠皮毛来防晒。

paras.en: What we did in our ancestry was to produce more permanent natural coloring in our skin cells.
paras.zh: 我们的祖先做的，是在皮肤细胞里产生更持久的天然色素。

paras.en: This was really an important revolution in human history, because it allowed us to continue to evolve in equatorial environments.
paras.zh: 这确实是人类历史上一场重要的变革，因为它让我们得以在赤道地区的环境里继续进化。

w.m: adj. 赤道的；赤道附近的

paras.en: It really made it possible for us to continue along the path toward modern humans in Africa.
paras.zh: 正是这一点，让我们得以在非洲沿着通往现代人的道路继续前进。

paras.en: For most of human history, we all had dark skin.
paras.zh: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，我们都是深色皮肤。

paras.en: What we see today is the product of evolutionary events resulting from the dispersal of a few human populations out of Africa around 60,000 to 70,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 我们今天看到的肤色，是大约六万到七万年前少数人群走出非洲、四处扩散之后，一系列进化事件的产物。
