paras.en: Our species originated around 200,000 years ago, and underwent tremendous diversification, culturally, technologically, linguistically, artistically, for 130,000 years.
paras.zh: 我们这个物种大约起源于二十万年前，在十三万年里，在文化、技术、语言、艺术等方面都经历了巨大的分化。

paras.en: After that, a few small populations left Africa to populate the rest of the world.
paras.zh: 之后，有几个小群体离开非洲，去世界其他地方繁衍生息。

paras.en: These early ancestors of modern Eurasians dispersed into parts of the world that had more seasonal sunshine and much lower levels of sun radiation.
paras.zh: 现代欧亚人的这些早期祖先，分散到了世界上季节性日照更多、太阳辐射水平低得多的地方。

paras.en: It’s in these populations that we begin to see real changes in the genetic makeup of natural coloring.
paras.zh: 正是在这些人群里，我们开始看到天然肤色的基因构成发生了真正的变化。

paras.en: Today, skin color is evolving via new mixtures of people coming together and having children with new mixtures of skin color genes.
paras.zh: 今天，随着不同的人走到一起，生下带有新的肤色基因组合的孩子，肤色仍在通过这些新的混合不断演变。

paras.en: We can see this in almost every large city worldwide.
paras.zh: 这一点在全世界几乎每一座大城市都能看到。

paras.en: Not only the coloring genes, but lots of other genes are getting mixed up too.
paras.zh: 不只是肤色基因，还有很多别的基因也在混合。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker mainly talk about?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人主要讲了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What had probably caused humans to lose most of their hair one and a half million years ago?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：大约一百五十万年前，人类失去大部分毛发的原因可能是什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What does the speaker say protected early humans from the sun?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：说话人说早期人类靠什么防晒？

paras.en: Question 25: What happened after humans migrated from Africa to other parts of the world?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：人类从非洲迁徙到世界其他地方之后，发生了什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2019年6月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2019年6月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，女士很崇拜奥黛丽·赫本，向男士讲了赫本的芭蕾经历、成名作和息影后投身儿童慈善的事，两人约好下周末一起去做慈善志愿者。第二段长对话里，两位同事准备一场关于公司重组的报告，商量怎样打消员工的顾虑、报告的提纲以及怎样把详细信息告诉员工。第一篇短文讲美国一些机场用迷你马、狗、猫、猪等治疗动物帮紧张的乘客放松。第二篇短文里，主持人在法国阿尔勒一处两千年前的古罗马遗址介绍新出土的精美壁画，以及壁画主人可能是谁。第一段录音讲科学研究中国际合作越来越多的原因、好处，以及不同学科、不同国家之间的差异。第二段录音里，一位科学家讲人们对金星的看法怎样从“可能有生命”变成“警示故事”，又讲新发现表明远古的金星也许适合生命存在。第三段录音里，一位文化心理学教授介绍自己研究文化如何影响自我提升的动机和睡眠，以及睡眠研究的做法。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解。

paras.en: Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Wow!
paras.zh: 哇！

paras.en: I would give anything to be more like Audrey Hepburn.
paras.zh: 要是能更像奥黛丽·赫本一点，让我做什么都愿意。

w.m: 做什么都愿意；无论如何都想

paras.en: I never really understood why so many girls were such big fans of her.
paras.zh: 我一直不太明白，为什么那么多女孩都是她的铁杆粉丝。

paras.en: I mean, I’ve seen the famous films Roman Holiday, Breakfast at Tiffany’s, and a few others, but I still don’t fully get it.
paras.zh: 我是说，她那几部有名的电影，《罗马假日》《蒂凡尼的早餐》，还有别的几部，我都看过，可我还是不太懂。

paras.en: Was she that great of an actress?
paras.zh: 她真是那么了不起的演员吗？

paras.en: Well, for me, my adoration goes beyond her movies.
paras.zh: 嗯，对我来说，我喜欢她远不只是因为她的电影。

paras.en: She had such a classic elegance about her.
paras.zh: 她身上有一种经典的优雅气质。

paras.en: She was always so poised, in part because she spent years training as a ballet dancer before becoming an actress.
paras.zh: 她总是那么从容优雅，部分原因是她当演员之前练了好几年芭蕾。

w.m: adj. 镇定的；姿态优雅的

paras.en: Why didn’t she stick to dancing as a career?
paras.zh: 那她为什么没有一直以跳舞为职业呢？

paras.en: It seems it was fate.
paras.zh: 看来这是命中注定吧。

paras.en: She suffered from inadequate nutrition during the war, and therefore a career as a professional dancer would have been too demanding on her body.
paras.zh: 她在战争期间营养不良，所以当职业舞蹈演员对她的身体来说负担太重了。

paras.en: So she focused on acting instead.
paras.zh: 所以她转而专心演戏了。

paras.en: Roman Holiday was her first big break, which made her a star.
paras.zh: 《罗马假日》是她第一次重大突破，让她成了明星。

paras.en: Was that the film that opened with her shopping for jewelry in New York City?
paras.zh: 是不是那部开头她在纽约买珠宝的电影？

paras.en: You know the scene.
paras.zh: 你知道那场戏的。

w.m: n. 场景；（戏剧、电影的）一场

paras.en: She was wearing a black dress and dark sunglasses with a pearl necklace and long black gloves.
paras.zh: 她穿着黑色连衣裙，戴着墨镜，配着珍珠项链和黑色长手套。

paras.en: I see the photo of her in that costume everywhere.
paras.zh: 她穿那身衣服的照片我到处都能看到。

paras.en: No, that one is Breakfast at Tiffany’s.
paras.zh: 不对，那部是《蒂凡尼的早餐》。

paras.en: That costume is often referred to as the most famous little black dress of all time.
paras.zh: 那身衣服常被称为史上最有名的小黑裙。

paras.en: Her character in that film is very outgoing and charming, even though in real life Audrey always described herself as shy and quiet.
paras.zh: 她在那部电影里演的角色非常外向、迷人，可现实生活中，奥黛丽总说自己害羞、文静。

paras.en: So, what did she do after her acting career.
paras.zh: 那她息影以后做了些什么？

paras.en: She dedicated much of her life to helping children in need.
paras.zh: 她把大半生都献给了帮助有困难的孩子。

paras.en: Her family received international aid during the war when she was growing up.
paras.zh: 她小时候，战争期间她家接受过国际援助。

paras.en: I think that left a big impression on her.
paras.zh: 我想这件事给她留下了很深的印象。

paras.en: That’s where I got the idea to volunteer for children’s charity next weekend.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，我才想到下周末去儿童慈善机构做志愿者。

paras.en: I’ll join you.
paras.zh: 我跟你一起去。

paras.en: I may not be as charming as Audrey Hepburn, but I’m all for supporting a good cause.
paras.zh: 我也许没有奥黛丽·赫本那么迷人，可我非常支持做善事。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the man say he never really understood?
paras.zh: 第一题：男士说他一直不太明白什么？

paras.en: Question two: What prevented Audrey Hepburn from becoming a professional dancer?
paras.zh: 第二题：是什么让奥黛丽·赫本没能成为职业舞蹈演员？

paras.en: Question three: What do we learn about Audrey Hepburn in real life?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于现实生活中的奥黛丽·赫本，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question four: Why did Audrey Hepburn devote much of her life to charity after her acting career?
paras.zh: 第四题：奥黛丽·赫本息影后为什么把大半生都献给了慈善事业？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: So, how’s our presentation about the restructuring of the company coming along?
paras.zh: 那么，我们那份关于公司重组的报告准备得怎么样了？

paras.en: Fine, I’m putting the finishing touches to it now, but we’ll have to be prepared for questions.
paras.zh: 挺好的，我现在正在做最后的润色，不过我们得准备好回答提问。

paras.en: Yes, there’s already a feeling that this is a top-down change.
paras.zh: 是啊，大家已经觉得这是一次自上而下的变革了。

paras.en: We really need to get everyone on board.
paras.zh: 我们真得让每个人都支持才行。

paras.en: Well, there’s been an extensive consultation period.
paras.zh: 嗯，我们已经征求了很长时间的意见了。

paras.en: I know, but there’s always the feeling that if it isn’t broke, don’t fix it.
paras.zh: 我知道，可大家总觉得，没坏的东西就别去修。

w.h: if it isn’t broke, don’t fix it
w.m: 没坏就别修；没问题就别瞎折腾

paras.en: People are worried about their jobs too.
paras.zh: 大家也在担心自己的饭碗。

paras.en: I think we need to stress that while there will be some job changes, there won’t be anyone getting dismissed.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们得强调，虽然有些岗位会调整，但不会有人被辞退。

paras.en: In fact, we’re looking to take on more staff.
paras.zh: 其实，我们还打算多招些人。

paras.en: Agreed.
paras.zh: 同意。

paras.en: You can hardly blame people for worrying, though.
paras.zh: 不过，大家担心也不能怪他们。

paras.en: We need to make it clear that it’s not just change for change’s sake.
paras.zh: 我们得讲清楚，这不是为了变而变。

paras.en: In other words, we really must make the case for why we are doing it.
paras.zh: 换句话说，我们真的必须讲清楚我们为什么要这么做。

w.m: 为……提出理由；说明……的理由

paras.en: So, what’s the outline of the presentation?
paras.zh: 那么，报告的提纲是什么样的？

paras.en: I’ll start with a brief review of the reasons for the change, that we really need to make a clean break to restart growth.
paras.zh: 我先简单回顾一下变革的原因，就是我们确实需要彻底告别过去，才能重新实现增长。

paras.en: After that, I’ll outline the new company structures and who’s going where.
paras.zh: 然后，我会概括介绍公司的新架构，以及谁调到哪儿。

paras.en: Then I’ll hand it over to you to discuss the timeline and summarize, and we’ll take questions together at the end.
paras.zh: 接下来我就交给你，由你讲时间安排并做总结，最后我们一起回答提问。

paras.en: Anything else?
paras.zh: 还有别的吗？

paras.en: Oh yeah, we should let the staff know the channels of communication.
paras.zh: 哦，对了，我们应该让员工知道有哪些沟通渠道。

paras.en: You know who they can contact or direct questions to about these changes.
paras.zh: 你知道的，就是关于这些变动，他们可以联系谁、可以向谁提问。

w.m: v. 把……指向；把（问题等）提交给

paras.en: Yes, and we can collect some frequently asked questions and present some general answers.
paras.zh: 对，我们还可以收集一些常见问题，给出一些大致的答复。

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

paras.en: And we’ll make the presentation and the questions available via the company’s own computer network, right?
paras.zh: 我们还会把报告和这些问题放到公司内网上，供大家查看，对吧？

paras.en: Yes, we’ll make a page on the network where staff can download all the details.
paras.zh: 对，我们会在内网上做一个页面，员工可以在上面下载全部详细信息。

paras.en: All right.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: Perhaps we should do a practice run of the presentation first.
paras.zh: 也许我们应该先把报告预演一遍。

paras.en: You bet.
paras.zh: 当然了。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is the man going to do?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士要做什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man say about the restructuring?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于重组，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What will the man explain first?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士首先要讲什么？

paras.en: Question eight: How can the staff learn more about the company’s restructuring?
paras.zh: 第八题：员工怎样才能更多地了解公司重组的情况？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with the single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: Airline passengers have to deal with a lot these days, getting bumped from flights and losing luggage, on top of the general anxiety that nervous passengers always feel, at the Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport, miniature horses deliver a calming force two times a month.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文：如今坐飞机的乘客要应付很多麻烦，被挤下航班、丢行李，再加上紧张的乘客总会有的那种焦虑；在辛辛那提北肯塔基国际机场，每月有两次，迷你马会来给大家带来一份安定的力量。

paras.en: Denver and Ruby are two of the four therapy horses brought in from a local farm, they can usually be found in the ticket counter area, interacting with travelers.
paras.zh: 丹佛和鲁比是从当地一家农场请来的四匹治疗马中的两匹，人们通常能在售票柜台一带看到它们和旅客互动。

paras.en: More than 30 airports across the country now have therapy dogs.
paras.zh: 如今，全国已有30多个机场配备了治疗犬。

paras.en: San Francisco has a therapy pig.
paras.zh: 旧金山有一头治疗猪。

paras.en: San Jose, California, began a dog program after the terrorist attacks of September the 11th.
paras.zh: 加利福尼亚州的圣何塞在九一一恐怖袭击之后推出了一个治疗犬项目。

paras.en: Since its beginning, the program has now grown and has 21 therapy dogs and a therapy cat.
paras.zh: 这个项目自启动以来不断扩大，现在已经有21只治疗犬和1只治疗猫。

paras.en: The animals don’t get startled; they have had hundreds of hours of airport training, so they are used to having luggage and people crowding around them, these professional animals are probably better at finding their way in the airports than the most frequent of travelers.
paras.zh: 这些动物不会受惊；它们接受过几百个小时的机场训练，早就习惯了行李和人群围在身边，这些“专业”动物在机场里认路的本事，大概比最常坐飞机的旅客还强。

paras.en: The passengers often say that seeing animals makes them feel much better and helps them to calm down before a flight.
paras.zh: 乘客们常说，看到这些动物，心情会好很多，起飞前也能平静下来。

paras.en: This little bit of support can sometimes make a big difference.
paras.zh: 这一点点支持，有时候能起很大的作用。

w.m: 产生很大的影响；很有作用

paras.en: Some passengers enjoy the animals so much that they call the airport to schedule flights around their visits.
paras.zh: 有些乘客特别喜欢这些动物，甚至打电话给机场，好按它们来访的时间安排航班。

paras.en: Visits to nursing homes and schools are also a regular part of the horse’s schedule.
paras.zh: 去养老院和学校探访，也是这些马的日常安排之一。

paras.en: Their owner is already working on a new idea for a therapy animal, donkeys.
paras.zh: 它们的主人已经在琢磨一个新点子：用驴当治疗动物。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What is special about the Cincinnati Northern Kentucky International Airport?
paras.zh: 第九题：辛辛那提北肯塔基国际机场有什么特别之处？

paras.en: Question 10: What are the trained animals probably capable of doing in an airport?
paras.zh: 第十题：这些受过训练的动物在机场里大概能做什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What do some passengers try to do?
paras.zh: 第十一题：有些乘客会想办法做什么？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Hello, viewers.
paras.zh: 观众朋友们好。

paras.en: Today I’m standing at a 2,000-year-old Roman-era site.
paras.zh: 今天我站在一处两千年前古罗马时期的遗址上。

paras.en: Here, the brightly colored scenes that once decorated a mansion are being dug up.
paras.zh: 在这里，人们正在发掘曾经装饰一座宅邸的色彩鲜艳的壁画。

paras.en: These scenes are turning up in the southern French city of Arles, surprising the historians who have been working here since 2014.
paras.zh: 这些画面陆续出现在法国南部城市阿尔勒，让2014年以来一直在这里工作的历史学家们大为惊讶。

paras.en: Patches of paint still cling to the stone walls of a bedroom and reception hall.
paras.zh: 卧室和接待厅的石墙上还残留着一块块颜料。

paras.en: Some of these painted walls are preserved in places to a height of one meter.
paras.zh: 有些彩绘墙面局部保存的高度达到一米。

paras.en: In addition, thousands of fragments that fell off the walls have been recovered.
paras.zh: 此外，从墙上掉下来的成千上万块碎片也已经找回来了。

paras.en: These pieces have been put back together with great care and display a variety of images.
paras.zh: 这些碎片经过精心拼合，呈现出各种各样的图案。

paras.en: Some of these images include figures never seen before in France, such as a woman playing a stringed instrument, possibly a character from mythology.
paras.zh: 其中有些人物形象在法国从未见过，比如一位弹奏弦乐器的女子，可能是神话里的人物。

paras.en: The paintings were done with such skill and with such expensive dyes that experts believe the artists originally came from Italy.
paras.zh: 这些画技艺精湛、颜料昂贵，专家们认为画家原本来自意大利。

paras.en: They were likely hired by one of the city’s elite, perhaps a Roman official wanted Pompeii-like interior to remind him of home.
paras.zh: 雇他们的很可能是城里的某位权贵，也许是一位罗马官员想要庞贝式的室内装饰，让自己想起家乡。

paras.en: He was probably stationed in this provincial trading port, founded in 46 B.C. as a colony for veterans of the Roman army, or maybe a wealthy local wanted to show off his worldly sophistication.
paras.zh: 他大概驻扎在这个外省的贸易港口，这里建于公元前46年，是罗马退伍老兵的殖民地；又或者是当地一位富人想炫耀自己见多识广、品位高雅。

w.m: adj. 见过世面的；世俗的

paras.en: The paintings may yield even more stunning surprises as additional sections are put together like pieces of a puzzle.
paras.zh: 随着更多的部分像拼图一样被拼起来，这些画也许还会带来更惊人的发现。

paras.en: Whoever it was that created such magnificent pieces of art, they surely had no idea that their work would still be around thousands of years later.
paras.zh: 不管创作出如此精美艺术品的是谁，他们肯定想不到，几千年后自己的作品还会留存于世。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Where is the speaker standing?
paras.zh: 第十二题：说话人站在什么地方？

paras.en: Question 13: What do the thousands of fragments display when they are put back together?
paras.zh: 第十三题：成千上万块碎片拼合之后呈现出什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What makes experts think the paintings were done by artists from Italy?
paras.zh: 第十四题：是什么让专家认为这些画出自意大利画家之手？

paras.en: Question 15: What do we learn from the passage about the owner of the mansion?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于宅邸的主人，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Good afternoon, class.
paras.zh: 同学们，下午好。

paras.en: Today I want to discuss with you a new approach to empirical research.
paras.zh: 今天我想和大家讨论一种新的实证研究方式。

w.m: adj. 实证的；以经验为依据的

paras.en: In the past, scientists often worked alone; they were confined to the university or research center where they worked.
paras.zh: 过去，科学家往往单打独斗，局限在自己工作的大学或研究中心里。

paras.en: Today, though, we are seeing mergers of some of the greatest scientific minds, regardless of their location.
paras.zh: 可如今，我们看到一些最顶尖的科学头脑在联手合作，不管他们身在何处。

paras.en: There has never been a better time for collaborations with foreign scientists.
paras.zh: 和外国科学家合作，从来没有像现在这样好的时机。

paras.en: In fact, the European Union is taking the lead.
paras.zh: 事实上，欧盟正走在前面。

paras.en: Spurred on by funding policies, half of European research articles had international co-authors in 2007.
paras.zh: 在资助政策的推动下，2007年欧洲一半的研究论文都有外国合著者。

paras.en: This is more than twice the level of two decades ago.
paras.zh: 这个比例是二十年前的两倍多。

paras.en: The European Union’s level of international co-authorship is about twice that of the United States, Japan, and India.
paras.zh: 欧盟的国际合著水平大约是美国、日本和印度的两倍。

paras.en: Even so, the levels in these countries are also rising.
paras.zh: 即便如此，这些国家的合著水平也在上升。

paras.en: This is a sign of the continued allure of creating scientific coalitions across borders.
paras.zh: 这说明，跨国组建科学联盟一直很有吸引力。

paras.en: Andrus Schubert, a researcher at the Institute for Science Policy Research, says that the rise in collaboration is partly out of necessity.
paras.zh: 科学政策研究所的研究员安德鲁斯·舒伯特说，合作增多部分是出于必要。

paras.en: This necessity comes with the rise of big science.
paras.zh: 这种必要是随着大科学的兴起而来的。

paras.en: Many scientific endeavors have become more complicated.
paras.zh: 很多科学研究项目都变得更复杂了。

paras.en: These new complications require the money and labor of many nations.
paras.zh: 这些新的复杂情况需要很多国家出钱出力。

paras.en: But he says, collaborations have also emerged because of increased possibilities.
paras.zh: 不过他说，合作的出现也是因为可能性增加了。

paras.en: The internet allows like-minded scientists to find each other.
paras.zh: 互联网让志同道合的科学家能找到彼此。

paras.en: Simultaneously, dramatic drops in communication costs ease long-distance interactions, and there’s a reward.
paras.zh: 与此同时，通信成本大幅下降，远距离交流变得更容易，而且合作还有回报。

paras.en: Studies of citation counts show that internationally co-authored papers have better visibility.
paras.zh: 对引用次数的研究表明，国际合著的论文受关注程度更高。

w.m: n. 能见度；受关注程度

paras.en: Schubert says, international collaboration is a way to spread ideas in wider and wider circles.
paras.zh: 舒伯特说，国际合作是一种让思想传播得越来越广的途径。

paras.en: Caroline Wagner, a research scientist at George Washington University, notes that international collaborations offer additional flexibility, whereas local collaborations sometimes persist past the point of usefulness because of social or academic obligations, international ones can be cultivated and dropped more freely.
paras.zh: 乔治·华盛顿大学的研究科学家卡罗琳·瓦格纳指出，国际合作更加灵活：本地的合作有时会因为社会或学术上的人情义务，在已经没用之后还维持着；而国际合作则可以更自由地发展和放弃。

paras.en: The collaborative trend is true across scientific Disciplines, some fields though have a greater tendency for it.
paras.zh: 各个科学学科都有这种合作的趋势，不过有些领域更明显。

paras.en: Particle physicists and astronomers collaborate often.
paras.zh: 粒子物理学家和天文学家经常合作。

paras.en: This is because they must share expensive facilities.
paras.zh: 这是因为他们必须共用昂贵的设施。

paras.en: Mathematicians, by contrast, tend historically towards solitude.
paras.zh: 相比之下，数学家历来倾向于独自工作。

paras.en: As a consequence, they lag behind other disciplines.
paras.zh: 因此，他们落后于其他学科。

paras.en: However, Wagner says partnerships are rising there too.
paras.zh: 不过瓦格纳说，数学领域的合作也在增加。

paras.en: The level of collaboration also varies from country to country.
paras.zh: 合作的程度也因国家而异。

paras.en: There are historical and political reasons as to why collaborations emerge, says Wagner.
paras.zh: 瓦格纳说，合作的出现有历史和政治方面的原因。

paras.en: This rise is also apparently boosted by policies embedded in European framework funding schemes.
paras.zh: 显然，欧洲框架资助计划中的政策也推动了合作的增加。

paras.en: These policies underlie funding requirements that often require teamwork.
paras.zh: 这些政策是资助要求的基础，而这些要求往往需要团队合作。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What do we learn about the research funding policies in the European Union?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于欧盟的科研资助政策，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 17: Why do researchers today favor international collaboration?
paras.zh: 第十七题：如今的研究人员为什么青睐国际合作？

paras.en: Question 18: What do we learn about the field of mathematics?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于数学这个领域，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Good evening.
paras.zh: 晚上好。

paras.en: In 1959, on the day that I was born, a headline in Life magazine proclaimed, “Target Venus.
paras.zh: 1959年，就在我出生的那一天，《生活》杂志的一条大标题宣称：“目标金星。

paras.en: There may be life there.”
paras.zh: 那里也许有生命。”

paras.en: It told of how scientists rode a balloon to an altitude of 80,000 feet to make telescope observations of Venus’s atmosphere, and how their discovery of water raised hopes that there could be living things there.
paras.zh: 文章讲到科学家们怎样乘气球升到八万英尺的高空，用望远镜观测金星的大气层，又讲到他们发现了水，让人们燃起希望，觉得那里可能有生物。

paras.en: As a kid, I thrilled to tales of adventure in Isaac Asimov’s juvenile science fiction novel Lucky Starr and the Oceans of Venus.
paras.zh: 小时候，我读艾萨克·阿西莫夫的少儿科幻小说《幸运·斯塔尔与金星海洋》，书里的冒险故事让我激动不已。

paras.en: For many of my peers, though, Venus quickly lost its romance.
paras.zh: 不过，对我的很多同龄人来说，金星很快就失去了浪漫色彩。

paras.en: The very first thing that scientists discovered with a mission to another planet was that Venus was not at all the earthly paradise that fiction had portrayed.
paras.zh: 人类第一次向另一颗行星派出探测器，科学家最先发现的就是：金星根本不是小说里描绘的那种人间天堂。

w.m: n. 任务；（太空）飞行任务

paras.en: It is nearly identical to our own planet in bulk properties such as mass, density, and size, but its surface has been cooked and dried by an ocean of carbon dioxide, trapped in the burning death grip of a runaway greenhouse effect.
paras.zh: 在质量、密度、大小这些总体特性上，它跟地球几乎一模一样，可它的表面被一片二氧化碳的海洋烤得又热又干，陷在失控的温室效应那灼热的死亡魔爪里。

paras.en: Venus has long been held up as a cautionary tale for everything that could go wrong on a planet like Earth, as a possible home for alien life, it has been voted the planet least likely to succeed.
paras.zh: 长期以来，金星一直被当作一个警示故事，告诉人们像地球这样的行星可能出现的种种问题；作为外星生命可能的家园，它被评为最不可能成功的行星。

paras.en: But I have refused to give up on Venus, and over the years my stubborn loyalty has been justified.
paras.zh: 可我一直不肯放弃金星，这些年来，我的执着也证明是对的。

paras.en: The rocky views glimpsed by Venera Nine and other Russian landers suggested a tortured volcanic history.
paras.zh: 金星9号和其他俄罗斯着陆器拍到的岩石景象表明，金星经历过剧烈的火山活动。

w.m: adj. 痛苦的；剧烈动荡的

paras.en: That was confirmed in the early 1990s by the American Magellan Orbiter, which used radar to peer through the planet’s thick clouds and map out a rich, varied, and dynamic surface.
paras.zh: 这一点在二十世纪九十年代初得到了美国麦哲伦号轨道飞行器的证实，它用雷达穿透金星厚厚的云层，绘出了一个丰富多样、充满变化的表面。

w.m: adj. 动态的；充满活力的

paras.en: The surface formed mostly in the last billion years, which makes it fresher and more recently active than any rocky planet other than Earth.
paras.zh: 金星表面大多是在最近十亿年里形成的，所以，除地球外，它比其他任何岩质行星都更新、活动也更近。

paras.en: Russian and American spacecraft also found hints that its ancient climate might have been wetter, cooler, and possibly even friendly to life.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯和美国的探测器还发现了一些迹象，表明金星远古时期的气候可能更湿润、更凉爽，甚至可能适合生命存在。

paras.en: Measurements of density and composition imply that Venus originally formed out of basically the same stuff as Earth, that presumably included much more water than the tiny trace we find blowing in the thick air today.
paras.zh: 对密度和成分的测量表明，金星最初形成时的物质和地球基本相同，其中大概含有很多水，远比今天浓密大气中飘荡的那点微量水多得多。

paras.en: Thus, our picture of Venus at around the time life was getting started on Earth is one of warm oceans, probably rich with organic molecules, splashing around rocky shores and volcanic vents.
paras.zh: 因此，在地球上生命开始出现的那个时候，金星的图景是：温暖的海洋里很可能富含有机分子，在岩石海岸和火山口周围翻腾激荡。

paras.en: The sun was considerably less bright back then, so Venus was arguably a cozier habitat for life than Earth.
paras.zh: 那时太阳比现在暗得多，所以可以说，金星当时比地球更适合生命居住。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn from the Life magazine article?
paras.zh: 第十九题：从《生活》杂志的那篇文章里，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What are scientists’ findings about Venus?
paras.zh: 第二十题：科学家对金星有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 21: What information did Russian and American space probes provide about Venus?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：俄罗斯和美国的太空探测器提供了哪些关于金星的信息？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: I’m a psychology professor at the University of British Columbia.
paras.zh: 我是不列颠哥伦比亚大学的心理学教授。

paras.en: I specialize in cultural psychology, examining similarities and differences between East Asians and North Americans.
paras.zh: 我专门研究文化心理学，考察东亚人和北美人之间的相同点和不同点。

paras.en: Our research team has been looking at cultural differences in self-enhancing motivations, how people have positive feelings towards not only themselves but things connected to themselves.
paras.zh: 我们的研究团队一直在研究自我提升动机方面的文化差异，也就是人们怎样不光对自己、还对和自己有关的东西抱有好感。

paras.en: For example, when you own something, you view it as more valuable than when you don’t own it.
paras.zh: 比如，你拥有一样东西时，会觉得它比你没拥有它时更值钱。

paras.en: It’s called the endowment effect.
paras.zh: 这叫作禀赋效应。

paras.en: The strength of that effect is stronger in Western cultures than in East Asian cultures, so we’ve been looking at other ways of seeing whether this motivation to view oneself positively is shaped by cultural experiences.
paras.zh: 这种效应在西方文化里比在东亚文化里更强，所以我们一直在寻找其他方法，看看这种积极看待自己的动机是不是由文化经历塑造的。

paras.en: We’ve also started to look at how culture shapes sleep.
paras.zh: 我们还开始研究文化如何影响睡眠。

paras.en: We are still in the exploratory stages of this project, although what’s noteworthy is that East Asians, on average, sleep about an hour and a half less each night than North Americans do, and it’s not a more efficient sleep, not like they’re compressing relatively more value out of their hours.
paras.zh: 这个项目还处在探索阶段，不过值得注意的是，东亚人平均每晚比北美人少睡大约一个半小时，而且他们的睡眠效率也并不更高，并不是他们在相对更少的时间里睡出了更多的价值。

paras.en: Other studies have found that even infants in East Asia sleep about an hour less than European infants.
paras.zh: 其他研究发现，就连东亚的婴儿也比欧洲婴儿少睡大约一个小时。

paras.en: So we’re trying to figure out how culture shapes the way you sleep.
paras.zh: 所以我们想弄清楚，文化是怎样塑造人们睡觉的方式的。

paras.en: Our experiment does not take place in a sleep lab.
paras.zh: 我们的实验不在睡眠实验室里做。

paras.en: Instead, we lend people motion-detecting watches, and they wear them for a week at a time.
paras.zh: 我们借给参与者能检测动作的手表，让他们每次连续戴一周。

paras.en: Whenever they are not having a shower or swimming, they keep it on.
paras.zh: 除了洗澡或游泳，其他时候都一直戴着。

paras.en: These kinds of watches are used in sleep studies as a way of measuring how long people are sleeping, how efficient their sleep is, and whether they are waking up in the night.
paras.zh: 这类手表在睡眠研究中用来测量人们睡了多长时间、睡眠效率如何、夜里有没有醒来。

paras.en: Ideally, I’d like to take this into a controlled lab environment.
paras.zh: 理想的话，我想把这项研究搬到可控的实验室环境里去做。

paras.en: We’ll see where the research points us.
paras.zh: 看研究结果会把我们带向哪里吧。

paras.en: We usually start off with the more affordable methods, and if everything looks promising, then it’ll justify trying to build a sleep lab and study sleep across cultures that way.
paras.zh: 我们通常先用比较省钱的方法，如果一切看起来有希望，那就有理由去建一个睡眠实验室，用那种方式研究不同文化的睡眠。

w.m: adj. 负担得起的；便宜的
adj. 有希望的；有前途的

paras.en: Why do we study sleep?
paras.zh: 我们为什么研究睡眠？

paras.en: Sleep is something that has really been an unexplored topic cross-culturally.
paras.zh: 在跨文化研究中，睡眠一直是个没人探索过的课题。

paras.en: I’m attracted to it because culture isn’t something that only shapes the way our minds operate, it shapes the way our bodies operate too, and sleep is at the intersection of those.
paras.zh: 它吸引我，是因为文化不只是影响我们大脑的运作方式，也影响我们身体的运作方式，而睡眠正是两者的交汇点。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker mainly study?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人主要研究什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the speaker say about North Americans?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于北美人，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: How did the speaker conduct the sleep study?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：说话人是怎样开展睡眠研究的？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker say about research on sleep?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于睡眠研究，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
