passages.name: 2019年12月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，时尚杂志专题编辑罗西·马伦德谈到自己的日常工作、这份工作光鲜与否，以及她怎样坚持不懈才入了行。第二段长对话里，两人聊起最近在看的剧：讽刺剧《弗兰基》由喜剧演员本人出演自己，喜剧《生活大爆炸》讲四个男科学家和一个女服务员。第一篇短文讲“保持活动”原则：人和河流、船只、飞机一样，一直动着、工作着才能长久。第二篇短文讲走神：它会让人出事故，但做白日梦也能帮人思考目标、提高创造力。第一段录音介绍挪威的维京木教堂，以及它们的保护工作和用木头建造的原因。第二段录音介绍三项研究，说明人类婴儿在记忆、分辨音乐情绪等方面的惊人能力。第三段录音讲过度合作的危害，以及怎样在团队合作和个人项目之间找到平衡。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Today our guest is Rosie Mullender, who works as a features editor for a fashion magazine.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是罗西·马伦德，她在一家时尚杂志担任专题编辑。

paras.en: Hi, Rosie.
paras.zh: 你好，罗西。

paras.en: You’re features editor at one of the most widely read women’s magazines in the UK.
paras.zh: 你是英国读者最多的女性杂志之一的专题编辑。

w.m: 读者众多的；广为阅读的

paras.en: What kind of responsibilities does that job entail?
paras.zh: 这份工作具体要负责哪些事情？

paras.en: We spend our days looking at ideas from journalists writing copy for the magazine and website and editing.
paras.zh: 我们每天都在审看给杂志和网站写稿的记者们提出的选题，还要编辑稿件。

paras.en: We do random things like asking people in the street questions and testing sports clothing.
paras.zh: 我们还会做一些五花八门的事，比如在街上向路人提问、试穿运动服装。

w.m: adj. 随意的；五花八门的

paras.en: We also do less tangible things like understanding what our readers want.
paras.zh: 我们还做一些不那么具体的事，比如弄清读者想要什么。

paras.en: It’s certainly varied and sometimes bizarre.
paras.zh: 这份工作确实花样繁多，有时还挺稀奇古怪的。

paras.en: During your working day, what kind of work might you typically do?
paras.zh: 在工作日里，你一般会做哪些工作？

paras.en: My day mainly incorporates responding to emails, writing and editing stories, and coming up with new feature ideas.
paras.zh: 我一天主要是回复邮件、写稿改稿，还有想新的专题选题。

paras.en: How does the job of features editor differ from that of fashion editor or other editorial positions, the features team deals with articles such as careers, reports, confidence, and confessions.
paras.zh: 专题编辑这份工作和时尚编辑或其他编辑岗位有什么不同？专题组负责的是职业、报道、自信、真情告白这类文章。

paras.en: Everything except fashion and beauty.
paras.zh: 除了时尚和美容，其他的都归我们管。

paras.en: A lot of people believe that working at a magazine is a glamorous job.
paras.zh: 很多人都觉得在杂志社工作很光鲜。

w.m: adj. 光鲜亮丽的；有魅力的

paras.en: Is this an accurate representation of what you do, I’d say it’s glamorous to an extent, but not in the way it’s portrayed in films.
paras.zh: 这符合你工作的真实情况吗？我觉得在某种程度上是挺光鲜的，但跟电影里演的不一样。

paras.en: We do have our moments, such as interviewing celebrities and attending parties, which is a huge thrill.
paras.zh: 我们也确实有风光的时候，比如采访名人、参加派对，那真是特别激动人心。

paras.en: Ultimately, though, we’re the same as our readers, but working in a job we’re all very lucky to have.
paras.zh: 不过说到底，我们跟读者是一样的人，只不过我们都很幸运，做着这样一份工作。

paras.en: Did you have to overcome any difficulties to reach this point in your career?
paras.zh: 你在职业生涯中走到今天这一步，有没有经历过什么困难？

paras.en: How did you manage to do this?
paras.zh: 你是怎么做到的？

paras.en: I had to be really persistent, and it was very hard work.
paras.zh: 我必须非常执着，那真的非常辛苦。

w.m: adj. 坚持不懈的；执着的

paras.en: After three years of working in a petrol station and doing unpaid work, I still hadn’t managed to get an entry-level job.
paras.zh: 我在加油站打了三年工，又做了不拿工资的活儿，还是没能找到一份入门级的工作。

paras.en: I was lucky that my last desperate attempt led to a job.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，我最后一次孤注一掷的尝试换来了一份工作。

w.m: adj. 孤注一掷的；拼命的

paras.en: I told myself that all experiences make you a better journalist in the long run, and luckily I was right.
paras.zh: 我告诉自己，从长远来看，所有的经历都会让你成为更好的记者；幸运的是，我说对了。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What is the woman’s profession?
paras.zh: 第一题：这位女士的职业是什么？

paras.en: Question two: What is one of the woman’s main responsibilities?
paras.zh: 第二题：这位女士的主要职责之一是什么？

paras.en: Question three: What do many people think about the woman’s job?
paras.zh: 第三题：很多人觉得这位女士的工作怎么样？

paras.en: Question four: What helped the woman to get her current position?
paras.zh: 第四题：是什么帮助这位女士得到了她现在的职位？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Are you watching any good shows these days?
paras.zh: 你最近在看什么好看的节目吗？

paras.en: Actually, yes.
paras.zh: 还真有。

paras.en: I’m watching a great satire called Frankie.
paras.zh: 我在看一部很棒的讽刺剧，叫《弗兰基》。

paras.en: I think you’d like it.
paras.zh: 我觉得你会喜欢的。

paras.en: Really, what’s it about?
paras.zh: 真的吗？讲的是什么？

paras.en: It’s about a real guy named Frankie.
paras.zh: 讲的是一个真实存在的人，名叫弗兰基。

paras.en: He’s a famous comedian in New York, and the show’s a mixture of comedy and drama, loosely depicting his life.
paras.zh: 他是纽约一位很有名的喜剧演员，这部剧把喜剧和正剧融合在一起，大致演绎了他的生活。

paras.en: I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 不好意思。

paras.en: Do you mean to say it’s a real life series about a real person?
paras.zh: 你的意思是，这是一部讲真人真事的剧？

paras.en: It’s nonfiction, is it?
paras.zh: 是纪实的，对吧？

w.m: n. 纪实作品；非虚构作品

paras.en: No, not really.
paras.zh: 不，不完全是。

paras.en: No, it’s fiction, as what happens in every episode is made up.
paras.zh: 不是，它是虚构的，因为每一集发生的事都是编出来的。

paras.en: However, the lead role is a comedian by the name of Frankie, and he plays himself.
paras.zh: 不过，主角是一位名叫弗兰基的喜剧演员，由他本人出演自己。

paras.en: So Frankie in both real life and in the TV show lives in New York City, is a comic, is divorced, and has two little daughters.
paras.zh: 所以说，弗兰基在现实生活和电视剧里都住在纽约，都是喜剧演员，都离了婚，都有两个小女儿。

paras.en: All those things are true, but aside from him, all his friends and family are played by actors, and the plots and events that take place are also invented.
paras.zh: 这些都是真的，不过除了他本人，他的亲朋好友都是由演员扮演的，剧里发生的情节和事件也都是编的。

paras.en: Oh, I think I see now.
paras.zh: 哦，我想我现在明白了。

paras.en: That sounds like a very original concept.
paras.zh: 这个构思听起来很有新意。

w.m: adj. 有独创性的；新颖的

paras.en: Yes, it is.
paras.zh: 是的，确实如此。

paras.en: In fact, the whole show is written, directed, edited, and produced by him, and it’s very funny and has won many awards.
paras.zh: 其实，整部剧的编剧、导演、剪辑和制作都是他一个人，剧非常好笑，还拿了很多奖。

paras.en: That’s cool.
paras.zh: 真不错。

paras.en: I will try to download it.
paras.zh: 我会试着下载来看看。

paras.en: I’m watching a comedy called The Big Bang Theory.
paras.zh: 我在看一部喜剧，叫《生活大爆炸》。

paras.en: It’s a huge hit around the world.
paras.zh: 这部剧在全世界都大受欢迎。

w.m: 大热作品；轰动一时的作品

paras.en: Oh yes, I’ve heard of it, but never actually watched it.
paras.zh: 哦，对，我听说过，但其实从来没看过。

paras.en: Well, then you should check it out.
paras.zh: 那你应该看看。

paras.en: It’s also very funny.
paras.zh: 它也很好笑。

paras.en: It’s about four male scientists and a female waitress.
paras.zh: 讲的是四个男科学家和一个女服务员的故事。

paras.en: The men are very socially awkward, but very bright, and this is contrasted by the lady’s social skills and common sense.
paras.zh: 这几个男人很不善于社交，但非常聪明，这一点和那位女士的社交能力和常识形成了对比。

paras.en: The show has been running for over 10 years, and some of the actors are practically global superstars now that they are such famous celebrities.
paras.zh: 这部剧已经播了十多年，有些演员如今名气大得几乎成了全球巨星。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the man think of the satire Frankie he recently watched?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士觉得他最近看的讽刺剧《弗兰基》怎么样？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man say is special about the satire Frankie?
paras.zh: 第六题：男士说讽刺剧《弗兰基》有什么特别之处？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the woman say she is going to do with the satire Frankie?
paras.zh: 第七题：关于讽刺剧《弗兰基》，女士说她打算做什么？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the woman say about the comedy The Big Bang Theory?
paras.zh: 第八题：关于喜剧《生活大爆炸》，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one, related to the use it or lose it law, is the keep moving principle.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。与“用进废退”法则相关的，是“保持活动”原则。

paras.en: We learn about stagnation from nature.
paras.zh: 我们可以从大自然中了解停滞是怎么回事。

paras.en: A river that stops moving gets smelly.
paras.zh: 一条不再流动的河会发臭。

paras.en: The same thing happens to people who stop moving, either mentally or physically.
paras.zh: 停止活动的人也是一样，不管是在思想上还是在身体上。

w.m: adv. 在精神上；在思想上

paras.en: Those who play contact sports know that the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still.
paras.zh: 参加对抗性运动的人都知道，通常受伤最多的球员就是站着不动的那个。

w.m: 有身体接触的运动；对抗性运动

paras.en: Of course, you’ll need some time to catch your breath every so often, but the essential message is: keep moving, extending, and learning.
paras.zh: 当然，你时不时需要些时间喘口气，但最根本的道理是：要不停地动、不断拓展、不断学习。

paras.en: Ships last a lot longer when they go to sea than when they stay in the harbor.
paras.zh: 船只出海航行，比停在港口里寿命长得多。

paras.en: The same is true for airplanes.
paras.zh: 飞机也是如此。

paras.en: You don’t preserve an airplane by keeping it on the ground; you preserve it by keeping it in service.
paras.zh: 让飞机一直停在地面上是保养不好的，要让它一直投入使用才行。

paras.en: We also get to live a long, healthy life by staying in service.
paras.zh: 我们也是通过一直工作，才能健康长寿。

paras.en: Longevity statistics reveal that the average person doesn’t last very long after retirement.
paras.zh: 长寿统计数据显示，一般人退休后活不了多久。

paras.en: The moral here is: don’t retire.
paras.zh: 这里的寓意是：不要退休。

paras.en: If a fellow says, “I’m 94 years old and I’ve worked all my life,” we need to realize that is how we got to be 94 by staying involved.
paras.zh: 如果有个人说：“我94岁了，工作了一辈子。”我们要明白，正是因为一直参与其中，他才活到了94岁。

paras.en: George Bernard Shaw won a Nobel Prize when he was nearly 70.
paras.zh: 萧伯纳将近70岁时获得了诺贝尔奖。

paras.en: Benjamin Franklin produced some of his best writings at the age of 84, and Pablo Picasso put brush to canvas right through his eighties.
paras.zh: 本杰明·富兰克林84岁时写出了他最好的几部作品，巴勃罗·毕加索直到八十多岁还在作画。

w.m: 本杰明·富兰克林（美国政治家、科学家）

paras.en: Isn’t the issue how old we think we are?
paras.zh: 问题难道不在于我们觉得自己有多老吗？

paras.en: A bonus with the keep moving principle is that while we keep moving, we don’t have a chance to worry.
paras.zh: “保持活动”原则还有一个额外的好处：只要我们一直在动，就没工夫去担心。

paras.en: Hence, we avoid the dreaded paralysis by analysis.
paras.zh: 因此，我们就能避免可怕的“分析瘫痪”，也就是想得太多反而迟迟不动。

w.m: adj. 可怕的；令人畏惧的
分析瘫痪（想得太多而迟迟不动）

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does the speaker say about players of contact sports?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于参加对抗性运动的人，讲话者说了什么？

w.m: 有身体接触的运动；对抗性运动

paras.en: Question 10: What do longevity statistics reveal about the average person?
paras.zh: 第十题：长寿统计数据揭示了一般人的什么情况？

paras.en: Question 11: What bonus does the keep moving principle bring us, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十一题：根据讲话者的说法，“保持活动”原则给我们带来了什么额外的好处？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: In 2014, one in 16 Americans visited the hospital emergency room for home injuries.
paras.zh: 2014年，每16个美国人中就有一个因为在家受伤去了医院急诊室。

paras.en: One of the main causes of these accidents, a wandering mind.
paras.zh: 这些事故的主要原因之一：走神。

paras.en: By one estimate, people daydream through nearly half of their waking hours, psychologists have recently focused on the tendency to think about something other than the task one is doing.
paras.zh: 据估计，人们醒着的时间里有将近一半都在做白日梦；心理学家最近开始关注人们去想与手头的事无关的东西的这种倾向。

paras.en: For one experiment, researchers developed an app to analyze the relationship between daydreaming and happiness.
paras.zh: 在一项实验中，研究人员开发了一个应用程序，来分析做白日梦和幸福感之间的关系。

paras.en: They found that the average person’s mind wandered most frequently, about 65 percent of the time during personal activities such as brushing their teeth and combing their hair.
paras.zh: 他们发现，一般人在刷牙、梳头这类个人活动时最容易走神，大约65%的时间都在走神。

paras.en: Respondents’ minds tended to wander more when they felt upset rather than happy.
paras.zh: 受访者心情不好的时候比心情好的时候更容易走神。

paras.en: They were more likely to wander toward pleasant topics than unpleasant ones.
paras.zh: 他们走神时更可能想到愉快的事，而不是不愉快的事。

paras.en: How do daydreams affect daydreamers?
paras.zh: 白日梦会对做白日梦的人产生什么影响？

paras.en: A wandering mind leaves us vulnerable when driving.
paras.zh: 开车时走神会让我们很容易出事。

w.m: adj. 易受伤害的；脆弱的

paras.en: In one study, researchers interviewed 955 people involved in traffic accidents.
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，研究人员采访了955名卷入交通事故的人。

paras.en: The majority of them reported having daydreamed just before the accident, yet other research suggests that daydreaming has benefits.
paras.zh: 他们中的大多数人说，事故发生前自己正在做白日梦；不过也有研究表明，做白日梦有好处。

paras.en: Researchers have found that it gives us a chance to think about our goals, and it also seems to increase creativity.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，做白日梦让我们有机会思考自己的目标，似乎还能提高创造力。

paras.en: In one experiment, 145 undergraduates completed four unusual uses tasks, each requiring them to list as many uses as possible for an everyday object.
paras.zh: 在一项实验中，145名本科生完成了四项“非常规用途”任务，每项都要求他们为一件日常物品列出尽可能多的用途。

paras.en: After the first pair of tasks was completed, one group of participants was assigned an undemanding activity intended to cause their minds to wander.
paras.zh: 完成前两项任务后，一组参与者被安排去做一项不费脑子的活动，目的是让他们走神。

w.m: adj. 不费力的；要求不高的

paras.en: When all the participants proceeded to the second pair of tasks, the daydreamers performed 40% better than the others.
paras.zh: 当所有参与者接着做后两项任务时，做白日梦的那一组比其他人的表现好40%。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the passage say about people’s mind?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于人们的思维，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 13: For what purpose did the researchers develop the new app?
paras.zh: 第十三题：研究人员开发这个新应用程序是为了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: How does daydreaming benefit people, according to some researchers?
paras.zh: 第十四题：根据一些研究人员的说法，做白日梦对人有什么好处？

paras.en: Question 15: What was the finding of the experiment with 145 undergraduates?
paras.zh: 第十五题：以145名本科生为对象的那项实验有什么发现？

paras.en: Section C: Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one, dating from as far back as the 12th century, they are claimed to be the rarest historic buildings in Western Europe.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。这些建筑最早可以追溯到12世纪，据称是西欧现存最稀有的历史建筑。

paras.en: These buildings offer vital insights into Scandinavia’s Viking past, but now with only 30 wooden churches remaining, and their condition deteriorating, experts are working to preserve the structures for future generations.
paras.zh: 这些建筑为了解斯堪的纳维亚的维京历史提供了重要线索，但如今木教堂只剩下30座，而且状况越来越差，专家们正努力保护这些建筑，留给子孙后代。

paras.en: Some of these spectacular churches are no more than small buildings, barely four metres wide and six metres tall.
paras.zh: 这些壮观的教堂中，有些只是很小的建筑，宽不过四米，高不过六米。

paras.en: Others are much larger structures that soar up to 40 metres into the cold air, most consist of timber frames that rest on stone blocks.
paras.zh: 另一些则是大得多的建筑，高高耸入寒冷的空中，最高可达40米；大多数是架在石块上的木框架结构。

paras.en: This means that they have no foundations.
paras.zh: 也就是说，它们没有地基。

paras.en: Although many of the churches appear from the outside to be complex structures, they normally feature only a single storey, but numerous different roof levels.
paras.zh: 虽然许多教堂从外面看结构很复杂，但它们通常只有一层，屋顶却分成许多不同的层次。

paras.en: Staff from the Norwegian government have carried out conservation work on 10 of the churches over the past two years.
paras.zh: 过去两年里，挪威政府的工作人员对其中10座教堂做了修缮保护。

paras.en: Most of these churches date from between the 12th and 14th centuries.
paras.zh: 这些教堂大多建于12到14世纪之间。

paras.en: Other churches were conserved in previous years.
paras.zh: 其他教堂在前几年已经修缮过了。

paras.en: So far, specialists have worked to add preservative materials to the churches’ exteriors.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，专家们已经在教堂外部涂上了防腐材料。

paras.en: They also replaced rotting roofs and halted the sinking of the churches into the ground.
paras.zh: 他们还换掉了腐烂的屋顶，并阻止了教堂继续往地下沉。

paras.en: In two cases, huge machines have been used to lift the buildings up to 30 centimetres into the air.
paras.zh: 有两座教堂还动用了大型机器，把建筑抬离地面达30厘米。

paras.en: This was accomplished so that the team could examine and repair the church’s original medieval stone blocks.
paras.zh: 这样做是为了让团队能检查和修复教堂原有的中世纪石块。

paras.en: The team plans to return to around a dozen of the buildings to assess progress and consider further action.
paras.zh: 团队计划再回到其中十来座建筑，评估进展、考虑下一步怎么做。

paras.en: The earliest free-standing wooden church was probably built in Norway in around 1080, however, the largest known wooden churches were built from the 1130s onwards.
paras.zh: 最早的独立式木教堂大概在1080年前后建于挪威，不过已知最大的木教堂是从1130年代起才建造的。

paras.en: This period was one of inter-elite rivalry, in which nobles sought to increase their influence by funding the construction of churches and other buildings.
paras.zh: 这一时期精英阶层相互争斗，贵族们通过出资建造教堂等建筑来扩大自己的影响力。

paras.en: The reason for constructing the buildings from wood, is probably that ideally proportioned, straight, and slender timber was available in large quantities in Scandinavia’s vast pine forests.
paras.zh: 用木头建造这些建筑，原因很可能是斯堪的纳维亚辽阔的松林里有大量比例理想、笔直细长的木材。

paras.en: As wood was so plentiful, it was cheaper to use than the stone used in the buildings of other European cultures.
paras.zh: 由于木材非常充足，用起来比其他欧洲文化建筑所用的石头便宜。

paras.en: The area’s shipbuilding tradition, partly established by the Vikings, also meant that sophisticated carpentry was a major aspect of the local culture.
paras.zh: 这一地区的造船传统部分由维京人奠定，这也意味着精湛的木工手艺是当地文化的重要组成部分。

paras.en: The complex style of the medieval wooden church carvings and the skills used to make them almost certainly derive from the ancient Viking tradition.
paras.zh: 中世纪木教堂雕刻的复杂风格以及雕刻用的技艺，几乎可以肯定是源自古老的维京传统。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about the Viking wooden churches?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于维京木教堂，讲话者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What is special about most of the Viking wooden churches?
paras.zh: 第十七题：大多数维京木教堂有什么特别之处？

paras.en: Question 18: Why were the Viking churches constructed from wood?
paras.zh: 第十八题：维京教堂为什么用木头建造？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: In last week’s lecture, we discussed the characteristics of the newly born offspring of several mammals.
paras.zh: 在上周的讲座中，我们讨论了几种哺乳动物新生幼崽的特点。

paras.en: You probably remember that human infants are less developed physically than other mammals of the same age, but in today’s lecture we’ll look at three very interesting studies that hint at the surprising abilities of human babies.
paras.zh: 大家可能还记得，人类婴儿在身体上不如同龄的其他哺乳动物发育得好，但在今天的讲座中，我们要看三项非常有意思的研究，它们表明人类婴儿有着惊人的能力。

paras.en: In the first study, three-year-olds watched two videos shown side by side, each featuring a different researcher, one of whom they’d met once two years earlier, the children spent longer watching the video showing the researcher they hadn’t met.
paras.zh: 在第一项研究中，三岁的孩子观看了并排播放的两段视频，每段视频里各有一位不同的研究人员，其中一位孩子们两年前见过一次；结果孩子们看那位没见过的研究人员的视频时间更长。

paras.en: This is consistent with young children’s usual tendency to look longer at things that aren’t familiar.
paras.zh: 这与小孩子通常爱盯着不熟悉的东西看的倾向是一致的。

paras.en: And really, this is amazing.
paras.zh: 说真的，这太神奇了。

paras.en: It suggests the children remembered the researcher they’d met just one time when they were only one-year-olds.
paras.zh: 这说明孩子们记得那位他们只在一岁时见过一次的研究人员。

paras.en: Of course, as most of us forget memories from our first few years as we grow older, these early long-term memories will likely be lost in subsequent years.
paras.zh: 当然，由于我们大多数人长大后会忘记最初几年的记忆，这些早期的长期记忆很可能在之后的几年里丢失。

paras.en: Our second study is about music.
paras.zh: 我们的第二项研究是关于音乐的。

paras.en: For this study, researchers played music to babies through speakers located on either side of a human face.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员通过放在一张人脸两侧的扬声器给婴儿放音乐。

paras.en: They waited until the babies got bored and averted their gaze from the face, and then they changed the mood of the music, either from sad to happy or the other way around.
paras.zh: 他们一直等到婴儿觉得无聊、把目光从那张脸上移开，然后改变音乐的情绪，要么从悲伤变成欢快，要么反过来。

paras.en: This mood switch made no difference to the three-month-olds, but for the nine-month-olds it was enough to renew their interest, and they started looking again in the direction of the face.
paras.zh: 情绪的转变对三个月大的婴儿没有影响，但对九个月大的婴儿来说，这足以重新引起他们的兴趣，他们又开始朝那张脸看了。

paras.en: This suggests that babies of that age can tell the difference between a happy melody and a sad tune.
paras.zh: 这说明这个年龄的婴儿能分辨欢快的旋律和悲伤的曲调。

paras.en: Our final study is from 1980, but it’s still relevant today.
paras.zh: 我们的最后一项研究来自1980年，但它在今天仍然有意义。

paras.en: In fact, it’s one of the most famous pieces of research about infant emotion ever published.
paras.zh: 事实上，它是迄今发表过的关于婴儿情绪的最著名的研究之一。

paras.en: The study involved ordinary adults watching video clips of babies nine months or younger.
paras.zh: 这项研究让普通成年人观看九个月及以下婴儿的视频片段。

paras.en: In the video clips, the babies made various facial expressions in response to real life events, including playful interactions and painful ones.
paras.zh: 在视频片段中，婴儿对现实生活中的事件做出各种面部表情，其中有好玩的互动，也有让他们疼的互动。

paras.en: The adult observers were able to reliably discern an assortment of emotions on the babies’ faces.
paras.zh: 成年观察者能可靠地辨认出婴儿脸上的各种情绪。

paras.en: These emotions included interest, joy, surprise, sadness, anger, disgust, contempt, and fear.
paras.zh: 这些情绪包括兴趣、喜悦、惊讶、悲伤、愤怒、厌恶、轻蔑和恐惧。

paras.en: Next week, we’ll be looking at this last study more closely.
paras.zh: 下周，我们会更细致地讲讲最后这项研究。

paras.en: In fact, we will be viewing some of the video clips from that study, and together see how well we do in discerning the baby’s emotions.
paras.zh: 其实，我们还会看那项研究中的一些视频片段，一起看看我们能多准确地辨认出婴儿的情绪。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What are the three interesting studies about?
paras.zh: 第十九题：这三项有意思的研究是关于什么的？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the second study find about nine-month-old babies?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于九个月大的婴儿，第二项研究有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 21: What is the 1980 study about?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：1980年的那项研究是关于什么的？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Today, I’d like to talk about the dangers of being too collaborative.
paras.zh: 今天我想谈谈过于强调合作的危害。

paras.en: Being a good team player is an essential skill in our modern workplace.
paras.zh: 做一名优秀的团队成员，是现代职场的一项基本技能。

w.m: 有团队精神的人；团队成员

paras.en: The ability to work well with others and collaborate on projects is a sought-after ability in nearly every position.
paras.zh: 能和别人合作得好、在项目上协作，几乎是每个岗位都看重的能力。

paras.en: However, placing too much emphasis on being a good team player can negatively affect your career growth.
paras.zh: 然而，过分强调做好团队成员，会对你的职业发展产生负面影响。

paras.en: Don’t be overly focused on gaining consensus.
paras.zh: 不要过分专注于争取一致意见。

paras.en: Don’t be too concerned with the opinions of others.
paras.zh: 不要太在意别人的意见。

paras.en: This can hinder your ability to make decisions, speak up, and gain recognition for your individual skills and strengths.
paras.zh: 这会妨碍你做决定、发表意见，也会让你的个人技能和长处得不到认可。

paras.en: Some people are too subordinate to others’ opinions, too focused on decision consensus, too silent about their own point of view, too agreeable to take things on when they don’t have time or energy.
paras.zh: 有些人太顺从别人的意见，太专注于让决策达成一致，对自己的观点太过沉默，太随和，连没时间没精力的时候也接下事情。

w.m: adj. 随和的；乐于同意的

paras.en: This leads to building a brand of underconfident, submissive, low-impact non-leaders, and hampers their growth and career advancement.
paras.zh: 这会让他们树立起一种不自信、顺从、影响力低、当不了领导的形象，还会阻碍他们的成长和职业晋升。

paras.en: Collaboration certainly makes your individual competencies and contributions more difficult for outsiders to identify.
paras.zh: 合作无疑会让外人更难看出你个人的能力和贡献。

paras.en: Collaborative projects mean you sharing the spotlight with others.
paras.zh: 合作项目意味着你要和别人一起分享荣誉。

paras.en: Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths.
paras.zh: 这样外人可能就很难判断你的贡献和长处。

paras.en: This may end up costing you opportunities for promotions or pay raises.
paras.zh: 最终你可能因此失去升职或加薪的机会。

paras.en: You certainly shouldn’t ditch teamwork, but how can you avoid the hazards of being an over collaborator?
paras.zh: 你当然不应该抛开团队合作，可怎样才能避免过度合作的种种危害呢？

paras.en: Working in a team can have huge benefits.
paras.zh: 团队合作会带来巨大的好处。

paras.en: Your team may have repeated successes and often gain recognition.
paras.zh: 你的团队可能会屡获成功，经常得到认可。

paras.en: You’ll then have more opportunities to expand your professional network than if you worked alone.
paras.zh: 这样你就会比单干时有更多机会拓展自己的职业人脉。

paras.en: However, finding a balance between team efforts and individual projects that give you independent recognition is important for making a name for yourself and providing opportunities for advancement.
paras.zh: 然而，要在团队工作和能让你独立获得认可的个人项目之间找到平衡，这对打响名气、获得晋升机会很重要。

paras.en: Be selective in who you work with.
paras.zh: 要有选择地挑合作对象。

paras.en: This will maximize the benefits and minimize the downsides of being a team player, collaborate with people who have complementary expertise.
paras.zh: 这样能让做团队成员的好处最大化、坏处最小化；要和专长互补的人合作。

paras.en: Select projects where there’s potential for mutual benefit.
paras.zh: 选择有可能实现互利的项目。

paras.en: Perhaps you’re bringing your unique knowledge and gaining access to someone else’s professional network, or maybe you’re able to learn a new skill by working with someone.
paras.zh: 也许你贡献了自己独特的知识，同时接触到了别人的职业人脉；又或者通过和别人合作，你学到了一项新技能。

paras.en: Seek out your teammates purposefully rather than jumping on every new group project opportunity.
paras.zh: 要有目的地寻找队友，而不是一有新的小组项目就扑上去。

paras.en: When we are too collaborative, we want everyone to agree with a decision before we proceed.
paras.zh: 我们过于看重合作的时候，就会想让每个人都同意某项决定后才往下推进。

paras.en: This can create unnecessary delays as you hold meetings trying to achieve a consensus.
paras.zh: 这可能造成不必要的拖延，因为你得开会，想办法达成共识。

paras.en: It’s fine to be collaborative when seeking input, but put a deadline on the input stage and arrive at a decision, even if it’s a decision that doesn’t have consensus.
paras.zh: 征求意见时合作一下没问题，但要给征求意见阶段定一个截止时间，然后做出决定，哪怕这个决定没有达成共识。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker say about being over collaborative?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于过度合作，讲话者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the speaker say about people engaged in collaborative projects?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于参与合作项目的人，讲话者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: How do people benefit from working in a team?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：人们从团队合作中能得到什么好处？

paras.en: Question 25: Why is it undesirable to spend too much time trying to reach consensus?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：为什么花太多时间去争取达成共识是不可取的？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2019年12月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2019年12月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，一位顾客到伦敦一家专营爵士乐的唱片店找摇滚乐，店员介绍了店里的业务，又谈到爵士乐听众变少、爵士乐很难下定义。第二段长对话里，女士向银行申请商业贷款被拒，因为信用记录不够好，她打算先攒钱、减少债务，男士则鼓励她别灰心。第一篇短文讲年轻农民利奥·桑切斯：农场很小，新旧工具都用，一心想为农业树立新标准。第二篇短文讲作者试吃英国超市卖的烤蟋蟀，以及昆虫食品的营养和环保优势。第一段录音讲“学习风格”：研究并不支持它是天生特质，用多种方式、尤其是借助图片，大多数人都学得更好。第二段录音认为自由市场资本主义让人被工作困住，主张缩短每周工作时间。第三段录音讲柏林新机场一再推迟开放、问题不断、耗资巨大，成了德国“高效”名声的笑柄。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Excuse me, where’s your rock music section?
paras.zh: 打扰一下，你们的摇滚乐区在哪儿？

paras.en: Rock music.
paras.zh: 摇滚乐？

paras.en: I’m sorry, we’re a jazz store.
paras.zh: 不好意思，我们是一家爵士乐唱片店。

paras.en: We don’t have any rock and roll.
paras.zh: 我们这儿没有摇滚乐。

paras.en: Oh, you only have jazz music, nothing else.
paras.zh: 哦，你们只有爵士乐，别的都没有。

paras.en: That’s right.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: We’re the only record store in London dedicated exclusively to jazz.
paras.zh: 我们是伦敦唯一一家专营爵士乐的唱片店。

paras.en: Actually, we’re more than just a record store.
paras.zh: 其实，我们不只是一家唱片店。

paras.en: We have a cafe and library upstairs, and a ticket office down the hall where you can buy tickets to all the major jazz concerts in the city.
paras.zh: 楼上有咖啡馆和图书室，走廊那头还有售票处，你可以在那里买到城里所有大型爵士音乐会的票。

paras.en: Also, we have our own studio next door where we produce albums for up-and-coming artists.
paras.zh: 另外，隔壁还有我们自己的录音棚，我们在那里为新晋艺人制作专辑。

w.m: adj. 崭露头角的；有前途的

paras.en: We are committed to fostering new music talent.
paras.zh: 我们致力于培养音乐新人。

paras.en: Wow, that’s so cool!
paras.zh: 哇，太酷了！

paras.en: I guess there’s not much of a jazz scene anymore, not like there used to be.
paras.zh: 我猜现在爵士乐圈子已经没那么热闹了，不像以前那样了。

paras.en: But here, you’re trying to promote this great music genre.
paras.zh: 但在你们这儿，你们在努力推广这种很棒的音乐类型。

paras.en: Yes, indeed.
paras.zh: 是的，确实如此。

paras.en: Nowadays, most people like to listen to pop and rock music, hip hop music from America is also getting more and more popular.
paras.zh: 如今，大多数人都喜欢听流行乐和摇滚乐，美国的嘻哈音乐也越来越受欢迎。

paras.en: So as a result, there are fewer listeners of jazz, which is a great shame, because it’s an incredibly rich genre.
paras.zh: 所以结果就是，听爵士乐的人越来越少，这真是太可惜了，因为它是一种内涵特别丰富的音乐类型。

paras.en: But that’s not to say there isn’t any good new jazz music being made out there anymore?
paras.zh: 但这并不是说，现在外面就再也没有好的爵士新作了吧？

paras.en: Far from it.
paras.zh: 远不是这样。

paras.en: It’s just a much smaller market today.
paras.zh: 只不过今天的市场小多了。

paras.en: So, how would you define jazz?
paras.zh: 那么，你会怎么给爵士乐下定义？

paras.en: Well, interestingly enough, there’s no agreed-upon definition of jazz.
paras.zh: 嗯，有意思的是，爵士乐并没有一个公认的定义。

w.m: adj. 公认的；一致同意的

paras.en: Indeed, there are many different styles of jazz.
paras.zh: 确实，爵士乐有很多不同的风格。

paras.en: Some have singing, but most don’t.
paras.zh: 有些有演唱，但大多数没有。

paras.en: Some are electric and some aren’t.
paras.zh: 有些用电声乐器，有些不用。

paras.en: Some contain live experimentation, but not always.
paras.zh: 有些含有现场即兴的尝试，但也不总是这样。

paras.en: While there’s no simple definition for it, and while there are many different styles of jazz, you simply know it when you hear it.
paras.zh: 虽然它没有简单的定义，爵士乐也有很多不同的风格，但你一听就知道那是爵士乐。

paras.en: Honestly, the only way to know what jazz is is listen to it yourself.
paras.zh: 说实话，要知道爵士乐是什么，唯一的办法就是自己去听。

paras.en: As the great trumpet player Louis Armstrong said, “If you gotta ask, you’ll never know.”
paras.zh: 正如伟大的小号手路易斯·阿姆斯特朗所说：“如果你还得问，那你永远都不会懂。”

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn about the woman’s store?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于女士的店，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say about jazz music?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于爵士乐，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman say about jazz?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于爵士乐，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What should you do to appreciate different styles of jazz according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第四题：根据女士的说法，要欣赏不同风格的爵士乐，应该怎么做？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: How did it go at the bank this morning?
paras.zh: 今天上午在银行办得怎么样？

paras.en: Not well.
paras.zh: 不太顺利。

paras.en: My proposal was rejected.
paras.zh: 我的申请被拒了。

paras.en: Really?
paras.zh: 真的吗？

paras.en: But why?
paras.zh: 可为什么呢？

paras.en: Bunch of reasons.
paras.zh: 原因一大堆。

paras.en: For starters, they said my credit history was not good enough.
paras.zh: 首先，他们说我的信用记录不够好。

paras.en: Did they say how you could improve that?
paras.zh: 他们有没有说你怎么才能改善？

paras.en: Yes, they said that after five more years of paying my mortgage, then I would become a more viable candidate for a business loan.
paras.zh: 说了，他们说我再还五年房贷，就会成为更合适的商业贷款申请人。

paras.en: But right now, it’s too risky for them to lend me money.
paras.zh: 但眼下，借钱给我对他们来说风险太大。

paras.en: They fear I will default on any business loan I’m given, well, that doesn’t sound fair.
paras.zh: 他们担心不管给我什么商业贷款，我都会还不上。——嗯，这听起来不太公平。

paras.en: Your business idea is amazing.
paras.zh: 你的创业点子太棒了。

paras.en: Did you show them your business plan?
paras.zh: 你给他们看商业计划书了吗？

paras.en: What did they say?
paras.zh: 他们怎么说？

paras.en: They didn’t really articulate any position regarding the actual business plan.
paras.zh: 他们并没有真正对这份商业计划本身表明任何态度。

paras.en: They simply looked at my credit history and determined it was not good enough.
paras.zh: 他们只看了我的信用记录，就认定不够好。

paras.en: They said the bank has strict guidelines and requirements as to who they can lend money to, and I simply don’t meet their financial threshold.
paras.zh: 他们说银行在可以借钱给谁这方面有严格的规定和要求，而我根本达不到他们的财务门槛。

paras.en: What if you asked for a smaller amount?
paras.zh: 要是你申请少一点的金额呢？

paras.en: Maybe you could gather capital from other sources, smaller loans from more lenders.
paras.zh: 也许你可以从别的渠道筹集资金，从更多的贷款方那里分别借小额贷款。

paras.en: You don’t get it.
paras.zh: 你没明白。

paras.en: It doesn’t matter the size of the loan I ask for, or the type of business I propose.
paras.zh: 我申请的贷款多少、提出的是哪种生意，都无关紧要。

paras.en: That’s all inconsequential.
paras.zh: 那些都无关紧要。

w.m: adj. 不重要的；无关紧要的

paras.en: The first thing every bank will do is study how much money I have and how much debt I have before they decide whether or not to lend me any more money.
paras.zh: 每家银行做的第一件事，就是在决定要不要再借钱给我之前，先研究我有多少钱、欠了多少债。

paras.en: If I want to continue ahead with this dream of owning my own business, I have no other choice but to build up my own finances.
paras.zh: 我要是想继续追逐自己开公司的梦想，就别无选择，只能先把自己的财务状况搞好。

paras.en: I need around 20% more in personal savings and 50% less debt.
paras.zh: 我的个人存款需要再多20%左右，债务要少一半。

paras.en: That’s all there is to it.
paras.zh: 就这么简单。

w.m: 就这么回事；就这么简单

paras.en: I see now.
paras.zh: 我现在明白了。

paras.en: Well, it’s a huge pity that they rejected your request, but don’t lose hope.
paras.zh: 嗯，他们拒绝了你的申请，真是太可惜了，不过别灰心。

paras.en: I still think that your idea is great, and that you would turn it into a phenomenal success.
paras.zh: 我还是觉得你的点子很棒，你一定能把它做得非常成功。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What did the woman do this morning?
paras.zh: 第五题：女士今天上午做了什么？

paras.en: Question six: Why was the woman’s proposal rejected?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士的申请为什么被拒了？

paras.en: Question seven: What is the woman planning to do?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士打算做什么？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the man suggest the woman do?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士建议女士做什么？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: There’s a lot about Leo Sanchez and his farm in Salinas, California, that seems unusual.
paras.zh: 利奥·桑切斯和他在加利福尼亚州萨利纳斯的农场有很多地方看起来与众不同。

paras.en: The national average farm size is around 440 acres, but his is only one acre.
paras.zh: 全国农场的平均面积约为440英亩，而他的只有1英亩。

paras.en: The average age of farmers hovers around 58 years old, but he is just 26, and Sanchez constantly attempts to improve everything, from seeding techniques out in the field to the promotion and sale of his produce online.
paras.zh: 农民的平均年龄徘徊在58岁左右，而他只有26岁；桑切斯还在不断尝试改进方方面面，从田里的播种技术到网上推广和销售自家农产品。

paras.en: This is evidence of an experimental approach.
paras.zh: 这体现了一种勇于尝试的做法。

paras.en: It’s an approach not dictated by the confines of conventional large-scale agriculture led by international corporations, while farming is often difficult for both the body and mind, Sanchez says he and many of his fellow young farmers are motivated by desire to set a new standard for agriculture.
paras.zh: 这种做法不受跨国公司主导的传统大规模农业的条条框框限制。虽然务农往往身心俱疲，桑切斯说，他和许多年轻的同行之所以干这行，是想为农业树立新标准。

paras.en: Many of them are employing a multitude of technologies, some new and some not so new.
paras.zh: 他们中许多人在使用大量技术，有些是新的，有些则没那么新。

paras.en: Recently, Sanchez bought a hand-operated tool which pulls out weeds and loosens soil.
paras.zh: 最近，桑切斯买了一件手动工具，可以拔草、松土。

paras.en: It actually dates back to at least 1701.
paras.zh: 这种工具其实至少可以追溯到1701年。

paras.en: It stands in sharp contrast to Sanchez’s other gadget, a gas-powered flame weed killer invented in 1997.
paras.zh: 它与桑切斯的另一件工具形成了鲜明对比——那是一台1997年发明的燃气火焰除草器。

paras.en: He simply doesn’t discriminate when it comes to the newness of tools.
paras.zh: 在工具新旧这件事上，他完全一视同仁。

paras.en: If it works, it works.
paras.zh: 管用就行。

paras.en: Farmers have a long history of invention, and it’s no different today.
paras.zh: 农民发明创造的历史由来已久，如今也不例外。

paras.en: Young farmers are guided by their love for agriculture, and aided by their knowledge of technology.
paras.zh: 年轻农民靠的是对农业的热爱，借助的是自己的技术知识。

paras.en: To find inexpensive and appropriately sized tools, they collaborate and innovate.
paras.zh: 为了找到便宜又大小合适的工具，他们互相合作、不断创新。

paras.en: Sometimes the old stuff just works better, or more efficiently.
paras.zh: 有时候，旧东西就是更好用，或者效率更高。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What do we learn about Leo Sanchez’s farm?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于利奥·桑切斯的农场，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What has motivated Leo Sanchez and his fellow young farmers to engage in farming?
paras.zh: 第十题：是什么激励利奥·桑切斯和他的年轻同行们投身农业？

paras.en: Question 11: Why did Leo Sanchez buy a hand-operated weeding tool?
paras.zh: 第十一题：利奥·桑切斯为什么买了一件手动除草工具？

paras.en: Passage two: Eat Grub is Britain’s first new food company that breaks Western food boundaries by introducing edible insects as a new source of food, and Sainsbury’s is the first UK supermarket to stock the company’s crunchy roasted crickets.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。Eat Grub是英国第一家打破西方饮食界限的新食品公司，它把可食用昆虫作为一种新的食物来源推了出来；塞恩斯伯里是英国第一家销售该公司香脆烤蟋蟀的超市。

paras.en: Sainsbury’s insists that such food is no joke, and could be a new sustainable source of protein.
paras.zh: 塞恩斯伯里坚称，这种食物可不是开玩笑，它有可能成为一种新的可持续蛋白质来源。

paras.en: Out of curiosity, I paid a visit to Sainsbury’s.
paras.zh: 出于好奇，我去了一趟塞恩斯伯里。

paras.en: As I put my hand into a packet of crickets with their tiny eyes and legs, the idea of one going in my mouth made me feel a little sick.
paras.zh: 我把手伸进一袋蟋蟀里，看到它们小小的眼睛和腿，一想到要把一只放进嘴里，我就有点恶心。

paras.en: But the first bite was a pleasant surprise, a little dry and lacking of taste, but at least a wing didn’t get stuck in my throat.
paras.zh: 不过第一口倒是让人惊喜：有点干，没什么味道，但至少没有翅膀卡在喉咙里。

paras.en: The roasted seasoning largely overpowered any other flavour, although there was a slightly bitter aftertaste.
paras.zh: 烤制的调味料基本盖过了其他味道，不过回味有一点点苦。

paras.en: The texture was crunchy, but smelt a little of cat food.
paras.zh: 口感很脆，但闻起来有点像猫粮。

paras.en: Eat Grub also recommends the crickets as a topping for noodles, soups, and salads.
paras.zh: Eat Grub还推荐把蟋蟀撒在面条、汤和沙拉上当配料。

paras.en: The company boasts that its dried crickets contain more protein than beef, chicken, and pork, as well as minerals like iron and calcium.
paras.zh: 这家公司夸口说，他们的干蟋蟀所含的蛋白质比牛肉、鸡肉和猪肉都多，还含有铁、钙等矿物质。

paras.en: Unlike the production of meat, bugs do not use up large amounts of land, water, or feed, and insect farming also produces far fewer greenhouse gases.
paras.zh: 和肉类生产不同，虫子不会消耗大量的土地、水和饲料，而且昆虫养殖排放的温室气体也少得多。

paras.en: However, despite 2 billion people worldwide already supplementing their diet with insects, consumer disgust remains a large barrier in many Western countries.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管全世界已有20亿人在用昆虫补充饮食，但在许多西方国家，消费者的厌恶心理仍是一大障碍。

paras.en: I’m not sure bugs will become a popular snack any time soon, but they’re definitely food for thought.
paras.zh: 我不确定虫子会不会很快成为受欢迎的零食，但它们确实值得好好想一想。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What do we learn from the passage about the food company Eat Grub?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于食品公司Eat Grub，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the speaker say about his first bite of roasted crickets?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于第一口烤蟋蟀，讲话者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does Eat Grub say about its dried crickets?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于自家的干蟋蟀，Eat Grub说了什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the passage say about insect farming?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于昆虫养殖，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Section C: Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Have you ever had someone try to explain something to you a dozen times with no luck, but then when you see a picture, the idea finally clicks.
paras.zh: 你有没有遇到过有人给你解释一件事，讲了十几遍都没用，可你一看到图，一下子就明白了？

paras.en: If that sounds familiar, maybe you might consider yourself a visual learner, or if reading or listening does a trick?
paras.zh: 如果你觉得这很熟悉，也许你会认为自己是视觉型学习者；又或者，如果读或听对你更管用……

paras.en: Maybe you feel like you’re a verbal learner.
paras.zh: ……那你可能觉得自己是语言型学习者。

paras.en: We call these labels learning styles.
paras.zh: 我们把这些标签称为学习风格。

paras.en: But is there really a way to categorize different types of students?
paras.zh: 但真的有办法把学生分成不同类型吗？

paras.en: Well, it actually seems that multiple presentation formats, especially if one of them is visual, help most people learn.
paras.zh: 嗯，事实上，用多种方式呈现内容，尤其是其中有一种是视觉方式时，对大多数人的学习似乎都有帮助。

paras.en: When psychologists and educators test for learning styles, they’re trying to figure out whether these are inherent traits that affect how well students learn, instead of just a preference.
paras.zh: 心理学家和教育工作者测试学习风格时，是想弄清楚这些究竟是会影响学生学习效果的天生特质，还是只是一种偏好。

paras.en: Usually, they start by giving a survey to figure out what style a student favors, like visual or verbal learning.
paras.zh: 通常，他们先做一个调查，弄清楚学生偏爱哪种风格，比如视觉学习还是语言学习。

paras.en: Then they try to teach the students something with a specific presentation style, like using visual aids, and do a follow-up test to see how much they learned.
paras.zh: 然后用一种特定的呈现方式教学生一些东西，比如使用直观教具，再做一次后续测试，看看他们学到了多少。

paras.en: That way, the researchers can see if the self-identified verbal learners really learned better when the information was just spoken aloud, for example.
paras.zh: 比如说，这样研究人员就能看出那些自认为是语言型学习者的人，在信息只是口头讲出来时，是不是真的学得更好。

paras.en: But according to a 2008 review, only one study that followed this design found that students actually learned best with their preferred style, but the study had some big flaws.
paras.zh: 不过根据2008年的一篇综述，只有一项按这种设计做的研究发现，学生用自己偏爱的方式确实学得最好，但这项研究有一些很大的缺陷。

paras.en: The researchers excluded two-thirds of the original participants because they didn’t seem to have any clear learning style from the survey at the beginning, and they didn’t even report the actual test scores in the final paper, so it doesn’t really seem like learning styles are an inherent trait that we all have, but that doesn’t mean that all students will do amazingly if they just spend all their time reading from a textbook.
paras.zh: 研究人员把三分之二的原始参与者排除在外，因为从一开始的调查来看，他们似乎没有任何明确的学习风格；而且他们在最终的论文里连实际考试分数都没有报告。所以，学习风格似乎并不是我们每个人都有的天生特质；但这并不意味着学生只要把时间都花在读课本上，就都能学得特别好。

paras.en: Instead, most people seem to learn better if they’re taught in several ways, especially if one is visual.
paras.zh: 相反，大多数人似乎在用几种方式教的时候学得更好，尤其是其中一种是视觉方式的时候。

paras.en: In one study, researchers tested whether students remembered lists of words better if they heard them, saw them, or both.
paras.zh: 在一项研究中，研究人员测试了学生是听到单词表、看到单词表还是既听又看时记得更好。

paras.en: And everyone seemed to do better if they got to see the words in print, even the self-identified auditory learners, their preference didn’t seem to matter.
paras.zh: 结果每个人只要能看到印出来的单词，似乎都表现得更好，连那些自认为是听觉型学习者的人也一样；他们的偏好似乎无关紧要。

paras.en: Similar studies tested whether students learned basic physics and chemistry concepts better by reading plain text or viewing pictures too, and everyone did better with the help of pictures.
paras.zh: 类似的研究还测试了学生学习物理和化学的基本概念时，是读纯文字学得好，还是看图片学得好，结果所有人借助图片都学得更好。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: Why do psychologists and educators study learning styles?
paras.zh: 第十六题：心理学家和教育工作者为什么要研究学习风格？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the speaker say about one study mentioned in the 2008 review?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于2008年综述中提到的一项研究，讲话者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What message does the speaker want to convey about learning at the end of the talk?
paras.zh: 第十八题：讲话者在结尾想就学习传达什么信息？

paras.en: Recording two, free market capitalism hasn’t freed us; it has trapped us.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。自由市场资本主义没有给我们自由，反而把我们困住了。

paras.en: It’s imperative for us to embrace a workplace revolution.
paras.zh: 我们必须迎接一场职场革命。

paras.en: We are unlikely to spend our last moments, regretting that we didn’t spend enough of our lives slaving away at work, we may instead find ourselves feeling guilty about the time we didn’t spend watching our children grow, or with our loved ones, or travelling, or on the cultural or leisure pursuits that bring us happiness.
paras.zh: 我们在生命的最后时刻，不太可能后悔这辈子没花够时间埋头苦干；相反，我们可能会感到愧疚：没花时间看着孩子长大，没多陪陪所爱的人，没去旅行，也没去追求那些给我们带来快乐的文化或休闲活动。

paras.en: Unfortunately, the average full-time employee in the world works 42 hours a week, well over a third of the time we’re awake.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，全世界全职员工平均每周工作42小时，远远超过我们醒着的时间的三分之一。

paras.en: Some of our all-too-precious time is being stolen.
paras.zh: 我们一部分本就太过宝贵的时间正被偷走。

paras.en: Office workers do around 2 billion hours of unpaid overtime each year, so it’s extremely welcome that some government coalitions have started looking into potentially cutting the working week to four days.
paras.zh: 上班族每年要无偿加班大约20亿小时，所以令人十分欣慰的是，有些政府执政联盟已经开始研究，有没有可能把每周工作日缩短到四天。

paras.en: The champions of free market capitalism promised their way of life would bring us freedom, but it wasn’t freedom at all.
paras.zh: 自由市场资本主义的拥护者曾承诺，他们的生活方式会给我们带来自由，但那根本不是自由。

paras.en: From the lack of secure, affordable housing to growing job insecurity and rising personal debt, the individual is trapped.
paras.zh: 从缺乏有保障、买得起的住房，到工作越来越没保障、个人债务不断增加，个人被困住了。

w.m: adj. 越来越多的；日益增长的

paras.en: Nine decades ago, leading economists predicted that technological advances and rising productivity would mean that we’d be working a 15-hour week by now.
paras.zh: 九十年前，顶尖的经济学家预测，技术进步和生产率提高意味着我们到现在每周只需工作15小时。

paras.en: That target has been somewhat missed.
paras.zh: 这个目标可以说多少有点落空了。

paras.en: Here is the most malignant threat to our personal freedom, particularly as the balance of power in the workplace has been shifted so dramatically from worker to boss, a huge portion of our lives involves the surrender of our freedom and personal autonomy.
paras.zh: 这就是对我们个人自由最致命的威胁。尤其是职场中的权力天平已经从员工那边大幅倒向老板那边，我们生活中有很大一部分都意味着交出自由和个人自主权。

paras.en: It’s time in which we are directed by the needs and desires of others, and denied the right to make our own choices.
paras.zh: 在这段时间里，我们受别人的需要和意愿支配，被剥夺了自己做选择的权利。

paras.en: That’s bad for us.
paras.zh: 这对我们是有害的。

paras.en: It’s hardly surprising that over half a million workers suffer from work-related mental health conditions each year.
paras.zh: 每年有超过50万名员工患上与工作有关的心理健康问题，这一点也不奇怪。

paras.en: All that 15.4 million working days were lost to work-related stress last year, a jump of nearly a quarter.
paras.zh: 去年，因工作压力损失的工作日约有1540万个，增加了近四分之一。

paras.en: Yes, there are those who, far from being overworked, actually seek more hours.
paras.zh: 是的，确实有人非但没有过度工作，反而想多干几个小时。

paras.en: But a shorter working week would enable us to redistribute hours from the overworked to the underworked.
paras.zh: 但缩短每周工作时间，能让我们把工作时间从工作过量的人那里，重新分配给工作不足的人。

paras.en: We need to look at ways of cutting the working week without slashing living standards, after all, the world’s workers have already suffered the worst deduction in wages since the early 1800s, and cutting the working week would be conducive to the individual, giving millions of workers more time to spend as they see fit.
paras.zh: 我们需要想办法在不大幅降低生活水平的前提下缩短每周工作时间。毕竟，全世界的劳动者已经经历了19世纪初以来最严重的工资缩水，而缩短每周工作时间对个人有好处，能让数以百万计的劳动者有更多时间，按自己的意愿去安排。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do people often feel guilty about, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十九题：根据讲话者的说法，人们常常对什么感到内疚？

paras.en: Question 20: What did leading economists predict 90 years ago?
paras.zh: 第二十题：九十年前，顶尖经济学家预测了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What is the result of denying workers right to make their own choices?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：剥夺员工自己做选择的权利会带来什么后果？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Today I’m going to talk about Germany’s dream airport in Berlin.
paras.zh: 今天我要讲讲德国柏林的“梦想机场”。

paras.en: The airport looks exactly like every other major modern airport in Europe, except for one big problem.
paras.zh: 这座机场看上去和欧洲其他大型现代机场一模一样，只有一个大问题。

paras.en: More than seven years after it was originally supposed to open, it still stands empty.
paras.zh: 原定开放时间已经过去七年多了，它却至今还空着。

paras.en: Germany is known for its efficiency and refined engineering, but when it comes to its new ghost airport, this reputation could not be further from the truth.
paras.zh: 德国以效率高、工程精湛著称，可说到它这座新的“幽灵机场”，这种名声可就完全不符合事实了。

w.h: could not be further from the truth

paras.en: Plagued by long delays, perpetual mismanagement, and ever soaring costs, the airport has become something of a joke among Germans, and a source of frustration for local politicians, business leaders, and residents alike.
paras.zh: 由于长期延误、管理一直混乱、成本不断飙升，这座机场在德国人当中简直成了笑话，也让当地政界人士、商界领袖和居民同样感到恼火。

paras.en: Planning for the new airport began in 1989, at the time it became clear that the newly reunified Berlin would need a modern airport with far greater capacity than its existing airports.
paras.zh: 新机场的规划始于1989年，当时人们已经清楚地意识到，刚刚重新统一的柏林需要一座现代化机场，容量要比现有的机场大得多。

paras.en: The city broke ground on the new airport in 2006.
paras.zh: 2006年，这座城市为新机场破土动工。

paras.en: The first major sign of problems came in summer 2010 when the construction corporation pushed the opening from October 2011 to June 2012.
paras.zh: 第一个大问题的迹象出现在2010年夏天，当时建设公司把开放时间从2011年10月推迟到了2012年6月。

paras.en: In 2012, the city planned an opening ceremony, but less than a month beforehand, inspectors found significant problems with the fire safety system, and pushed the opening back again to 2013.
paras.zh: 2012年，柏林市计划举行开幕典礼，但在开幕前不到一个月，检查人员发现消防安全系统存在重大问题，于是又把开放时间推迟到了2013年。

paras.en: It wasn’t just the smoke system; many other major problems subsequently emerged.
paras.zh: 不只是排烟系统，后来还出现了许多其他重大问题。

paras.en: More than 90 meters of cable were incorrectly installed, 4000 doors were wrongly numbered.
paras.zh: 有90多米长的电缆没有正确安装；还有4000扇门的编号标错了。

paras.en: Escalators were too short, and there was a shortage of check-in desks.
paras.zh: 自动扶梯太短，值机柜台也不够。

paras.en: So why, with so many problems discovered, didn’t the airport corporation decide to give up on the project and start over?
paras.zh: 那么，发现了这么多问题，机场公司为什么不决定放弃这个项目、从头再来呢？

paras.en: The reason is simple: people are often hesitant to terminate a project when they’ve already invested time or resources into it, even if it might make logical sense to do so.
paras.zh: 原因很简单：人们在一个项目上已经投入了时间或资源后，往往不愿意终止它，即使终止在逻辑上说得通。

paras.en: The longer the delays continued, the more problems inspectors found.
paras.zh: 延误持续得越久，检查人员发现的问题就越多。

paras.en: Leadership of the planning corporation has changed hands nearly as many times as the opening date has been pushed back.
paras.zh: 规划公司换领导的次数，差不多和开放日期推迟的次数一样多。

paras.en: Initially, rather than appointing a general contractor to run the project, the corporation decided to manage it themselves, despite lack of experience with an undertaking of that scale.
paras.zh: 一开始，公司没有指定总承包商来负责这个项目，而是决定自己管理，尽管他们缺乏做这么大规模工程的经验。

paras.en: To compound the delays, the unused airport is resulting in massive costs.
paras.zh: 让延误雪上加霜的是，这座闲置的机场还造成了巨额开支。

paras.en: Every month it remains unopened costs between nine and 10 million euros.
paras.zh: 它每闲置一个月，就要花掉九百万到一千万欧元。

paras.en: Assuming all goes well, the airport should open in October 2020, but the still empty airport stands as the biggest embarrassment to Germany’s reputation for efficiency, and a continuing drain on city and state resources.
paras.zh: 如果一切顺利，机场应该会在2020年10月开放，但这座至今仍空着的机场，是德国“高效”名声的最大耻辱，也在不断耗费市里和州里的资源。

w.m: n. 尴尬；令人难堪的事

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker say about the dream airport in Berlin?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于柏林的“梦想机场”，讲话者说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: Why was there a need for a new airport in Berlin?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：柏林为什么需要一座新机场？

paras.en: Question 24: Why did Berlin postpone the opening of its dream airport again and again?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：柏林为什么一再推迟“梦想机场”的开放？

paras.en: Question 25: What happens while the airport remains unused?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：机场闲置期间会发生什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2020年9月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2020年9月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，牛津大学物理学教授谈到自己为什么精力充沛、教学怎样加深她对科学的理解，以及大量数据还没人分析，新的科学发现就藏在其中。第二段长对话里，两人谈梦有没有特殊含义：女士讲了迷信的奶奶因为一个梦改签航班的事，又谈到心理学家怎样解释梦。第一篇短文介绍南极冰层下的沃斯托克湖，以及科学家打算用机器人在湖里寻找生命。第二篇短文讲语言学家詹姆斯·科普兰研究墨西哥塔拉乌马拉部落的经历和收获。第一段录音为“激进分子”正名：他们是推动社会变革的人。第二段录音讲人很容易受身边的人影响，所以要谨慎选择交往的人。第三段录音介绍美元钞票的特点和美国纸币的历史。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two: Listening Comprehension, Section A: Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one: You are a professor of physics at the University of Oxford.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。您是牛津大学的物理学教授。

paras.en: You’re a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research.
paras.zh: 您还担任欧洲核子研究组织的高级顾问。

paras.en: You also seem to tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks, and in addition, you have your own weekly TV show on science.
paras.zh: 您好像还不知疲倦地到世界各地巡回演讲，而且您还有自己的科学电视节目，每周播出。

paras.en: Where do you get the energy?
paras.zh: 您哪来这么多精力？

paras.en: Oh well, I just love what I do.
paras.zh: 哦，我就是热爱自己的工作。

paras.en: I’m extremely fortunate to have this life doing what I love doing, Professor.
paras.zh: 能过上这样的生活，做自己喜欢的事，我真是太幸运了，教授。

paras.en: What exactly is your goal?
paras.zh: 您的目标到底是什么？

paras.en: Why do you do all of this?
paras.zh: 您做这一切是为了什么？

paras.en: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on, but these I think can be divided into two groups: the education of science and the further understanding of science.
paras.zh: 嗯，正如您所说，我确实同时在忙好几件事，不过我觉得可以分成两类：科学教育和对科学的深入认识。

w.m: adj. 进一步的；更深入的

paras.en: Don’t these two things get in the way of each other?
paras.zh: 这两件事不会互相妨碍吗？

paras.en: What I mean is, doesn’t giving lectures take time away from the lab?
paras.zh: 我的意思是，讲课不会占用您做实验的时间吗？

paras.en: Not really.
paras.zh: 不太会。

paras.en: No, I love teaching, and I don’t mind spending more time doing that now than in the past.
paras.zh: 不会，我热爱教学，也不介意现在比过去花更多时间在这上面。

paras.en: Also, what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself.
paras.zh: 另外我想说的是，教一门学科也能让我自己理解得更透彻。

paras.en: I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly, when I have to aid others in understanding it, and when I have to answer questions about it.
paras.zh: 我发现，当我必须把一件事讲清楚、帮别人弄懂它、回答有关它的问题时，我自己的知识也会更深入。

paras.en: Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating for anyone, no matter how much expertise they may already have in the field they are instructing.
paras.zh: 高水平的教学对任何人都很有启发，不管他们在自己所教的领域已经有多深的专业造诣。

w.m: adj. 有启发的；激励人的

paras.en: Are there any scientific breakthroughs that you see on the near horizon?
paras.zh: 您觉得近期会有什么科学突破吗？

paras.en: A significant discovery or invention we can expect soon.
paras.zh: 就是我们很快就能看到的重大发现或发明。

paras.en: The world is always conducting science, and there are constantly new things being discovered.
paras.zh: 世界上一直都在进行科学研究，新东西也在不断被发现。

paras.en: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers.
paras.zh: 事实上，现在电脑里积压的数据太多了。

paras.en: For example, we have thousands of photos of planet Mars taken by telescopes that nobody has ever seen.
paras.zh: 比如，我们有成千上万张望远镜拍下的火星照片，至今没人看过。

paras.en: We have them, yet nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them.
paras.zh: 照片就在那儿，可是谁都没时间亲眼看一看，更别说分析了。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: Why does the woman say she can be so energetic?
paras.zh: 第一题：女士说她为什么能这么精力充沛？

paras.en: Question two: What has the woman been engaged in?
paras.zh: 第二题：女士一直在从事什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman say about the benefit teaching brings to her?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于教学给自己带来的好处，女士是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question four: How does the woman say new scientific breakthroughs can be made possible?
paras.zh: 第四题：女士说怎样才能有新的科学突破？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
paras.zh: 你觉得梦有特殊含义吗？

paras.en: No, I don’t think they do.
paras.zh: 不，我觉得没有。

paras.en: I don’t either, but some people do.
paras.zh: 我也不觉得，不过有些人觉得有。

paras.en: I would say people who believe that dreams have special meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays.
paras.zh: 我得说，相信梦有特殊含义的人都很迷信，现在尤其如此。

paras.en: In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece, or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future.
paras.zh: 过去，在古埃及、古希腊或古代中国，人们曾相信梦能预见未来。

paras.en: But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it’s much harder to believe in these sorts of things.
paras.zh: 可如今我们有了这么多科学知识，我觉得这类东西就很难让人相信了。

paras.en: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future.
paras.zh: 我奶奶就很迷信，她认为梦能预测未来。

paras.en: Once she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed.
paras.zh: 有一次，她梦见自己第二天要坐的航班坠毁了。

paras.en: Can you guess what she did?
paras.zh: 你猜她怎么做的？

paras.en: She didn’t take that flight.
paras.zh: 她没坐那趟航班。

paras.en: She didn’t even bother to go to the airport the following day.
paras.zh: 第二天她连机场都没去。

paras.en: Instead, she took the same flight, but a week later, and everything was fine.
paras.zh: 她改坐了一周后的同一趟航班，结果一切正常。

paras.en: Of course, no plane ever crashed.
paras.zh: 当然，根本没有飞机坠毁。

paras.en: How funny!
paras.zh: 真好笑！

paras.en: Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport?
paras.zh: 你知道吗，坐飞机其实比其他任何交通方式都安全。

paras.en: It’s been statistically proven.
paras.zh: 这是有统计数据证明的。

w.m: adv. 从统计上；统计学上

paras.en: People can be so irrational sometimes.
paras.zh: 人有时候就是这么不理性。

w.m: adj. 不理性的；不合理的

paras.en: Yes, absolutely.
paras.zh: 是啊，完全正确。

paras.en: But even if we think they are ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking.
paras.zh: 不过，即使我们觉得情绪很荒唐，它的力量也和理性思考一样强大。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings.
paras.zh: 人们会因为一些不理性的感受做出各种疯狂的事。

paras.en: But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day.
paras.zh: 但事实上，有些心理学家认为，梦是我们当天的情绪和记忆造成的。

paras.en: I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children’s dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wished would happen.
paras.zh: 我记得是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德说过，孩子的梦通常是他们愿望的简单呈现，也就是他们希望发生的事。

paras.en: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments.
paras.zh: 但成年人的梦要复杂得多，反映的是他们更微妙的情感。

paras.en: Isn’t it interesting how psychologists try to understand using the scientific method something as bizarre as dreams?
paras.zh: 心理学家想用科学方法去理解梦这么离奇的东西，是不是很有意思？

paras.en: Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings.
paras.zh: 心理学就像是用理性去研究不理性的情感。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do both speakers think of dreams?
paras.zh: 第五题：两位说话人对梦怎么看？

paras.en: Question six: Why didn’t the woman’s grandmother take her scheduled flight?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士的奶奶为什么没坐原定的航班？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the woman say about people’s emotions?
paras.zh: 第七题：关于人的情绪，女士是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question eight: What did psychologist Sigmund Freud say about adults’ dreams?
paras.zh: 第八题：关于成年人的梦，心理学家西格蒙德·弗洛伊德是怎么说的？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometers beneath the ice pack.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。一些科学家在考察南极洲的地表，另一些则在深入研究冰层下四公里处的一个巨大水体。

paras.en: Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice.
paras.zh: 20世纪70年代，科学家利用能穿透冰层的无线电波，首次发现了沃斯托克湖。

paras.en: Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water.
paras.zh: 从那以后，他们用声波甚至卫星来绘制这片巨大水域的地图。

paras.en: How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet?
paras.zh: 沃斯托克湖的水在冰盖下面怎么能保持液态呢？

paras.en: The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing, says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales.
paras.zh: 威尔士大学的冰川学家马丁·西格特说，上面厚厚的冰川就像一条保温毯，让湖水不会结冰。

paras.en: In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the Earth may warm the hidden lake.
paras.zh: 此外，来自地球深处的地热也可能让这个隐藏的湖保持温暖。

paras.en: The scientists suspect that microorganisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than 2 million years.
paras.zh: 科学家推测，沃斯托克湖里可能生活着微生物，它们与外界隔绝了两百多万年。

paras.en: Anything found there will be totally alien to what’s on the surface of the Earth, says Siegert.
paras.zh: 西格特说，在那里发现的任何东西，都会和地球表面的东西完全不同。

w.m: adj. 陌生的；完全不同的

paras.en: Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination.
paras.zh: 科学家正在想办法钻透冰层、提取水样，同时又不造成污染。

paras.en: Again, robots might be the solution.
paras.zh: 而这一次，办法可能又是机器人。

paras.en: If all goes as planned, a drill-shaped robot will melt through the surface ice.
paras.zh: 如果一切按计划进行，一个钻头形状的机器人会融穿表层的冰。

paras.en: When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life.
paras.zh: 它到达湖里后，会放出另一个机器人，这个机器人能在湖里游动、拍照、寻找生命迹象。

paras.en: The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and airless conditions.
paras.zh: 科学家希望他们的发现能帮助揭示外太空的生命，那里的生命可能也生存在类似的黑暗、没有空气的环境里。

paras.en: Recently, close-up pictures of Jupiter’s moon Europa showed signs of water beneath its icy surface.
paras.zh: 最近，木星的卫星木卫二的近距离照片显示，它冰冷的表面下有水的迹象。

paras.en: Once tested in Antarctica, robots could be sent to Europa to search for life there too.
paras.zh: 机器人一旦在南极洲测试成功，就可以被送往木卫二，也去那里寻找生命。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What did scientists first use to discover Lake Vostok in the 1970s?
paras.zh: 第九题：20世纪70年代，科学家最初是用什么发现沃斯托克湖的？

paras.en: Question 10: What do scientists think about Lake Vostok?
paras.zh: 第十题：科学家对沃斯托克湖有什么看法？

paras.en: Question 11: What do the scientists hope their discoveries will do?
paras.zh: 第十一题：科学家希望他们的发现能起到什么作用？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: The idea to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras came to James Copeland in 1984 when he discovered that very little research had been done on their language.
paras.zh: 1984年，詹姆斯·科普兰发现几乎没有人研究过美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人的语言，于是有了研究这个部落的想法。

paras.en: He contacted a tribe member through a social worker, who worked with the tribesmen in Mexico.
paras.zh: 他通过一位社工联系上了一名部落成员，这位社工在墨西哥专门和这些部落的人打交道。

paras.en: At first, the tribe member named Gonzalez was very reluctant to cooperate.
paras.zh: 起初，这位名叫冈萨雷斯的部落成员很不愿意合作。

paras.en: He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language, but after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzalez agreed to help.
paras.zh: 他对科普兰说，多少钱也买不走他的语言。但科普兰向他说明了自己打算用这项研究做什么、会给塔拉乌马拉人带来什么好处，之后冈萨雷斯就同意帮忙了。

paras.en: He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary.
paras.zh: 他带科普兰去了自己的村子，还充当中间人。

paras.en: Copeland says, thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us.
paras.zh: 科普兰说，多亏了他，塔拉乌马拉人才明白我们来做什么，开始信任我们。

paras.en: Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland.
paras.zh: 对科普兰来说，走进塔拉乌马拉人的世界是一项艰辛的工作。

paras.en: To reach their homeland, he must drive two and a half days from Houston, Texas.
paras.zh: 要到他们的家园，他得从得克萨斯州的休斯敦开两天半的车。

paras.en: He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can’t easily get and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship.
paras.zh: 他在车里装满部落成员不容易弄到的物品，送给他们，表示友好。

paras.en: The Tarahumaras, who don’t believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves.
paras.zh: 塔拉乌马拉人不看重积累财富，他们收下食物后，大家会一起分享。

paras.en: For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, but also has enriched his life in several ways.
paras.zh: 对科普兰来说，这段经历不仅在学术上让他很有收获，还在好几个方面丰富了他的人生。

paras.en: I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the Western tradition.
paras.zh: 我看到人们拒绝科技，过着非常艰苦的传统生活，这让我对西方传统里所说的进步有了另一种理解。

paras.en: He says, “I experience the simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about.
paras.zh: 他说：“我体验到了生活在大自然中的那种简单，要不是这样，我只能在书上读到。

paras.en: I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other.
paras.zh: 他们乐于分享、彼此关心，我从中看到了很多美好的东西。”

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Why did James Copeland want to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras?
paras.zh: 第十二题：詹姆斯·科普兰为什么想研究美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人？

paras.en: Question 13: How did Gonzalez help James Copeland?
paras.zh: 第十三题：冈萨雷斯是怎样帮助詹姆斯·科普兰的？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the speaker say about James Copeland’s trip to the Tarahumaras village?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于詹姆斯·科普兰去塔拉乌马拉人村子的路程，说话人是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 15: What impresses James Copeland about the Tarahumaras tribe?
paras.zh: 第十五题：塔拉乌马拉部落的什么让詹姆斯·科普兰印象深刻？
