paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: What is a radical?
paras.zh: 什么是激进分子？

paras.en: It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them, accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs and, more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white males in Western society, feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon.
paras.zh: 如今人们似乎都害怕这个词，尤其害怕被贴上这个标签。指责某些人或某些群体激进，往往能迫使他们沉默、屈服，从而维持现状，更重要的是，维护少数特定人群的权力，在西方社会，这些人大多是富有的白人男性。女权主义就是这一现象的绝佳例子。

paras.en: The women’s movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man-hating and radicalism.
paras.zh: 女权运动一直饱受刻板印象、媒体歪曲以及“仇视男性”“激进主义”等指责的困扰。

paras.en: When the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life.
paras.zh: 可女权主义的根本基础其实很简单，就是女性在生活的方方面面都应享有平等的权利。

paras.en: When faced with the threat of being labeled radical, women back down from their worthy cause and consequently participate in their own oppression.
paras.zh: 一旦面临被贴上“激进”标签的威胁，女性就会从自己正当的事业中退缩，结果反倒参与了对自己的压迫。

paras.en: It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word, if people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power.
paras.zh: 事情已经到了这种地步：因为“女权主义者”这个词背着污名，很多女性都不敢自称女权主义者。如果人们拒绝被污名控制和恐吓，污名就会失去全部力量。

paras.en: Without fear on which to feed, such stigmas can only die.
paras.zh: 没有了赖以滋长的恐惧，这样的污名只能消亡。

paras.en: To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm or advocates a change in the existing state of affairs.
paras.zh: 在我看来，激进分子不过是反抗常规或主张改变现状的人。

paras.en: On closer inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity.
paras.zh: 仔细一看就会发现，常态一直在变化，因此并不是一成不变的东西。

paras.en: So why then is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation.
paras.zh: 那么，既然现状本身就不稳定、总在不停地变化，为什么偏离现状会被看成这么大的威胁呢？

paras.en: It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the rise of those who don’t.
paras.zh: 说到底，这都是为了维护掌权者的权力，阻止没有权力的人崛起。

paras.en: In fact, when we look at the word radical in a historical context, nearly every figure we now hold up as a hero was considered a radical in his or her time.
paras.zh: 事实上，如果我们从历史的角度来看“激进分子”这个词，如今被我们奉为英雄的人物，几乎每一位在他或她那个时代都被看作激进分子。

paras.en: Radicals are people who effect change.
paras.zh: 激进分子是带来变革的人。

paras.en: They are the people about whom history is written.
paras.zh: 历史写的就是他们这些人。

paras.en: Abolitionists were radicals.
paras.zh: 废奴主义者是激进分子。

paras.en: Civil rights activists were radicals.
paras.zh: 民权运动人士是激进分子。

paras.en: Even the founders of our country, in their fight to win independence from England were radicals.
paras.zh: 就连我们国家的开国元勋，在为脱离英国、争取独立而战的时候，也是激进分子。

paras.en: Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed.
paras.zh: 他们在历史上的出现改变了我们社会的运作方式，主要是改变了原有的权力平衡。

paras.en: Of course, there are some radicals who have made a negative impact on humanity, but undeniably there would simply be no progress without radicals.
paras.zh: 当然，有些激进分子给人类带来了负面影响，但不可否认，没有激进分子就根本不会有进步。

paras.en: That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride.
paras.zh: 话虽如此，下次再有人说我是激进分子，我会自豪地接受这个标签。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What usually happens when people are accused of being radical?
paras.zh: 第十六题：人们被指责激进时，通常会发生什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What is the speaker’s definition of a radical?
paras.zh: 第十七题：说话人怎样定义激进分子？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker think of most radicals in the American history?
paras.zh: 第十八题：说话人怎么看美国历史上的大多数激进分子？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: We are very susceptible to the influence of the people around us.
paras.zh: 我们非常容易受身边人的影响。

paras.en: For instance, you may have known somebody who has gone overseas for a year or so, and has returned with an accent.
paras.zh: 比如，你也许认识这样的人：出国待了一年左右，回来就带上了口音。

paras.en: Perhaps we become part of our immediate environment.
paras.zh: 也许我们会成为身边环境的一部分。

paras.en: None of us are immune to the influences of our own world, and let us not kid ourselves that we are untouched by the things and the people in our life.
paras.zh: 我们谁都免不了受自己周围世界的影响，别自欺欺人，以为自己不受生活中的人和事影响。

w.m: adj. 不受影响的；免疫的

paras.en: Fred goes off to his new job at a factory, Fred takes his 10-minute coffee break, but the other workers take a half an hour.
paras.zh: 弗雷德去一家工厂上新班。他只休十分钟的咖啡时间，其他工人却休半个小时。

paras.en: Fred says, “What’s the matter with you guys?”
paras.zh: 弗雷德说：“你们这些人怎么回事？”

paras.en: Two weeks later, Fred is taking 20-minute breaks.
paras.zh: 两周后，弗雷德休息二十分钟了。

paras.en: A month later, Fred takes his half hour.
paras.zh: 一个月后，弗雷德也休半个小时了。

paras.en: Fred is saying, “If you can’t beat them, join them.”
paras.zh: 弗雷德说：“既然打不过他们那就加入他们。

paras.en: Why should I work any harder than the next guy?
paras.zh: 我凭什么要比别人干得更卖力？”

paras.en: The fascinating thing about being human is that generally we are unaware that there are changes taking place in our mentality.
paras.zh: 身为人类，有一点很有意思：我们通常意识不到自己的心态正在发生变化。

w.m: adj. 迷人的；很有意思的

paras.en: It is like returning to the city smog after some weeks in the fresh air.
paras.zh: 这就像在空气清新的地方待了几周，再回到烟雾弥漫的城市。

paras.en: Only then do we realize that we have become accustomed to the nasty smells, mix with critical people and we learn to criticize, mix with happy people and we learn about happiness.
paras.zh: 只有到那时，我们才发现自己已经习惯了难闻的气味。和爱挑剔的人在一起，我们就学会了挑剔；和快乐的人在一起，我们就懂得了快乐。

w.m: adj. 难闻的；令人厌恶的

paras.en: What this means is that we need to decide what we want from life and then choose our company accordingly.
paras.zh: 这意味着，我们要决定自己想从生活中得到什么，然后据此选择交往的人。

paras.en: You may well say that is going to take some effort.
paras.zh: 你很可能会说，这得费点力气。

paras.en: It may not be comfortable.
paras.zh: 这么做可能不太舒服。

paras.en: I may offend some of my present company, right?
paras.zh: 我可能会得罪现在交往的一些人，对吧？

paras.en: But it is your life.
paras.zh: 但这是你自己的人生。

paras.en: Fred may say, “I’m always broke, frequently depressed.
paras.zh: 弗雷德可能会说：“我总是没钱，经常情绪低落。

w.m: adj. 沮丧的；情绪低落的

paras.en: I’m going nowhere, and I never do anything exciting.”
paras.zh: 我一事无成，也从来没做过什么让人兴奋的事。”

paras.en: Then we discover that Fred’s best friends are always broke, frequently depressed, going nowhere, and wishing that life was more exciting.
paras.zh: 然后我们发现，弗雷德最好的朋友们也总是没钱、经常情绪低落、一事无成，还盼着生活能更刺激一些。

w.m: adj. 沮丧的；情绪低落的

paras.en: This is not coincidence, nor is it our business to stand in judgment of Fred.
paras.zh: 这不是巧合，我们也没资格对弗雷德评头论足。

paras.en: However, if Fred ever wants to improve his quality of life, the first thing he’ll need to do is recognize what has been going on all these years, it’s no surprise that doctors, as a profession, suffer a lot of ill health because they spend their lives around sick people.
paras.zh: 不过，如果弗雷德想提高自己的生活质量，他首先要做的就是认清这些年来到底发生了什么。医生这一行的人健康状况普遍不好，这不奇怪，因为他们一辈子都和病人打交道。

paras.en: Psychiatrists have a higher incidence of suicide in their profession for related reasons.
paras.zh: 出于相关的原因，精神科医生这一行的自杀率更高。

paras.en: Traditionally, nine out of 10 children whose parents smoke smoke themselves.
paras.zh: 一直以来，父母吸烟的孩子，十个里有九个自己也吸烟。

paras.en: Obesity is in part an environmental problem.
paras.zh: 肥胖在一定程度上是环境造成的问题。

paras.en: Successful people have successful friends, and so the story goes on.
paras.zh: 成功的人交的也是成功的朋友，诸如此类。

w.m: 诸如此类；情况就是这样

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about us as human beings?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于我们人类，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the speaker say Fred should do first to improve his quality of life?
paras.zh: 第二十题：说话人说，弗雷德要提高生活质量，首先应该做什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say about psychiatrists?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于精神科医生，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Virtually every American can recognize a dollar bill at a mere glance.
paras.zh: 几乎每个美国人只要看一眼就能认出一美元钞票。

paras.en: Many can identify it by its sound or texture, but few people indeed can accurately describe the world’s most powerful, important currency.
paras.zh: 很多人能凭声音或手感认出它，但能准确描述这种世界上最强大、最重要的货币的人确实寥寥无几。

paras.en: The American dollar bill is colored with black ink on one side and green on the other.
paras.zh: 美元钞票一面用的是黑色油墨，另一面是绿色。

paras.en: The exact composition of the paper and ink is a closely guarded government secret.
paras.zh: 纸张和油墨的确切成分是政府严加保守的秘密。

paras.en: Despite its weighty importance, the dollar bill actually weighs little.
paras.zh: 尽管美元钞票地位举足轻重，它本身其实很轻。

paras.en: It requires nearly 500 bills to tip the scales at a pound.
paras.zh: 将近五百张钞票才有一磅重。

paras.en: Not only is the dollar bill lightweight, but it also has a brief lifespan.
paras.zh: 美元钞票不仅很轻，寿命也很短。

paras.en: Few dollar bills survive longer than 18 months.
paras.zh: 很少有美元钞票能用过十八个月。

paras.en: The word dollar is taken from the German word thaler, the name for the world’s most important currency in the 16th century.
paras.zh: “美元”这个词来自德语单词“塔勒”，它是16世纪世界上最重要的货币的名称。

w.m: n. 塔勒（旧时德国银币）

paras.en: The thaler was a silver coin first minted in 1518 under the reign of Charles V, Emperor of Germany, the concept of paper money is a relatively recent innovation in the history of American currency.
paras.zh: 塔勒是一种银币，1518年德国皇帝查理五世在位时首次铸造。纸币这个概念，在美国货币史上算是比较新的事物。

w.m: n. 塔勒（旧时德国银币）

paras.en: When the Constitution was signed, people had little regard for paper money because of its steadily decreasing value during the colonial era.
paras.zh: 美国宪法签署时，人们并不看重纸币，因为殖民时期纸币一直在不断贬值。

paras.en: Because of this lack of faith, the new American government minted only coins for common currency.
paras.zh: 由于缺乏信任，新成立的美国政府只铸造硬币作为通用货币。

paras.en: Interest-bearing banknotes were issued at the same time, but their purpose was limited to providing money for urgent government crises, such as American involvement in the War of 1812.
paras.zh: 当时也发行过有息银行券，但用途仅限于为政府应对紧急危机筹钱，比如美国参与1812年战争。

paras.en: The first non-interest-bearing paper currency was authorized by Congress in 1862, at the height of the Civil War.
paras.zh: 1862年，正值南北战争最激烈的时候，国会批准发行了第一种无息纸币。

paras.en: At this point, citizens’ old fears of devalued paper currency had calmed, and the dollar bill was born.
paras.zh: 这时，公民对纸币贬值的旧有担忧已经平息，美元钞票就此诞生。

paras.en: The new green-colored paper money quickly earned the nickname “greenback.”
paras.zh: 这种新的绿色纸币很快就得了个绰号，叫“绿背钞”。

paras.en: Today, the American dollar bill is a product of the Federal Reserve and is issued from the 12 Federal Reserve banks around the United States.
paras.zh: 如今，美元钞票由美联储负责，由遍布美国的12家联邦储备银行发行。

paras.en: The government keeps a steady supply of approximately 2 billion bills in circulation at all times.
paras.zh: 政府始终保持着约20亿张钞票的稳定流通量。

paras.en: Controversy continues to surround the true value of the dollar bill, American history has seen generations of politicians argue in favor of a gold standard for American currency.
paras.zh: 围绕美元钞票真正价值的争议一直没有停止。美国历史上，一代又一代的政客都主张美国货币采用金本位制。

paras.en: However, for the present, the American dollar bill holds the value that is printed on it and little more.
paras.zh: 不过，就目前而言，美元钞票的价值就是上面印的面值，仅此而已。

paras.en: The only other guarantee on the bill is a Federal Reserve pledge as a confirmation in the form of government securities.
paras.zh: 钞票上唯一的另一项保证，是美联储以政府债券的形式作出的确认承诺。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker say about the American dollar bill?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于美元钞票，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the speaker say about the exact composition of the American dollar bill?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于美元钞票的确切成分，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: Why did the new American government mint only coins for common currency?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：新成立的美国政府为什么只铸造硬币作为通用货币？

paras.en: Question 25: What have generations of American politicians argued for?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：一代又一代的美国政客主张什么？

paras.en: This is the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.name: 2020年12月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，威尔逊小姐打电话给保险公司投诉：家里被洪水淹了，保险公司却以她漏缴一个月保费为由拒绝理赔，她气得扬言要起诉。第二段长对话里，一男一女争论人工智能的未来：女士很乐观，男士则担心人工智能会让工作失去意义，甚至取代人类。第一篇短文讲年轻人怎样存钱、怎样安排存下的钱，才能在经济上有保障。第二篇短文里，一位做广告的女士讲自己怎样给自己定一套“制服”，并建议在看重形象的世界里，穿着不妨稳妥一些。第一段录音提倡少买东西、住小空间，过一种“删减过”的简单生活。第二段录音介绍一项研究：人们有时会为了显得诚实而撒谎，哪怕自己吃亏。第三段录音分析老年人为什么不喜欢新音乐。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Good morning, Safe House Insurance.
paras.zh: 早上好，这里是安居保险公司。

paras.en: My name is Paul.
paras.zh: 我叫保罗。

paras.en: How can I help you today?
paras.zh: 今天有什么可以帮您的吗？

paras.en: Morning.
paras.zh: 早上好。

paras.en: I wouldn’t say that is good from where I am standing.
paras.zh: 照我现在的处境，我可不觉得有什么好的。

paras.en: This is Miss Wilson, and this is the third time I’ve called this week since receiving your letter about our insurance claim.
paras.zh: 我是威尔逊小姐，自从收到你们那封关于我们保险索赔的信以来，这已经是我这周第三次打电话了。

paras.en: I’m getting a little fed up with my calls about my claim being completely disregarded.
paras.zh: 我为索赔的事打了几次电话，全都被当成耳旁风，我有点受够了。威尔逊小姐，

paras.en: Miss Wilson, thank you for calling back.
paras.zh: 谢谢您再次来电。

paras.en: Can I take some details to help me look at your claim?
paras.zh: 我可以记一下详细情况，帮您查查索赔的事吗？

paras.en: It’s Miss May Wilson of 15 South Sea Road in Cornwall, and the details are that our village was extensively flooded two months ago.
paras.zh: 我是康沃尔南海路15号的梅·威尔逊小姐，详细情况是：两个月前，我们村子大面积被淹。

paras.en: The entire ground floor of our cottage was submerged in water, and five of us have been living in a caravan ever since.
paras.zh: 我们小屋的整个一楼都泡在水里，从那以后，我们一家五口一直住在房车里。

paras.en: You people are still withholding the money we are entitled to over a bizarre technical detail, and it’s not acceptable, Paul.
paras.zh: 你们这些人还在因为一个莫名其妙的技术细节，扣着我们应得的钱不给，这让人无法接受，保罗。

w.m: adj. 离奇的；莫名其妙的

paras.en: Miss Wilson, according to the notes on your account, the bizarre technical detail that you mentioned refers to the fact that you hadn’t paid house insurance the month before the incident.
paras.zh: 威尔逊小姐，根据您账户上的记录，您说的那个莫名其妙的技术细节，指的是出事前一个月您没有缴房屋保险费。

w.m: adj. 离奇的；莫名其妙的

paras.en: That money left our account, and now that you should be paying out, you are suddenly saying that you didn’t receive it on time.
paras.zh: 那笔钱已经从我们账户上扣走了，现在该你们赔钱了，你们却突然说没有按时收到。

paras.en: I’m really skeptical about this claim.
paras.zh: 你们这种说法我实在不敢相信。

paras.en: The contract does say that any missed payment in a year will affect the terms and conditions of the insurance contract and may affect claims.
paras.zh: 合同上确实写着，一年里只要漏缴一次，就会影响保险合同的条款，还可能影响理赔。

paras.en: Of course, I can pass you on to my manager to talk to you more about this.
paras.zh: 当然，我可以帮您转给我们经理，让他跟您细谈。

paras.en: I’ve already spoken to him, and you can tell him I’m furious now, and that your company has a lawsuit on its hands, you will be hearing from my lawyer.
paras.zh: 我已经跟他谈过了，你可以告诉他，我现在非常生气，你们公司要吃官司了，我的律师会联系你们的。

paras.en: Goodbye.
paras.zh: 再见。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What is the woman complaining about?
paras.zh: 第一题：女士在投诉什么？

paras.en: Question two: What is the problem the woman’s family encountered?
paras.zh: 第二题：女士一家遇到了什么问题？

paras.en: Question three: What has caused the so-called bizarre technical detail, according to the man?
paras.zh: 第三题：根据男士所说，所谓莫名其妙的技术细节是由什么造成的？

w.m: adj. 离奇的；莫名其妙的

paras.en: Question four: What does the woman say she will do at the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第四题：对话快结束时，女士说她要做什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: How do you feel about the future of artificial intelligence?
paras.zh: 你怎么看人工智能的未来？

paras.en: Personally, I feel quite optimistic about it.
paras.zh: 我个人对它相当乐观。

paras.en: AI, I’m not so optimistic actually.
paras.zh: 啊，其实我可没那么乐观。

paras.en: In fact, it’s something we should be concerned about.
paras.zh: 事实上，这是我们应该担心的事。

paras.en: Well, it will help us humans understand ourselves better, and when we have a better understanding of ourselves, we can improve the world.
paras.zh: 嗯，它能帮我们人类更好地了解自己，而我们更了解自己之后，就能让世界变得更好。

paras.en: Well, one thing is for sure: technology is evolving faster than our ability to understand it, and in the future, AI will make jobs kind of pointless.
paras.zh: 嗯，有一点是肯定的：技术发展的速度比我们理解它的能力更快，将来人工智能会让工作变得有点没意义。

paras.en: I think artificial intelligence will actually help create new kinds of jobs, which would require less of our time and allow us to be centered on creative tasks.
paras.zh: 我觉得人工智能其实会帮着创造出新的工作，这些工作占用我们的时间更少，能让我们专心做有创造性的事。

paras.en: I doubt that very much.
paras.zh: 我非常怀疑。

paras.en: Probably the last job that will remain will be writing AI software, and then eventually, AI will just write its own software.
paras.zh: 最后剩下的工作可能就是编写人工智能软件了，再往后，人工智能干脆会自己写软件。

paras.en: At that time, we are going to have a lot of jobs which nobody will want to do.
paras.zh: 到那时，会有很多谁都不愿意干的活儿。

paras.en: So we’ll need artificial intelligence for the robots to take care of the old guys like us.
paras.zh: 所以我们需要人工智能，让机器人来照顾像我们这样的老家伙。

paras.en: I don’t know.
paras.zh: 我说不好。

paras.en: There’s a risk that human civilization could be replaced by a superior type of digital life.
paras.zh: 人类文明有可能被一种更高级的数字生命取代。

w.m: adj. 更高级的；更优越的

paras.en: AI will be able to completely simulate a person in every way possible.
paras.zh: 人工智能将能够完全在各个方面模拟一个人。

paras.en: In fact, some people think we’re in a simulation right now.
paras.zh: 事实上，有些人认为我们现在就活在一场模拟里。

paras.en: That’s impossible.
paras.zh: 这不可能。

paras.en: Humans can’t even make a mosquito.
paras.zh: 人类连一只蚊子都造不出来。

paras.en: Computers only have chips.
paras.zh: 电脑只有芯片。

paras.en: People have brains, and that’s where the wisdom comes from.
paras.zh: 人有大脑，智慧就是从大脑来的。

paras.en: Once it’s fully developed, AI will become tired of trying to communicate with humans, as we would be much slower thinkers in comparison.
paras.zh: 人工智能一旦发展成熟，就会厌倦和人类交流，因为相比之下，我们思考起来要慢得多。

paras.en: I’m not so sure.
paras.zh: 我可没那么肯定。

paras.en: A computer is a computer, and a computer is just a toy.
paras.zh: 电脑就是电脑，电脑只是个玩具。

paras.en: Computers can easily communicate incredibly fast, so the computer will just get impatient talking to humans.
paras.zh: 电脑之间轻轻松松就能以极快的速度交流，所以电脑跟人类说话时会不耐烦的。

paras.en: It’ll be barely getting any information out.
paras.zh: 它几乎什么信息都得不到。

paras.en: Well, I believe there’s a benevolent future with AI.
paras.zh: 嗯，我相信人工智能会带来一个美好的未来。

paras.en: I also think you watch too many science fiction films.
paras.zh: 我还觉得你科幻电影看得太多了。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about the speakers from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第五题：从对话中我们可以了解到两位说话人的什么情况？

paras.en: Question six: What will new kinds of jobs be like, according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第六题：根据女士所说，新型工作会是什么样子的？

paras.en: Question seven: What is the risk the man anticipates?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士预料到了什么风险？

paras.en: Question eight: What is the man’s concern about AI technology?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士对人工智能技术有什么担忧？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you’ll hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: To achieve financial security, how much you save is always more important than the amount you earn or how shrewdly you invest.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。要在经济上有保障，存多少钱永远比挣多少钱、投资多精明更重要。

paras.en: If you are under 30 years old, your goal should be to save 20% of your monthly income after tax deductions.
paras.zh: 如果你不到30岁，你的目标应该是把每月税后收入的20%存起来。

paras.en: This is irrespective of how much you earn.
paras.zh: 不管你挣多少钱，都是这样。

paras.en: Approximately 50% should be reserved for essentials like food and accommodation.
paras.zh: 大约50%应该留给食物和住宿这些必需开支。

paras.en: The remaining 30% is for recreation and entertainment.
paras.zh: 剩下的30%用于休闲娱乐。

paras.en: But for many young people, it’ll be difficult to designate such a large proportion of their income for savings.
paras.zh: 但对很多年轻人来说，要把收入的这么一大部分专门拿来存，是很难的。

paras.en: If you find it hard to save any money at all, start by cutting all unnecessary spending, allocate a tiny amount of one or 2% for savings, and gradually increase that amount.
paras.zh: 如果你觉得一分钱都很难存下来，那就先砍掉所有不必要的开支，拿出一两个百分点这样很小的一部分存起来，再逐步增加。

paras.en: Always keep that 20% goal in mind to prevent yourself from becoming complacent.
paras.zh: 一定要始终记着20%的目标，免得自己松懈下来。

paras.en: It can be challenging to stick to such a strict plan, but if you adopt the right mindset, you should be able to make it work for you.
paras.zh: 坚持这么严格的计划可能很难，但只要心态对了，你应该就能让它为你所用。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: So, what should you be doing with the money that you are saving?
paras.zh: 那么，存下来的钱该怎么处理呢？

paras.en: Some must be kept easily accessible in case you need some cash in an emergency.
paras.zh: 一部分钱一定要放在随时能取到的地方，以防遇到紧急情况需要现金。

w.m: adj. 可获得的；可取用的

paras.en: The largest proportion should be invested in retirement plans, either through your employer or privately, and you can keep some money for high-risk, but potentially lucrative investments.
paras.zh: 最大的一部分应该投进养老计划，可以通过雇主，也可以自己投；你还可以留一些钱，做高风险但可能收益丰厚的投资。

w.m: adj. 赚钱的；利润丰厚的

paras.en: Dividends can be reinvested or used to purchase something you like.
paras.zh: 分红可以再拿去投资，也可以用来买自己喜欢的东西。

paras.en: By following this plan, you should hopefully be able to enjoy your life now and still be financially secure in the future.
paras.zh: 按照这个计划做，你现在应该就能享受生活，将来经济上也有保障。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What are people under 30 advised to do to achieve financial security?
paras.zh: 第九题：为了在经济上有保障，建议30岁以下的人怎么做？

paras.en: Question 10: What should people do if they find it difficult to follow the speaker’s advice on their financial plan?
paras.zh: 第十题：如果人们觉得很难按照说话人在理财计划上的建议去做，该怎么办？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the speaker think is important for achieving financial security?
paras.zh: 第十一题：说话人认为什么对实现经济保障很重要？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: I work in advertising, and I like to keep up with current trends, mainly because I’m aware that we live in an image-obsessed world.
paras.zh: 我是做广告的，喜欢紧跟潮流，主要是因为我知道，我们生活在一个痴迷于形象的世界里。

paras.en: However, when I first started my job, occasionally I’d catch a glimpse of myself in the lifts and find myself thinking that I looked a total mess.
paras.zh: 不过，刚开始工作时，我偶尔在电梯里瞥见自己，会发现自己在想：我看上去真是一团糟。

paras.en: Was I being held back by my choice of clothing?
paras.zh: 是不是我选的衣服拖了我的后腿？

paras.en: The short answer is yes, especially when clients are quick to judge you on your style rather than your work.
paras.zh: 简单地说，是的，尤其是客户往往很快就根据你的打扮、而不是你的工作来评判你。

paras.en: But no one can be unique with their outfit every day.
paras.zh: 可是谁也不可能每天都穿得与众不同。

w.m: adj. 独特的；与众不同的

paras.en: I mean, that’s why uniforms were invented.
paras.zh: 我是说，这就是人们发明制服的原因。

paras.en: So here’s what I did: I created my own uniform.
paras.zh: 所以我是这么做的：我给自己定了一套制服。

paras.en: To do this, I chose an appropriate outfit.
paras.zh: 为此，我选了一套合适的衣服。

paras.en: Then I bought multiple items of the same style in different shades.
paras.zh: 然后我买了好几件款式相同、颜色深浅不同的衣服。

paras.en: Now I never worry about what I’m wearing in the morning, even if I do get a bit tired of just wearing the same classic pieces.
paras.zh: 现在我早上再也不用为穿什么发愁了，虽然老穿这几件经典款，确实有点腻。

paras.en: Overall, when it comes to work, you have to ask yourself: Would looking smarter enhance my ability to do my job?
paras.zh: 总之，说到工作，你得问问自己：穿得更体面些，会不会让我更能胜任工作？

w.m: adj. 衣着整洁的；体面的

paras.en: For some, this question may not be an issue at all, especially if you work remotely and rarely see your colleagues or clients face to face.
paras.zh: 对有些人来说，这根本不成问题，尤其是如果你远程办公，很少和同事或客户见面的话。

paras.en: But if your job involves interacting with other people, the answer to this is often yes.
paras.zh: 但如果你的工作需要和别人打交道，答案往往是肯定的。

paras.en: So rather than fighting the system, I think we should just do whatever helps us to achieve our goals at work.
paras.zh: 所以，与其和这套规则对着干，我觉得我们不如做一切有助于实现工作目标的事。

paras.en: If that means playing it safe with your image, then let’s face it, it’s probably worth it.
paras.zh: 如果这意味着在形象上求稳，那么说实话，这可能也是值得的。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard, Question 12: What do we learn about the speaker when she first started her job?
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。第十二题：说话人刚开始工作时，我们能了解到她的什么情况？

paras.en: Question 13: Why were uniforms invented, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十三题：根据说话人所说，人们为什么发明了制服？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the speaker say about looking smarter?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于穿得更体面，说话人是怎么说的？

w.m: adj. 衣着整洁的；体面的

paras.en: Question 15: What does the speaker advise people to do in an image-obsessed world?
paras.zh: 第十五题：在痴迷于形象的世界里，说话人建议人们怎么做？

paras.en: Section C, directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Did you know that Americans have approximately three times the amount of space we had 50 years ago?
paras.zh: 你知道吗？美国人现在拥有的空间，大约是我们50年前的三倍。

paras.en: Therefore, you’d think we’d have sufficient room for all of our possessions.
paras.zh: 所以你会觉得，我们应该有足够的地方放所有的东西。

paras.en: On the contrary, the personal storage business is now a growing industry.
paras.zh: 恰恰相反，个人仓储业如今是一个正在壮大的行业。

paras.en: We’ve got triple the space, but we’ve become such enthusiastic consumers that we require even more.
paras.zh: 我们的空间多了两倍，可我们成了狂热的消费者，以至于还需要更多空间。

paras.en: This phenomenon has resulted in significant credit card debt, enormous environmental footprints, and perhaps not coincidentally, our happiness levels have failed to increase over the same half century.
paras.zh: 这种现象导致了大量信用卡欠款、巨大的环境足迹，而且也许并非巧合的是，在这半个世纪里，我们的幸福感一直没有提升。

paras.en: I’m here to suggest an alternative: that having less might actually be a preferable decision.
paras.zh: 我在这里想提出另一种选择：拥有的东西少一些，也许其实是更好的决定。

w.m: n. 替代选择；另一种办法

paras.en: Many of us have experienced at some stage the pleasure of possessing less.
paras.zh: 我们很多人都在某个时候体会过东西少一点的快乐。

paras.en: I propose that less stuff and less space can not only help you economize but also simplify your life.
paras.zh: 我认为，东西少一点、空间小一点，不但能帮你省钱，还能让你的生活更简单。

paras.en: I recently started an innovative project to discover some creative solutions that offered me everything I required.
paras.zh: 我最近开始了一个创新项目，想找到一些有创意的办法，满足我的全部需要。

paras.en: By purchasing an apartment that was 40 square meters instead of 60, I immediately saved $200,000.
paras.zh: 我买了一套40平方米、而不是60平方米的公寓，一下子就省了20万美元。

paras.en: Smaller space leads to reduced utility bills and also a smaller carbon footprint, because it’s designed around an edited collection of possessions limited to my favorite stuff.
paras.zh: 空间小了，水电燃气费就少了，碳足迹也更小，因为整套房子是围绕一批精挑细选的物品设计的，只留下我最喜欢的东西。

paras.en: I’m really excited to live there.
paras.zh: 我真的很期待住在那里。

paras.en: How can we live more basically?
paras.zh: 我们怎样才能生活得更简单呢？

paras.en: Firstly, we must ruthlessly cut the unnecessary objects out of our lives.
paras.zh: 首先，我们必须毫不留情地把不必要的东西清出生活。

w.m: adv. 无情地；毫不留情地

paras.en: To stem consumption, we should think before we buy and ask ourselves: Will it truly make me happier?
paras.zh: 为了遏制消费，我们应该买东西之前先想一想，问问自己：它真的会让我更快乐吗？

paras.en: Obviously, we should possess some great stuff, but we want belongings that we’re going to love for years.
paras.zh: 当然，我们应该拥有一些好东西，但我们要的是能喜欢好几年的东西。

paras.en: Secondly, we require space efficiency.
paras.zh: 第二，我们需要高效利用空间。

paras.en: We want appliances that are designed for use most of the time, not for occasional use.
paras.zh: 我们需要的是大部分时间都会用的电器，而不是偶尔才用一次的。

paras.en: Why own a six-burner stove when you rarely use even three burners?
paras.zh: 你连三个灶眼都很少用，干吗要买一个六眼灶呢？

paras.en: Finally, we need multifunctional spaces and housewares.
paras.zh: 最后，我们需要多功能的空间和家居用品。

paras.en: I combined a movable wall with transforming furniture to get more out of my limited space.
paras.zh: 我把一面可移动的墙和可变形家具结合起来，让有限的空间发挥更大的作用。

paras.en: Consider my coffee table; it increases in size to accommodate 10.
paras.zh: 比如我的咖啡桌，它可以变大，坐得下10个人。

paras.en: My office is tucked away, easily hidden.
paras.zh: 我的办公区藏在一边，很容易收起来。

paras.en: My bed simply pops out of the wall.
paras.zh: 我的床直接从墙里弹出来。

paras.en: For guests, I can relocate the movable wall and utilize the foldable guest beds I installed.
paras.zh: 有客人来时，我可以挪开那面可移动的墙，用上我装好的折叠客床。

paras.en: I’m not saying we should all live in tiny apartments, but consider the benefits of an edited life.
paras.zh: 我不是说我们都该住小公寓，但想一想删繁就简的生活有什么好处吧。

paras.en: When you return home and walk through your front door, take a moment to ask yourselves: Could I do with a little life editing?
paras.zh: 当你回到家、走进家门的时候，花点时间问问自己：我是不是该给生活做点删减？

paras.en: Would that give me more freedom and more time.
paras.zh: 这会不会让我更自由、有更多时间？

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What has prevented Americans’ happiness levels from increasing?
paras.zh: 第十六题：是什么让美国人的幸福感没能提升？

paras.en: Question 17: What things should we possess according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十七题：根据说话人所说，我们应该拥有什么样的东西？

paras.en: Question 18: What do we learn about the items in the speaker’s home?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于说话人家里的物品，我们能了解到什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Now, believe it or not, people sometimes lie in order to maintain a good, honest reputation, even if it hurts them to do so.
paras.zh: 信不信由你，人们有时会为了维护好的、诚实的名声而撒谎，哪怕这么做对自己不利。

paras.en: At least this is what a team of scientists is suggesting, with evidence to prove it.
paras.zh: 至少，一组科学家是这么说的，而且他们有证据证明这一点。

paras.en: Picture this scenario: You often drive for work and can be compensated for up to 400 miles per month.
paras.zh: 想象一下这种情景：你经常开车出差，每月最多可以报销400英里的里程。

paras.en: Most people at your company drive about 300 miles each month, but this month you drove 400 miles.
paras.zh: 你们公司大多数人每月开大约300英里，但你这个月开了400英里。

paras.en: How many miles do you think you’d claim in your expense report?
paras.zh: 你觉得你会在报销单上报多少英里？

paras.en: The scientists asked this exact question as part of the study we’re discussing today, with surprising results.
paras.zh: 在我们今天要讨论的这项研究中，科学家就问了这个问题，结果出人意料。

paras.en: They found that 12 percent of respondents reported the distance they drove as less than the actual figure, giving an average answer of 384 miles.
paras.zh: 他们发现，12%的受访者报的里程比实际开的少，平均答案是384英里。

paras.en: In other words, they lied about the number of miles, even though they would forfeit money they were owed.
paras.zh: 换句话说，他们在里程上撒了谎，哪怕会因此拿不到本该给他们的钱。

paras.en: The researchers believe this was to seem honest, with the assumption being that others would be suspicious of a high expense claim.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，这样做是为了显得诚实，他们的设想是，报销金额高了，别人会起疑心。

paras.en: But why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment?
paras.zh: 可人们为什么要编造数字、让自己吃亏呢？

paras.en: The researchers explain that many people care a great deal about their reputation and how they’ll be judged by others.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说，很多人非常在乎自己的名声，在乎别人会怎么评价自己。

paras.en: If they care enough, their concern about appearing honest and not losing the respect of others may be greater than their desire to actually be honest.
paras.zh: 如果足够在乎，他们对显得诚实、不失去别人尊重的在意，可能会超过他们真正诚实的意愿。

paras.en: The researchers assert that the findings suggest that when people obtain very favorable outcomes, they anticipate other people’s suspicious reactions and prefer lying and appearing honest to telling the truth and appearing as selfish liars.
paras.zh: 研究人员断言，这些发现表明，当人们得到非常有利的结果时，会预料到别人的怀疑，宁可撒谎显得诚实，也不愿说实话却显得像自私的骗子。

paras.en: So why is this research important?
paras.zh: 那这项研究为什么重要呢？

paras.en: Well, experts generally agree there are two main types of lie: selfish lies and lies that are meant to benefit others, the first, as you may predict, is for selfish gain, such as submitting a fraudulent claim to an insurance company, while the second involves lying to help others or not offend others.
paras.zh: 嗯，专家们普遍认为谎言主要有两种：自私的谎言和为了别人好的谎言。第一种，你可能也猜到了，是为了一己私利，比如向保险公司提交虚假的索赔；第二种则是为了帮助别人或者不得罪别人而撒谎。

paras.en: For example, telling a friend whose outfit you don’t like that they look great.
paras.zh: 比如，朋友的衣服你并不喜欢，却跟他说他穿着很好看。

paras.en: But the Researchers are suggesting a third type of lying, lying to maintain a good reputation.
paras.zh: 但研究人员提出了第三种谎言，就是为了维护好名声而撒谎。

paras.en: Now, this hypothesis is new, and some skeptics argue that this isn’t a whole new category of lie.
paras.zh: 这个假设很新，有些持怀疑态度的人认为，这并不是一种全新的谎言。

paras.en: But the findings seem intuitive to me.
paras.zh: 但在我看来，这些发现符合直觉。

w.m: adj. 符合直觉的；直观的

paras.en: After all, one of the main motivations for lying is to increase our worth in the eyes of others.
paras.zh: 毕竟，撒谎的主要动机之一，就是提高自己在别人眼中的价值。

paras.en: So it seems highly likely that people will lie to seem honest.
paras.zh: 所以，人们很有可能会为了显得诚实而撒谎。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What did a team of scientists find in their study?
paras.zh: 第十九题：一组科学家在研究中发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: Why would people fabricate numbers to their own detriment, according to the researchers?
paras.zh: 第二十题：根据研究人员的说法，人们为什么会编造数字、让自己吃亏？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker think of the researcher’s findings?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人怎么看研究人员的发现？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Why do old people dislike new music?
paras.zh: 老年人为什么不喜欢新音乐？

paras.en: As I’ve grown older, I often hear people my age say things like they just don’t make good music like they used to.
paras.zh: 随着年龄增长，我常听到同龄人说，现在的人再也做不出以前那样的好音乐了。

paras.en: Why does this happen?
paras.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

paras.en: Luckily, psychology can give us some insights into this puzzle.
paras.zh: 好在心理学能帮我们解开这个谜。

paras.en: Musical tastes begin to crystallize as early as age 13 or 14, and by the time we’re in our early 20s, these tastes get locked into place pretty firmly.
paras.zh: 音乐品味早在13、14岁时就开始定型，到了20出头，这些品味就相当牢固地固定下来了。

paras.en: In fact, studies have found that by the time we turn 33, most of us have stopped listening to new music.
paras.zh: 事实上，研究发现，到33岁时，我们大多数人已经不再听新音乐了。

paras.en: Meanwhile, popular songs released when you’re in your early teens are likely to remain quite popular among your age group for the rest of your life.
paras.zh: 同时，在你十三四岁时发行的流行歌曲，很可能在你这一辈子里都会在你的同龄人中一直很受欢迎。

paras.en: There could be a biological explanation for this, as there’s evidence that the brain’s ability to make subtle distinctions between different chords, rhythms, and melodies deteriorates with age.
paras.zh: 这可能有生物学上的原因，因为有证据表明，大脑细致区分不同和弦、节奏和旋律的能力会随着年龄增长而衰退。

paras.en: So, to older people, newer, less familiar songs might all sound the same, but there may be some simpler reasons for older people’s aversion to newer music.
paras.zh: 所以，对年纪大的人来说，比较新、不太熟悉的歌听起来可能都一样，不过老年人反感新音乐，也许还有一些更简单的原因。

paras.en: One of the most researched laws of social psychology is something called the mere exposure effect, which in essence means that the more we’re exposed to something, the more we tend to like it.
paras.zh: 社会心理学里研究得最多的规律之一，叫作“单纯曝光效应”，本质上就是说，我们接触某样东西越多，就越容易喜欢它。

paras.en: This happens with people we know, the advertisements we see, and the songs we listen to.
paras.zh: 我们认识的人、看到的广告、听的歌，都是这样。

paras.en: When you’re in your early teens, you probably spend a fair amount of time listening to music or watching music videos, your favorite songs and artists become familiar, comforting parts of your routine.
paras.zh: 十三四岁的时候，你可能会花不少时间听音乐、看音乐视频，你最喜欢的歌曲和歌手就会变得熟悉，成为你日常生活中让人安心的一部分。

paras.en: For many people over 30, job and family obligations increase, so there’s less time to spend discovering new music.
paras.zh: 对很多30岁以上的人来说，工作和家庭的责任增加了，花在发现新音乐上的时间也就少了。

paras.en: Instead, many will simply listen to old familiar favorites from that period of their lives when they had more free time.
paras.zh: 相反，很多人干脆只听那些熟悉的老歌，那是他们人生中空闲时间更多的那段时期最喜欢的歌。

paras.en: Of course, those teen years weren’t necessarily carefree; they’re famously confusing, which is why so many TV shows and movies revolve around high school turmoil.
paras.zh: 当然，十几岁那几年也不见得无忧无虑；出了名的让人困惑，所以才有那么多电视节目和电影都以高中时期的混乱为题材。

paras.en: Psychology research has shown that the emotions that we experience as teens seem more intense than those that come later, and we also know that intense emotions are associated with stronger memories and preferences.
paras.zh: 心理学研究表明，我们十几岁时体验到的情绪，似乎比后来的更强烈；我们还知道，强烈的情绪会带来更深刻的记忆、更强的偏好。

paras.en: Both of these might explain why the songs we listen to during this period become so memorable and beloved.
paras.zh: 这两点或许都能解释，为什么我们在这个时期听的歌会让人这么难忘、这么喜爱。

paras.en: So there’s nothing wrong with your parents because they don’t like your music.
paras.zh: 所以，你的父母不喜欢你的音乐，并不是他们有什么问题。

paras.en: Rather, it’s all part of the natural order of things.
paras.zh: 这其实都是事物的自然规律。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker mainly discuss in this talk?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人在这次讲话中主要讨论了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What have studies found about most people by the time they turn 33?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于大多数人到33岁时的情况，研究发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What do we learn from one of the most researched laws of social psychology?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：从社会心理学研究得最多的规律之一中，我们能了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What might explain the fact that songs people listen to in their teen years are memorable and beloved?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：人们十几岁时听的歌令人难忘、深受喜爱，这一现象可以用什么来解释？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2020年12月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2020年12月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，两人聊起一款驾驶模拟游戏，觉得它枯燥却让人放松，又真实有教育意义，女士还因此报了安全驾驶课。第二段长对话里，两位自由职业者谈自己单干的感受：缺少经理的激励和表扬，但最看重的是自主。第一篇短文介绍一项研究：晴天和雪天会让消费者想象使用户外产品，从而愿意多花钱，网上卖家可以借此定价。第二篇短文说办公室空调定在22度未必效率最高，23到26度更合适，人也能适应新的温度。第一段录音介绍新研究：短暂独处会减弱兴奋、愤怒等强烈情绪，放大平静、孤独等较弱的情绪，可以用来调节情绪。第二段录音解释多动脑子并不能明显多消耗热量，国际象棋冠军消瘦主要是压力大、吃得少。第三段录音讲面试时怎样回答“介绍一下你自己”：讲好职业故事，了解公司需求，回答一分钟左右。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: This is unbelievable.
paras.zh: 这也太不可思议了。

w.m: adj. 难以置信的；不可思议的

paras.en: Unlike any video game I’ve ever played before, it’s so boring yet so relaxing at the same time.
paras.zh: 它跟我以前玩过的任何电子游戏都不一样，既那么枯燥，同时又那么让人放松。

paras.en: How did you hear about this driving simulator?
paras.zh: 你是怎么知道这个驾驶模拟游戏的？

paras.en: My brother introduced it to me last year.
paras.zh: 我哥哥去年介绍给我的。

paras.en: I was surprised to find how educational and realistic it was.
paras.zh: 我惊讶地发现它既有教育意义，又特别逼真。

paras.en: It’s called Euro Truck Simulator, but they have other versions as well for America and so on.
paras.zh: 它叫《欧洲卡车模拟》，不过也有美国等其他地方的版本。

paras.en: I was really drawn to the scenery.
paras.zh: 我特别喜欢里面的风景。

paras.en: The routes go through parts of the country you don’t normally see as a tourist.
paras.zh: 这些路线会经过这个国家里游客平时看不到的地方。

paras.en: Yeah, I can see that.
paras.zh: 是啊，我能理解。

paras.en: It seems so simple, just transporting cargo from point A to point B, driving from one city to another, but I really appreciate all the details that go into the game.
paras.zh: 它看起来很简单，就是把货物从A地运到B地，从一个城市开到另一个城市，但游戏里花在细节上的那些心思，我真的很欣赏。

paras.en: It’s even given me a new appreciation for the logistics industry and traffic on the road.
paras.zh: 它甚至让我对物流业和道路交通有了新的认识。

paras.en: I completely agree.
paras.zh: 我完全同意。

paras.en: My brother also introduced me to some videos of someone that streams their game online.
paras.zh: 我哥哥还给我看过一些视频，是有人在网上直播自己玩这个游戏。

paras.en: It was fascinating to watch.
paras.zh: 看着特别有意思。

w.m: adj. 引人入胜的；极有意思的

paras.en: Really, this guy drove very carefully, obeyed all the road signs and traffic rules.
paras.zh: 真的，这个人开车特别小心，所有的路标和交通规则都遵守。

paras.en: Such a contrast to most violent games.
paras.zh: 跟大多数暴力游戏形成了鲜明的对比。

paras.en: Honestly, playing has inspired me to look into the industry more.
paras.zh: 说实话，玩这个游戏让我更想深入了解这个行业了。

paras.en: I’ve read articles about how self-driving trucks may soon be available and could greatly impact cargo logistics.
paras.zh: 我读过一些文章，说自动驾驶卡车可能很快就会问世，而且可能对货物物流产生很大影响。

paras.en: Considering all that goes into driving these larger vehicles, it’s amazing that we could soon have that kind of technology.
paras.zh: 想想开这些大型车辆要顾及的方方面面，我们可能很快就会有那样的技术，真是太神奇了。

paras.en: Ha?
paras.zh: 哈？

w.m: int. 哈（表示惊讶或得意）

paras.en: I’ve gone one step further.
paras.zh: 我更进了一步。

paras.en: I registered to take a safe driving course to improve my real-life driving skills.
paras.zh: 我报名参加了一个安全驾驶课程，来提高自己在现实中的驾驶技术。

paras.en: In a way, I feel like I have a head start compared to other students in the class.
paras.zh: 从某种意义上说，我觉得跟班上其他学员比，我已经领先一步了。

paras.en: Playing this video game has given me some maneuvering practice already.
paras.zh: 玩这个游戏已经让我练过一些操控车辆的技巧了。

paras.en: I’m not sure how accurate the video game is compared to real-life situations, but if it results in more drivers looking both ways before entering an intersection, I’d say that’s a positive outcome.
paras.zh: 我不确定这个游戏跟现实情况比有多准确，但如果它能让更多司机在进十字路口之前左右看一看，我觉得那就是个好结果。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
paras.zh: 第一题：两人主要在谈论什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say about the driving simulator?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于这个驾驶模拟游戏，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman say she really appreciates?
paras.zh: 第三题：女士说她非常欣赏什么？

paras.en: Question four: What outcome does the woman expect from the driving simulator?
paras.zh: 第四题：女士期望这个驾驶模拟游戏带来什么结果？

paras.en: Conversation two: How do you like being self-employed?
paras.zh: 第二段对话。你觉得自己单干怎么样？

paras.en: There are obvious benefits, though I don’t seem to have the freedom I anticipated, as I just don’t seem able to decline work offers.
paras.zh: 好处是明摆着的，不过我好像并没有预想中那么自由，因为别人找上门的活儿，我好像就是推不掉。

paras.en: And working alone, there have been times when I’ve found that money alone provides insufficient motivation.
paras.zh: 而且一个人干活，有些时候我发现，光靠钱是不足以让人有干劲的。

paras.en: Have you experienced the same since you began working for yourself?
paras.zh: 你自己出来干以后，也有过同样的感受吗？

paras.en: Sometimes, yes.
paras.zh: 有时候会。

paras.en: Unlike the rest of the workforce who have managers to prompt motivation whenever they’re feeling lazy or bored, we self-employed workers perform our jobs without a manager to lift our spirits.
paras.zh: 其他上班族有经理管着，一觉得懒散或无聊，经理就会激励他们；我们这些自己干的人就不一样了，干活的时候没有经理来给我们打气。

paras.en: There’s no one around to offer praise or initiate collaboration, no one to make greater use of our interests and talents.
paras.zh: 身边没有人夸你，也没有人主动找你合作，没有人能把我们的兴趣和才能更好地发挥出来。

paras.en: That’s a fact.
paras.zh: 确实如此。

paras.en: Not every manager behaves with such awareness and care, of course, and certainly not all managers have a clue how to motivate people.
paras.zh: 当然，不是每个经理都这么有心、这么体贴，也肯定不是所有经理都懂得怎么激励人。

paras.en: Still, having a manager nearby at least indicates there’s an opportunity.
paras.zh: 不过，身边有个经理，至少说明还是有机会的。

paras.en: They’ll be decent enough to look out for you when your energy and focus begin to deplete.
paras.zh: 当你的精力和注意力开始下降时，他们会好心地关照你。

paras.en: The motivator I value most is autonomy.
paras.zh: 我最看重的激励因素是自主。

paras.en: I’ve learned not to sacrifice my prized autonomy by working all hours of the day and by saying yes to every client request.
paras.zh: 我已经学会了，不再因为没日没夜地工作、对客户的每个要求都点头答应，而牺牲掉我所珍视的自主权。

paras.en: Yes, I need to remind myself that I selected this lifestyle for the independence.
paras.zh: 是啊，我得提醒自己，我选择这种生活方式，就是为了独立。

paras.en: I don’t miss aspects of permanent full-time employment I disliked, such as the office politics, job insecurity, inflexible hours, and so on.
paras.zh: 长期全职工作里那些我不喜欢的东西，比如办公室政治、工作没保障、上班时间死板等等，我一点也不怀念。

paras.en: I wouldn’t mind a bit more in the form of praise, though, praise which is on the record.
paras.zh: 不过，要是能多得到一点表扬，我倒是不介意，而且是那种正式留下记录的表扬。

w.m: 正式记录在案的；公开的

paras.en: That’ll come with time.
paras.zh: 那会随着时间慢慢来的。

paras.en: Relatedness is inevitably cultivated via human interaction, engaging with clients, getting written testimony and recommendations, staying in contact with clients afterwards.
paras.zh: 归属感必然要通过与人打交道来培养：跟客户来往，拿到书面评价和推荐信，事后跟客户保持联系。

paras.en: These are things you’ll find will come in due course and provide you with motivation.
paras.zh: 你会发现，这些东西到时候自然会有，也会给你带来动力。

paras.en: You’re right.
paras.zh: 你说得对。

paras.en: That’s an area I do need to put some more effort into, building closer relationships with those who engage my services and skills.
paras.zh: 这方面我确实得多下点功夫，就是跟那些请我提供服务、用我技能的人建立更密切的关系。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the man say about his life of being self-employed?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于自己单干的生活，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man say about managers?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于经理，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What do both speakers value most about self-employment?
paras.zh: 第七题：两人最看重自己单干的哪一点？

paras.en: Question eight: On what point does the man agree with the woman?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士在哪一点上同意女士的看法？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you’ll hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: Weather is a constant force in our lives, but there’s little marketing research on how it affects businesses.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。天气是我们生活中一股始终存在的力量，但关于它怎样影响商业的营销研究却很少。

w.m: adj. 持续不断的；始终存在的

paras.en: Now, a new study reveals how sunny and snowy conditions influence consumer behavior.
paras.zh: 现在，一项新研究揭示了晴天和雪天会怎样影响消费者的行为。

paras.en: Those weather conditions trigger consumers to mentally visualize using products associated with the respective weather.
paras.zh: 这些天气状况会促使消费者在脑子里想象自己使用与这种天气相关的产品。

paras.en: This leads to consumers placing a higher value on those products.
paras.zh: 这会让消费者觉得那些产品更值钱。

paras.en: That is, they’re willing to pay more money for them.
paras.zh: 也就是说，他们愿意为这些产品多花钱。

paras.en: But the correlation is only found with products related to being outside.
paras.zh: 不过，这种关联只出现在跟户外有关的产品上。

paras.en: How does this work?
paras.zh: 这是怎么起作用的呢？

paras.en: Researchers give the example of a beach towel.
paras.zh: 研究人员举了沙滩巾的例子。

paras.en: On a sunny day, consumers who see that product are not just looking at the towel itself; they are likely imagining themselves lying on the towel in the sun.
paras.zh: 在晴天，看到这件商品的消费者不只是在看毛巾本身，他们很可能在想象自己躺在阳光下的毛巾上。

paras.en: This mental picture of using the towel increases the value of the product in the consumer’s mind.
paras.zh: 这种使用毛巾的画面浮现在脑海里，就提高了这件商品在消费者心中的价值。

paras.en: Researchers put forward the following hypothesis to explain their findings.
paras.zh: 研究人员提出了下面这个假设来解释他们的发现。

paras.en: They think the mental picture works in sunshine and snow because these weather conditions have a positive association with outside activities.
paras.zh: 他们认为，这种心理画面之所以在晴天和雪天起作用，是因为这些天气跟户外活动有着正面的联系。

paras.en: The effect is not seen with rainy weather.
paras.zh: 雨天就看不到这种效果。

paras.en: Researchers assert this is because there aren’t many activities that are enabled by rain.
paras.zh: 研究人员断言，这是因为下雨天能做的活动不多。

paras.en: Most products associated with rain, like umbrellas, are only used for protection from the weather and not for any activities, researchers believe that companies that sell a wide array of products online can benefit most from the insights this study provides.
paras.zh: 跟雨有关的大多数产品，比如雨伞，都只是用来挡雨，而不是用来开展什么活动。研究人员认为，在网上销售各种各样商品的公司，最能从这项研究提供的见解中受益。

paras.en: Online sellers often use complex mathematical formulas to determine what products to feature and how to price those products.
paras.zh: 网上卖家常常用复杂的数学公式，来决定重点推哪些产品、给这些产品定什么价。

w.m: v. 重点推出；以……为特色

paras.en: Incorporating more data about weather would allow them to make better decisions.
paras.zh: 纳入更多天气数据，能让他们做出更好的决策。

paras.en: This could bolster sales.
paras.zh: 这可能会提升销量。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What do we learn about the findings of the new study?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于这项新研究的结果，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the passage say may increase the value of products for consumers?
paras.zh: 第十题：短文说什么可能会提高产品在消费者心中的价值？

paras.en: Question 11: How can the findings of the new study benefit online sellers, according to the researchers?
paras.zh: 第十一题：根据研究人员的说法，这项新研究的结果能怎样让网上卖家受益？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Setting the office air conditioning at about 22 degrees Celsius has become standard practice across the world.
paras.zh: 把办公室空调设在22摄氏度左右，已经成了全世界的通行做法。

paras.en: Numerous guidebooks across the world on heating, ventilation, and air conditioning claim office performance peaks at 22 degrees.
paras.zh: 全世界许多关于供暖、通风和空调的指南都声称，办公效率在22度时最高。

paras.en: Many people indeed find relief from soaring summer temperatures in air-conditioned offices, but recent studies have challenged the accepted wisdom that a cool office is more productive.
paras.zh: 夏天气温飙升，许多人确实能在有空调的办公室里松一口气，但最近的研究对“办公室凉快效率就高”这一公认的看法提出了质疑。

paras.en: The reality is more complex.
paras.zh: 实际情况要复杂得多。

paras.en: Researchers conducted a review of all studies relating to air conditioning and productivity.
paras.zh: 研究人员把所有涉及空调和工作效率的研究都梳理了一遍。

paras.en: They found that 22 degrees was probably a little chilly, even at the height of summer.
paras.zh: 他们发现，即使是在盛夏，22度可能也有点偏凉。

paras.en: For a person dressed in typical summer clothing, an optimal range would be between 23 and 26 degrees, and people can even tolerate temperatures beyond this comfort zone as long as they can adjust their clothing and expectations.
paras.zh: 对一个穿着普通夏装的人来说，最适宜的温度是23到26度；而且只要能调整衣着和心理预期，人们甚至能忍受超出这个舒适区间的温度。

paras.en: In fact, even on very hot days, it makes sense to turn the air conditioning up.
paras.zh: 事实上，即使在很热的日子里，把空调温度调高一点也是合理的。

paras.en: People often chase just one optimum temperature, and this is understandable when people feel hot, but there is a range of at least three to four degrees which does not have any adverse impact.
paras.zh: 人们往往只追求一个最佳温度，人觉得热的时候，这也可以理解，但其实有一个至少三到四度的区间，在这个区间内不会有任何不良影响。

paras.en: Another issue related to this is that people can become psychologically dependent on air conditioning.
paras.zh: 与此相关的另一个问题是，人们可能会在心理上依赖空调。

paras.en: If they are used to the environment which is air-conditioned, they tend to prefer lower temperatures.
paras.zh: 如果他们习惯了有空调的环境，往往就会更喜欢低一些的温度。

paras.en: But the studies found that almost all humans became accustomed to the new temperature.
paras.zh: 但研究发现，几乎所有人都会适应新的温度。

paras.en: It was only at the extreme ends of the temperature range where people’s productivity suffered.
paras.zh: 只有在温度区间的两头极端处，人们的工作效率才会受影响。

paras.en: This range was above 26 degrees and below 19 degrees.
paras.zh: 这个区间指的是26度以上和19度以下。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What is the accepted wisdom concerning the office environment?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于办公环境，公认的看法是什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What did researchers find from their review of all studies relating to air conditioning and productivity?
paras.zh: 第十三题：研究人员梳理了所有涉及空调和工作效率的研究，他们发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What do we learn about using a little less air conditioning during hot weather?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于在炎热天气里少开一点空调，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What happens when people are used to an air-conditioned environment?
paras.zh: 第十五题：人们习惯了有空调的环境以后会怎样？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you’ll hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Psychology research has tended to portray solitude as a negative experience, studies conducted in the 1970s and 1990s suggested that people felt less happy when alone as compared to being with others.
paras.zh: 心理学研究往往把独处描绘成一种负面的体验。20世纪70年代和90年代开展的研究表明，跟和别人在一起时相比，人们独处时没那么开心。

paras.en: However, a new paper shows an alternative view of solitude, one in which solitude can be positive.
paras.zh: 然而，一篇新论文提出了看待独处的另一种观点，认为独处也可以是积极的。

paras.en: Let’s start by looking at the earlier research.
paras.zh: 我们先来看看早期的研究。

paras.en: It had a couple of shortcomings.
paras.zh: 它有几个不足之处。

paras.en: First, it measured emotion on a scale from positive to negative, overlooking the possibility that our positive and negative emotions can fluctuate independently.
paras.zh: 第一，它用一个从正面到负面的量表来衡量情绪，忽视了一种可能：我们的正面情绪和负面情绪是可以各自独立起伏的。

paras.en: Also, it categorized emotions as simply positive or negative.
paras.zh: 另外，它只是简单地把情绪分成正面和负面两类。

paras.en: It didn’t consider that emotions arouse us to different degrees, and that both positive and negative emotions can arouse us a lot or a little.
paras.zh: 它没有考虑到，情绪唤起我们的程度有高有低，而且正面情绪和负面情绪都可能强烈地唤起我们，也可能只是轻微地唤起我们。

paras.en: That is, whether positive or negative, emotions can be either high arousal or low arousal.
paras.zh: 也就是说，不管是正面还是负面，情绪都可以分为高唤醒和低唤醒两种。

paras.en: High arousal emotions include excitement on the positive side, or anger on the negative side, while low arousal ones include feeling calm on the positive side or lonely on the negative.
paras.zh: 高唤醒情绪，正面的有兴奋，负面的有愤怒；低唤醒情绪，正面的有平静，负面的有孤独。

paras.en: This new research attempted to overcome these shortcomings.
paras.zh: 这项新研究试图克服这些不足。

paras.en: Researchers began with a simple study.
paras.zh: 研究人员先做了一个简单的研究。

paras.en: They asked participants to spend 15 minutes sitting alone without engaging in any activity, and measured how this solitude influenced their emotional state.
paras.zh: 他们让参与者独自坐15分钟，什么活动也不做，然后测量这段独处对他们情绪状态的影响。

paras.en: This experiment specifically aimed to determine the effect of solitude on high arousal emotions.
paras.zh: 这项实验专门用来确定独处对高唤醒情绪的影响。

paras.en: It looked at positive emotions such as being excited or interested, and negative emotions including being scared or distressed, the results were clear.
paras.zh: 它考察了兴奋、感兴趣之类的正面情绪，以及害怕、苦恼之类的负面情绪。结果很明确。

paras.en: After 15 minutes of solitude, the participants showed reductions in both types of emotion.
paras.zh: 独处15分钟以后，参与者这两类情绪都减弱了。

paras.en: A second study measured the effects of solitude on low arousal emotions.
paras.zh: 第二项研究测量了独处对低唤醒情绪的影响。

paras.en: These included both positive and negative emotions, such as feeling calm, relaxed, sad, or lonely.
paras.zh: 其中既有正面情绪，也有负面情绪，比如感到平静、放松、难过或孤独。

paras.en: That experiment found that all of these emotions were increased by time alone.
paras.zh: 那项实验发现，独处的时间让所有这些情绪都增强了。

paras.en: Thus, it seems past depictions of solitude were wrong.
paras.zh: 由此看来，过去对独处的描述是错的。

paras.en: It doesn’t have a simple emotional effect that can be characterized as good or bad.
paras.zh: 独处并不会产生一种简单归为好或坏的情绪效果。

paras.en: Rather, it changes the intensity of our inner experience, it amplifies quieter emotions, but it diminishes the intensity of stronger feelings.
paras.zh: 相反，它改变的是我们内心体验的强度：它会放大比较平静的情绪，却会减弱比较强烈的感受。

paras.en: It’s worth clarifying that these findings relate to relatively brief periods of solitude.
paras.zh: 有一点值得说明：这些发现针对的是比较短暂的独处。

paras.en: This is distinct from prolonged loneliness.
paras.zh: 这跟长期的孤独是两回事。

paras.en: Research has demonstrated that the latter is correlated with an assortment of negative physical and psychological effects, how can people benefit from being alone?
paras.zh: 研究已经证明，后者跟一系列负面的生理和心理影响有关。那么，人们怎样才能从独处中受益呢？

paras.en: The findings here suggest that people can use solitude to regulate their emotions.
paras.zh: 这里的发现表明，人们可以借助独处来调节自己的情绪。

paras.en: Solitude can help us become quiet after excitement, calm after an angry episode, or simply feel at peace.
paras.zh: 独处能帮我们在兴奋之后静下来，在发完火之后平静下来，或者只是让心里感到安宁。

w.m: n. 一段经历；一次发作

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What is one of the criticisms directed at the early research on solitude?
paras.zh: 第十六题：对早期独处研究的批评之一是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What do we learn about the results of the new research?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于这项新研究的结果，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What did the second experiment in the new research find about solitude?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于独处，新研究中的第二项实验发现了什么？

paras.en: Recording two, in 1984, the World Chess Championships was called off abruptly due to the withered frame of a player who was competing for the title.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。1984年，世界国际象棋锦标赛突然中止，原因是一名争夺冠军的棋手瘦得不成样子。

paras.en: He wasn’t alone in experiencing the extreme physical effects of the game.
paras.zh: 遭受这项比赛带来的极端身体反应的，并不只有他一个人。

paras.en: Elite players can reportedly burn up to an absurd 6000 calories in one day.
paras.zh: 据报道，顶尖棋手一天能消耗的热量高达6000卡路里，多得离谱。

paras.en: Does that mean that thinking harder is a simple route to losing weight?
paras.zh: 这是不是意味着，多动脑子就是减肥的一条捷径？

paras.en: Well, when the body is at rest, we know that the brain uses up a startling 20 to 25% of the body’s overall energy.
paras.zh: 嗯，我们知道，身体在休息、不活动的时候，大脑消耗的能量要占全身总能量的20%到25%，这个比例高得惊人。

paras.en: This level of utilization actually makes the brain the most energy-expensive organ in the body, and yet it makes up only 2% of the body’s weight overall.
paras.zh: 这么高的利用率，实际上让大脑成了人体内最耗能的器官，可它只占体重的2%。

paras.en: So, the more we put this organ to work, the more calories we’ll burn.
paras.zh: 那么，我们越让这个器官工作，消耗的热量就越多吗？

paras.en: Technically, the answer is yes, for cognitively difficult tasks.
paras.zh: 严格来说，对于认知上有难度的任务，答案是肯定的。

w.m: adv. 严格来说；从技术上讲

paras.en: What counts as a difficult mental task varies between individuals, but generally it could be described as something that the brain cannot solve easily using previously learned routines or tasks that change the conditions continuously.
paras.zh: 什么样的脑力任务算难，因人而异，但大体上可以说，就是大脑没法用以前学会的套路轻松解决的事，或者条件在不断变化的任务。

paras.en: However, deep thinking will not burn off the calories gained from eating a sugary snack, because in relation to the brain’s huge overall energy usage, which is devoted to a multitude of tasks, the energy required just to think harder is actually comparatively tiny.
paras.zh: 不过，深度思考并不会消耗掉吃一份甜食摄入的热量，因为大脑总的能耗非常大，要用来完成大量各种各样的任务，相比之下，单单为了多动脑子所需的能量其实少得可怜。

paras.en: We’re unconscious of most of what uses up the brain’s energy.
paras.zh: 大脑能量的大部分消耗，我们自己是意识不到的。

paras.en: A lot of that activity is unrelated to conscious activities like learning how to sing or play the guitar.
paras.zh: 其中很多活动跟有意识的活动无关，比如学唱歌、学弹吉他。

paras.en: The brain is able to allocate blood and thus energy to particular regions that are being active at that point, but the overall energy availability in the brain is thought to be constant, so while there might be significant increases in energy use at localized regions of the brain when we perform difficult cognitive tasks, when it comes to the whole brain’s energy budget overall, these activities don’t significantly alter it.
paras.zh: 大脑能把血液、进而把能量分配到当时正活跃的特定区域，但一般认为大脑里可用的总能量是恒定的。所以，虽然我们做有难度的认知任务时，大脑局部区域的能耗可能会大幅增加，但就整个大脑的总能量预算来说，这些活动并不会让它有明显变化。

w.m: n. 可用性；可得到的量

paras.en: So why did the chess champion grow too skinny to compete in his chess competition.
paras.zh: 那么，那位国际象棋冠军为什么会瘦到没法参加比赛呢？

paras.en: The general consensus is that it mostly comes down to stress and reduced food consumption, not mental exhaustion.
paras.zh: 大家普遍认为，这主要是压力大、吃得少造成的，而不是脑力耗尽。

paras.en: Keeping your body pumped up for action for long periods of time is very energy demanding.
paras.zh: 让身体长时间处于随时准备行动的亢奋状态，是非常耗能的。

paras.en: If you can’t eat as often or as much as you can, or would normally, then you might lose weight.
paras.zh: 如果你不能像平常那样按时吃饭、吃那么多，就可能会掉体重。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What do we learn about the brain when the body is at rest?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于身体休息时的大脑，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the speaker say about the consumption of the brain’s energy?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于大脑能量的消耗，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What do we learn about the overall energy availability in the brain?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于大脑里可用的总能量，我们了解到什么？

w.m: n. 可用性；可得到的量

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Tell me about yourself may seem like an easy job interview question, but the open-ended nature of this question often leaves job seekers at a loss where to start.
paras.zh: “介绍一下你自己”看起来可能是个简单的面试问题，但这个问题很开放，常常让求职者不知道从哪儿说起。

paras.en: This common question is actually a critical test of a job candidate’s communication skills, so it’s important not to give an unprepared response or mess it up.
paras.zh: 这个常见的问题其实是对求职者沟通能力的一次关键考验，所以千万不要毫无准备就作答，更不能把它搞砸。

paras.en: Tell me about yourself is often the first question professional career coaches prepare people for when they give interview guidance.
paras.zh: 职业教练做面试辅导时，“介绍一下你自己”往往是他们首先帮人准备的问题。

paras.en: It’s the opportunity for the candidate to take control of the narrative and tell their story in a way that really matters to their audience, it takes hard work and extensive preparation to answer this question well.
paras.zh: 这是求职者掌握话语主动权的机会，可以用真正打动听众的方式讲出自己的故事。要答好这个问题，得下苦功、做大量准备。

paras.en: When a person goes to a job interview, their interviewer has presumably read their resume, so they don’t need to repeat the information.
paras.zh: 一个人去参加求职面试时，面试官大概已经看过他的简历了，所以他不需要再把那些信息重复一遍。

paras.en: But that’s what most people will do, as it’s their instinct to recite things that are already on their resume.
paras.zh: 但大多数人偏偏就会这么做，因为他们本能地就想把简历上已经写着的东西背一遍。

paras.en: It’s important for job seekers to do their homework on two crucial aspects.
paras.zh: 求职者必须在两个关键方面做足功课。

paras.en: First, they are not just telling someone a fact about themselves; they’re telling a story, and stories take work to create.
paras.zh: 第一，他们不只是在告诉别人一个关于自己的事实，而是在讲一个故事，而故事是要花功夫去编的。

paras.en: Coming up with a good story means getting reflective about what made their career accomplishments something they’re proud of and what strengths those accomplishments highlight.
paras.zh: 想出一个好故事，就意味着要好好反思：是什么让自己的职业成就值得骄傲，这些成就又突显出自己的哪些长处。

paras.en: Candidates shouldn’t pick a broad, general strength to elaborate on, such as “I’m smart,” “I work hard, and I get things done.”
paras.zh: 求职者不应该挑一个宽泛、笼统的长处来展开讲，比如“我很聪明”“我工作努力，能把事情办成”。

paras.en: To come up with multiple career accomplishments or examples for different interview questions, job seekers should talk with others, especially people who know them, partners, friends, or coworkers who will bring up different stories than the ones they remember.
paras.zh: 要针对不同的面试问题想出多个职业成就或例子，求职者应该跟别人聊聊，尤其是了解他们的人，比如伴侣、朋友或同事，这些人提起的故事会跟他们自己记得的不一样。

paras.en: Secondly, candidates should know what’s at stake for the company with this job opening, what they really are asking you is, tell me why you are going to help me.
paras.zh: 第二，求职者应该了解这个职位空缺对公司来说关系到什么。他们真正问你的其实是：告诉我，你为什么能帮到我。

paras.en: If the person is a prepared candidate, they should have already figured out those things.
paras.zh: 如果是一个有准备的求职者，应该早就把这些事想清楚了。

paras.en: They’ve read the job description and researched the company on the internet.
paras.zh: 他们看过职位描述，也在网上查过这家公司。

paras.en: What job applicants ought to be looking for is what the company is up to, what they are trying to accomplish, and what is preventing them from accomplishing those things.
paras.zh: 求职者应该弄清楚的是：公司在忙什么，想达成什么目标，又是什么在阻碍他们达成这些目标。

paras.en: How long should it take to answer?
paras.zh: 回答应该用多长时间呢？

paras.en: Around a minute.
paras.zh: 一分钟左右。

paras.en: That’s about right for most people’s attention spans.
paras.zh: 这对大多数人的注意力持续时间来说正合适。

paras.en: Under a minute could seem rushed, while over two minutes will start to feel more like a speech, but the length of the answer is not an exact science, and candidates need to keep their career story focused and tailored to their audience.
paras.zh: 不到一分钟可能会显得仓促，而超过两分钟就会开始让人觉得更像一场演讲。不过，回答的长短并没有精确的标准，求职者要让自己的职业故事有重点，并且根据听众量身定制。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker say about the job interview question “Tell me about yourself”?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于“介绍一下你自己”这个面试问题，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What will most people do when they come to a job interview?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：大多数人来参加求职面试时会怎么做？

paras.en: Question 24: Why should job seekers talk with partners, friends, and co-workers?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：求职者为什么要跟伴侣、朋友和同事聊一聊？

paras.en: Question 25: What other important preparations should job seekers make before an interview?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：求职者在面试前还应该做好哪些重要的准备？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2021年6月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2021年6月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，男士明天离职，两人讨论离职面谈时要不要说实话：一吐为快固然痛快，但信息未必保密，还可能影响名声和前途。第二段长对话里，植物学家简·福斯特谈她在东南亚雨林的考察：条件艰苦、天气湿热，又因飓风提前撤离，但收获了大量数据。第一篇短文讲科学家对外行使用专业术语的害处：术语会让读者失去兴趣，甚至怀疑科学本身。第二篇短文讲1901年得克萨斯州希金斯油井的发现，它开创了现代石油钻井业，也带来了大起大落的经济模式。第一段录音分析员工觉得经理糟糕的四个原因：公司文化、经理性格、资历不足和按资历提拔。第二段录音介绍西澳大利亚矿区使用自动驾驶卡车和火车，以及自动化对工作岗位和偏远社区的影响。第三段录音讲泰国道路交通死亡率高，各国交通安全一般经历的三个阶段，以及社会激励机制的作用。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: It’s my last day at work tomorrow.
paras.zh: 明天是我上班的最后一天了。

paras.en: I start my new job in two weeks.
paras.zh: 两周后我就去新单位上班了。

paras.en: My human resources manager wants to conduct an interview with me before I leave.
paras.zh: 我们人力资源部的经理想在我走之前跟我面谈一次。

paras.en: Ah, an exit interview.
paras.zh: 啊，离职面谈。

paras.en: Are you looking forward to it?
paras.zh: 你盼着这次面谈吗？

paras.en: I’m not sure how I feel about it.
paras.zh: 我也说不清自己是什么感觉。

paras.en: I resigned because I’ve been unhappy at that company for a long time, but I’m not sure if I should tell them how I really feel.
paras.zh: 我辞职是因为我在那家公司一直干得不开心，干了很久了，可我拿不准该不该把真实感受告诉他们。

paras.en: To my way of thinking, there are two main potential benefits that come from unleashing an agitated stream of truth during an exit interview.
paras.zh: 在我看来，在离职面谈时把憋着的实话一股脑儿倒出来，主要可能有两个好处。

w.m: adj. 激动的；焦虑不安的
n. 一连串；（话语的）滔滔不绝

paras.en: The first is release, unburdening yourself of frustration and perhaps even anger to someone who isn’t a friend or close colleague can be wonderfully freeing.
paras.zh: 第一个是宣泄。把心里的不满甚至愤怒说给一个既不是朋友、也不是亲密同事的人听，会让人感觉特别轻松。

paras.en: And let me guess, the second is that the criticism will theoretically help the organization I’m leaving to improve, making sure employees of the future are less likely to encounter what I did, that’s right.
paras.zh: 让我猜猜，第二个好处是，这些批评从理论上说能帮我要离开的这家单位改进，让以后的员工不太可能再碰上我遇到的那些事。——没错。

paras.en: But the problem with the company improvement part is that very often it doesn’t happen.
paras.zh: 可问题是，公司改进这一点往往根本实现不了。

paras.en: An exit interview is supposed to be private, but often isn’t.
paras.zh: 离职面谈本该是保密的，但实际上常常不是。

paras.en: In my company, the information gained from these interviews is often not confidential, and the information is used as dirt against another manager, or can be traded among senior managers.
paras.zh: 在我们公司，从这种面谈里得到的信息常常并不保密，会被当作攻击另一个经理的把柄，或者在高层经理之间拿来做交易。

paras.en: Now you’ve got me rethinking what I’ll disclose in the interview.
paras.zh: 你这么一说，我得重新想想在面谈里要透露些什么了。

paras.en: There is always the chance that it could affect my reputation and my ability to network in the industry.
paras.zh: 这总有可能会影响我的名声，还有我在这个行业里拓展人脉的能力。

paras.en: It is a pretty small industry, after all.
paras.zh: 毕竟这个行业圈子很小。

paras.en: Anything you initially gain from the instant satisfaction of telling it like it is, you might lose down the track by injuring your future career prospects.
paras.zh: 实话实说能让你当下痛快一时，可不管一开始得到什么，以后都可能因为毁了自己的职业前途而赔进去。

paras.en: Right.
paras.zh: 对。

paras.en: Perhaps I would be better getting things off my chest by going to one of those rate your employer websites.
paras.zh: 也许我去那种给雇主打分的网站上把心里话说出来会更好。

w.m: 把心里话说出来；一吐为快

paras.en: You could, and don’t do the interview at all.
paras.zh: 可以啊，那就干脆别参加面谈了。

paras.en: Exit interviews are not mandatory.
paras.zh: 离职面谈并不是非参加不可的。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第一题：从对话中我们可以了解到这位男士的什么情况？

paras.en: Question two: What does the woman think about the information gained from an exit interview?
paras.zh: 第二题：女士怎样看待从离职面谈中得到的信息？

paras.en: Question three: Why does the man want to rethink what he will say in the coming exit interview?
paras.zh: 第三题：男士为什么想重新考虑在即将进行的离职面谈中要说的话？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man think he had better do?
paras.zh: 第四题：男士认为自己最好做什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Today, I’m talking to the renowned botanist Jane Forster.
paras.zh: 今天，我请到的是著名植物学家简·福斯特。

paras.en: Thank you for inviting me to join you on the show, Henry.
paras.zh: 谢谢你邀请我来上节目，亨利。

paras.en: Recently, Jane, you’ve become quite a celebrity since the release of your latest documentary.
paras.zh: 简，你最新的纪录片上映以后，你最近可成名人了。

paras.en: Can you tell us a little about it?
paras.zh: 能给我们简单介绍一下吗？

paras.en: Well, it follows my expedition to study the vegetation indigenous to the rainforest in equatorial areas of Southeast Asia.
paras.zh: 嗯，它记录的是我去东南亚赤道地区雨林考察当地原生植被的过程。

paras.en: You certainly get to travel to some very exotic locations.
paras.zh: 你可真能去到一些特别有异域风情的地方。

w.m: adj. 异国情调的；奇异的

paras.en: It was far from glamorous, to be honest.
paras.zh: 说实话，那可一点也不光鲜。

paras.en: The area we visited was accessible only by canoe, and the living conditions in the hut were primitive, to say the least.
paras.zh: 我们去的那个地方只能坐独木舟进去，住的棚屋条件说得轻点也是很原始的。

w.m: adj. 可到达的；可进入的
说得轻点；至少可以这么说

paras.en: There was no electricity, and our water supply was a nearby stream.
paras.zh: 那里没有电，我们的水源就是附近的一条小溪。

paras.en: How were the weather conditions while you were there?
paras.zh: 你们在那里的时候天气怎么样？

paras.en: The weather was not conducive to our work at all, since the humidity was almost unbearable.
paras.zh: 天气一点也不利于我们工作，因为湿度高得几乎让人受不了。

paras.en: At midday, we stayed in the hut and did nothing.
paras.zh: 中午我们就待在棚屋里，什么也不干。

w.m: 什么也不做=什么也不做

paras.en: It was too humid to either work or sleep.
paras.zh: 太潮湿了，既没法干活，也没法睡觉。

w.m: 要么……要么；（否定）既不……也不

paras.en: How long did your team spend in the jungle?
paras.zh: 你们团队在丛林里待了多久？

paras.en: Originally, we planned to be there for a month, but in the end, we stayed for only two weeks.
paras.zh: 我们原本计划在那儿待一个月，但最后只待了两个星期。

paras.en: Why did you cut the expedition short?
paras.zh: 你们为什么提前结束了考察？

paras.en: Halfway through the trip, we received news that a hurricane was approaching, and we had to evacuate at very short notice.
paras.zh: 考察进行到一半时，我们接到消息说有飓风正在逼近，只好在很短的时间内紧急撤离。

paras.en: That sounds like a fascinating anecdote.
paras.zh: 听起来是段很精彩的经历。

w.m: adj. 极有趣的；引人入胜的

paras.en: It was frightening.
paras.zh: 当时可吓人了。

w.m: adj. 令人恐惧的；吓人的

paras.en: The fastest evacuation route was through river rapids.
paras.zh: 最快的撤离路线要经过河里的急流。

paras.en: We had to navigate them carrying all of our equipment.
paras.zh: 我们得带着所有设备穿过那些急流。

paras.en: So overall, was the journey unsuccessful?
paras.zh: 那总的来说，这次考察是不是失败了？

paras.en: Absolutely not.
paras.zh: 当然不是。

paras.en: We gathered a massive amount of data about the local plant life.
paras.zh: 我们收集了大量关于当地植物的数据。

paras.en: Why do you put up with such adverse conditions?
paras.zh: 你为什么能忍受这么恶劣的条件呢？

paras.en: Botany is an obsession for me.
paras.zh: 我对植物学特别着迷。

paras.en: Many of the destinations I visit have stunning scenery, and I get to meet a variety of people from all over the world.
paras.zh: 我去的很多地方风景都特别美，我还能认识来自世界各地的各种各样的人。

w.m: adj. 极美的；令人惊叹的

paras.en: So, where will your next destination be?
paras.zh: 那么，你的下一个目的地是哪儿呢？

paras.en: I haven’t decided yet.
paras.zh: 我还没定呢。

paras.en: Then we can leave it for another occasion.
paras.zh: 那我们就留到下次再聊吧。

paras.en: Thanks.
paras.zh: 谢谢。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the man want Jane Forster to talk about?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士想让简·福斯特谈些什么？

paras.en: Question six: Why does the woman describe her experience as far from glamorous?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士为什么说她的经历一点也不光鲜？

paras.en: Question seven: Why did the woman and those who went with her end their trip halfway?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士和同行的人为什么半路结束了行程？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the woman think of the journey?
paras.zh: 第八题：女士怎样看待这次考察之旅？

paras.en: Section B: Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Scientists often use specialized jargon terms while communicating with laymen.
paras.zh: 科学家在跟外行交流时，常常会用一些专业术语。

w.m: n. 外行；门外汉（layman 的复数）

paras.en: Most of them don’t realize the harmful effects of this practice.
paras.zh: 他们大多数都没有意识到这种做法的害处。

paras.en: In a new study, people exposed to jargon when reading about subjects like autonomous vehicles and surgical robots later said they were less interested in science than others who read about the same topics, but without the use of specialized terms, they also felt less informed about science and less qualified to discuss science topics.
paras.zh: 在一项新研究中，有些人在阅读自动驾驶汽车、手术机器人这类话题时接触到了术语，事后他们说，跟阅读同样话题但内容里没有专业术语的人相比，自己对科学没那么感兴趣。他们还觉得自己对科学了解得更少，也更没资格讨论科学话题。

w.m: adj. 有见识的；了解情况的

paras.en: It’s noteworthy that it made no difference if the jargon terms were defined in the text.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，文中有没有给这些术语下定义，结果都一样。

paras.en: Even when the terms were defined, readers still felt the same lack of engagement as readers who read jargon that wasn’t explained.
paras.zh: 即使术语有定义，读者也和读到没有解释的术语的读者一样，觉得自己没什么参与感。

paras.en: The problem is that the mere presence of jargon sends a discouraging message to readers.
paras.zh: 问题在于，光是出现术语，就会给读者传递一个让人泄气的信号。

paras.en: Hillary Shulman, the author of the study, asserts that specialized words are a signal.
paras.zh: 这项研究的作者希拉里·舒尔曼断言，专业词汇就是一种信号。

paras.en: Jargon tells people that the message isn’t for them.
paras.zh: 术语是在告诉人们：这条信息不是说给你听的。

paras.en: There’s an even darker side to how people react to jargon.
paras.zh: 人们对术语的反应，还有更阴暗的一面。

paras.en: In another study, researchers found that reading scientific articles containing jargon led people to doubt the actual science.
paras.zh: 在另一项研究中，研究人员发现，阅读含有术语的科学文章，会让人们怀疑科学本身。

paras.en: They found the opposite when a text is easier to read.
paras.zh: 而文章更容易读懂时，他们发现情况正好相反。

paras.en: Then, people are more persuaded.
paras.zh: 这时候，人们更容易被说服。

paras.en: Thus, it’s important to communicate clearly when talking about complex science subjects.
paras.zh: 因此，谈论复杂的科学话题时，表达清楚很重要。
