paras.zh: 不管是哪种理论，它通常都基于对熟人的仔细观察，而且我们有大量练习的机会。

paras.en: On average, we’re lied to some 200 times per day.
paras.zh: 平均来说，我们每天被骗大约两百次。

paras.en: These are mostly harmless lies, but lies none the less.
paras.zh: 这些大多是无害的谎言，但终究还是谎言。

paras.en: But there’s a problem with our theories, even though they’re based on all this observation.
paras.zh: 可是我们的这些理论有个问题，尽管它们都是基于这么多观察得出的。

paras.en: The average person, you and me, tested rigorously on how well we detect lies, fails to do better than chance.
paras.zh: 普通人，也就是你和我，在严格测试识别谎言的能力时，表现并不比瞎猜好。

paras.en: That’s well established over many studies and lots of attempts by researchers to work out reliable ways to detect lies.
paras.zh: 这一点已经被许多研究证实了，研究人员也做过很多尝试，想找出识别谎言的可靠方法。

paras.en: It’s even relatively easy to fool lie detectors.
paras.zh: 要骗过测谎仪甚至都比较容易。

paras.en: The gold standard of lie detection by training yourself in breathing techniques and symptom suppression.
paras.zh: 只要练练呼吸技巧、学会压住紧张的症状，就连测谎的“金标准”也能骗过去。

paras.en: Is there any way to get better at detecting lies?
paras.zh: 有没有什么办法能更好地识别谎言呢？

paras.en: The new research offers some surprising advice.
paras.zh: 这项新研究给出了一些出人意料的建议。

paras.en: Stop looking and listen instead.
paras.zh: 别看了，改成听吧。

paras.en: It turns out that if we’re unable to see the face but rather focus on the voice of the person in question, our accuracy rate improves considerably.
paras.zh: 结果发现，如果我们看不到对方的脸，而是专注于这个人的声音，我们判断的准确率会大大提高。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: According to the passage, how do most people detect lying?
paras.zh: 第十二题：根据这篇短文，大多数人是怎样识别谎言的？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the passage say about most lies?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于大多数谎言，这篇短文是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 14: What have many studies uncovered about the average person’s lie detection?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于普通人识别谎言的能力，许多研究发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What advice does the new research offer regarding lie detection?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于识别谎言，这项新研究给出了什么建议？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Appear to be submissive, humble, grateful, and undemanding.
paras.zh: 要表现得顺从、谦卑、心怀感激、不提要求。

w.m: adj. 要求不高的；不苛求的

paras.en: Show great pleasure when a doctor comes into your room, even if the visit is brief and useless, don’t challenge anyone with authority unless you’re famous or very rich.
paras.zh: 医生到你病房来时，就算只待了一会儿、一点用都没有，你也要表现得非常高兴。除非你很出名或者非常有钱，否则不要和任何有权威的人对着干。

paras.en: Those are a few strategies for dealing with today’s American medical establishment.
paras.zh: 这是应对如今美国医疗体制的几条策略。

paras.en: What patients want is to be treated with respect and consideration, but in my experience, too few hospitals and doctors are ready to do that.
paras.zh: 病人希望得到的是尊重和体谅，但根据我的经验，愿意这样做的医院和医生太少了。

paras.en: In his book *A Whole New Life*, novelist Reynolds Price recalls that his doctors chose a crowded hallway as the place to tell him he might have a tumor on his spinal cord.
paras.zh: 小说家雷诺兹·普赖斯在他的书《全新的生活》中回忆说，他的医生们选了一条拥挤的走廊，在那儿告诉他脊髓上可能长了肿瘤。

paras.en: It did not occur to the two physicians that a hallway was not the most appropriate place for that particular piece of news.
paras.zh: 那两位医生根本没想到，走廊并不是说这种消息最合适的地方。

paras.en: My surgeon, who is in his mid-thirties, looks tired.
paras.zh: 我的外科医生三十五岁上下，看上去很疲惫。

paras.en: He has been overwhelmed with patients who have fallen on the winter ice?
paras.zh: 他接诊了太多在冬天的冰上摔倒的病人，忙得不可开交。

w.m: 被……压得喘不过气；忙于应付

paras.en: He is a witty man, but sometimes his wit is unwelcome.
paras.zh: 他是个风趣的人，可他的玩笑有时让人很不舒服。

w.m: adj. 不受欢迎的；讨厌的

paras.en: The health insurance company Blue Cross wants me to put you out in the snow tomorrow afternoon.
paras.zh: “蓝十字保险公司想让我明天下午就把你赶到雪地里去。”

paras.en: He tells me after I have been in the hospital for more than a week.
paras.zh: 我住院一个多星期以后，他这样对我说。

paras.en: I’m terrified, because I have no idea where to go.
paras.zh: 我吓坏了，因为我根本不知道该去哪儿。

w.m: adj. 吓坏的；非常害怕的

paras.en: I cannot walk or even lift my leg a few inches.
paras.zh: 我不能走路，连腿都抬不起几英寸。

paras.en: The hospital social worker strikes me as an idiot, but my complaints about her only annoy my surgeon.
paras.zh: 我觉得医院的社工是个白痴，可我对她的抱怨只会惹我的外科医生生气。

paras.en: I have to work with these people.
paras.zh: “我得跟这些人共事。”

paras.en: He tells my friend, Dr Karen Brudney, when she mercifully intervenes on my behalf and arranges for me to be transferred to another hospital.
paras.zh: 我的朋友卡伦·布鲁德尼医生好心出面替我说话，安排我转到另一家医院时，他这样对她说。

paras.en: If you say one negative thing, they get defensive.
paras.zh: “你只要说一句不好听的，他们就会摆出防备的姿态。”

paras.en: She tells me later, they have this kind of institutional loyalty.
paras.zh: 她后来对我说：“他们就是有这种对本单位的维护心理。”

paras.en: Always bring an advocate, that is, any other person with you to the hospital, and write down every single question and the answer, the name of every doctor and nurse.
paras.zh: “去医院一定要带个陪同的人，也就是随便哪个人都行，把每一个问题和答案、每一位医生和护士的名字都写下来。”

w.m: n. 拥护者；（替人说话的）陪同者

paras.en: When people know you have their names, they behave better.
paras.zh: “人们知道你记下了他们的名字，表现就会好一些。”

paras.en: And Brudney adds, if you, as a patient, suggest that you might like to control even part of the situation, or be consulted or informed, then you are considered difficult.
paras.zh: 布鲁德尼还说，作为病人，如果你表示自己哪怕只想掌控一部分情况，或者想让医生跟你商量、把情况告诉你，那你就会被看成是难缠的病人。

paras.en: They want you to be totally passive.
paras.zh: “他们要你完全被动。”

paras.en: The entire healthcare system, particularly hospitals and nursing homes, exists for reasons that have nothing to do with taking care of patients.
paras.zh: 整个医疗体系，尤其是医院和养老院，它们的存在都另有缘由，跟照顾病人毫无关系。

paras.en: Patients are incidental.
paras.zh: 病人只是次要的。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about most American hospitals?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于大多数美国医院，说话人是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 17: What does Karen Brudney suggest patients do?
paras.zh: 第十七题：卡伦·布鲁德尼建议病人怎么做？

paras.en: Question 18: What do American doctors expect their patients to be, according to Karen Brudney?
paras.zh: 第十八题：根据卡伦·布鲁德尼的说法，美国医生希望他们的病人是什么样的？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: There are probably Teams you’ve worked with that you never want to work with again.
paras.zh: 你合作过的团队里，大概有一些是你再也不想跟他们一起工作的。

paras.en: But there must have also been other teams that you would prize reuniting with professionally.
paras.zh: 但肯定也有另一些团队，你会非常珍惜在工作中再次与他们重聚的机会。

paras.en: In other words, your team had vitality.
paras.zh: 换句话说，你的团队有活力。

paras.en: Vitality comes about when the ties people form with their fellow team members are such that they stay connected even after the team breaks up.
paras.zh: 所谓活力，就是团队成员彼此之间结下的关系牢固到即使团队解散了，他们仍然保持联系。

paras.en: What characteristics of a team make its members more likely to stay in contact despite no longer working together?
paras.zh: 一个团队有哪些特点，会让成员即使不再一起工作，也更有可能保持联系？

paras.en: This question has been answered recently in a study published in a business journal.
paras.zh: 最近发表在一份商业期刊上的一项研究回答了这个问题。

paras.en: One of the two key factors the research team discovered is sameness, specifically sharing the same gender or ethnic origin.
paras.zh: 研究团队发现的两个关键因素之一是相同性，具体来说，就是性别或族裔相同。

paras.en: The more members of a team share similar demographics, the more inclined they’ll be to remain associates long after the team has served its purpose.
paras.zh: 团队成员的人口特征越相似，他们就越愿意在团队完成任务之后很久仍然保持合作伙伴的关系。

paras.en: After ties are established, similarity strengthens them.
paras.zh: 关系一旦建立，相似性就会让它更牢固。

paras.en: As a result, they regard these individuals with greater trust and mutual understanding, which motivates them to seek further opportunities for collaboration.
paras.zh: 因此，他们对这些人更信任、更理解，这又促使他们去寻找更多合作的机会。

paras.en: In effect, people tend to create stronger and longer-lasting connections with similar others.
paras.zh: 实际上，人们往往会和与自己相似的人建立更牢固、更长久的关系。

paras.en: Someone who looks and sounds different from us may have the resources we need to be more successful, yet we find them to be significantly less credible simply because they are different.
paras.zh: 一个在外表和说话上跟我们不一样的人，也许拥有能让我们更成功的资源，可我们仅仅因为他们跟我们不一样，就觉得他们远没那么可信。

paras.en: If you are a fierce advocate of workplace diversity, you’ll no doubt be horrified by such a revelation.
paras.zh: 如果你是职场多元化的坚定拥护者，这样的发现无疑会让你大吃一惊。

paras.en: The second factor identified by the researchers is the quality of the relationships among the team members.
paras.zh: 研究人员找出的第二个因素是团队成员之间关系的质量。

paras.en: The more they trust one another, share the same goals, and depend on each other for the achievement of those goals, the stronger their chances of maintaining their connections despite no longer working as one team.
paras.zh: 他们越是彼此信任、目标一致，越是相互依靠来实现这些目标，即使不再作为一个团队工作，他们保持联系的可能性也就越大。

paras.en: Teams with quality relationships have a shared belief that it’s safe to take risks with each other, and that members are obliged to share the workload and help out.
paras.zh: 关系好的团队有一个共同的信念：彼此之间冒险是安全的，而且成员有义务分担工作、互相帮忙。

paras.en: From personal experience, I can see both the truth and the inconsistency of such studies.
paras.zh: 根据我的亲身经历，我能看出这类研究既有道理，也有对不上的地方。

paras.en: The truth is, some of my closest friendships were formed as a result of having worked together on teams, and I actively seek opportunities to work with them again.
paras.zh: 说它有道理，是因为我最亲密的几段友情，有一些就是因为在团队里一起工作过才建立起来的，而且我也在主动找机会再和他们一起工作。

paras.en: The inconsistency, though, is that I’ve never worked for a team more successful and cohesive than the one of which I’m a member right now, and yet the four of us have very little in common and are completely different demographically.
paras.zh: 说它对不上，是因为我从来没在比现在这个团队更成功、更有凝聚力的团队里工作过，可我们四个人几乎没有什么共同点，人口特征也完全不同。

w.m: adj. 有凝聚力的；团结的
adv. 在人口统计特征上

paras.en: So I’m unlikely to question the value of a diverse workforce.
paras.zh: 所以，我不大会去质疑多元化员工队伍的价值。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about a team with vitality?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于有活力的团队，说话人是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 20: What do the researchers find out about members of a team?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于团队成员，研究人员发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What do we learn about the team the speaker is currently working in?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于说话人现在所在的团队，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: An American researcher who studied 600 millionaires found how rich you can get comes down to six wealth factors.
paras.zh: 一位美国研究人员研究了六百位百万富翁，发现你能有多富归结起来取决于六个财富因素。

paras.en: She found that six behaviors are related to net worth potential, regardless of age or income.
paras.zh: 她发现，不论年龄或收入如何，有六种行为都与积累净资产的潜力有关。

paras.en: These were thriftiness, confidence, responsibility, planning, focus, and social indifference.
paras.zh: 它们是：节俭、自信、负责、有计划、专注，以及不在意社交眼光。

paras.en: Being thrifty comes as no great surprise.
paras.zh: 节俭这一点并不让人意外。

paras.en: Spending above your means, spending instead of saving for retirement, spending in anticipation of becoming wealthy, makes you a slave to the paycheck, even with an astronomical level of income.
paras.zh: 入不敷出地花钱，只顾花钱不为退休存钱，指望自己会发财就提前花钱，这些都会让你成为工资的奴隶，就算你的收入高得惊人也一样。

w.m: adj. 天文数字的；极大的

paras.en: She wrote, to properly build wealth, experts recommend saving 20% of your income and living off the remaining 80%.
paras.zh: 她写道，要想好好积累财富，专家建议存下百分之二十的收入，靠剩下的百分之八十过日子。

paras.en: Having confidence is another key characteristic, as it helps people to be thrifty.
paras.zh: 自信是另一个关键特点，因为它能帮人做到节俭。

paras.en: It takes confidence to live within your means.
paras.zh: 量入为出需要自信。

paras.en: It also takes confidence to invest properly.
paras.zh: 好好投资也需要自信。

paras.en: Instead of making investing decisions with your emotions, financial planners advise that you should leave your investments alone and focus on a long-term investment plan.
paras.zh: 理财规划师建议，不要凭情绪做投资决定，而应该把投资放着别动，专注于一个长期的投资计划。

paras.en: But people can’t invest or manage their own money without accepting responsibility for the outcomes.
paras.zh: 但是，人们要是不对结果负起责任，就没法投资或管理自己的钱。

paras.en: Many millionaires take on personal responsibility, and most also happen to be self-made, meaning they didn’t acquire their wealth through luck.
paras.zh: 许多百万富翁都自己承担责任，而且大多数恰好也是白手起家的，也就是说，他们的财富不是靠运气得来的。

paras.en: Millionaires don’t count on anyone else to make them rich, and they don’t blame anyone else if they fall short.
paras.zh: 百万富翁不指望别人让自己发财，如果没达到目标，也不怪罪别人。

paras.en: They focus on things they can control and align their daily habits to the goals they have set for themselves.
paras.zh: 他们专注于自己能掌控的事情，让日常习惯和给自己定下的目标保持一致。

paras.en: They tend to be goal-oriented and hard workers, which enables them to plan financially and focus on seeing those plans through.
paras.zh: 他们往往目标明确、工作勤奋，这让他们能做好财务规划，并专心把计划执行到底。

w.m: adj. 目标明确的；以目标为导向的

paras.en: 92% of millionaires surveyed developed a long-term plan for their money, and 97 percent almost always achieved the goals they set for themselves.
paras.zh: 接受调查的百万富翁中，百分之九十二为自己的钱制订了长期计划，百分之九十七几乎总能实现给自己定下的目标。

paras.en: And it is these behaviors that make it easy for them to be socially indifferent.
paras.zh: 正是这些行为让他们很容易做到不在意社交眼光。

paras.en: They resist lifestyle creep, the tendency to spend more whenever one earns more.
paras.zh: 他们能抵制“生活方式蠕变”，也就是赚得越多、花得越多的倾向。

w.m: 生活方式蠕变（收入涨了开销也跟着涨）

paras.en: Essentially, they don’t yield to pressure to buy the latest thing or to keep up with others or what they have acquired.
paras.zh: 说到底，他们不会迫于压力去买最新的东西，也不会去跟别人或别人拥有的东西攀比。

paras.en: Instead of being focused on what might make them happy today, they’re focused on their long-term wealth-building plan.
paras.zh: 他们关注的不是什么能让自己今天开心，而是自己长期的财富积累计划。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do experts recommend concerning being thrifty?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：关于节俭，专家有什么建议？

paras.en: Question 23: How does confidence help people to be thrifty?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：自信是怎样帮助人们做到节俭的？

paras.en: Question 24: How do millionaires react when they fail in their investment?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：百万富翁投资失败时会怎么做？

paras.en: Question 25: Why does the speaker say millionaires are socially indifferent?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人为什么说百万富翁不在意社交眼光？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2022年12月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2022年12月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，两位研究生谈毕业论文：女士因为找不到足够的资料，迟迟没法动笔，男士劝她听导师的，把题目放宽。第二段长对话里，读书节目主持人采访畅销书作家约翰·罗宾斯，谈他讲美国人为什么会胖、怎样减肥的新书。第一篇短文讲适度的压力对大脑和身体都有好处：能增强记忆，还能提高免疫力。第二篇短文讲管理者被电子邮件牵着走，顾不上管人，解决办法是培养自制力。第一段录音介绍营销学教授的研究：让健康食品看起来诱人、吃起来愉快，比强调营养更能改善饮食。第二段录音讲环保家用清洁产品的兴起及其原因。第三段录音讲人们扔进许愿池的硬币最后都去了哪里。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two: Listening Comprehension, Section A: Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: How’s your dissertation going?
paras.zh: 你的毕业论文写得怎么样了？

paras.en: I’m proofreading my first draft, and will submit it to my professor tomorrow.
paras.zh: 我在校对初稿，明天就交给导师。

paras.en: Oh, I haven’t even started writing mine yet, so I’m really worried about finishing by the end of next semester.
paras.zh: 哦，我的还没开始动笔呢，所以特别担心下学期末之前写不完。

paras.en: You mean you haven’t even begun yours yet?
paras.zh: 你是说你的还没开始写？

paras.en: The final draft is due in five months.
paras.zh: 定稿五个月后就要交了。

paras.en: Of course, I’ve started it, but I can’t get to the writing yet as I haven’t found enough resources to use, so I’m still researching the topic.
paras.zh: 当然开始了，可我还没法动笔写，因为能用的资料还没找够，所以还在研究这个题目。

paras.en: Maybe the problem is the way you’re doing your research.
paras.zh: 也许问题出在你做研究的方法上。

paras.en: I started by talking to my professor about where to look for information, and based on that, I found books in the library and a lot of reputable journal articles on the internet.
paras.zh: 我一开始先跟导师聊了聊该去哪儿找资料，然后照他说的，在图书馆找到了一些书，在网上找到了很多权威期刊的论文。

paras.en: I’ve tried all that, but don’t have enough to write the dissertation, as my department’s minimum length is 70 pages.
paras.zh: 这些我都试过了，可还是不够写论文的，我们系规定论文最少要七十页。

paras.en: I think the problem is that my topic isn’t viable, and honestly, my professor did warn me at the beginning that I might not be able to find enough material, but I was so interested in the topic that I didn’t let his advice deter me.
paras.zh: 我觉得问题在于我的题目不可行。说实话，导师一开始确实提醒过我，可能找不到足够的资料，可我对这个题目太感兴趣了，没让他的建议拦住我。

w.m: adj. 可行的；切实可行的

paras.en: Well, I suggest you find a new topic.
paras.zh: 嗯，我建议你换个新题目。

paras.en: After all, our professors are here to guide us, so it’s best to listen to them.
paras.zh: 毕竟导师就是来指导我们的，所以最好还是听他们的。

paras.en: In retrospect, I wish I had listened to him, but I didn’t, and now I don’t want to give up my topic as I’ve already invested so much time and energy.
paras.zh: 现在回想起来，我真希望当初听了他的话，可我没听。现在我又不想放弃这个题目，因为已经投入了那么多时间和精力。

paras.en: If you’re committed to your current topic, maybe you could make some adjustments rather than abandoning it completely.
paras.zh: 如果你非要坚持现在这个题目，也许可以做些调整，不用完全放弃。

paras.en: What is your topic?
paras.zh: 你的题目是什么？

paras.en: It’s depictions of femininity and folklore from the south of the country.
paras.zh: 是关于本国南方民间传说里对女性气质的描绘。

w.m: n. 女性气质；女性特质

paras.en: That’s pretty narrow.
paras.zh: 这个范围挺窄的。

paras.en: You could find more material if you made the topic broader, maybe by including other kinds of depictions.
paras.zh: 要是把题目放宽一点，比如把别的描绘也加进来，你就能找到更多资料了。

paras.en: Broadening the topic is a great idea.
paras.zh: 放宽题目真是个好主意。

paras.en: I’ll start by including folklore from other regions of the country.
paras.zh: 我先把本国其他地区的民间传说也加进来。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the woman say about her dissertation?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于自己的毕业论文，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say about his professor?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于自己的导师，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman say about her professor?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于自己的导师，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What do we learn the woman will do to complete her dissertation?
paras.zh: 第四题：从对话中我们了解到，女士要怎样才能完成论文？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Today on Book Talk, we are lucky enough to host John Robbins and discuss his new book, Why Americans Are Fat and How We Can Lose Weight.
paras.zh: 今天的《图书漫谈》节目很荣幸请到了约翰·罗宾斯，跟我们聊聊他的新书《美国人为什么会胖，我们又该怎样减肥》。

paras.en: John isn’t just a respected writer; he’s also one of the rare celebrity authors writing about science today.
paras.zh: 约翰不只是一位受人尊敬的作家，他还是当今为数不多的写科学的名人作家之一。

paras.en: Thanks for having me, Rebecca.
paras.zh: 谢谢你邀请我，丽贝卡。

paras.en: But I’m hardly a celebrity.
paras.zh: 不过我可算不上什么名人。

paras.en: That’s very modest of you to say, considering that your four books have sold a total of 7 million copies worldwide, and they’ve been translated into 12 different languages.
paras.zh: 您太谦虚了，您的四本书在全球一共卖出了七百万册，还被译成了十二种语言。

paras.en: What makes people so fascinated with your work?
paras.zh: 为什么大家对您的作品这么着迷呢？

paras.en: Well, people read my books because more than 60% of Americans are overweight or obese, and other countries are facing similar problems.
paras.zh: 嗯，大家读我的书，是因为超过百分之六十的美国人超重或者肥胖，别的国家也面临类似的问题。

paras.en: Basically, we all want to know how to fix things.
paras.zh: 说到底，我们都想知道怎么解决问题。

paras.en: We certainly do.
paras.zh: 确实如此。

paras.en: I’ve read your new book, and it’s fabulous, especially when it comes to the way you make difficult science easy for laymen to understand.
paras.zh: 我读了您的新书，写得太棒了，尤其是您能把深奥的科学讲得让外行也看得懂。

w.m: n. 外行；门外汉（layman 的复数）

paras.en: That’s no small achievement.
paras.zh: 这可不是件容易的事。

paras.en: I’m glad to hear you find my work accessible, because I was worried, when I wrote it, that discussing the science might make the book more suited for a specialist audience.
paras.zh: 听到你觉得我的书好懂，我很高兴，因为写书的时候我一直担心，讲科学会让这本书更适合专业读者。

w.m: adj. 易懂的；容易理解的

paras.en: My last book was written primarily for the medical community, but this time, I want to help ordinary people take control of their weight.
paras.zh: 我上一本书主要是写给医学界看的，可这一次，我想帮普通人管住自己的体重。

paras.en: And how do you suggest they do that?
paras.zh: 那您建议他们怎么做呢？

paras.en: Can you give us the basics of your advice for people who want to lose weight, briefly, I argue that every person needs to consider their metabolism and eat what suits their body’s needs.
paras.zh: 能给我们简单讲讲您给想减肥的人的建议要点吗？——简单地说，我认为每个人都要考虑自己的新陈代谢，吃适合自己身体需要的东西。

paras.en: I don’t advocate one single diet.
paras.zh: 我不提倡只用一种饮食方案。

paras.en: Some people should eat more carbohydrates than others, and different people need different amounts of protein and fat.
paras.zh: 有些人应该比别人多吃碳水化合物，不同的人需要的蛋白质和脂肪的量也不一样。

paras.en: But you do have some recommendations for everyone, including eating 10 servings of vegetables and three of fruit a day.
paras.zh: 不过您确实也有一些适合所有人的建议，比如每天吃十份蔬菜、三份水果。

paras.en: We’ll talk about those recommendations next.
paras.zh: 下面我们就来谈谈这些建议。

paras.en: But now we need to take a short break for a message from our sponsor.
paras.zh: 不过现在先休息一下，插播一段赞助商的广告。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the woman say about the man in her introduction?
paras.zh: 第五题：女士在介绍中是怎么说男士的？

paras.en: Question six: What has motivated the man to write his books?
paras.zh: 第六题：是什么促使男士写书的？

paras.en: Question seven: Who does the man say his last book was mainly written for?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士说他上一本书主要是写给谁看的？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the man recommend people do?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士建议人们做什么？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Stress is often depicted as negative, but research shows that moderate amounts of it can be beneficial for your brain and your body.
paras.zh: 压力常被说成坏事，可研究表明，适度的压力对大脑和身体都有好处。

paras.en: First, the benefits for the brain.
paras.zh: 先说对大脑的好处。

paras.en: Studies have shown that short periods of stress can actually bolster cognitive functioning.
paras.zh: 研究表明，短时间的压力其实能增强认知功能。

paras.en: Researchers discovered that placing rats in a stressful situation for just a few hours doubled the growth of new brain cells.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，把老鼠放在有压力的环境里只要几个小时，新生的脑细胞就增加了一倍。

paras.en: The rats also did better on a memory test later on.
paras.zh: 这些老鼠后来在记忆测试中的表现也更好。

paras.en: Scientists think the same thing happens in humans.
paras.zh: 科学家认为，人身上也会发生同样的情况。

paras.en: But how does stress improve memory?
paras.zh: 可压力是怎么增强记忆的呢？

paras.en: It’s simple.
paras.zh: 很简单。

paras.en: When your brain cells multiply, your memory can improve.
paras.zh: 脑细胞增多了，记忆力就可能增强。

paras.en: Viewed from a biological perspective, this makes sense because animals that are better at remembering dangerous situations can avoid them in the future.
paras.zh: 从生物学的角度看，这是说得通的，因为越能记住危险情况的动物，以后就越能躲开危险。

paras.en: If an animal encounters a predator and escapes, for example, it’s important to remember where and when that encounter happened.
paras.zh: 比如说，一只动物遇到捕食者后逃脱了，那么记住这次遭遇发生在哪里、什么时候就很重要。

paras.en: Experts assert that the same principle applies to humans.
paras.zh: 专家断言，这个原理同样适用于人类。

paras.en: Now let’s turn to how stress benefits the body.
paras.zh: 下面我们来看压力对身体有什么好处。

paras.en: This may come as a surprise to laymen, but experts say that stress can keep you from getting sick.
paras.zh: 外行人听了也许会感到意外，但专家说，压力能让你不生病。

w.m: n. 外行；门外汉（layman 的复数）

paras.en: Scientists concede that chronic stress can make you more prone to illness, but research shows that short periods of stress can actually provide some protection against getting sick, because it increases your immune functioning.
paras.zh: 科学家承认，长期的压力会让人更容易生病，但研究表明，短时间的压力其实能起到一定的防病作用，因为它能提高免疫功能。

paras.en: One study shows that rats that experienced brief stress had a surge of immune cell response, which makes the immune system better prepared to fight illness.
paras.zh: 一项研究表明，经历过短暂压力的老鼠，免疫细胞反应会激增，这让免疫系统更有准备去对抗疾病。

paras.en: For humans, there is even evidence that experiencing stress before getting vaccinated could help make vaccines more effective.
paras.zh: 至于人，甚至还有证据表明，打疫苗之前经历一点压力，可能有助于让疫苗更有效。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What did researchers discover about rats placed briefly in a stressful situation?
paras.zh: 第九题：把老鼠短暂放进有压力的环境里，研究人员有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 10: Why do people tend to have clearer memories of dangerous situations they have encountered?
paras.zh: 第十题：人们为什么往往对自己遇到过的危险情况记得更清楚？

paras.en: Question 11: What do scientists believe chronic stress can do?
paras.zh: 第十一题：科学家认为长期的压力会带来什么后果？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: For many managers and people who work in leadership positions, dealing with emails is a dilemma.
paras.zh: 对许多经理和担任领导职务的人来说，处理电子邮件是个难题。

paras.en: It’s likely the unpredictable, uncontrollable, and ongoing nature of day-to-day email, in terms of volume, importance, and urgency, contributes to their levels of anxiety, and to diminished leadership skills.
paras.zh: 每天的邮件在数量、重要程度和紧急程度上都难以预料、难以控制，而且没完没了，这很可能加重了他们的焦虑，也削弱了他们的领导能力。

paras.en: That’s because it’s not unusual for many leaders to prioritize email management over people management.
paras.zh: 这是因为，很多领导把管邮件看得比管人还重要，这种情况并不少见。

paras.en: An obsession with managing their inbox prevents them from dealing with their employees.
paras.zh: 他们一门心思管理收件箱，就顾不上处理员工的事了。

paras.en: As a result, they ignore the issues that might only be mild problems at first, until, unfortunately, they inevitably transform into a major problem or crisis by virtue of neglect.
paras.zh: 结果，他们对那些一开始可能只是小毛病的问题不闻不问，可惜到后来，因为没人管，这些问题必然会变成大问题，甚至危机。

w.m: adv. 必然地；不可避免地

paras.en: As leaders, they are expected to motivate and inspire their team in pursuit of longer-term strategic goals, and also, less ambitiously but more practically, to monitor their daily output, to set clear expectations, and to give regular feedback.
paras.zh: 作为领导，人们期望他们激励、鼓舞团队去追求长远的战略目标；还有一些没那么远大但更实际的事：监督团队每天的产出，提出明确的要求，经常给出反馈。

paras.en: When presented with a choice between the appeal of their inbox and other more important activities, many sacrifice the latter.
paras.zh: 一边是收件箱的吸引力，一边是其他更重要的工作，要他们二选一时，很多人会牺牲后者。

paras.en: Daily email demands have a negative impact on their goal progress.
paras.zh: 每天要处理的邮件会拖累他们实现目标的进度。

paras.en: This is because leaders must divert resources from other tasks to check, filter, and respond to emails.
paras.zh: 这是因为领导必须把本该用在别的工作上的精力挪过来，去查看、筛选和回复邮件。

paras.en: The solution is cultivating self-control, which is like a muscle.
paras.zh: 解决办法是培养自制力，自制力就像肌肉一样。

paras.en: It can be strengthened or improved over time through exercise.
paras.zh: 它可以通过锻炼慢慢增强、提高。

paras.en: Some suggestions include making space in your diary for the only periods during which you’ll be checking emails, setting a timer for yourself so you don’t become distracted by your inbox for too long, turning off email alerts so you’re not interrupted by them.
paras.zh: 一些建议包括：在日程本上专门留出几段查邮件的时间，只在这些时间里查邮件；给自己定个闹钟，免得被收件箱分心太久；关掉邮件提醒，免得被它打断。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the speaker say is a common problem with managers?
paras.zh: 第十二题：说话人说经理们普遍有什么问题？

paras.en: Question 13: What may happen when managers ignore minor problems?
paras.zh: 第十三题：经理们不理会小问题会有什么后果？

paras.en: Question 14: What are leaders expected to do in pursuing their strategic goals?
paras.zh: 第十四题：人们期望领导在追求战略目标时做什么？

paras.en: Question 15: How can a manager best avoid being distracted by email?
paras.zh: 第十五题：经理怎样才能最好地避免被电子邮件分心？

paras.en: Section C. Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: In last week’s lecture, we talked about the problems caused by poor eating habits, focusing on how medical professionals are trying to solve these problems.
paras.zh: 上周的课上，我们讲了不良饮食习惯带来的问题，重点讲了医学专业人士在怎样设法解决这些问题。

w.m: 医学专业人士；医务人员

paras.en: Today, we’ll continue with the topic, but focus on research from a different field: marketing.
paras.zh: 今天我们继续讲这个话题，不过重点讲另一个领域的研究：市场营销。

paras.en: Now, what can marketing tell us about improving nutrition?
paras.zh: 那么，营销学能告诉我们哪些改善营养的方法呢？

paras.en: Well, a team of marketing professors has studied the importance of the visual aspect of food, and how that influences food choices.
paras.zh: 嗯，一个营销学教授团队研究了食物外观的重要性，以及外观怎样影响人们对食物的选择。

paras.en: Those marketing experts assert that the impact of the appearance of food is greater than we might presume, and might hold the key to encouraging better eating.
paras.zh: 这些营销专家断言，食物外观的影响比我们想象的要大，可能正是鼓励人们吃得更好的关键。

paras.en: So, how important is the appearance of food?
paras.zh: 那么，食物的外观到底有多重要呢？

paras.en: Research shows that just seeing an appealing photograph of a hamburger in an advertisement, for example, can cause individuals to imagine the taste or smell of that hamburger.
paras.zh: 研究表明，比如说，光是在广告里看到一张诱人的汉堡照片，就能让人想象出那个汉堡的味道或香味。

paras.en: This can make them more likely to purchase and consume it.
paras.zh: 这会让他们更有可能去买来吃。

paras.en: Of course, that’s the point of advertisements.
paras.zh: 当然，广告的目的就在于此。

paras.en: So, isn’t that a good thing?
paras.zh: 那么，这难道不是件好事吗？

paras.en: Well, the marketing professors argue that this is actually a problem, because the combination of pleasing aesthetics of and easy access to unhealthy foods such as hamburgers and pizza may be contributing to a worldwide health crisis.
paras.zh: 嗯，这些营销学教授认为，这其实是个问题，因为汉堡、比萨这类不健康的食物既好看又容易买到，两样加在一起，可能正在加剧一场全球性的健康危机。

w.m: adj. 令人愉快的；讨人喜欢的

paras.en: In fact, statistics show that 39 percent of all adults in the world weigh too much, and another 13 percent are obese.
paras.zh: 事实上，统计数据显示，全世界所有成年人中有百分之三十九超重，另有百分之十三肥胖。

paras.en: Now, as we discussed last time, medical professionals have tried to fight the obesity epidemic by focusing on the nutrients found in different foods, emphasizing things like carbohydrate, fat, sugar, and calorie content, but they’ve had limited success.
paras.zh: 上次我们讲过，医学专业人士一直想通过关注不同食物所含的营养成分来对抗肥胖的流行，强调碳水化合物、脂肪、糖和卡路里的含量这些东西，可收效甚微。

w.m: 医学专业人士；医务人员

paras.en: The marketing professors believe that the real solution to obesity is making food look appealing and focusing on the pleasure of both looking at and eating that food.
paras.zh: 这些营销学教授认为，真正解决肥胖问题的办法是让食物看起来诱人，同时注重看食物、吃食物带来的愉悦。

paras.en: That pleasure can be used as a tool to promote healthy food choices.
paras.zh: 这种愉悦可以用作一种手段，来促使人们选择健康食品。

paras.en: In fact, the research done by the team showed that associating healthy food with pleasant images, experiences, and emotions led to greater interest in purchasing or eating it.
paras.zh: 事实上，这个团队的研究表明，把健康食品同美好的画面、经历和情感联系起来，会让人们更想买来吃。

paras.en: This is a better strategy, they claim, than reminding consumers that a certain food is good for them.
paras.zh: 他们说，这比提醒消费者某种食物对他们有好处更管用。

paras.en: But are they right?
paras.zh: 可他们说得对吗？

paras.en: Well, the researchers cited a marketing campaign designed to reverse the sales decline of carrots.
paras.zh: 嗯，研究人员举了一个营销活动的例子，这个活动是为了扭转胡萝卜销量下滑的局面。

paras.en: The campaign didn’t emphasize the carrots’ healthy qualities, but embraced their beauty and the pleasure derived from eating them.
paras.zh: 这次活动没有强调胡萝卜对健康有好处，而是突出它的美，以及吃胡萝卜带来的乐趣。

paras.en: For example, the ads focused on the bright, beautiful orange color and crisp texture of the carrots.
paras.zh: 比如，广告重点展示胡萝卜鲜亮漂亮的橙色和脆生生的口感。

paras.en: The campaign led to an impressive increase in product sales of more than 10%.
paras.zh: 这次活动让产品销量大增，涨了百分之十以上。

paras.en: The researchers believe that other companies could bolster sales of healthy foods with similar ads, depicting their products as attractive and a source of pleasure.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，其他公司也可以做类似的广告，把自己的产品塑造成既好看又能带来愉悦的东西，以此提高健康食品的销量。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say a team of marketing professors has studied?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人说一个营销学教授团队研究了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: How have medical professionals tried to fight obesity?
paras.zh: 第十七题：医学专业人士是怎样设法对抗肥胖的？

w.m: 医学专业人士；医务人员

paras.en: Question 18: What can other companies learn from the example of the carrot promotion campaign?
paras.zh: 第十八题：其他公司能从胡萝卜促销活动的例子中学到什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: The household cleaning products industry really began to take off in the 1950s.
paras.zh: 家用清洁产品行业是在二十世纪五十年代真正开始兴起的。

paras.en: Prior to that, resourceful housewives who had grown up in a less prosperous era relied on substances that they used in their kitchens, such as vinegar used to clean windows.
paras.zh: 在那之前，在不那么富裕的年代长大的家庭主妇们很会想办法，用的是厨房里的东西，比如用醋擦窗户。

w.m: adj. 足智多谋的；会想办法的

paras.en: Today, the household cleaning products industry is worth billions of dollars a year, and is dominated by large global companies.
paras.zh: 如今，家用清洁产品行业每年的产值达数十亿美元，由几家全球大公司主导。

paras.en: In recent years, however, many countries have witnessed a surge in the number of small businesses and companies offering more environment-friendly cleaning products, and they’re doing good business too.
paras.zh: 不过近年来，许多国家都出现了大量提供更环保清洁产品的小企业和公司，它们的生意也做得不错。

paras.en: One reason for this is that consumers are becoming more aware of environment and sustainability issues.
paras.zh: 原因之一是消费者越来越关注环境问题和可持续发展问题。

paras.en: They also want to make their home a safe place, free from toxic chemicals.
paras.zh: 他们还想让自己的家成为一个安全的地方——不含有毒化学物质。

paras.en: The third reason is people’s awareness of and knowledge about technology has never been greater.
paras.zh: 第三个原因是，人们对科技的认识和了解从来没有像现在这么多。

paras.en: In the past, people might have been skeptical of a new product claimed to be able to achieve amazing cleaning results, but they now have faith in technology’s ability to do what was once thought impossible.
paras.zh: 过去，如果有新产品声称能达到惊人的清洁效果，人们可能会将信将疑，可现在他们相信科技能做到过去被认为不可能的事。

paras.en: There is perhaps no better example of this than a patented cloth sold by one company, which remarkably uses only water rather than traditional cleaning products.
paras.zh: 也许最好的例子莫过于一家公司卖的一种专利抹布，它居然只用清水，不用传统的清洁产品。

paras.en: The company claims its cloth lifts, traps, and removes dirt and bacteria.
paras.zh: 这家公司称，它的抹布能把污垢和细菌吸起来、粘住、清除掉。

paras.en: And considering that people don’t see these products in shops or advertised on TV or in the press, it has been a pretty steep rise.
paras.zh: 考虑到这些产品在商店里看不到，在电视和报刊上也没有广告，它们的销量涨得可谓相当快了。

paras.en: Many of the people behind these companies began testing the viability of their products by selling them at local markets.
paras.zh: 这些公司背后的很多人，一开始都是先在本地集市上卖产品，看看产品行不行得通。

paras.en: Then, in many cases, customers are doing the marketing for these products by leaving threads of comments on social media, praising their virtues.
paras.zh: 之后，很多时候是顾客在帮这些产品做营销：他们在社交媒体上留下一串串评论，称赞产品的优点。

paras.en: There are also TV shows and books dedicated to maintaining home tidiness and cleanliness, and the benefits of having a clean home.
paras.zh: 还有一些电视节目和书，专门讲怎样保持家里整洁干净，以及家里干净有什么好处。

paras.en: Having a safe and clean home might be one thing people feel they can control in an increasingly out of control world.
paras.zh: 在这个越来越失控的世界里，拥有一个安全干净的家，也许是人们觉得自己能掌控的一件事。

paras.en: And there are social media celebrities.
paras.zh: 还有一些社交媒体上的名人。

paras.en: One woman in Britain has become a social media sensation with more than 2 million followers for her cleaning tips page.
paras.zh: 英国有位女士凭着自己的清洁小窍门主页，在社交媒体上火了，粉丝超过两百万。

w.m: n. 轰动；引起轰动的人

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about the cleaning products industry in recent years?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于近年来的清洁产品行业，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: Why are newly developed cleaning products selling well?
paras.zh: 第二十题：新研发的清洁产品为什么卖得好？

paras.en: Question 21: What are some customers doing to help promote non-traditional cleaning products?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：一些顾客在做什么来帮助推广非传统的清洁产品？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Throwing spare change into a fountain is a time-honored ritual.
paras.zh: 往喷泉里扔零钱是一种由来已久的习俗。

w.m: adj. 由来已久的；历史悠久的

paras.en: Throw a penny into the water, and your wish might come true.
paras.zh: 往水里扔一枚硬币，你的愿望也许就会实现。

paras.en: But all that money has to go somewhere; otherwise, the growing piles of pennies, quarters, and euros could clog up the fountain’s works.
paras.zh: 可这些钱总得有个去处，不然越堆越多的一分硬币、二十五分硬币和欧元硬币，就可能把喷泉的设备堵住。

w.m: n. （机器的）运转部件；机械装置

paras.en: Today, I’m going to talk about where all the coins go.
paras.zh: 今天我要讲讲这些硬币都去了哪里。

paras.en: Well, the coins collected can go to all sorts of different places, from fountain maintenance to charity or public service.
paras.zh: 嗯，收上来的硬币去处五花八门，有的用于维护喷泉，有的捐给慈善机构或用于公共服务。

paras.en: In New York City, for example, coins collected from fountains in public parks often go towards the fountain’s maintenance itself, though entrepreneurs who don’t mind getting their hands wet often get to it first.
paras.zh: 比如在纽约市，从公园喷泉里收上来的硬币通常用于维护喷泉本身，不过那些不怕把手弄湿的“创业者”往往会抢先一步把硬币捞走。

paras.en: There are over 50 beautiful decorative display fountains in New York City parks.
paras.zh: 纽约市的公园里有五十多座漂亮的装饰性观赏喷泉。

paras.en: They are cleaned by the park’s staff every few weeks, but most of the coins have already been removed by entrepreneurial New Yorkers, and there is not a significant amount left to be collected.
paras.zh: 公园的工作人员每隔几周清理一次，可大部分硬币早就被那些会做生意的纽约人捞走了，剩下能收的已经不多了。

w.m: adj. 有创业精神的；会做生意的
adj. 相当数量的；重要的

paras.en: Other cities, though, can pull in a much more serious haul.
paras.zh: 不过，别的城市能收到的钱就可观多了。

w.m: n. 收获量；（偷得或捞得的）一批东西

paras.en: Take, for example, Rome’s famous Trevi Fountain.
paras.zh: 就拿罗马著名的特雷维喷泉来说吧。

paras.en: For hundreds of years, visitors have thrown coins over their shoulder into the fountain to ensure that they will return.
paras.zh: 几百年来，游客们一直背对着喷泉、越过肩膀把硬币抛进去，好保证自己以后还能再回来。

paras.en: So many tourists toss in coins that Roman officials have the fountain cleaned every night, reportedly getting as much as $4,000 in loose change from around the world each day.
paras.zh: 往里扔硬币的游客太多了，罗马官方每天晚上都要请人清理喷泉，据说每天能收到来自世界各地的零钱多达四千美元。

paras.en: Most of the money collected each night goes towards running a supermarket for the needy, and collecting that cash is serious business.
paras.zh: 每晚收上来的钱大部分用来经营一家给穷人开的超市，收这笔钱可是件严肃的事。

paras.en: Roman officials have been known to be tough on anyone caught skimming coins from the fountain.
paras.zh: 据了解，罗马官方对任何被抓到从喷泉里偷捞硬币的人都很严厉。

paras.en: In one case in 2005, police arrested four fountain cleaners after they were spotted slipping coins into their own pockets after collecting them.
paras.zh: 2005年有一次，警方逮捕了四名喷泉清洁工，因为有人发现他们把收上来的硬币偷偷塞进了自己的口袋。

paras.en: Authorities finally caught one notorious thief named Thomas Morgan and banned him from the fountain after he fished out thousands of dollars in change over 34 years using a magnetic stick.
paras.zh: 当局最终抓住了一个叫托马斯·摩根的惯偷，并禁止他再靠近这座喷泉，因为他三十四年来一直用一根磁棒捞零钱，捞走了好几千美元。

paras.en: For the most part, money collected from privately owned fountains in the United States also goes to charity.
paras.zh: 在美国，私人所有的喷泉里收上来的钱，大部分也捐给了慈善机构。

paras.en: The fountain in New York City’s Bryant Park is owned and operated by a not-for-profit corporation, which puts the cash collected by cleaners towards the fountain’s own maintenance.
paras.zh: 纽约市布莱恩特公园的喷泉归一家非营利公司所有并负责运营，这家公司把清洁工收上来的钱用于喷泉自身的维护。

paras.en: Tens of thousands of dollars in coins removed from wishing wells, fountains, and ponds in Florida’s Walt Disney World are donated each year to support foster children living in the state.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州沃尔特·迪士尼世界的许愿井、喷泉和池塘里，每年都能捞出价值几万美元的硬币，这些钱被捐出来，资助该州的寄养儿童。

paras.en: Whether or not your wish comes true after tossing a coin into a fountain, you can rest assured knowing that the change is likely going to someone who needs it.
paras.zh: 不管你往喷泉里扔了硬币之后愿望能不能实现，你都可以放心：这些零钱很可能会到需要它的人手里。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What problem might be caused by the growing piles of coins in fountains?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：喷泉里越堆越多的硬币可能会带来什么问题？

w.m: adj. 越来越多的；增长的

paras.en: Question 23: What does the speaker say about the coins collected from New York City’s park fountains?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于从纽约市公园喷泉里收上来的硬币，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What do we learn about the money collected from Rome’s Trevi Fountain?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于从罗马特雷维喷泉里收上来的钱，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker say about Thomas Morgan?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：关于托马斯·摩根，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2022年12月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2022年12月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，读书节目主持人采访理财畅销书作者苏珊·莱恩，她主张把幸福放在金钱前面，改变价值观，花钱的习惯也就跟着变了。第二段长对话里，美术馆馆长克里斯托弗带凯瑟琳参观画家丹妮尔·格雷戈里的新藏风景画，还邀她当晚一起去见画家。第一篇短文讲宽恕：宽恕不等于和好，它对身心健康有益，也讲了怎样宽恕别人、宽恕自己。第二篇短文介绍格拉斯哥地铁一百多年来的兴衰和现代化改造。第一段录音讲国家公园里的熊不再怕人，游客喂熊既违法又危险。第二段录音讲偏见是怎样形成的、有什么危害，以及我们该怎样克服偏见。第三段录音里，一位中学老师回忆自己从上高中、参加越战到重新振作、走上讲台的经历。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two: Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解。

paras.en: Section A: Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with the single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Welcome to the book club.
paras.zh: 欢迎收听读书俱乐部节目。

paras.en: Today’s guest is Susan Lane, the author of a new book on personal finances that has already sold half a million copies.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是苏珊·莱恩，她写了一本讲个人理财的新书，已经卖出了五十万册。

paras.en: Hi, Susan, your book is extremely successful.
paras.zh: 你好，苏珊，你的书特别成功。

paras.en: Why do you think that is?
paras.zh: 你觉得为什么会这样呢？

paras.en: I think that’s because of my message, which is making happiness a priority over money.
paras.zh: 我觉得是因为书里传达的理念：把幸福放在金钱前面。

w.m: n. 主旨；要传达的信息

paras.en: So many of us in my generation have spent decades trying to earn more money just to consume more, but it made us more miserable.
paras.zh: 我们这一代人里，很多人几十年来拼命挣更多的钱，只是为了花得更多，可这反而让我们更不快乐了。

paras.en: You yourself were once caught in that cycle, working for two decades as an executive and earning a high salary, but still accumulating debt.
paras.zh: 你自己也曾经陷在这个怪圈里：当了二十年高管，薪水很高，却还是越欠越多。

paras.en: I most certainly was.
paras.zh: 一点没错，我就是这样。

paras.en: I earned millions, but by the time I quit my job four years ago to become a writer, I owed over $30,000.
paras.zh: 我挣过几百万，可到四年前辞职当作家的时候，我还欠着三万多美元。

paras.en: So, how did you escape that pattern, and what would you advise other people to do?
paras.zh: 那你是怎么跳出这个怪圈的？你会建议别人怎么做呢？

paras.en: The first change is in what we value.
paras.zh: 首先要改变的是我们看重什么。

paras.en: We need to emphasize things that actually make us happy, like relationships, the environment, or even our hobbies.
paras.zh: 我们要重视那些真正让我们快乐的东西，比如人际关系、环境，甚至我们的爱好。

paras.en: Once we make the right things our priority, our goals will change, and so will our financial behavior.
paras.zh: 一旦把该看重的东西放在首位，我们的目标就会改变，花钱的方式也会跟着变。

paras.en: How does that translate into practical action?
paras.zh: 那具体该怎么做呢？

paras.en: Can you give our audience examples of what you’re talking about on an everyday basis, the major areas for action are usually housing, food, and transportation.
paras.zh: 能给听众举几个例子，说说你讲的具体是什么吗？——在日常生活中，需要着手的主要是住房、饮食和交通这几方面。

paras.en: So people might share a home with friends instead of living on their own, bring lunch from home instead of going to restaurants, and use public transport instead of owning a car.
paras.zh: 所以，人们可以跟朋友合住，不必自己一个人住；可以从家里带午饭，不必去餐馆吃；可以坐公共交通，不必自己买车。

paras.en: Those sound like major sacrifices.
paras.zh: 这些听起来都是很大的牺牲啊。

paras.en: I could never share my home.
paras.zh: 我可绝对没法跟别人合住。

paras.en: I need my own space.
paras.zh: 我需要自己的空间。

paras.en: But they aren’t sacrifices.
paras.zh: 可这些并不是牺牲。

paras.en: When people change their values, their desires change.
paras.zh: 人的价值观一变，想要的东西也就变了。

paras.en: So, in the example of housing, if we value relationships, sharing a home isn’t depriving ourselves of space, but giving us an opportunity to spend more time with our loved ones.
paras.zh: 就拿住房来说，如果我们看重人际关系，那么跟别人合住就不是剥夺自己的空间，而是给了我们一个机会，多陪陪我们爱的人。

paras.en: Indeed, it is.
paras.zh: 确实是这样。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What message does the woman convey in her book?
paras.zh: 第一题：女士在书中传达了什么理念？

w.m: n. 主旨；要传达的信息

paras.en: Question two: What do we learn about the woman before she became a writer?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于女士当作家之前的情况，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman say about one’s financial behavior?
paras.zh: 第三题：关于一个人花钱的方式，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man say about sharing a home?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于跟别人合住，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Thank you for inviting me to the gallery, Christopher.
paras.zh: 谢谢你请我来美术馆，克里斯托弗。

paras.en: I haven’t visited here since your predecessor’s retirement function.
paras.zh: 自从你前任的退休仪式以后，我就再没来过这里。

paras.en: Would you like to see the newest additions to our collection first, Catherine?
paras.zh: 凯瑟琳，你想先看看我们最新的藏品吗？

paras.en: Are those the landscapes by Danielle Gregory?
paras.zh: 是丹妮尔·格雷戈里的那几幅风景画吗？

paras.en: I absolutely adore her work.
paras.zh: 我太喜欢她的作品了。

paras.en: This first piece was a gift to the gallery from the artist herself, and it’s quite exquisite.
paras.zh: 这第一幅是画家本人送给美术馆的礼物，画得十分精美。

paras.en: I love how she depicts the barren landscape.
paras.zh: 我很喜欢她描绘荒凉景色的手法。

paras.en: The colors complement each other perfectly.
paras.zh: 这些颜色搭配得恰到好处。

w.m: adv. 完美地；恰到好处地

paras.en: You can sense the desolation in the picture.
paras.zh: 你能从画里感受到那种荒凉。

paras.en: This piece was inspired by Gregory’s recent trek in the Gobi Desert, and how did you obtain her other piece over here?
paras.zh: 这幅作品的灵感来自格雷戈里最近在戈壁沙漠的徒步旅行。——那这边她的另一幅作品，你们是怎么弄到的？

w.m: n. 艰苦跋涉；徒步旅行

paras.en: It was purchased at auction by an anonymous collector, who lent it to the gallery for display.
paras.zh: 是一位不愿透露姓名的收藏家在拍卖会上买下的，他把画借给美术馆展出。

w.m: v. 借给（lend 的过去式）

paras.en: This composition is one of her most acclaimed paintings.
paras.zh: 这幅作品是她最受赞誉的画作之一。

paras.en: It must have cost that collector a small fortune to purchase this.
paras.zh: 那位收藏家买下这幅画，一定花了一大笔钱吧。

paras.en: Obviously, I can’t disclose the exact amount he paid, but it was substantial.
paras.zh: 他到底花了多少钱，我当然不能透露，不过数目确实不小。

paras.en: There’s so much detail in this painting.
paras.zh: 这幅画的细节真丰富。

paras.en: I feel like I can really immerse myself in the scene.
paras.zh: 我觉得自己真的能融入画里的场景。

paras.en: I particularly like the symmetry created by the reflection of the mountain in the lake.
paras.zh: 我特别喜欢山在湖中的倒影营造出的那种对称感。

paras.en: This particular piece was the one that was nominated for a gateway award, I was lucky enough to attend the award ceremony as Gregory’s guest.
paras.zh: 正是这幅作品获得了“门户奖”提名，我很幸运，作为格雷戈里的嘉宾参加了颁奖典礼。

paras.en: So you know her personally.
paras.zh: 这么说你跟她私下认识。

paras.en: I assume she’s an eccentric artist.
paras.zh: 我猜她一定是个性情古怪的艺术家吧。

paras.en: Quite the opposite, in fact.
paras.zh: 其实正好相反。

paras.en: She’s not at all eccentric.
paras.zh: 她一点也不古怪。

paras.en: I would say she’s one of the most easygoing and intelligent people I know.
paras.zh: 要我说，她是我认识的人里最随和、最聪明的之一。

paras.en: I’d love to be able to meet her.
paras.zh: 我真想见见她。

w.m: 很想；非常愿意（’d love to = would love to）

paras.en: There are so many questions I’d like to ask.
paras.zh: 我有好多问题想问她。

paras.en: What a coincidence!
paras.zh: 真巧啊！

paras.en: I’m meeting her for dinner tonight.
paras.zh: 我今晚正要跟她一起吃饭。

paras.en: Would you like to come along?
paras.zh: 你想一起去吗？

paras.en: I’d love to.
paras.zh: 太好了，我很愿意。

w.m: 很想；非常愿意（’d love to = would love to）

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢你。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about one of the newest additions to the gallery’s collection?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于美术馆最新的一件藏品，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man say about one of the most acclaimed paintings by Danielle Gregory?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于丹妮尔·格雷戈里最受赞誉的一幅画，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: Why does the woman say she can feel immersed in the scene in the painting?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士为什么说她能融入画里的场景？

paras.en: Question eight: How does the man describe Danielle Gregory?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士是怎样描述丹妮尔·格雷戈里的？

paras.en: Section B. Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Forgiveness is the release of resentment or anger.
paras.zh: 宽恕就是放下怨恨或愤怒。

paras.en: Forgiveness doesn’t mean reconciliation.
paras.zh: 宽恕不等于和好。

paras.en: We don’t have to return to the same relationship, nor do we have to accept the same harmful behaviors from an offender.
paras.zh: 我们不必回到原来的关系里，也不必继续忍受伤害我们的人那些同样有害的行为。

paras.en: Forgiveness is vitally important for the mental health of certain victims, it propels people forward rather than keeping them emotionally engaged in an injustice or trauma.
paras.zh: 对某些受害者的心理健康来说，宽恕极其重要。它推动人们向前走，而不是让他们在情感上一直纠缠于不公或创伤之中。

paras.en: Carrying the hurt or anger of an offense leads the body to release stress chemicals.
paras.zh: 心里一直带着被冒犯后的伤痛或愤怒，会让身体释放压力激素。

paras.en: Eliminating the perpetual flow of those chemicals may also explain why forgiveness provides physical health benefits.
paras.zh: 不再让这些物质源源不断地分泌，也许正可以解释为什么宽恕对身体健康有好处。

paras.en: There are scenarios in which forgiveness is not the best course.
paras.zh: 也有一些情况下，宽恕并不是最好的做法。

paras.en: Sometimes a victim becomes more empowered when they give themselves permission not to forgive.
paras.zh: 有时候，受害者允许自己不去原谅，反而会变得更有力量。

w.m: adj. 有力量的；被赋予权力的

paras.en: Forgiveness can be challenging.
paras.zh: 宽恕可能很难。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: This is especially true when the offending party offers an insincere apology, or maybe they haven’t offered anything at all.
paras.zh: 如果犯错的一方道歉毫无诚意，或者根本就没有任何表示，那就更难了。

paras.en: However, it’s often the healthiest path forward.
paras.zh: 不过，这往往是对自己最健康的出路。

paras.en: It’s important to cultivate forgiveness by developing compassion for the offender.
paras.zh: 要学会宽恕，重要的是对犯错的人多一些同情。

paras.en: Reflect on whether the act was due to malicious intent, or whether it was caused by challenging circumstances in the offender’s life.
paras.zh: 想一想，对方这么做是出于恶意，还是因为生活中遇到了难处。

paras.en: What about forgiving ourselves?
paras.zh: 那原谅自己又该怎么做呢？

paras.en: We sometimes need to take responsibility for mistakes, but intense guilt and shame aren’t a desirable outcome in the long run.
paras.zh: 有时我们需要为错误承担责任，但从长远看，强烈的内疚和羞愧并不是我们想要的结果。

w.m: adj. 可取的；令人满意的

paras.en: Forgiving yourself may seem like an ambiguous process.
paras.zh: 原谅自己似乎是个说不太清的过程。

w.m: adj. 模棱两可的；不明确的

paras.en: You can begin by acknowledging that you are at fault.
paras.zh: 你可以先承认是自己错了。

paras.en: Take responsibility for the hurt you caused.
paras.zh: 为你造成的伤害承担责任。

paras.en: Then reflect on why the event occurred.
paras.zh: 然后想一想这件事为什么会发生。

paras.en: Draw the lessons you learned and try to avoid committing a similar offense in the future.
paras.zh: 总结学到的教训，争取以后不再犯类似的错误。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does the passage say about forgiveness?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于宽恕，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: When is forgiveness especially challenging?
paras.zh: 第十题：什么时候宽恕特别难？

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: Question 11: What should one do in order to forgive the offender?
paras.zh: 第十一题：要原谅冒犯自己的人，应该怎么做？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: The Glasgow subway first opened in 1896 as a cable-hauled system, it is generally recognized as the world’s third underground railway after London and Budapest.
paras.zh: 格拉斯哥地铁于1896年开通，最初是缆索牵引系统，人们普遍认为它是世界上继伦敦和布达佩斯之后的第三条地铁。

paras.en: In its long history, it has never been expanded, remaining as a single loop line with a mere 15 stations.
paras.zh: 在漫长的历史中，它从未扩建过，一直只是一条环线，只有区区十五个车站。

paras.en: At its peak, it served the shipyard workers on the south side of the city.
paras.zh: 在最鼎盛的时候，它为城南的造船厂工人服务。

paras.en: In the 1960s, there was a decline in the shipbuilding industry, and the popularity of private transport grew.
paras.zh: 到了二十世纪六十年代，造船业衰落，私人交通工具越来越普及。

paras.en: As a result, the subway saw a rapid decline in ridership.
paras.zh: 结果，地铁的客流量迅速下降。

paras.en: It ran with little further change until 1977, when its new operators closed it for major modernization investment.
paras.zh: 此后它一直运营，没再有什么改动，直到1977年，新的运营方把它关闭，投入大笔资金进行现代化改造。

paras.en: Carriages were replaced, ventilation was improved, and the main depot was also renovated and fitted with connecting tracks to replace the outdated crane transfer mechanism.
paras.zh: 车厢换了新的，通风改善了，主车库也经过翻修，还铺设了连接轨道，取代过时的起重机转运装置。

paras.en: The subway, in its present form, reopened for operation in April 1980.
paras.zh: 现在这个样子的地铁于1980年4月重新开放运营。

paras.en: Since its relaunch, the subway has seen a revival in its fortunes.
paras.zh: 重新开通以来，地铁的境况有了好转。

w.m: n. 重新推出；重新开通

paras.en: It serves as a viable alternative to other forms of transport, and has gone a long way to alleviate traffic jams in the city center.
paras.zh: 它成了其他交通方式之外一个切实可行的选择，大大缓解了市中心的交通拥堵。

paras.en: In 1996, the system reached an important milestone: 100 years.
paras.zh: 1996年，这个系统迎来了一个重要的里程碑：一百周年。

paras.en: To commemorate this special event, the color scheme of the train carriages was updated.
paras.zh: 为了纪念这个特别的日子，列车车厢换上了新的配色。

paras.en: Recently, high-tech systems such as smart card ticketing machines and smart gates are used across all subway stations.
paras.zh: 最近，所有地铁站都用上了智能卡售票机、智能闸机这类高科技系统。

paras.en: The smart card provides more convenient travel, and passengers simply top up their cards and tap them to get in and out the subway.
paras.zh: 智能卡让出行更方便，乘客只要给卡充值，进出地铁时刷一下就行。

paras.en: Since its launch, the technology has been adopted by more than 100,000 subway customers.
paras.zh: 这项技术推出以来，已经有十多万地铁乘客用上了它。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the passage say about the Glasgow subway in the 1960s?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于二十世纪六十年代的格拉斯哥地铁，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 13: Why was the Glasgow subway closed in 1977?
paras.zh: 第十三题：格拉斯哥地铁为什么在1977年关闭？

paras.en: Question 14: Why does the Glasgow subway remain important today?
paras.zh: 第十四题：为什么格拉斯哥地铁如今仍然很重要？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the passage say about all subway stations in Glasgow nowadays?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于如今格拉斯哥的所有地铁站，这篇短文说了什么？

paras.en: Section C: Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: If you visit the Great Smoky Mountains National Park, chances are you will remember the roadside or campground bears above all else.
paras.zh: 如果你去大雾山国家公园游玩，你最难忘的很可能是路边或营地里的熊。

paras.en: Bears are the most popular animals in a number of our national parks, in these mountains where the population of bears runs into the hundreds, opportunities to observe these large wild animals are plentiful during the summer.
paras.zh: 在我们的不少国家公园里，熊是最受欢迎的动物。在这片山区，熊的数量多达几百只，夏天有很多机会观察这些大型野生动物。

paras.en: Since national parks are wildlife sanctuaries where no disturbance of the native animals is allowed, years of protection have served to break down the wild bears’ fear of humans.
paras.zh: 由于国家公园是野生动物保护区，不允许打扰本地的动物，多年的保护让野生熊不再那么怕人了。

w.m: adj. 本地的；土生土长的

paras.en: Now, instead of depending on their own resources for a living, many bears patrol park roads and campgrounds.
paras.zh: 如今，许多熊不再靠自己觅食为生，而是在公园的道路和营地里转悠。

paras.en: They give the garbage cans a frequent going over, an occasional offer of food from a park visitor, an illegal and dangerous practice, makes beggars of them.
paras.zh: 它们经常翻垃圾桶；偶尔有游客给它们吃的——这种做法既违法又危险——就把它们变成了乞讨者。

paras.en: Bears are very often hungry, and since they will feed on almost any kind of plant or animal, garbage is quite acceptable.
paras.zh: 熊常常是饿着的，而且它们几乎什么植物、动物都吃，所以垃圾它们也完全能接受。

paras.en: Feeding them, however, represents misguided kindness because the bears come to expect such generosity from everyone, and consequently, trouble could lie ahead.
paras.zh: 不过，喂熊是一种用错了地方的好心，因为熊会指望每个人都这么大方，结果麻烦可能就在后面。

w.m: adj. 误入歧途的；用错地方的

paras.en: Park rules prohibit the feeding of bears; violators are arrested.
paras.zh: 公园规定禁止喂熊，违反者会被逮捕。

paras.en: Every year, doctors who have offices near the park treat a number of cases of bear bites and bear scratches.
paras.zh: 每年，在公园附近开诊所的医生都要处理一些被熊咬伤、抓伤的病例。

paras.en: Some of the accidents have come about in strange ways.
paras.zh: 有些事故发生得很离奇。

paras.en: One man was in the process of feeding two small cubs when the mother bear appeared and insisted upon having some of the food.
paras.zh: 有个男人正在喂两只小熊崽，这时熊妈妈出现了，非要分一些吃的不可。

paras.en: Shoving the big bear aside with one hand, the man continued feeding the cubs when suddenly he was struck a fierce blow in the face.
paras.zh: 他一只手把大熊推到一边，继续喂小熊，突然脸上就挨了狠狠一掌。

paras.en: A bear, prompted by the food that a lady kept offering to him, entered the car where the generous person was sitting.
paras.zh: 一位女士不停地给一只熊递吃的，那只熊被食物引诱，钻进了这位好心人坐着的车里。

paras.en: Her efforts to push the bear out of the car resulted in injuries.
paras.zh: 她想把熊推出车外，结果受了伤。

paras.en: A man required medical attention after he applied a lighted cigarette to a bear’s nose, another man tried to boost a bear into the front seat of his car so that he might take a picture of a bear sitting beside his wife, who was behind the wheel.
paras.zh: 有个男人把点着的香烟按到熊鼻子上，结果需要就医；还有个男人想把一只熊推上自己汽车的前座，好拍一张熊坐在他妻子旁边的照片，当时他妻子正坐在驾驶座上。

paras.en: Because bears prefer roads and campgrounds, the possibility of a hiker meeting up with a bear along park trails is small, but there’s always that chance.
paras.zh: 由于熊更喜欢待在道路和营地附近，徒步的人在公园小路上碰到熊的可能性很小，但总还是有可能的。

paras.en: For a bear seems to know if you are carrying a lunch or a candy bar, he may even insist on taking it.
paras.zh: 因为熊似乎知道你身上带没带午饭或巧克力棒，它甚至还可能非要抢走不可。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about the bears in national parks now?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于如今国家公园里的熊，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the speaker say about visitors feeding bears in national parks?
paras.zh: 第十七题：关于游客在国家公园里喂熊，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What is the speaker’s advice to people who carry some food while hiking on a park trail?
paras.zh: 第十八题：对于在公园小路上徒步时带着食物的人，说话人有什么建议？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Why do we form opinions or attitudes about someone or something without really knowing much about them?
paras.zh: 为什么我们对某个人或某件事并不真正了解，就形成了看法或态度？

paras.en: Just hearing something good or bad about a person, a place, or thing can influence our opinions positively or negatively.
paras.zh: 光是听到关于某个人、某个地方或某样东西的好话或坏话，就可能让我们的看法变好或变坏。

paras.en: But letting the opinions of another person determine what our opinions will be is dangerous.
paras.zh: 可是让别人的看法来决定我们自己的看法，是很危险的。

paras.en: Forming opinions about someone or something before really knowing them well is called prejudice.
paras.zh: 在真正了解某个人或某件事之前就对其形成看法，这叫作偏见。

paras.en: Pre means before, and judice refers to judgment.
paras.zh: 前缀pre的意思是“在……之前”，judice指的是“判断”。

paras.en: Hence, prejudice means to judge before having adequate knowledge.
paras.zh: 因此，偏见的意思就是在了解得还不够的时候就下判断。

paras.en: We can be prejudiced toward or against someone or something.
paras.zh: 我们对某个人或某件事的偏见，可能是偏向它，也可能是反对它。

paras.en: In either case, we are only allowing ourselves to see half of the picture.
paras.zh: 不管是哪种情况，我们都只让自己看到了事情的一半。

paras.en: Very few people or things in this world are all good or all bad.
paras.zh: 这世上，十全十美或一无是处的人和事都极少。

paras.en: Prejudiced attitudes are usually based on myths, half truths, or incorrect information, and they are dangerous because they can keep us from learning the truth about someone or something.
paras.zh: 带偏见的态度通常建立在谣传、片面之词或错误信息的基础上。它们很危险，因为它们会妨碍我们了解某个人或某件事的真相。

w.m: 片面之词；半真半假的话

paras.en: People form prejudices against others for many reasons: differences in their race, religion, gender, or occupation.
paras.zh: 人们对别人产生偏见的原因有很多：种族、宗教、性别或职业不同。

paras.en: Prejudices keep people apart; they keep us from really knowing and understanding each other.
paras.zh: 偏见让人们彼此疏远，让我们没法真正认识、理解对方。

paras.en: We should feel proud of who we are and the group of people we represent.
paras.zh: 我们应该为自己是谁、为自己所代表的群体感到自豪。

paras.en: If feelings of pride begin to turn to feelings of superiority when we think that our group or our beliefs are better than those around us.
paras.zh: 如果自豪感开始变成优越感，也就是我们觉得自己所在的群体或自己的信仰比周围人更好，

paras.en: However, then we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes that can be harmful.
paras.zh: 那么，我们就开始形成可能有害的偏见态度了。

paras.en: For example, the prejudiced attitudes of one group may keep another group from attending certain schools, from living in any neighborhood they want, or from getting a job or a promotion.
paras.zh: 比如，一个群体的偏见态度，可能让另一个群体上不了某些学校，没法住进自己想住的街区，或者找不到工作、得不到晋升。

paras.en: Extreme feelings of prejudice have caused the deaths of innocent people.
paras.zh: 极端的偏见曾经害死过无辜的人。

paras.en: We are responsible for our own thoughts and opinions.
paras.zh: 我们要为自己的想法和看法负责。

paras.en: When we let someone else tell us what to think about someone or something, we are giving up some control of our own lives.
paras.zh: 如果我们让别人告诉我们该怎样看待某个人或某件事，就等于放弃了对自己生活的一部分掌控权。

paras.en: Before you form an attitude or opinion, find out for yourself about the person or the thing in question.
paras.zh: 在形成某种态度或看法之前，先自己去了解一下所说的那个人或那件事。

paras.en: Sometimes we don’t realize that we hold prejudiced attitudes toward or against someone or something.
paras.zh: 有时候我们意识不到，自己对某个人或某件事抱有偏见，或偏向，或反对。

paras.en: We need to carefully examine our lives and our fears, and to ask ourselves whether our attitudes come from our personal knowledge and experience, or from rumors and fear of the unknown.
paras.zh: 我们需要认真审视自己的生活和恐惧，问问自己：我们的态度是来自亲身的了解和经历，还是来自谣言和对未知的恐惧。

paras.en: The good news about prejudice is that we are not born with it.
paras.zh: 关于偏见，好消息是我们并不是生来就有偏见的。

paras.en: Prejudiced attitudes and opinions develop over time, but with education and knowledge, we can replace our prejudices with cooperation and understanding.
paras.zh: 带偏见的态度和看法是慢慢形成的，但通过教育和了解，我们可以用合作和理解来取代偏见。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about prejudice?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于偏见，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: Why does the speaker say prejudiced attitudes are dangerous?
paras.zh: 第二十题：说话人为什么说带偏见的态度很危险？

paras.en: Question 21: When does the speaker say we begin to develop prejudiced attitudes?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说我们什么时候开始形成带偏见的态度？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: When I started high school, it was a shock.
paras.zh: 我刚上高中的时候，很受打击。

paras.en: I had spent eight years fighting my way to be the most popular kid in the Catholic school student body.
paras.zh: 我花了八年时间拼命奋斗，才成了那所天主教学校里最受欢迎的学生。

paras.en: I had been a big, tough eighth grader, and suddenly I was a lowly ninth grader bullied by the big, tough 12th-grade seniors who ran the high school.
paras.zh: 八年级时我又高又壮，是个厉害角色，可一下子就成了地位低下的九年级新生，被掌管着高中的那些又高又壮的十二年级高年级生欺负。

w.m: n. （高中或大学的）毕业班学生；高年级生

paras.en: I realized then that it’s nice to strive for something, but that you also have to enjoy the moment you’re in and be happy where you are.
paras.zh: 那时我才明白，为某个目标奋斗固然好，但也要享受当下，安于现状、开开心心。

paras.en: Rock and roll had always been an important part of my life.
paras.zh: 摇滚乐一直是我生活中很重要的一部分。

paras.en: I remember my friends and I used to drive around until the late hours of the nights, listening to the music of rock and roll legends.
paras.zh: 我还记得，我和朋友们以前常常开着车四处转，一直转到深夜，听那些摇滚传奇人物的音乐。

paras.en: During those teenage years, I built friendships that I thought would last a lifetime.
paras.zh: 在那些十几岁的日子里，我结下了一些自以为会维持一辈子的友谊。

w.m: adj. 十几岁的；青少年的

paras.en: Most people that age think the same thing, but people drift apart.
paras.zh: 那个年纪的人大多也这么想，可人与人之间会渐渐疏远。

paras.en: Jobs, families, and tragedies separate people from those lasting friendships.
paras.zh: 工作、家庭和不幸的变故，会让人和那些长久的友谊分开。

paras.en: The tragedy that separated me from my friends forever was the Vietnam War.
paras.zh: 让我和朋友们永远分开的不幸变故，就是越南战争。

paras.en: A year after I graduated from high school, I left for Vietnam.
paras.zh: 高中毕业一年后，我去了越南。

paras.en: I came back burned out and tired, as though I had lived 10 lifetimes in the short span of 14 months.
paras.zh: 回来的时候，我身心俱疲，仿佛在短短十四个月里过了十辈子。

paras.en: The 14 months I was in the war, I couldn’t relate to the friends I had had in high school.
paras.zh: 打仗的那十四个月过去以后，我跟高中时的朋友就再也合不来了。

paras.en: They still seemed childish, concerned with childish things that weren’t important to me.
paras.zh: 他们好像还是那么幼稚，关心的都是些对我来说无关紧要的孩子气的事。

paras.en: I was still trying to cope with the death, destruction, and evil I had seen in Vietnam.
paras.zh: 我还在努力面对自己在越南见过的死亡、破坏和罪恶。

paras.en: I felt like we had done terrible things to innocent people there, and in turn, I had seen terrible things done to my friends.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们在那里对无辜的人做了可怕的事，反过来，我也看到我的朋友们遭受了可怕的事。

paras.en: I withdrew from my friends and started college.
paras.zh: 我疏远了朋友，上了大学。

paras.en: Then I quit college and took many different jobs.
paras.zh: 后来我从大学退了学，换过很多份工作。

paras.en: I spent a lot of my time and money on alcohol and other drugs.
paras.zh: 我把大量时间和钱都花在了酒和其他毒品上。

paras.en: Finally, in an effort to get my life going in the right direction again, I sold everything and took what little money I had and bought myself an airplane ticket to Israel.
paras.zh: 最后，为了让生活重新走上正轨，我卖掉了所有东西，拿着身上仅有的一点钱，给自己买了一张去以色列的机票。

paras.en: I went there to study history.
paras.zh: 我去那里学历史。

paras.en: While studying at Haifa University, I met my wife, who was also an American student.
paras.zh: 在海法大学读书的时候，我认识了我的妻子，她也是美国来的留学生。

paras.en: I now teach in a high school back in America.
paras.zh: 现在我回到美国，在一所高中教书。

paras.en: I look at my students and see them struggling with many of the very things I struggled with many years ago.
paras.zh: 我看着我的学生，发现他们正在为许多事情苦苦挣扎，正是我多年前挣扎过的那些事。

paras.en: As a teacher, I try to help them over the rough spots as best I can.
paras.zh: 作为老师，我尽我所能帮他们度过难关。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: How did the speaker feel when he started high school?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人刚上高中时有什么感受？

paras.en: Question 23: What did the speaker once think of teenage friendships?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：说话人曾经怎样看待十几岁时的友谊？

w.m: adj. 十几岁的；青少年的

paras.en: Question 24: What do we learn about the speaker when he returned from the Vietnam War?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于说话人从越南战争回来时的情况，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker try to do as a teacher?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：作为老师，说话人努力做什么？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2023年6月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2023年6月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，莉莉刚搬进新公寓，觉得冷清，想念大学室友，哥哥安慰她这很正常，第一套公寓值得庆祝。第二段长对话里，教育批评者弗兰克·琼斯主张大学把更多预算投向理工科、为就业做准备，主持人苏珊则认为文科对社会有价值。第一篇短文讲现代人很难抽出时间思考，建议定期留出时间反思。第二篇短文讲邮政服务在美国西部开拓中的作用，以及历史学家布莱文斯用数据科学和交互式地图研究邮政史。第一段录音介绍一项研究：焦虑水平较高的人在负面心态下对信息记得更牢。第二段录音讲互联网时代营销的变化：消费者要即时信息，视频越来越重要，人们的注意力越来越短。第三段录音讲工作以外的朋友能增强自尊、提高工作满意度，管理者应一视同仁地对待员工的弹性工作申请。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six Part Two Listening Comprehension Section A Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hi, Lily.
paras.zh: 嗨，莉莉。

paras.en: How’s the new apartment?
paras.zh: 新公寓怎么样？

paras.en: It’s okay.
paras.zh: 还行吧。

paras.en: What?
paras.zh: 什么？

paras.en: How can it be just okay when last week you were thrilled about the place and kept posting photos of it online?
paras.zh: 上周你还对那地方兴奋得不得了，一个劲儿在网上发照片，怎么现在就只是“还行”了？

w.m: adj. 非常兴奋的；极为激动的

paras.en: Well, last week when I moved in, the apartment seemed cozy, just the right size for one person, but now it just seems tiny, shabby, and solitary.
paras.zh: 嗯，上周刚搬进去的时候，公寓看着挺舒适，一个人住大小正合适，可现在只觉得它又小、又破、又冷清。

paras.en: Ah, that’s the problem.
paras.zh: 啊，问题就在这儿。

paras.en: You miss your roommates from university, don’t you?
paras.zh: 你想你大学的室友了，对吧？

paras.en: I’m going to sound like an idiot because I used to complain to you all the time about how crowded our dormitory room was and about all the things they did to irritate me, like watching movies late at night without headphones or talking loudly early in the morning, but now I miss them terribly.
paras.zh: 我这话听起来肯定像个傻瓜：以前我老跟你抱怨宿舍有多挤，抱怨他们干的那些惹我烦的事，比如深夜看电影不戴耳机，或者一大早就大声说话，可现在我想他们想得要命。

paras.en: Of course you do.
paras.zh: 那当然了。

paras.en: That’s perfectly normal.
paras.zh: 这再正常不过了。

paras.en: When I got my first place, I remember thinking I couldn’t wait to live by myself and get away from my juvenile roommates and all their annoying habits.
paras.zh: 我刚有自己的住处时，记得当时想的是：真是迫不及待要一个人住，远离那几个幼稚的室友和他们那些烦人的习惯。

paras.en: But then I began missing them and feeling lonely and thinking that our dormitory was like paradise, even though there were six of us guys in one small room.
paras.zh: 可后来我开始想他们，觉得孤单，觉得我们的宿舍简直就是天堂，尽管我们六个男生挤在一个小房间里。

paras.en: I thought it was just me who felt like that.
paras.zh: 我还以为只有我是这种感觉。

paras.en: Look, you lived at home with us, and then you had three roommates, and this is your first time living alone, so it’s hard.
paras.zh: 你看，你以前在家跟我们一起住，后来又有三个室友，这是你第一次一个人住，所以会不好受。

paras.en: But your first apartment is a milestone in your life, and you should celebrate it.
paras.zh: 不过第一套公寓是你人生的一个里程碑，你应该好好庆祝一下。

paras.en: Tell me about the apartment.
paras.zh: 跟我说说你的公寓吧。

paras.en: Actually, it’s not bad.
paras.zh: 其实还不错。

paras.en: In fact, it’s pretty adorable now that I have decorated it and it has everything I need.
paras.zh: 说实话，现在我把它布置好了，什么都不缺，还挺可爱的。

w.m: adj. 可爱的；讨人喜欢的

paras.en: I have a kitchen to cook in and a bathroom all to myself, and then another room with my bed at one end and a sofa, a small table, and chairs at the other end.
paras.zh: 我有个能做饭的厨房，有个自己独用的卫生间，还有一个房间，一头放床，另一头放沙发、小桌子和椅子。

paras.en: That does sound adorable, and I can’t wait to see it.
paras.zh: 听起来确实很可爱，我都等不及要去看看了。

w.m: adj. 可爱的；讨人喜欢的

paras.en: And neither can mom and dad.
paras.zh: 爸妈也一样。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What was the woman’s first impression of the apartment?
paras.zh: 第一题：这位女士对公寓的第一印象是什么？

paras.en: Question two: Why does the woman say she is going to sound like an idiot?
paras.zh: 第二题：这位女士为什么说自己听起来会像个傻瓜？

paras.en: Question three: What do we learn about the man when he left the dormitory to live on his own?
paras.zh: 第三题：这位男士搬出宿舍、独自生活时是什么情况？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man say he can’t wait to do?
paras.zh: 第四题：这位男士说他迫不及待想做什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Welcome to our program Book Talk.
paras.zh: 欢迎收听我们的节目《书谈》。

paras.en: Our guest today is Frank Jones, a critic of our education system, and the author of a new book, *How to Reform Our Universities*.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是弗兰克·琼斯，他是我国教育体制的批评者，也是新书《如何改革我们的大学》的作者。

paras.en: Hello, Susan.
paras.zh: 你好，苏珊。

paras.en: Frank, you support radically changing universities in America.
paras.zh: 弗兰克，您主张彻底改造美国的大学。

paras.en: Yes, I believe that the purpose of higher education is to prepare young people to enter the workforce, and that our current system fails to do this.
paras.zh: 是的，我认为高等教育的目的是让年轻人做好进入职场的准备，而我们现行的体制做不到这一点。

paras.en: We’re allocating too many resources to disciplines that don’t match the needs of employers.
paras.zh: 我们把太多资源分给了与雇主需求不对口的学科。

paras.en: I think your attitude to education is a bit cynical, Frank.
paras.zh: 弗兰克，我觉得你对教育的态度有点功利。

w.m: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；（看问题）只讲功利的

paras.en: Surely the purpose of university is to prepare young people to participate fully in civic life, rather than just to find well-paid jobs.
paras.zh: 大学的目的当然是让年轻人做好准备、充分参与公民生活，而不只是找份高薪工作。

paras.en: Susan, many young graduates struggle to find any job, let alone a good one.
paras.zh: 苏珊，很多年轻毕业生连随便一份工作都很难找到，更别说好工作了。

paras.en: The job market is grim, particularly for students who study the arts.
paras.zh: 就业市场很不景气，学文科的学生尤其如此。

w.m: adj. 严峻的；令人沮丧的

paras.en: I agree that it isn’t easy for young people to find work, but you propose closing down all departments that aren’t directly related to science and technology.
paras.zh: 我同意，对年轻人来说，找工作确实不容易，可你提议把所有和科学技术没有直接关系的院系都关掉。

paras.en: Is that really the solution?
paras.zh: 这真的是解决办法吗？

paras.en: You’re overstating my point.
paras.zh: 你把我的观点说过头了。

paras.en: My argument is that we need to use more of our budget on areas like science and engineering.
paras.zh: 我的意思是，我们需要把更多预算用在科学、工程这类领域。

paras.en: To do that, we need to take money from subjects like literature and music, but the arts have value.
paras.zh: 要做到这一点，就得从文学、音乐这类学科里拿走经费，可是文科是有价值的。

paras.en: They’re an important part of our culture.
paras.zh: 它们是我们文化的重要组成部分。

paras.en: Studying literature or music or sculpture might not result in a job in that area, but it helps young people to think about the world in a deeper way, which makes them better citizens and makes for a better society.
paras.zh: 学文学、音乐或雕塑，也许不能让人在这些领域找到工作，但能帮助年轻人更深入地思考世界，让他们成为更好的公民，也有助于建设更好的社会。

paras.en: I agree that the arts are valuable to society, but it’s naive to think that not only the most talented but all students should study them at university level.
paras.zh: 我同意文科对社会有价值，但认为不光是最有天赋的学生、而是所有学生都该在大学阶段学文科，这种想法太天真了。

paras.en: The arts are very competitive, and most graduates will end up with a great deal of debt, obtaining a degree that has little value on the job market.
paras.zh: 文科竞争非常激烈，大多数毕业生最后会背上一大笔债，拿到的学位在就业市场上没什么价值。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn from the conversation about the man?
paras.zh: 第五题：从对话中我们可以了解到这位男士的什么情况？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man believe is the problem with the current American system of higher education?
paras.zh: 第六题：这位男士认为美国现行的高等教育体制有什么问题？

paras.en: Question seven: How should the education budget be allocated according to the man?
paras.zh: 第七题：这位男士认为教育预算应该怎样分配？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the woman say the arts can do?
paras.zh: 第八题：这位女士说文科能起什么作用？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Do you ever have the annoying feeling that you don’t have time to really think anymore?
paras.zh: 你有没有过这种烦人的感觉：好像再也没时间好好思考了？

paras.en: You are not alone.
paras.zh: 不只你一个人这样。

paras.en: A variety of factors have conspired to rob us of time for reflection about ourselves and our lives.
paras.zh: 多种因素凑到一起，夺走了我们反思自己、反思生活的时间。

paras.en: Today, our preoccupied minds are rarely silent.
paras.zh: 如今，我们的头脑被各种事情占着，很少有安静的时候。

w.m: adj. 心事重重的；被占据的
