paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: So I’ve been thinking this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I’d like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.
paras.zh: 我这个夏天一直在想，不再像往常那样租度假屋了，我想试试租一辆露营车，多去些地方转转。

paras.en: A camper van?
paras.zh: 露营车？

paras.en: You mean to spend the summer living out of a car?
paras.zh: 你是说整个夏天都住在车里？

paras.en: Yes, a camper van.
paras.zh: 对，露营车。

paras.en: And no, it’s nothing like living out of a car.
paras.zh: 还有，不是，这跟住在车里完全是两码事。

paras.en: These are proper vans with full-sized beds to sleep in.
paras.zh: 这些都是正规的露营车，车上有标准尺寸的床可以睡。

w.m: adj. 标准尺寸的；全尺寸的

paras.en: Some even have kitchens.
paras.zh: 有的甚至还有厨房。

paras.en: This way, we wouldn’t have to be locked into one place during our holiday.
paras.zh: 这样一来，我们度假时就不用被困在一个地方了。

paras.en: We’d be able to visit so many more places and travel at our own pace.
paras.zh: 我们能去的地方会多得多，还能按自己的节奏旅行。

paras.en: The rates of most hotels and holiday homes really soar in the summer anyway, we’d probably save a lot of money as well.
paras.zh: 反正大多数酒店和度假屋夏天的价格都会猛涨，我们可能还能省一大笔钱。

paras.en: I think my grandfather had a van like that.
paras.zh: 我想我爷爷以前就有一辆那样的车。

paras.en: It doesn’t sound that appealing to me.
paras.zh: 我觉得听起来没那么吸引人。

w.m: adj. 吸引人的；有魅力的

paras.en: Today’s camper vans are completely different.
paras.zh: 现在的露营车已经完全不一样了。

paras.en: These days they’re equipped with all the modern comforts.
paras.zh: 如今的露营车配备了各种现代化的舒适设施。

paras.en: I’ve seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you’re stopped, this way you can still use your computer or charge your phone, and most even have Wi-Fi.
paras.zh: 我见过不少车装了太阳能电池板，停车时能供电，这样你照样可以用电脑、给手机充电，大多数车甚至还有无线网。

paras.en: So if the weather’s not great, you could stream videos.
paras.zh: 所以要是天气不好，你还可以在线看视频。

w.m: v. 在线播放；流式传输

paras.en: I’m warming up to the idea.
paras.zh: 我开始对这个主意感兴趣了。

w.m: 渐渐喜欢上；开始对……感兴趣

paras.en: Keep talking.
paras.zh: 接着说。

paras.en: Loads of people are committing to this trend full time.
paras.zh: 很多人全职投身于这种潮流。

paras.en: Check it out online.
paras.zh: 你上网看看。

paras.en: Lots of people stream videos of their alternative lifestyles and actually earn a salary.
paras.zh: 很多人在网上直播自己另类的生活方式，还真能挣到一份工资。

paras.en: Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world.
paras.zh: 想想看，能拥有那样的自由，想去哪儿就去哪儿，在世界上任何地方都能工作。

paras.en: Okay, we can consider it as long as the basic needs like toilet and showers are covered.
paras.zh: 好吧，只要厕所、淋浴这些基本需求能解决，我们就可以考虑。

paras.en: I’m definitely in.
paras.zh: 算我一个，我肯定去。

paras.en: Do you think there will be enough room for my mountain bike.
paras.zh: 你觉得车上有足够的地方放我的山地车吗？

paras.en: What about food delivery?
paras.zh: 那外卖呢？

paras.en: Will we be able to order to the van?
paras.zh: 我们能把外卖叫到车上吗？

paras.en: Will there be enough space for the dog?
paras.zh: 车上有足够的地方给狗待吗？

paras.en: We wouldn’t want to leave him behind.
paras.zh: 我们可不想把它丢下。

paras.en: Slow down.
paras.zh: 慢点儿。

paras.en: Glad you’re excited about it.
paras.zh: 很高兴你对这件事这么兴奋。

paras.en: Let’s start by looking at what’s available first.
paras.zh: 我们先从看看有哪些车可租开始吧。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What has the woman been thinking of doing for this summer?
paras.zh: 第一题：女士一直在考虑今年夏天做什么？

paras.en: Question two: What do we learn about the man’s grandfather from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第二题：从对话中，我们可以了解到男士的爷爷的什么情况？

paras.en: Question three: What can many camper vans do nowadays, according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第三题：据女士说，如今很多露营车能做什么？

paras.en: Question four: What idea does the woman find attractive?
paras.zh: 第四题：女士觉得什么想法很吸引人？

w.m: adj. 吸引人的；有魅力的

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: You wanted to see me.
paras.zh: 你想见我。

paras.en: Yes, I’ll get straight to the point.
paras.zh: 是的，我就开门见山了。

paras.en: Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped.
paras.zh: 过去一个月左右，你的工作表现明显下滑了。

w.m: adj. 明显的；显而易见的

paras.en: You’ve been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you.
paras.zh: 这几个星期你上班迟到了好几次，这很不像你。

w.m: adj. 不像（某人）的；不典型的

paras.en: But what really concerns me is your curtailed output.
paras.zh: 但我真正担心的是你的工作量少了。

paras.en: Lately, you seem to be constantly one step behind.
paras.zh: 最近你好像总是慢半拍。

paras.en: What’s going on?
paras.zh: 到底怎么了？

paras.en: I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 对不起。

paras.en: I’m going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment.
paras.zh: 我现在家里遇到了一些不幸的事。

paras.en: It’s a personal matter, so if you don’t mind, I much prefer we don’t get into it.
paras.zh: 这是我的私事，所以如果您不介意的话，我真的不想多说。

paras.en: Nevertheless, I expect it to have all blown over in another month or so.
paras.zh: 不过，我估计再过一个月左右，这事应该就都过去了。

paras.en: Do you need some time off?
paras.zh: 你需要休息一段时间吗？

paras.en: Actually, yes.
paras.zh: 其实需要。

paras.en: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off?
paras.zh: 我能不能接下来的两个星期一请假？

paras.en: I was deliberating whether I should ask for this, but now that we’re here, sure thing.
paras.zh: 我一直在犹豫要不要提这个请求。——既然说到这儿了，当然可以。

paras.en: But if you needed some leave, why didn’t you ask for it earlier?
paras.zh: 不过你要是需要请假，为什么不早点提呢？

paras.en: I’m not sure why.
paras.zh: 我也说不清为什么。

paras.en: I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it.
paras.zh: 我想我有点不好意思开口。

paras.en: You shouldn’t feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it.
paras.zh: 请假不用觉得不好意思，尤其是你确实需要的时候。

paras.en: I know you’re right.
paras.zh: 我知道您说得对。

paras.en: I’m sorry.
paras.zh: 对不起。

paras.en: Look, you’ve been with us almost five years, and I personally really value your proficiency at your job.
paras.zh: 听我说，你在我们这儿干了快五年了，我个人非常看重你的业务能力。

paras.en: It makes my job far easier.
paras.zh: 有你在，我的工作轻松多了。

paras.en: In addition, I can assure you that management as a whole also holds you in high regard.
paras.zh: 另外，我可以向你保证，管理层整体上也非常器重你。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢您。

paras.en: What I need is for you to be back at your 100%.
paras.zh: 我需要的是你恢复到百分之百的状态。

paras.en: Are you sure taking two Mondays off will suffice?
paras.zh: 你确定休两个星期一就够了吗？

paras.en: It’ll be enough.
paras.zh: 够了。

paras.en: I’m sure of it.
paras.zh: 这一点我很确定。

paras.en: Okay, good.
paras.zh: 好，那就好。

paras.en: So this is what we’re going to do.
paras.zh: 那我们就这么办。

paras.en: You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self.
paras.zh: 那几天你就休假，我希望你能慢慢恢复到平常的状态。

paras.en: Then, in two months’ time, we will catch up again to see how you are faring.
paras.zh: 然后，两个月以后我们再聊一次，看看你情况怎么样。

paras.en: Sounds good.
paras.zh: 听起来不错。

paras.en: Thank you for your understanding.
paras.zh: 谢谢您的理解。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about the woman from the man’s description?
paras.zh: 第五题：从男士的描述中，我们可以了解到女士的什么情况？

paras.en: Question six: What does the woman say she’s experiencing at the moment?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士说她现在正经历着什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the man say makes his job far easier?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士说什么让他的工作轻松多了？

paras.en: Question eight: What agreement have the speakers reached by the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第八题：到对话结束时，两人达成了什么约定？

paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: There are many factors that impact our health.
paras.zh: 影响我们健康的因素有很多。

paras.en: These include our finances, our emotions, and the way we work.
paras.zh: 包括我们的财务状况、情绪，还有我们的工作方式。

paras.en: Education is one such factor.
paras.zh: 教育就是这样的一个因素。

paras.en: Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity, but what about the education of your partner?
paras.zh: 研究表明，受教育程度越高，健康状况会越好，甚至寿命也会更长，可是伴侣的受教育程度又会怎样呢？

paras.en: New research seeks to answer this question.
paras.zh: 一项新研究试图回答这个问题。

paras.en: Researchers use data from a longitudinal study.
paras.zh: 研究人员使用了一项纵向研究的数据。

paras.en: The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957.
paras.zh: 这些数据来自调查问卷，最早是在一九五七年发给高中毕业班学生填写的。

paras.en: The surveys ended in 2011.
paras.zh: 这些调查到二〇一一年结束。

paras.en: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.
paras.zh: 研究团队发现，配偶受教育程度较高的人，自己报告的健康状况往往更好。

paras.en: This remained the case when adjusting for other factors such as participants’ own education, social background, and health status before and after marriage.
paras.zh: 即使把参与者本人的受教育程度、社会背景以及婚前婚后的健康状况等其他因素考虑进去，情况依然如此。

paras.en: The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional, and financial resources.
paras.zh: 作者认为，较高的受教育程度会带来社会、智力、情感和经济方面的共享资源。

paras.en: These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money.
paras.zh: 这包括更高的情商、特定的技能或知识，或者更多的钱。

paras.en: The researchers concede that an individual’s own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner’s education.
paras.zh: 研究人员承认，一个人自身的受教育程度显然对其健康很重要，但他们也断言，一个人还可以从伴侣的受教育程度中获益。

paras.en: It is noteworthy that the effects varied by gender.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，这种影响因性别而异。

paras.en: For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouse’s education than for men, the team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study.
paras.zh: 女性的健康与配偶受教育程度的关联比男性更紧密；研究团队认为，这可能和研究所处的时期有关。

paras.en: Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men.
paras.zh: 这个样本中的女性，受教育程度和职业成就都比男性低。

paras.en: The researchers’ hypothesis is that this made the husband’s resources more likely to have a shared impact.
paras.zh: 研究人员的假设是，这使得丈夫的资源更有可能产生共同的影响。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does research suggest about a higher level of education?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于较高的受教育程度，研究表明了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What do we learn from the finding of the new research?
paras.zh: 第十题：从这项新研究的发现中，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于这项新研究样本中的男性，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods.
paras.zh: 气候科学家预测，世界上很多地区会越来越容易发生洪水。

paras.en: This is a serious risk to human lives and property.
paras.zh: 这对人的生命和财产是严重的威胁。

paras.en: So, understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.
paras.zh: 因此，了解并准确预报洪水风险，是全球各地易受洪灾的城市面临的一大挑战。

w.m: adj. 易受伤害的；脆弱的

paras.en: In 2017, Derek Loftis of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King.
paras.zh: 二〇一七年，弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的德里克·洛夫蒂斯启动了一个名为“捕捉大潮”的项目。

paras.en: It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides.
paras.zh: 这个项目用一款智能手机应用程序，收集普通市民在涨大潮时提供的数据。

paras.en: He’ll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model called TideWatch.
paras.zh: 他会用这些数据来验证和改进他的洪水数学模型“潮汐观察”。

paras.en: Loftis’s mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there, but collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy.
paras.zh: 洛夫蒂斯的使命是在水流到某个地方之前就知道它会流向哪里，可是要收集必要的数据，再足够快地处理这些信息，做出能用的预报，一点也不容易。

paras.en: Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground.
paras.zh: 准确的洪水预报需要了解实地情况。

paras.en: By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements, but they still didn’t have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.
paras.zh: 到二十一世纪初，超级计算已经发展到了一定程度，科学家能把天气预报模型和这类测量数据结合起来，但他们仍然不具备实时预报快速推进的洪水这项极其重要的能力。

paras.en: So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia.
paras.zh: 于是在二〇一七年，洛夫蒂斯和同事们在洪水风险很高的弗吉尼亚州诺福克社区各处，安装了一组二十八个联网的水位传感器。

paras.en: The new sensors relay rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute.
paras.zh: 这些新传感器把关于水位高度和水流动向的粗略测量数据传给弗吉尼亚研究所的一台电脑。

paras.en: Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them real time to the institute.
paras.zh: 除了这些传感器，还有数百名当地市民拍下涨潮的照片，实时发给研究所。

paras.en: Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.
paras.zh: 科学家希望这些市民收集的数据能帮助提高预报能力，准确预测破坏性洪水会在何时何地发生。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods?
paras.zh: 第十二题：对易受洪灾的城市来说，什么被认为是一大挑战？

paras.en: Question 13: For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides?
paras.zh: 第十三题：德里克·洛夫蒂斯收集普通市民在涨大潮时提供的数据，目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the passage say is Derek Loftis’s mission?
paras.zh: 第十四题：短文说德里克·洛夫蒂斯的使命是什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement?
paras.zh: 第十五题：洛夫蒂斯和同事们做了什么来获取水位高度和水流动向的数据？

paras.en: Section C, directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Now it’s become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree, but as current population survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.
paras.zh: 如今，争论大学学位的价值几乎成了一种惯例；但正如当前人口调查的数据所显示的，与有大学学位的男性相比，没有大学学位的男性就业率大幅下降。

paras.en: This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.
paras.zh: 这种下降始于二十世纪六十年代，而且随着时间推移越来越严重。

paras.en: What has actually caused this decline?
paras.zh: 到底是什么导致了这种下降？

paras.en: Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades and have come up with several theories.
paras.zh: 嗯，经济学家几十年来一直在努力查明这种下降的根源，并提出了几种理论。

paras.en: One popular theory is that it’s a case of too low wages for jobs that don’t require a degree.
paras.zh: 一种流行的理论认为，这是因为不需要学位的工作工资太低。

paras.en: An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
paras.zh: 另一种理论认为，过去不需要大学学位的工作比现在多。

w.m: adj. 另外的；可供选择的

paras.en: A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem.
paras.zh: 美国国家经济研究局最近的一份工作论文梳理了这些理论，并就这个问题的原因提出了更多假设。

paras.en: Let’s look at that paper now.
paras.zh: 我们现在就来看看这篇论文。

paras.en: First, the researchers considered the issue of wages, as the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without.
paras.zh: 首先，研究人员考虑了工资问题，因为有大学学位的人和没有学位的人之间的工资差距已经拉大了。

paras.en: Economists have suggested that men aren’t as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs.
paras.zh: 经济学家提出，男性不太愿意去做一些收入较低的工作。

w.m: adj. 赚钱的；有利可图的

paras.en: While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can’t be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven’t changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
paras.zh: 这篇论文的作者虽然认为这种解释有道理，但他们断言，低工资不可能是唯一的因素，因为扣除通货膨胀因素后，没有大学学位的男性的工资自二十世纪六十年代以来变化不大，所以很难解释为什么愿意接受这种工资的男性似乎越来越少。

paras.en: This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past.
paras.zh: 这就引出了第二种理论：如今需要大学学位的工作比过去多。

paras.en: Indeed, that theory seems valid because in America today, two thirds of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education.
paras.zh: 的确，这种理论似乎站得住脚，因为在当今的美国，三分之二的工作是由至少上过一段时间大学的人来做的。

w.m: adj. 有根据的；站得住脚的

paras.en: However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem, they identified two new potential explanations.
paras.zh: 然而，论文作者认为，还有其他因素在加剧这个问题，他们找出了两种新的可能解释。

paras.en: The first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s, and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage, these two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing.
paras.zh: 第一，自二十世纪六十年代以来，没有大学学位的男性结婚的人数大幅减少；第二，与婚姻减少同时出现的，是参加工作的女性增多了。这两种变化意味着，男性可能没有需要养活的家庭；即使有家庭，他们的妻子也可能承担了更多养家的责任。

paras.en: Both of which might remove the financial incentive to work.
paras.zh: 这两点都可能让男性失去工作的经济动力。

paras.en: The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn’t complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.
paras.zh: 论文作者承认，关于这个课题的研究还不完整，但他们认为，自己的研究证明了大学教育的价值。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say has become something of a ritual?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人说什么在某种程度上已经成了一种惯例？

paras.en: Question 17: What did the researchers of a recent working paper consider first?
paras.zh: 第十七题：最近一份工作论文的研究人员首先考虑的是什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What did the recent paper identify as a new potential explanation of the problem concerning men’s employment?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于男性就业问题，最近这篇论文找出的一种新的可能解释是什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet.
paras.zh: 越来越多的人在努力少吃肉；而一个市场研究团队在其最新的时尚与可持续发展报告中发现，这种潮流正从厨房蔓延到衣橱。

paras.en: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them.
paras.zh: 报告发现，在人们买衣服前会考虑的问题中，动物福利排在第一位，有百分之四十二的人说这一点对他们很重要。

paras.en: The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal-free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as vegan, meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.
paras.zh: 这个团队的研究人员预测，明年无动物成分的鞋履系列将迎来热潮，因为他们听到各个年龄段的顾客都说，会购买标明“纯素”的鞋，也就是说，这些商品在生产过程中没有使用任何动物或动物身上的部分。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的
v. 意思是；也就是说（mean 的现在分词）

paras.en: As well as being on trend and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction.
paras.zh: “纯素”这个标签不仅紧跟潮流，听起来也比“合成皮革”好听得多，而且它确实传达了一个重要的额外区别。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal-free.
paras.zh: 如果你给某样东西贴上“纯素”标签，那整个产品都必须不含动物成分。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them.
paras.zh: 比如说，这就意味着要检查把鞋粘在一起的胶水，以及鞋子最后一道工序所用的化学品。

w.m: n. 最后加工；收尾工序

paras.en: At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.
paras.zh: 在高端市场，一些世界知名的时装设计师已经有一段时间不用皮革和皮草了。

paras.en: In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.
paras.zh: 事实上，一些公司现在正在研发用蘑菇制成的皮革替代品和丝绸替代品。

paras.en: The Animal Free Product Society says they’ve seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark.
paras.zh: 无动物制品协会表示，注册纯素商标的产品数量激增。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: In 2018, there were 119.
paras.zh: 二〇一八年有一百一十九种。

paras.en: So far this year, it says an unprecedented 1,956 have been registered.
paras.zh: 该协会说，今年到目前为止，已经有前所未有的一千九百五十六种产品注册。

w.m: adj. 前所未有的；空前的

paras.en: New products are being added daily.
paras.zh: 每天都有新产品加入。

paras.en: There are fur coats that are vegan, plastic vegan belts, and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labelled vegan.
paras.zh: 有纯素的皮草大衣、塑料材质的纯素腰带，还有用树皮或天然橡胶制成、贴着纯素标签的鞋。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: These new products aren’t coming at an extra cost to consumers, though.
paras.zh: 不过，这些新产品并不会让消费者多花钱。

paras.en: Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals.
paras.zh: 纯素靴子的价格和原来的皮靴一样。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99 and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
paras.zh: New Look 是最早使用纯素商标的知名连锁店之一，它的芭蕾舞鞋定价七点九九英镑，纯素笔记本电脑手提包定价二十九点九九英镑，和它的其他产品价格相当。

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: This signifies a change.
paras.zh: 这标志着一种变化。

paras.en: In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium.
paras.zh: 过去，合乎道德的产品，无论是公平贸易产品还是有机产品，价格都偏高。

w.m: adj. 合乎道德的；伦理的

paras.en: However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical.
paras.zh: 然而，这些新产品能不能算是合乎道德，还不清楚。

w.m: adj. 合乎道德的；伦理的

paras.en: The debate over durability, crop-growing impacts, pollution, and recyclability is a complicated one.
paras.zh: 围绕耐用性、种植作物的影响、污染和可回收性的争论十分复杂。

paras.en: Not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials.
paras.zh: 更不用说，不管用的是什么原材料，还有生产这些产品的工人的工作条件这一道德问题。

paras.en: Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.
paras.zh: 环保人士建议，最好的办法是少买，不管东西是用什么做的。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What has a market research team found in its latest fashion and sustainability report?
paras.zh: 第十九题：一个市场研究团队在其最新的时尚与可持续发展报告中发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What have some world-renowned fashion designers done for some time?
paras.zh: 第二十题：一些世界知名的时装设计师一段时间以来做了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say is unclear concerning vegan products?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说，关于纯素产品，什么还不清楚？

w.m: adj. 纯素的；不含动物成分的

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell.
paras.zh: 到二〇一六年底，凡是对新闻头条稍加留意的人，很可能都会断定一切都糟透了，世界正在走向地狱。

paras.en: It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.
paras.zh: 世界各地的战争、致命病毒的传播、恐怖袭击，都很容易让人感到沮丧。

paras.en: Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity.
paras.zh: 然而，二〇一六年却是人类历史上最好的一年。

paras.en: Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990, and 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day.
paras.zh: 儿童死亡率大约只有一九九〇年时的一半，而且每天都有三十万人新用上电。

paras.en: Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa, and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated.
paras.zh: 在美洲、欧洲、亚洲、非洲乃至整个世界，衡量物质和环境福祉的每一项指标都有所改善，而不是恶化。

paras.en: We are living in history’s most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline.
paras.zh: 我们生活在历史上最和平的时代，各种暴力都在急剧减少。

paras.en: Those are the facts.
paras.zh: 这些都是事实。

paras.en: So why aren’t we all optimists?
paras.zh: 那么，为什么我们不都是乐观主义者呢？

w.m: n. 乐观主义者；乐天派

paras.en: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
paras.zh: 在舆观二〇一五年做的一项调查中，百分之六十五的英国人和百分之八十一的法国人说，他们认为世界正变得越来越糟。

paras.en: However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong.
paras.zh: 然而，根据大量可靠的统计数据，这些人完全错了。

paras.en: Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century.
paras.zh: 头脑正常的人，谁也不应该希望自己活在以前的某个世纪。

paras.en: Yet people do.
paras.zh: 可人们偏偏就是这么想的。

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么？

paras.en: Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational.
paras.zh: 我们普遍的绝望情绪是不理性的。

w.m: adj. 不理性的；不合理的

paras.en: It says more about us than it does about how things really are.
paras.zh: 它反映的更多是我们自己，而不是事情的真实状况。

paras.en: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors, but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us.
paras.zh: 最好的解释是，这是各种心理偏向造成的结果；这些偏向对我们进化过程中的祖先曾经有用，可如今在这个媒体泛滥的时代，却总是误导我们。

paras.en: Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong.
paras.zh: 从前，对一切可能出问题的事情都感到担忧，对生存有很大的价值。

paras.en: This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
paras.zh: 这就是坏消息格外吸引人的原因。

w.m: adj. 引人注目的；令人信服的

paras.en: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival.
paras.zh: 在我们进化的过去，注意力很容易被负面信息吸引是一件非常好的事，因为负面信息很可能预示着对我们自身生存的危险。

paras.en: The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he’d be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite.
paras.zh: 总以为下一块石头后面有狮子的穴居人，通常都是想错了，但他生存和繁衍的可能性，要比总是做相反假设的人大得多。

paras.en: But that was all before newspapers, television, and the internet.
paras.zh: 不过，那都是有报纸、电视和互联网之前的事了。

paras.en: In today’s hyper-connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe, whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are.
paras.zh: 在当今这个高度互联的时代，我们对坏消息的沉迷，只会让我们把来自全球各地令人沮丧或愤怒的报道统统吸收进来，无论这些新闻是否威胁到我们，我们都会断定事情比实际情况糟糕得多。

paras.en: Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events, by definition, aren’t news.
paras.zh: 而真正的好消息，在报纸上却难找得多，因为可以预料的日常事件，按定义来说就不算新闻。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What is one of the facts stated by the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人陈述的事实之一是什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What do we learn about most British and French people in a 2015 survey for YouGov?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：从舆观二〇一五年的一项调查中，我们了解到大多数英国人和法国人的什么情况？

paras.en: Question 24: What does our prevailing mood of despair indicate?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：我们普遍的绝望情绪说明了什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What was a very good thing in our evolutionary past?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：在我们进化的过去，什么是一件非常好的事？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，男士新买了一台高档搅拌机，讲自己买前做了大量功课，用它每周打几次蔬果汁，饮食更多样、更健康。第二段长对话里，伯克顿村长格里姆讲这个小村子怎样靠统一房屋外观，十年间变成热门旅游地。第一篇短文介绍美国西北大学研制的一种遥控微型机器人，只有半毫米宽，将来可在狭小空间里修理零件、做微创手术。第二篇短文里，作者原以为自己是“精英睡眠者”，后来才知道那是少数人天生的基因特点，于是研究人能不能练得少睡觉。第一段录音介绍一项研究：人们读了有说服力的文章后，往往意识不到自己的观点变了，连原来的看法都记偏了。第二段录音讲美国母亲在人口中的比例降到二十五年来最低，生育年龄推迟，母亲节的消费却在增长。第三段录音讲室内植物净化空气的作用被夸大了，开几扇窗户的效果都比它好。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I’ve just bought a new blender.
paras.zh: 我刚买了一台新的搅拌机。

paras.en: What’s that?
paras.zh: 那是什么？

paras.en: A blender, you know, a machine that blends food.
paras.zh: 搅拌机啊，就是那种把食物打碎搅匀的机器。

paras.en: Ah, yes, of course, the electric kitchen appliance.
paras.zh: 啊，对，当然，那种电动厨房电器。

paras.en: Exactly, this one is state of the art.
paras.zh: 没错，这一台可是最先进的。

paras.en: I’ve been meaning to buy one for a while, and I did thorough research on which specific model to get.
paras.zh: 我一直想买一台，想了好一阵了，具体买哪个型号，我做了很仔细的调查。

paras.en: I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews.
paras.zh: 网上的用户评价我大概看了好几百条。

paras.en: Anyway, it’s amazing.
paras.zh: 总之，它特别棒。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；极好的

paras.en: Really, what could be so special about it?
paras.zh: 真的吗？它能有什么特别的？

paras.en: I mean, it’s just a blender.
paras.zh: 我是说，它不过就是个搅拌机嘛。

paras.en: Well, basically, it’s just a very good one.
paras.zh: 嗯，说白了，它就是一台特别好的搅拌机。

paras.en: It feels heavy and sturdy and well made.
paras.zh: 它拿在手里沉甸甸的，很结实，做工也好。

paras.en: It also has lots of power and can easily cut and crush practically anything.
paras.zh: 它功率也很大，几乎什么东西都能轻松切碎、压碎。

paras.en: This way, the soups and juices I make come out really fine and smooth, with no lumpy bits.
paras.zh: 这样一来，我做的汤和果汁都特别细、特别顺滑，一点渣块都没有。

w.m: adj. 有块的；疙疙瘩瘩的

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: I’ve never thought of getting one myself.
paras.zh: 我自己倒从没想过要买一台。

paras.en: It sounds like the kind of thing that, for me personally, I would rarely use.
paras.zh: 听起来这种东西，就我个人来说，很少会用到。

paras.en: I’ve never had one before, and now that I do, I use it all the time.
paras.zh: 我以前从来没有过搅拌机，现在有了，就一直在用。

paras.en: I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning.
paras.zh: 我每天早上做一杯新鲜果汁。

paras.en: Maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic.
paras.zh: 也许不是每天早上，不过一周三四次吧，感觉好极了。

paras.en: It’s a really healthy habit.
paras.zh: 这是个很健康的习惯。

w.m: adj. 健康的；有益健康的

paras.en: I can imagine that must feel quite satisfying.
paras.zh: 我能想象，那一定挺有满足感的。

w.m: adj. 令人满意的；有满足感的

paras.en: I can picture you getting all creative in the kitchen and trying out a multitude of different ingredients, and it’s obviously going to be healthier than buying packaged juice from a supermarket.
paras.zh: 我都能想象出你在厨房里大展身手、试各种各样不同食材的样子，而且这肯定比在超市买包装果汁要健康。

paras.en: It’s so much healthier.
paras.zh: 健康多了。

w.m: adj. 健康的；有益健康的

paras.en: It’s not even close.
paras.zh: 根本没法比。

paras.en: Did you know that store-bought juice is like 10% sugar?
paras.zh: 你知道吗，商店买的果汁大概有百分之十是糖？

paras.en: Right.
paras.zh: 对。

paras.en: So then you bought it for the health benefits?
paras.zh: 这么说你买它是为了健康？

paras.en: Mostly, yes.
paras.zh: 主要是吧，对。

paras.en: Basically, it allows me to have a more varied diet with a far wider assortment of nutrients, because it’s not only fruit in my morning juices, you see, I can also throw in vegetables, nuts, yogurts, cereals, anything that tickles my fancy.
paras.zh: 简单来说，它能让我吃得更多样，摄入的营养种类也丰富得多，因为我早上的果汁里不光有水果，你知道，我还能加蔬菜、坚果、酸奶、麦片，什么想吃就加什么。

w.m: adj. 多样的；各种各样的
n. 各种各样；什么都有
合某人心意；让某人感兴趣

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the man say he did before buying the blender?
paras.zh: 第一题：男士说他买搅拌机之前做了什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the woman say she has never thought of doing?
paras.zh: 第二题：女士说她从没想过要做什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the man say is a really healthy habit?
paras.zh: 第三题：男士说什么是很健康的习惯？

w.m: adj. 健康的；有益健康的

paras.en: Question four: What do we learn about store-bought juice from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于商店买的果汁，从对话中我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Today we have a very interesting guest, Mr. Thomas Benjamin Grimm, the mayor of Berkton, is here to talk about his job and responsibilities overseeing this charming village.
paras.zh: 今天我们请来了一位很有意思的嘉宾，托马斯·本杰明·格里姆先生，他是伯克顿的村长，今天来跟我们聊聊他的工作，以及他管理这个美丽村庄的职责。

w.m: n. 先生（用于男子姓氏前）
托马斯·本杰明·格里姆（人名）

paras.en: Mr. Grimm, thank you for being here.
paras.zh: 格里姆先生，感谢您的到来。

w.m: n. 先生（用于男子姓氏前）

paras.en: Thank you for having me.
paras.zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

paras.en: I’d like to start by stating the obvious.
paras.zh: 我想先从一个明摆着的事情说起。

paras.en: Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch.
paras.zh: 伯克顿已经成了全国最热门的旅游地之一，而这正是在您任上发生的。

w.m: 在某人任内；在某人看管下

paras.en: Just how did you achieve this?
paras.zh: 您到底是怎么做到的？

paras.en: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton.
paras.zh: 这个成绩属于伯克顿的全体居民。

paras.en: It was a shared effort where everybody pitched in for the communal good.
paras.zh: 这是大家共同努力的结果，每个人都为了集体的利益出了一份力。

paras.en: But how did this change happen?
paras.zh: 可这个变化是怎么发生的呢？

paras.en: In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of, sleepy village to a must-see destination.
paras.zh: 十年左右，伯克顿就从一个几乎无人知晓、冷冷清清的村子，变成了一个必去的旅游地。

w.m: adj. 默默无闻的；前所未闻的
adj. 必看的；不可错过的

paras.en: Yes, the change has truly been remarkable.
paras.zh: 是的，变化确实非常显著。

paras.en: Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure.
paras.zh: 伯克顿一直很幸运，天生就有这样美丽的自然风光。

paras.en: The Enbury Hills above the village remain untouched by human development, and the Sonora Valley just below it is equally stunning.
paras.zh: 村子上方的恩伯里山至今没有被人类开发过，山下的索诺拉谷也同样美得惊人。

w.m: adj. 未受影响的；原封未动的
adj. 极美的；令人惊叹的

paras.en: The transformation commenced in a town hall meeting in spring 2008, over 10 years ago now, when an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of Motion 836.
paras.zh: 这一转变始于十多年前，也就是2008年春天的一次镇民大会，会上绝大多数邻居投票赞成第836号动议。

paras.en: This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the esthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton.
paras.zh: 这项立法提案的主要目的，是让伯克顿所有房屋的外观在审美上协调一致。

paras.en: The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful, and it worked.
paras.zh: 想法是，如果所有房子都有统一的设计特点、看起来是同一种风格，那么村子整体上就会更美，结果确实如此。

paras.en: It certainly did.
paras.zh: 确实如此。

paras.en: I’m looking now at a before and after photo, and the change is truly remarkable.
paras.zh: 我现在正看着一张前后对比照片，变化真的非常显著。

paras.en: It’s hard to believe it’s the same place.
paras.zh: 真难相信这是同一个地方。

paras.en: And how do the neighbors feel now?
paras.zh: 那邻居们现在感觉如何？

paras.en: Great pride, I would say.
paras.zh: 我想说，大家都非常自豪。

paras.en: But what about the multitudes of visitors now crowding the streets?
paras.zh: 可现在街上挤满了游客，这又怎么说呢？

paras.en: Is everyone happy about that?
paras.zh: 大家都乐意吗？

paras.en: The tourists we receive are a blessing as they have completely revitalized our local economy.
paras.zh: 我们接待的游客是一件好事，他们让我们当地的经济重新焕发了活力。

paras.en: Every visitor is warmly welcome.
paras.zh: 我们热烈欢迎每一位游客。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What is the question the woman asked Mr. Grimm after the introduction?
paras.zh: 第五题：介绍完嘉宾后，女士问格里姆先生的问题是什么？

paras.en: Question six: What do we learn about Berkton of 10 years ago?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于十年前的伯克顿，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What resulted from the passing of the legislative proposal “Motion 836”?
paras.zh: 第七题：“第836号动议”这项立法提案通过后带来了什么结果？

paras.en: Question eight: Why does the man say the tourists are a blessing to Berkton?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士为什么说游客是伯克顿的福气？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Researchers in the U.S. have created a remote-controlled robot that is so small it can walk on the top of a U.S. penny.
paras.zh: 美国研究人员研制出一种遥控机器人，它小到能在一枚美国一美分硬币上面行走。

paras.en: In research published in the journal Science Robotics, a team at Northwestern University said the crab-like robot is 0.5 millimeters wide.
paras.zh: 在发表于《科学·机器人学》期刊上的研究中，西北大学的一个团队表示，这种螃蟹状的机器人只有0.5毫米宽。

paras.en: Researchers described it as the smallest ever remote-controlled walking robot.
paras.zh: 研究人员称，这是迄今为止最小的遥控步行机器人。

paras.en: The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn, and even jump without the use of complex hardware or special power.
paras.zh: 这个小小的机器人能弯曲、扭动、爬行、走路、转身，甚至还能跳，用不着复杂的硬件，也用不着特殊的动力。

paras.en: The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body.
paras.zh: 工程师们说，这是因为机器人靠自身身体的弹性来驱动。

paras.en: To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
paras.zh: 为了造出这个机器人，研究人员用了一种形状记忆合金材料，这种材料一受热就会恢复到它“记住”的形状。

paras.en: Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape.
paras.zh: 研究团队用激光给机器人身体的特定部位加热，让它改变形状。

paras.en: As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another.
paras.zh: 机器人变形、再恢复原来的形状，就能从一个地方移动到另一个地方。

paras.en: Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast.
paras.zh: “因为这些结构非常小，所以冷却速度非常快。”

paras.en: Project Lead Professor John A. Rogers said.
paras.zh: 项目负责人约翰·A·罗杰斯教授说。

paras.en: In fact, reducing the sizes of these robots allows them to run faster.
paras.zh: “事实上，把这些机器人做得更小，它们就能跑得更快。”

paras.en: While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes that technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces.
paras.zh: 虽然这项研究还处于探索阶段，但研究团队相信，这项技术将来可能造出微型机器人，在非常狭小的空间里完成实际工作。

w.m: 非常狭窄的；空间极受限的

paras.en: You might imagine micro robots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry, or as surgical assistance to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding or to eliminate cancerous tumors, all in minimally invasive procedures.
paras.zh: “你可以想象，微型机器人在工业上充当帮手，修理或组装细小的结构或机器；或者在手术中当助手，疏通堵塞的动脉、止住内出血、切除癌性肿瘤，而且都是微创手术。”

paras.en: Rogers said.
paras.zh: 罗杰斯说。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does the passage say about a team of researchers at Northwestern University?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于西北大学的一个研究团队，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What did the researchers say about the robot they created?
paras.zh: 第十题：研究人员对他们研制的机器人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What do the researchers expect their robots to do in the future?
paras.zh: 第十一题：研究人员希望他们的机器人将来能做什么？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: I don’t want to boast or anything, but I have always considered myself something of an elite sleeper.
paras.zh: 我不是要吹牛，不过我一直觉得自己算得上是个“精英睡眠者”。

paras.en: Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches and can doze through the most extreme situations.
paras.zh: 只要有机会，我能一口气睡上很长时间，再极端的情况下也能打瞌睡。

w.m: adj. 马拉松式的；持久的

paras.en: On one very rough ferry crossing on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire three-hour ride throwing up in the bathroom, while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
paras.zh: 比如有一次，坐渡轮去锡利群岛，海上颠簸得厉害，我的旅伴三个小时都在洗手间里吐，我却坐在一把塑料椅子上睡得香香的。

w.m: adj. （海面）波涛汹涌的；颠簸的

paras.en: Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all.
paras.zh: 可惜我后来注意到，我根本不是什么精英睡眠者。

paras.en: It seems I am just lazy, because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3% of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us.
paras.zh: 看来我只是懒，因为所谓精英睡眠者，指的是大约百分之三的人，他们天生需要的睡眠比我们其他人少。

w.m: adj. 设定好的；预先编排的

paras.en: According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals without any risk of cognitive decline.
paras.zh: 根据三月份发表的一项研究，精英睡眠者有罕见的基因变异，所以他们睡得比普通人少，也不会有认知能力下降的风险。

paras.en: It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep?
paras.zh: 自己的基因也许没法改变，可人能不能训练自己，让自己需要的睡眠少一些呢？

paras.en: Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status.
paras.zh: 有没有一种不靠生物遗传的方法，也能达到精英睡眠者的水平？

paras.en: I have spent the past year trying to answer that question, not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion.
paras.zh: 过去这一年，我一直在找这个问题的答案，我得说一句，这可不是闹着玩的，而是因为生了孩子以后，我的睡眠被严重打乱了，可我还是非常爱睡觉。

paras.en: For a while, I assumed I’d be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn, after a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.
paras.zh: 有一阵子，我以为自己不得不变成那种天一亮就从床上跳起来的人。可是经过一年艰苦的科学研究，我发现，被迫早起和天生早起完全是两回事。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the speaker say she did on her ride to the Isles of Scilly?
paras.zh: 第十二题：说话人说她在去锡利群岛的路上做了什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What do we learn from the passage about elite sleepers?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于精英睡眠者，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What has the speaker been trying to find out over the past year?
paras.zh: 第十四题：过去一年里，说话人一直在设法弄清楚什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What has the speaker discovered after a year of tough scientific study?
paras.zh: 第十五题：经过一年艰苦的科学研究，说话人发现了什么？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you’d realize if it had changed your beliefs?
paras.zh: 如果你读了一篇讨论有争议问题的文章，你觉得要是它改变了你的看法，你自己会意识到吗？

paras.en: No one knows your own mind like you do.
paras.zh: 谁也没有你更了解你自己的想法。

paras.en: It seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted, and yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we’ve been swayed by a convincing article.
paras.zh: 自己的看法变没变，自己应该知道，这似乎是明摆着的事。可是《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文指出，其实我们很难察觉自己的看法变了，也就是说，我们往往会低估一篇有说服力的文章对我们的影响有多大。

paras.en: The researchers recruited over 200 undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline.
paras.zh: 研究人员在两项研究中招募了两百多名本科生，重点关注他们是否认为体罚孩子是一种有效的管教方式。

paras.en: The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child, on a scale from one completely disbelieve to nine completely believe.
paras.zh: 学生们先报告自己最初的看法，即体罚是不是管教孩子的有效方式，打分从一到九，一表示完全不相信，九表示完全相信。

paras.en: Several weeks later, they were given one of two research-based texts to read, each with several pages long, and either presented the arguments and data in favor of physical punishment or against it.
paras.zh: 几周后，研究人员给他们一篇根据研究写成的文章去读，一共有两篇，每篇都有好几页长，要么摆出支持体罚的论点和数据，要么摆出反对体罚的。

paras.en: After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text.
paras.zh: 读完之后，学生们回答了一些问题，用来测试他们对文章的理解和记忆。

paras.en: Then, the students again scored their belief in whether physical punishment is effective or not.
paras.zh: 接着，学生们再次给自己的看法打分，即是否认为体罚有效。

paras.en: Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
paras.zh: 最后，研究人员让他们回忆一下，研究开始时自己的看法是什么。

paras.en: The students’ belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position.
paras.zh: 学生们读了反驳自己最初立场的文章后，对体罚的看法就变了。

paras.en: Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief.
paras.zh: 关键在于，他们对自己最初看法的记忆，也朝着新看法的方向偏移了。

paras.en: In fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief.
paras.zh: 其实，他们记得的看法更接近现在的看法，而不是原来的看法。

paras.en: The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce their initial belief.
paras.zh: 看法变化越大，这种记忆偏差往往就越大，这说明学生们是根据现在的看法来推测自己最初的看法的。

paras.en: The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they’d understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn’t play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
paras.zh: 这种记忆偏差，跟他们对文章理解得怎么样、记住了多少都没有关系，这说明这些因素既不影响他们对最初看法的记忆，也不影响他们是否察觉到自己看法的变化。

paras.en: The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs.
paras.zh: 研究人员承认，这项研究关注的主要是温和观点的变化。

paras.en: It’s likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
paras.zh: 如果变的是极端的或根深蒂固的看法，研究结果很可能就不一样了。

paras.en: However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.
paras.zh: 不过，我们在大多数话题上的看法都比较温和，日常生活中我们读着各种信息类的材料，这些有趣的发现表明，刚读到的东西怎样更新、改变了我们自己的立场，我们大多一无所知。

w.m: adj. 引人入胜的；有趣的

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggest?
paras.zh: 第十六题：《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文指出了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What happened when the students read a text that argued against their own initial position?
paras.zh: 第十七题：学生们读了反驳自己最初立场的文章后，发生了什么？

paras.en: Question 18: What did the researchers concede concerning their findings?
paras.zh: 第十八题：关于研究结果，研究人员承认了什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms.
paras.zh: 随着美国人口增长，美国母亲的人数也在增长。

paras.en: But more than a century after Mother’s Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
paras.zh: 可是，母亲节成为正式节日已经一百多年了，尽管母亲的人数在增加，母亲在美国人口中所占的比例却降到了二十五年来的最低点。

paras.en: It’s frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries, but the less observed consequence of this trend is that a decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in general.
paras.zh: 人们常说，富裕国家的生育率正在急剧下降，但这一趋势有一个不太受关注的后果：出生人数下降，也可能意味着母亲这个群体整体在缩小。

paras.en: According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau: the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly and may continue for some time yet.
paras.zh: 我分析了人口普查局的数据，发现美国母亲人数减少是真实存在的，减少得很快，而且可能还会持续一段时间。

paras.en: Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline.
paras.zh: 母亲不仅在人口中所占的比例变小了，她们的特点也在变化，而这种变化可能跟她们比例的下降有关。

paras.en: Moms today tend to be older than in the past.
paras.zh: 如今的母亲往往比过去年龄大。

paras.en: Just looking at recent years, the change in age-specific birth rates has been drastic.
paras.zh: 光看最近几年，各年龄段生育率的变化就非常大。

paras.en: In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25 to 29 to that of 30 to 34.
paras.zh: 仅仅在过去几年里，美国女性的生育高峰年龄段就从二十五到二十九岁推迟到了三十到三十四岁。

paras.en: Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
paras.zh: 与此同时，二十岁以下女性的生育减少了一半甚至更多，而三十五岁及以上女性的生育却在增加。

paras.en: One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children.
paras.zh: 这种年龄变化有一个好处：在新妈妈中，经济上有能力养孩子的人比例更高了。

paras.en: Less positively, however, many women find that as they age, they can’t have as many kids as they would like.
paras.zh: 不过也有不太好的一面，很多女性发现，随着年龄增长，她们没法想生几个就生几个了。

paras.en: Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications.
paras.zh: 再说，晚育还会增加出现健康并发症的风险。

paras.en: These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older mom’s trend is that fewer years of a woman’s life are spent as a mother.
paras.zh: 这些细节先不说，母亲年龄变大这一趋势有一个主要后果，就是女性一生中当母亲的年数变少了。

paras.en: This means that at any given time, a larger share of women, and thus of the whole population, will report not having children in government surveys.
paras.zh: 这意味着，在任何一个时间点，都会有更大比例的女性，也就是更大比例的总人口，在政府调查中报告自己没有孩子。

paras.en: In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
paras.zh: 换句话说，生孩子晚，母亲就少。

paras.en: Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother’s Day, of course, endure.
paras.zh: 尽管母亲的比例在下降，母亲节当然还是会延续下去。

paras.en: In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising.
paras.zh: 事实上，尽管人口结构变了，人们在这个节日上的零售消费似乎还在增加。

w.m: adj. 人口的；人口结构的

paras.en: It is hard to say if Mother’s Day spending is rising more than one would expect, given that the American population keeps growing.
paras.zh: 考虑到美国人口一直在增长，母亲节的消费是不是比预想的增长得更多，很难说。

paras.en: But one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising, and those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.
paras.zh: 不过，有一个因素可能是，孩子已经成年的母亲所占的比例在上升，而这些成年子女给不住在一起的妈妈过节时，可能会更舍得花钱。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker conclude from her analysis of the Census Bureau’s data?
paras.zh: 第十九题：说话人分析了人口普查局的数据后，得出了什么结论？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the speaker say is a positive consequence of the age shift in childbearing?
paras.zh: 第二十题：说话人认为生育年龄的变化有什么好处？

paras.en: Question 21: What might be one explanation for the rise in retail spending on Mother’s Day?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：母亲节零售消费增长的原因之一可能是什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that house plants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air, but a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
paras.zh: 1989年，美国国家航空航天局发表了一篇论文，称室内植物能吸收污染物和有毒化学物质，从那以后，企业和住户越来越多地花钱买绿植来净化空气，但一项新的分析表明，每平方米可能要放一千多株植物，效果才能超过简单地开两扇窗户。

paras.en: The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people’s homes or offices.
paras.zh: 问题在于，美国国家航空航天局是在密封容器里做的试验，这模拟不了大多数人家里或办公室里的条件。

paras.en: The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations, and helping to combat sick building syndrome, which had become a problem due to the super-insulated and energy-efficient offices of the late 1970s, by the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleepiness, headaches, and allergies as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
paras.zh: 这家航天机构最关心的，是让困在生物圈或空间站里的宇航员呼吸到新鲜空气，同时帮助对付“病态建筑综合征”。这个问题是20世纪70年代末那些高度隔热、节能的办公楼造成的，到了80年代初，员工们吸进油漆和塑料里散发的有毒化学物质，经常抱怨皮疹、嗜睡、头痛和过敏。

paras.en: NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today, garden centers recommend the plants for air cleaning properties.
paras.zh: 美国国家航空航天局发现，某些植物能清除空气中的化学物质，直到今天，园艺中心还在推荐这些植物，说它们能净化空气。

paras.en: However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that house plants in a normal environment have little impact.
paras.zh: 可是，一项对三十年来几十项研究的新评估发现，在正常环境下，室内植物的作用微乎其微。

paras.en: In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air.
paras.zh: 事实上，自然通风净化空气的效果要好得多。

paras.en: The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analyzed, and found that the rate at which plants disperse the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange in a normal building, caused by the movement of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
paras.zh: 研究人员还计算了所分析的研究中植物的洁净空气输出率，发现植物驱散（清除）这些化合物的速度远远低于普通建筑里正常的换气速度，换气是由人们进进出出、开门开窗带来的。

paras.en: Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air-purifying virtues of plants.
paras.zh: 很多研究的确显示，挥发性有机化合物的浓度会随着时间推移而降低，人们大概就是抓住了这一点，来夸植物净化空气的好处。

paras.en: But the researchers’ calculations showed it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air cleaning capacity of a building’s air handling system, or even just a couple of open windows in a house.
paras.zh: 可研究人员的计算表明，每平方米地面要放十到一千株植物，才比得上一栋楼的空气处理系统的净化能力，甚至才比得上家里开着的两扇窗户。

paras.en: In contrast, NASA’s sealed experiment recommended one pot plant per 100 square feet.
paras.zh: 相比之下，美国国家航空航天局的密封试验建议每一百平方英尺放一盆植物。

paras.en: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time, but it’s also a great example of how scientific research should continually re-examine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what’s actually happening.
paras.zh: 这无疑是一个例子，说明科学发现随着时间推移可能会误导人，或者被人误解；但它也是一个很好的例子，说明科学研究应当不断重新检验、质疑已有的发现，才能更接近事情的真相，弄清楚到底发生了什么。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does NASA’s 1989 paper claim house plants can do?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：美国国家航空航天局1989年的论文称室内植物能做什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What is said to be the problem with NASA’s study reported in its 1989 paper?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：美国国家航空航天局1989年论文里报告的那项研究，据说有什么问题？

paras.en: Question 24: What is the finding of a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：一项对三十年来几十项研究的新评估有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 25: What does NASA’s Sealed Experiment Recommendation exemplify in scientists’ pursuit of truth?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：美国国家航空航天局的密封试验所给的建议，体现了科学家追求真理过程中的什么？

w.m: v. 是……的典型；举例说明

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2024年6月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2024年6月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，经纪人玛格丽特同意签赞助合同，但要求把中东排除在外，因为她的客户在中东还有房地产方面的广告合作；斯蒂芬认为问题不大，但还得跟几个部门核实。第二段长对话里，记者葆拉·汉考克在丹佛天文台报道奥本海默彗星：今晚它离地球是一百多年来最近的一次，用普通望远镜就能看清，找它可以借助手机应用。第一篇短文介绍营养学界关于膳食指南该不该提醒人们少吃超加工食品的争论。第二篇短文讲限制反而能激发创造力，资源少的时候，人们更会想办法换个方式用资源。第一段录音介绍处理冲突的五种风格：乌龟、鲨鱼、泰迪熊、狐狸和猫头鹰。第二段录音讲科学家要测出地球上全部一百五十万种已知动植物的基因序列，以拯救物种、促进人类健康。第三段录音介绍英国学者汤姆·奥利弗的观点：个体自我只是一种错觉，人与世界紧密相连，只有认识到这一点，才能解决环境和社会问题。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Thank you for meeting with me, Stephen, at such short notice.
paras.zh: 斯蒂芬，谢谢你这么临时还肯跟我见面。

paras.en: Not a problem, Margaret.
paras.zh: 没问题，玛格丽特。

paras.en: Now, please give me some good news.
paras.zh: 好了，请给我带来点好消息吧。

paras.en: Have you agreed to my last proposal?
paras.zh: 我上次的提议你同意了吗？

paras.en: I have indeed, and I wish to sign the agreement pending one small change to be made to the contract.
paras.zh: 确实同意了，我愿意签这份协议，只是合同里还有一处小地方要改，改好就签。

paras.en: Margaret, we have been through this for almost a year now, back and forth making alterations.
paras.zh: 玛格丽特，这件事我们已经来来回回改了快一年了。

paras.en: Are you sure you want to make a sponsorship deal for your clients or not?
paras.zh: 你到底想不想给你的客户签这份赞助协议？

paras.en: I ask this because, frankly, some people at my end are running out of patience.
paras.zh: 我这么问，是因为说实话，我这边有些人已经快没耐心了。

paras.en: I understand your concerns, but as I’m sure you understand, we hold our clients’ best interests to be of the utmost concern.
paras.zh: 你的担心我理解，不过我相信你也明白，客户的最大利益是我们最看重的。

paras.en: We therefore comb through the fine details of all contracts, rest assured, we all appreciate your firm’s patience.
paras.zh: 所以我们会仔细审查所有合同的每一处细节。请放心，你们公司的耐心，我们都很感激。

paras.en: Okay, fine.
paras.zh: 好吧，行。

paras.en: So, what changes do you wish to make?
paras.zh: 那么，你想改哪些地方？

paras.en: Essentially, we would like the new deal to exclude the Middle East.
paras.zh: 简单来说，我们希望新协议不包括中东。

paras.en: That’s all.
paras.zh: 就这些。

paras.en: The Middle East.
paras.zh: 中东。

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么？

paras.en: My client has a couple of other prospective marketing deals from companies in the Middle East; those offers, should they materialize, would exclusively employ my client’s image in the Middle East only.
paras.zh: 我的客户另外还有几家中东公司可能会找她做营销合作；这些合作要是真谈成了，就只会在中东使用我客户的形象。

paras.en: Therefore, in order to avoid any conflict, we would need to ensure that both marketing campaigns do not overlap geographically.
paras.zh: 所以，为了避免冲突，我们得确保两项营销活动在地域上不重叠。

paras.en: What business sector in the Middle East are we talking about here?
paras.zh: 我们说的是中东的哪个行业？

paras.en: Real estate.
paras.zh: 房地产。

paras.en: Well, that should be okay then, so long as the product is very different from our food and beverage market, there should be no conflict of interest.
paras.zh: 嗯，那应该没问题，只要产品跟我们的食品饮料市场差别很大，就不会有利益冲突。

paras.en: Nevertheless, I will have to run this through my people.
paras.zh: 不过，我还得让我手下的人过一遍。

paras.en: I don’t foresee any problem, though.
paras.zh: 不过我估计不会有什么问题。

paras.en: The Middle East is a negligible market for us, but I still need to check this with a couple of departments.
paras.zh: 中东对我们来说是个可以忽略不计的市场，但我还是得跟几个部门核实一下。

w.m: adj. 可以忽略的；微不足道的

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the woman say she will do?
paras.zh: 第一题：女士说她会做什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say about some people he represents?
paras.zh: 第二题：关于他所代表的一些人，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Question three: What reason does the woman give for the New Deal to exclude the Middle East?
paras.zh: 第三题：女士给出了什么理由，要求新协议不包括中东？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man say about the Middle East?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于中东，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Next, we have a special science-related news story.
paras.zh: 接下来，我们有一条与科学有关的特别新闻。

paras.en: Paula Hancock is at the Denver Observatory.
paras.zh: 葆拉·汉考克现在在丹佛天文台。

paras.en: Paula, what is the big story over there?
paras.zh: 葆拉，你那边有什么大新闻？

paras.en: Hi, John.
paras.zh: 你好，约翰。

paras.en: Yes, all the astronomers on site here are very excited.
paras.zh: 是的，现场所有的天文学家都非常兴奋。

paras.en: In fact, space enthusiasts all across North America and the rest of the northern hemisphere will be congregating on mountain tops tonight to watch the night sky.
paras.zh: 事实上，今晚整个北美以及北半球其他地方的太空爱好者都会聚到山顶上观看夜空。

paras.en: Why?
paras.zh: 为什么？

paras.en: What’s the big event?
paras.zh: 是什么大事？

paras.en: Is there an eclipse happening soon?
paras.zh: 是快有日食或月食了吗？

paras.en: Tonight, the Earth will come into close proximity with the Oppenheimer comet.
paras.zh: 今晚，地球将与奥本海默彗星靠得非常近。

paras.en: It is the closest our planet has been to such a phenomenon in over 100 years.
paras.zh: 这是一百多年来，我们的星球离这类天象最近的一次。

paras.en: For this reason, it is expected that 1000s of people will gaze up at the sky tonight in order to see this formidable object.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，预计今晚会有成千上万的人抬头仰望天空，来看这个令人惊叹的天体。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；了不起的

paras.en: How far away is this comet?
paras.zh: 这颗彗星离我们有多远？

paras.en: Will people be able to see it with the naked eye?
paras.zh: 人们用肉眼能看到它吗？

paras.en: The Oppenheimer comet will still be millions of miles away, on the edge of our galaxy.
paras.zh: 奥本海默彗星仍然在几百万英里以外，在我们星系的边缘。

paras.en: But nevertheless, this is a relatively close distance, close enough for people to observe in good detail through a telescope.
paras.zh: 但这个距离已经算比较近了，近到人们用望远镜就能看清它的细节。

paras.en: People will only see a blur without one.
paras.zh: 没有望远镜的话，人们只能看到模模糊糊的一团。

paras.en: However, that does not mean one needs professional equipment.
paras.zh: 不过，这并不是说一定要有专业设备。

paras.en: Even the most ordinary of telescopes should be conducive for people to observe and wonder at this flying object.
paras.zh: 哪怕是最普通的望远镜，也足以让人们观察这个飞行的天体，感叹它的神奇。

paras.en: Many of our viewers will be wondering how they too can take part in this once-in-a-lifetime event.
paras.zh: 我们很多观众肯定在想，自己怎样才能也参与这一生难得一遇的盛事。

paras.en: Where will this comet be in the sky.
paras.zh: 这颗彗星会出现在天空的什么位置？

paras.en: How can people find it?
paras.zh: 人们怎么才能找到它？

paras.en: The comet will be almost exactly due north, at 60 degrees above the equator.
paras.zh: 这颗彗星几乎就在正北方向，在赤道以上六十度的位置。

paras.en: However, finding the comet is indeed very tricky, and scientists here have told me there are plenty of phone apps that will facilitate this.
paras.zh: 不过，要找到这颗彗星确实很不容易，这里的科学家告诉我，有很多手机应用能帮上忙。

paras.en: How fantastic!
paras.zh: 太棒了！

paras.en: Thank you, Paula, for the information.
paras.zh: 葆拉，谢谢你带来的消息。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the woman say about all the astronomers at the Denver Observatory?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于丹佛天文台的所有天文学家，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question six: What do we learn from the conversation about the Oppenheimer comet?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于奥本海默彗星，我们从对话中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the woman say people will only see in the sky without a telescope?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士说，没有望远镜的话，人们在天空中只能看到什么？

paras.en: Question eight: What do scientists at the Denver Observatory advise amateurs do to facilitate their observation?
paras.zh: 第八题：丹佛天文台的科学家建议业余爱好者用什么来方便观测？

paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: Passage one: Dietary guidelines form the basis for nutrition advice and regulations around the world.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文：膳食指南是世界各地营养建议和法规的基础。

paras.en: While there is strong scientific consensus around most existing guidelines, one question has recently stirred debate: Should consumers be warned to avoid ultra-processed foods?
paras.zh: 虽然现有的大多数指南在科学界都有很强的共识，但最近有一个问题引发了争论：要不要提醒消费者避免吃超加工食品？

paras.en: Two papers published today in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition outline the case for and against using the concept of ultra-processed foods to help inform dietary guidelines beyond conventional food classification systems.
paras.zh: 今天发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上的两篇论文，分别阐述了支持和反对的理由：在常规的食物分类体系之外，要不要借助“超加工食品”这个概念来为膳食指南提供依据。

paras.en: The authors, Carlos Monteiro of the University of Sao Paulo, and Arne Astrup of Novo Nordisk Foundation will discuss the issue in a live virtual debate, august 14, during Nutrition 2024 live online.
paras.zh: 两位作者，圣保罗大学的卡洛斯·蒙泰罗和诺和诺德基金会的阿尔内·阿斯特鲁普，将于8月14日在“2024营养大会”线上直播期间，进行一场网络直播辩论，讨论这个问题。

paras.en: The debate centers around a system developed by Monteiro and colleagues that classifies foods by their degree of industrial processing, ranging from unprocessed to ultra-processed.
paras.zh: 这场辩论的核心，是蒙泰罗和同事们开发的一套体系，它按工业加工程度给食物分类，从未加工到超加工。

paras.en: The system defines ultra-processed foods as those made using sequences of processes that extract substances from foods and alter them with chemicals in order to formulate the final product.
paras.zh: 这套体系对超加工食品的定义是：经过一系列工序制成的食品，这些工序从食物中提取物质，再用化学品改变它们，最后配制成成品。

paras.en: Ultra-processed foods are characteristically designed to be cheap, tasty, and convenient.
paras.zh: 超加工食品的特点就是设计得便宜、好吃、方便。

paras.en: Examples include soft drinks and candy, packaged snacks and pastries, ready-to-heat products, and reconstituted meat products.
paras.zh: 比如汽水和糖果、包装零食和糕点、加热即食的产品，还有重组肉制品。

paras.en: Studies have linked consumption of ultra-processed foods, which are often high in salt, sugar, and fat, with weight gain and an increased risk of chronic diseases, even after adjusting for the amount of salt, sugar, and fat in the diet.
paras.zh: 研究发现，超加工食品往往盐、糖、脂肪含量都很高，吃这类食品与体重增加、慢性病风险上升有关，即使把饮食中盐、糖、脂肪的量考虑进去之后也是如此。

paras.en: While the mechanisms behind these associations are not fully understood, Monteiro argues that the existing evidence is sufficient to justify discouraging consumption of ultra-processed foods in dietary recommendations and government policies.
paras.zh: 虽然这些关联背后的机制还没有完全弄清楚，但蒙泰罗认为，现有证据已经足以说明，膳食建议和政府政策应当劝人们少吃超加工食品。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What question is said to have recently stirred debate?
paras.zh: 第九题：据说最近引发争论的是什么问题？

paras.en: Question 10: How does the system developed by Monteiro and colleagues classify foods?
paras.zh: 第十题：蒙泰罗和同事们开发的体系是怎样给食物分类的？

paras.en: Question 11: What is consumption of ultra-processed foods linked with, according to studies?
paras.zh: 第十一题：据研究，吃超加工食品与什么有关？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Believe it or not, human creativity benefits from constraints.
paras.zh: 信不信由你，人的创造力能从限制中获益。

paras.en: According to psychologists, when you have less to work with, you actually begin to see the world differently.
paras.zh: 心理学家认为，手头可用的东西越少，人们看世界的眼光其实就会不一样。

paras.en: With constraints, you dedicate your mental energy to acting more resourcefully.
paras.zh: 有了限制，你就会把心思花在怎样更巧妙地利用资源上。

w.m: adv. 机智地；足智多谋地

paras.en: When challenged, you figure out new ways to be better.
paras.zh: 遇到挑战时，你就会想出新办法，让自己做得更好。

paras.en: The most successful creative people know that constraints give their minds the impetus to leap higher.
paras.zh: 最成功的创意人士都知道，限制能激励他们的头脑跳得更高。

paras.en: People who invent new products are not limited by what they don’t have or can’t do; they leverage their limitations to push themselves even further.
paras.zh: 发明新产品的人不会被自己没有的东西、做不到的事情所束缚；他们会利用自身的局限，逼自己走得更远。

paras.en: Many products and services are created because the founders saw a limitation in what they use, they created innovation based on what was not working for them at the moment.
paras.zh: 很多产品和服务之所以诞生，是因为创始人看到了自己所用东西的局限，于是根据当时对自己行不通的地方进行创新。

paras.en: Innovation is a creative person’s response to limitation.
paras.zh: 创新是有创造力的人对局限做出的回应。

paras.en: In a 2015 study, which examined how thinking about scarcity or abundance influences how creatively people use their resources, Ravi Mehta at the University of Illinois and Meng Zhu at Johns Hopkins University found that people simply have no incentive to use what’s available to them in novel ways.
paras.zh: 在2015年的一项研究中，研究人员考察了人们想到资源稀缺或充足时，会怎样影响他们使用资源的创造性，伊利诺伊大学的拉维·梅塔和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的朱萌发现，人们在资源充足时根本就没有动力用新方法利用手头的东西。

paras.en: When people face scarcity, they give themselves the freedom to use resources in less conventional ways because they have to.
paras.zh: 人们面对稀缺时，就会允许自己用不那么常规的方式利用资源，因为他们不得不这样做。

paras.en: Obstacles can broaden your perception and open up your thinking processes.
paras.zh: 障碍能拓宽你的视野，打开你的思路。

paras.en: Consistent constraints help you improve at connecting unrelated ideas and concepts.
paras.zh: 持续不断的限制有助于你更善于把互不相关的想法和概念联系起来。

paras.en: Marissa Mayer, former vice president for search products and user experience at Google once wrote in a publication on Bloomberg: constraints shape and focus problems and provide clear challenges to overcome.
paras.zh: 谷歌前搜索产品与用户体验副总裁玛丽莎·梅耶尔，曾在彭博社的一篇文章中写道：限制能让问题成形、更有针对性，还能提供明确的挑战让人去攻克。

w.m: n. 出版物；发表的文章

paras.en: Creativity thrives best when constrained.
paras.zh: 创造力在受到限制时最能蓬勃发展。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard, Question 12: What do psychologists say people do when they are short of resources?
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。第十二题：心理学家说人们在资源短缺时会怎么做？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the passage say about innovation?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于创新，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What did a 2015 study by Ravi Mehta and Meng Zhu find?
paras.zh: 第十四题：拉维·梅塔和朱萌2015年的研究发现了什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What did Marissa Mayer once write concerning creativity?
paras.zh: 第十五题：关于创造力，玛丽莎·梅耶尔曾经写过什么？

paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。
