paras.zh: 第十七题：关于咖啡，说话人提醒人们注意什么？

paras.en: Question 18: How can we get sufficient nutrients according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十八题：根据说话人的说法，我们怎样才能获得足够的营养？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: The late Swedish academic Hans Rosling has identified a worrying trend.
paras.zh: 已故瑞典学者汉斯·罗斯林发现了一个令人担忧的趋势。

paras.en: Not only do many people across advanced economies have no idea that the world is becoming a much better place, but they actually even think the opposite.
paras.zh: 发达经济体中的许多人不仅不知道世界正在变得越来越好，实际上甚至还认为恰恰相反。

paras.en: This is no wonder, when the news focuses on reporting catastrophes, terrorist attacks, wars, and famines.
paras.zh: 新闻总是集中报道灾难、恐怖袭击、战争和饥荒，这也就难怪了。

paras.en: Who wants to hear about the fact that every day some 200,000 people around the world are lifted above the two-dollar-a-day poverty line.
paras.zh: 谁会想听这样的事实：每天全世界约有20万人跨过了每天两美元的贫困线？

paras.en: Or that more than 300,000 people get access to electricity and clean water for the first time every day.
paras.zh: 或者，每天都有30多万人第一次用上电和干净的水？

paras.en: These stories of people in low-income countries simply don’t make for exciting news coverage, but as Rosling pointed out in his book Factfulness, it’s important to put all the bad news in perspective.
paras.zh: 这些关于低收入国家人民的故事，根本成不了吸引人的新闻报道。但正如罗斯林在他的《事实》一书中所指出的，把所有坏消息放到全局中去看，是很重要的。

w.m: adj. 令人兴奋的；吸引人的

paras.en: While it is true that globalization has put some downward pressure on middle-class wages in advanced economies in recent decades, it has also helped lift hundreds of millions of people above the global poverty line.
paras.zh: 诚然，近几十年来，全球化给发达经济体中产阶级的工资带来了一些下行压力，但它也帮助数亿人跨过了全球贫困线。

paras.en: If we really care about global welfare, globalization is the only way forward to ensure that economic prosperity is shared among all countries and not only a select few advanced economies.
paras.zh: 如果我们真的关心全球福祉，全球化就是唯一的出路，能确保经济繁荣由所有国家共享，而不只是少数几个发达经济体。

paras.en: While some people glorify the past, one of the big facts of economic history is that until quite recently, a significant part of the world population has lived under quite miserable conditions, and this has been true throughout most of human history.
paras.zh: 虽然有些人美化过去，但经济史上的一个重要事实是，直到不久之前，世界上相当一部分人口一直生活在相当悲惨的条件下，而且在人类历史的大部分时间里都是如此。

paras.en: While there were many long-lasting ups and downs, like the Great Depression or the recent Great Recession, the constancy of the long-run growth rate is actually quite miraculous.
paras.zh: 虽然经历过许多长期的起起落落，比如大萧条和最近的大衰退，但长期增长率保持稳定，其实相当了不起。

paras.en: Low-income countries, including China and India, have been growing at a significantly faster pace in recent decades, and are quickly catching up to the West.
paras.zh: 近几十年来，包括中国和印度在内的低收入国家发展速度明显更快，正在迅速追赶西方。

paras.en: A 10% growth rate over a prolonged period means that income levels double roughly every seven years.
paras.zh: 在一段很长的时期内保持10%的增长率，意味着收入水平大约每七年翻一番。

w.m: adj. 持续很久的；长期的

paras.en: It is obviously good news if prosperity is more shared across the globe, while inequality within countries has gone up as a result of globalization, global inequality has been on a steady downward trend for several decades.
paras.zh: 如果繁荣能在全球得到更广泛的共享，这显然是好消息。尽管全球化导致各国国内的不平等加剧，但几十年来，全球不平等一直在稳步下降。

paras.en: This is mostly a result of the improvement of hundreds of millions of people’s living standards.
paras.zh: 这主要是因为数亿人的生活水平得到了改善。

paras.en: In fact, for the first time ever since the Industrial Revolution, about half of the global population can be considered middle class.
paras.zh: 事实上，自工业革命以来，全球大约一半的人口第一次可以算作中产阶级。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What is the worrying trend the late Swedish academic has identified?
paras.zh: 第十九题：这位已故瑞典学者发现的令人担忧的趋势是什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the speaker say about globalization?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于全球化，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What do we learn about half of the global population?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：关于全球一半的人口，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: We all know that the sense of smell is powerful.
paras.zh: 我们都知道，嗅觉的力量很强大。

paras.en: The delicious scent of bread, for example, can act like a time machine.
paras.zh: 比如，面包的香味就能像时光机一样。

paras.en: One sniff can bring back a memory from many years ago.
paras.zh: 闻一下，就能唤起多年前的一段记忆。

paras.en: Indeed, scent particles in general can revive memories that have been long forgotten.
paras.zh: 确实，一般来说，气味分子能唤醒早已遗忘的记忆。

paras.en: But why do smells sometimes trigger powerful memories, especially emotional ones?
paras.zh: 但为什么气味有时会引发强烈的记忆，尤其是带有情感的记忆？

paras.en: The short answer is that the brain regions that handle smells, memories, and emotions are linked.
paras.zh: 简单来说，因为大脑中处理气味、记忆和情感的区域是相互联系的。

paras.en: A scent is a chemical particle that floats in through the nose and into the region of the brain responsible for smell, where the sensation is first processed into a form that the brain can read.
paras.zh: 气味是一种化学微粒，它从鼻子飘进去，进入大脑负责嗅觉的区域，在那里，这种感觉首先被处理成大脑能读懂的形式。

paras.en: Brain cells then carry that information to the area of the brain where emotions are processed, and then to an adjacent area of the brain where learning and memory formation take place.
paras.zh: 然后，脑细胞把这些信息传送到大脑处理情感的区域，再传到旁边一个负责学习和形成记忆的区域。

paras.en: Scents are the only sensations that travel such a direct path to the emotional and memory centers of the brain, that results in an intimate connection between emotions, memories, and scents, which is why memories triggered by scents are experienced as more emotional than those triggered by sight or sound.
paras.zh: 气味是唯一能走这样一条直接通路、到达大脑情感和记忆中枢的感觉，这就使情感、记忆和气味之间有了密切的联系，所以由气味引发的记忆，比由视觉或声音引发的记忆更带有情感色彩。

paras.en: Let’s take a closer look at how those memories are activated.
paras.zh: 我们来仔细看看这些记忆是怎样被激活的。

paras.en: Usually, when a person smells something that’s connected to a meaningful event in their past, they’ll first have an emotional response to the sensation, and then a memory might follow.
paras.zh: 通常，当一个人闻到与自己过去某件重要的事有关的气味时，他会先对这种感觉产生情绪反应，随后记忆才可能浮现。

paras.en: But sometimes the memory doesn’t come to the surface.
paras.zh: 但有时候，记忆并不会浮现出来。

paras.en: The person might feel the emotion of something that happened in the past but won’t remember what they experienced.
paras.zh: 这个人可能感受到过去某件事带来的情绪，却想不起自己经历过什么。

paras.en: What causes this baffling phenomenon?
paras.zh: 是什么导致了这种令人费解的现象？

paras.en: The explanation is context.
paras.zh: 答案是情境。

paras.en: Imagine this scenario: a person is walking down the street, smelling a scent that they first encountered decades ago, which activates an emotional response.
paras.zh: 设想这样一个情景：一个人走在街上，闻到一种几十年前第一次闻到的气味，这引起了一种情绪反应。

paras.en: If the person had first come across that smell in a very different context, it will be much more difficult to recover the associated memory because the brain uses the context to give meaning to the information and find that memory.
paras.zh: 如果这个人最初是在一个非常不同的情境下闻到这种气味的，要找回相关的记忆就会难得多，因为大脑要靠情境来赋予信息意义、找到那段记忆。

paras.en: The special nature of memories brought back by scents, notwithstanding, they have the same drawbacks as other memories, they aren’t always accurate, and they can change over time.
paras.zh: 尽管由气味唤起的记忆很特别，但它们和其他记忆有着同样的缺点：不总是准确，而且会随着时间改变。

w.m: prep. 尽管（可放在名词之后）

paras.en: In fact, each time we remember something, that memory can become distorted.
paras.zh: 事实上，每次我们回忆某件事，那段记忆都可能被扭曲。

paras.en: But because of the strong emotional associations these memories evoke, people who remember something due to a scent are often convinced that the memories are accurate, even when they aren’t.
paras.zh: 但由于这些记忆唤起的情感联想很强烈，因为闻到某种气味而想起某件事的人，往往深信这些记忆是准确的，即使事实并非如此。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What question does the speaker try to answer in this talk?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人在这段讲话中试图回答什么问题？

paras.en: Question 23: What is said to result in an intimate connection between emotions, memories, and scents?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：据说是什么导致了情感、记忆和气味之间的密切联系？

paras.en: Question 24: What does the brain use to give meaning to information and find a memory?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：大脑用什么来赋予信息意义、找到记忆？

paras.en: Question 25: What drawback do memories of scents share with other memories?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：气味唤起的记忆和其他记忆有什么共同的缺点？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2025年6月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2025年6月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，电脑维修工程师上门修电脑，女士抱怨等了十天才来人，工程师道歉，并提醒数据要先备份。第二段长对话里，一位专做房地产纠纷调解的律师向想学法律的年轻人介绍这一行，说明庭外解决纠纷的好处和律师需要的能力。第一篇短文讲老年人提取记忆比较困难，是因为积累的知识太多，但这也有助于创造力和决策。第二篇短文讲美国工作中的四大问题，并介绍“后工作”理论的主张。第一段录音介绍一项婴儿实验：看到大人努力后成功的婴儿，会更坚持地去按玩具的按钮。第二段录音教经常迟到的人怎样做到准时：提早出门、定两个闹钟、提前准备、给行程留出余地。第三段录音讲波士顿人为什么显得匆忙、不够礼貌，以及专家给出的几种解释。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six Part Two, Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解。

paras.en: Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Good morning.
paras.zh: 早上好。

paras.en: My name is Bob Fetterman.
paras.zh: 我叫鲍勃·费特曼。

paras.en: I’m the computer technician.
paras.zh: 我是电脑维修技术员。

paras.en: Didn’t I call for you last week?
paras.zh: 我上周不是打电话找过你们吗？

paras.en: Maybe.
paras.zh: 也许吧。

paras.en: I work for Alpha Maintenance.
paras.zh: 我在阿尔法维修公司工作。

paras.en: I imagine someone from your office called our central office, and I’m the engineer designated to your case.
paras.zh: 我想是你们办公室有人给我们总部打了电话，我就是被指派来处理你们这件事的工程师。

w.m: n. 事例；（需处理的）事情

paras.en: Yeah, I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago.
paras.zh: 是啊，我上周二跟那边一位女士通过电话，到现在都十天了。

paras.en: I made it clear it was an urgent matter, and please send someone as soon as possible.
paras.zh: 我说得很清楚，这事很急，请尽快派人来。

paras.en: Couldn’t you or someone else have come sooner?
paras.zh: 你或者别的人就不能早点来吗？

paras.en: I’m sorry, but I’m not in charge of scheduling all logistics.
paras.zh: 很抱歉，不过所有的后勤安排都不归我管。

paras.en: I simply do not know.
paras.zh: 我真的不知道。

paras.en: All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could.
paras.zh: 我只能告诉你，我这周接到电话，就尽快赶过来了。

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: Well, I’ll have you know my manager is rather indignant that it’s taken you this long to come.
paras.zh: 那我得让你知道，你们拖了这么久才来，我们经理相当生气。

paras.en: I understand it might not be your fault, but nevertheless you should know what the feeling is around here.
paras.zh: 我知道这可能不是你的错，不过你也该知道这里大家是什么感受。

paras.en: I understand, and I’m sorry for any inconvenience.
paras.zh: 我明白，给您带来不便，很抱歉。

paras.en: I will try to resolve your computer problem as swiftly and optimally as I can.
paras.zh: 我会尽量又快又好地解决您的电脑问题。

w.m: adv. 最佳地；以最好的方式

paras.en: What and where is the issue?
paras.zh: 是什么问题，出在哪里？

paras.en: It’s this machine right here.
paras.zh: 就是这儿的这台机器。

paras.en: It was running slow for a while, I guess, and gradually got worse and worse.
paras.zh: 我想它有一阵子运行得很慢，后来越来越糟。

paras.en: Last Tuesday, it just stopped working altogether.
paras.zh: 上周二，它干脆完全不动了。

paras.en: If you switch it on, you will see what I mean.
paras.zh: 你一开机就知道我说的是什么意思了。

paras.en: Okay.
paras.zh: 好的。

paras.en: Do you know if it’s backed up?
paras.zh: 你知道它有没有备份吗？

paras.en: Backed up.
paras.zh: 备份？

paras.en: I mean, do you know if its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else?
paras.zh: 我是说，你知道它里面的内容有没有复制、保存到别的地方吗？

paras.en: I don’t know.
paras.zh: 我不知道。

paras.en: Well, depending on the ensuing operative scenario, if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols, then my first intervention should be to intricately retrieve all inventories that I can.
paras.zh: 嗯，要看接下来的操作情况，如果我需要把系统目录全部清空来重新设置默认协议，那我首先要做的就是把能找回的所有资料都仔细地取出来。

w.m: adj. 接着发生的；随后的
n. （此处指电脑里存的）全部资料；清单

paras.en: Otherwise, all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost.
paras.zh: 不然，存在硬盘上的所有数据都会永远丢失。

paras.en: My manager would know.
paras.zh: 我们经理应该知道。

paras.en: Let me go get him.
paras.zh: 我去叫他来。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What did the woman do last Tuesday?
paras.zh: 第一题：这位女士上周二做了什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say he did when he got the call?
paras.zh: 第二题：男士说他接到电话后做了什么？

paras.en: Question three: What is the feeling about the problem around the woman’s workplace?
paras.zh: 第三题：女士的工作单位里大家对这个问题是什么感受？

paras.en: Question four: What does the woman say her manager would know?
paras.zh: 第四题：女士说她的经理会知道什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Have you given more thought to studying law?
paras.zh: 学法律的事，你又多考虑了吗？

paras.en: I’ve been thinking about it a lot.
paras.zh: 我一直在认真考虑这件事。

paras.en: Yes, in fact, this is why I wished to speak to you.
paras.zh: 是的，其实我就是为这个才想跟您聊聊的。

paras.en: I wanted to hear more about what it’s like.
paras.zh: 我想多了解一下这行是什么样的。

paras.en: A career in law is a beautiful thing, in my opinion.
paras.zh: 在我看来，从事法律工作是件很美好的事。

paras.en: Many people will say it’s a boring field, but I disagree.
paras.zh: 很多人会说这一行很枯燥，但我不这么认为。

paras.en: The thing is, there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.
paras.zh: 关键是，法律有很多不同的分支，工作也有很多种。

paras.en: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?
paras.zh: 你是做房屋和建筑方面的，对吧？

paras.en: Correct.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: I’m a solicitor specializing in real estate.
paras.zh: 我是专做房地产的事务律师。

paras.en: Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.
paras.zh: 我的工作大多是调解土地纠纷。

paras.en: Do you mind giving me an example?
paras.zh: 能给我举个例子吗？

paras.en: Sure.
paras.zh: 当然可以。

paras.en: So, in many cases, I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties.
paras.zh: 比如说，很多时候，我受雇在两个发生冲突的当事方之间做仲裁。

w.m: n. （协议或争端的）一方；当事人

paras.en: Let’s say, for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something, like the borders of their adjacent plots.
paras.zh: 比方说，有两个土地所有者在某件事上僵持不下，比如两块相邻地块的边界。

paras.en: Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute.
paras.zh: 可能就会有人雇我来打破僵局、解决纠纷。

paras.en: Often, my work involves negotiating agreements.
paras.zh: 我的工作往往就是谈判，达成协议。

paras.en: Plain and simple.
paras.zh: 就这么简单。

paras.en: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people’s legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.
paras.zh: 所以您是说，您做的很多事情就是解决人们的法律问题，就像是设法找到一个对大家都有利、又能防止问题升级的办法。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 完全正确。

w.m: adv. 完全正确；一点不错

paras.en: Well put.
paras.zh: 说得好。

paras.en: You need to remember that.
paras.zh: 这一点你得记住。

paras.en: Courts, like all bureaucracies, really can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive.
paras.zh: 法院跟所有的官僚机构一样，确实可能很混乱、让人憋屈，而且花钱很多。

w.m: adj. 令人沮丧的；令人憋闷的

paras.en: For this reason, it’s usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
paras.zh: 所以，只要有可能，最好还是在法庭外解决问题。

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: So, besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?
paras.zh: 那么，除了要对法律了如指掌，您还需要很强的与人打交道的能力，对吧？

paras.en: Of course.
paras.zh: 当然。

paras.en: Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating their argument.
paras.zh: 凡是跟人打交道的工作，都需要良好的人际交往能力，任何法律从业者都必须能把自己的论点讲得非常有说服力。

w.m: adj. 雄辩的；有说服力的

paras.en: Right.
paras.zh: 对。

paras.en: So I’ve been thinking about studying criminal law.
paras.zh: 所以我一直在考虑学刑法。

paras.en: I think it sounds very interesting.
paras.zh: 我觉得它听起来很有意思。

paras.en: Yes, I’d say there’s more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law.
paras.zh: 是的，我觉得做房地产法挣钱更多，但刑法的利害关系更大。

paras.en: I can see how you would find it more interesting.
paras.zh: 我能理解你为什么会觉得它更有意思。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What will many people say about a career in law?
paras.zh: 第五题：很多人会怎么评价法律这一行？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man say most of his work involves?
paras.zh: 第六题：男士说他的工作大多是什么？

paras.en: Question seven: Why does the man say it’s usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士为什么说只要有可能，最好在法庭外解决问题？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the man think is required of any law professional?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士认为任何法律从业者都需要具备什么？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information.
paras.zh: 人在试图提取一段记忆时，大脑会迅速检索其中储存的所有内容，找出相关的信息。

paras.en: But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
paras.zh: 但随着年龄增长，我们很多人都会发现提取记忆越来越难。

paras.en: In a review published in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening.
paras.zh: 2月11日，研究人员在《认知科学趋势》期刊上发表了一篇综述，对这种情况的成因提出了一种解释。

paras.en: The brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories.
paras.zh: 老年人的大脑把更多空间分配给了积累下来的知识，所以在提取记忆时要搜寻的材料也更多。

paras.en: While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides.
paras.zh: 虽然这么丰富的已有知识会让提取记忆变得困难，但研究人员说，它也有好处。

w.m: adj. 有挑战性的；困难的

paras.en: This life experience can aid with creativity and decision making.
paras.zh: 这种人生阅历有助于创造力和决策。

paras.en: Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn, and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant, and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other irrelevant memories along with it, the studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
paras.zh: 研究人员塔里克·阿梅尔、乔达娜·温和林恩·哈舍尔研究了几项行为和脑成像研究，这些研究表明，老年人很难抑制已经不再相关的信息，而且在寻找某段特定记忆时，常常会连带提取出其他无关的记忆；研究还表明，在执行认知任务时，老年人比年轻人更依赖以前的知识。

paras.en: While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful.
paras.zh: 虽然研究人员主要关注的是这些杂乱拥挤的记忆可能带来的困难，但他们也强调了这些记忆模式可能派上用场的几种情况。

paras.en: Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved and at times enhanced creativity as a function of enriched memories.
paras.zh: 有证据表明，由于记忆更加丰富，老年人的创造力保持不变，有时甚至会增强。

paras.en: The researchers write, they further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge, when it comes to decision making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道，他们还进一步推测，在做决策时，老年人可能会因已有的知识而受益，因为他们可以借助积累下来的智慧。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What did the researchers do in their review in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences?
paras.zh: 第九题：研究人员在《认知科学趋势》期刊上的综述里做了什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What do several behavioral and brain imaging studies show?
paras.zh: 第十题：几项行为和脑成像研究表明了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What does evidence suggest regarding older adults?
paras.zh: 第十一题：关于老年人，证据表明了什么？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
paras.zh: 如今美国的工作至少存在四大问题。

paras.en: First, work can be alienating.
paras.zh: 第一，工作可能让人产生疏离感。

w.m: adj. 使人疏远的；使人感到疏离的

paras.en: Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
paras.zh: 劳动者往往无法掌控自己怎样工作、何时工作，也无法决定自己生产的商品和服务如何处置、工作所创造的利润如何使用。

paras.en: Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor.
paras.zh: 第二，劳动者没有拿到与其劳动全部价值相当的报酬。

paras.en: Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor’s share of income.
paras.zh: 实际工资的增长没有跟上生产率的提高，这加剧了经济不平等，也让劳动所得在收入中的份额下降。

paras.en: Third, people are time poor.
paras.zh: 第三，人们缺少时间。

w.m: 时间匮乏的；缺少时间的

paras.en: In the U.S., full-time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day, despite productivity increases.
paras.zh: 在美国，尽管生产率提高了，全职员工平均每天仍要工作8.72小时。

paras.en: Long working hours contribute to the feeling of time poverty, which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
paras.zh: 工作时间长会让人觉得时间不够用，这对心理健康有不利影响。

paras.en: Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk.
paras.zh: 第四，自动化让工作岗位和工资面临风险。

paras.en: Technological innovation could, in theory, liberate people from the 40-hour work week, but unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
paras.zh: 从理论上讲，技术创新可以把人们从每周40小时的工作中解放出来，但除非改变工作的结构，否则自动化只会给工资带来下行压力，并进一步减少工作机会。

paras.en: So, what can be done to alleviate these problems?
paras.zh: 那么，可以做些什么来缓解这些问题呢？

paras.en: There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution.
paras.zh: 对于找到解决办法的最佳途径，有几种相互竞争的看法。

w.m: adj. 相互竞争的；对立的

paras.en: One vision is what’s known as the post-work position.
paras.zh: 其中一种看法被称为“后工作”观点。

paras.en: The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time.
paras.zh: “后工作”理论家认为，工作不应该在我们的生活中占据核心地位，也不应该占用我们这么多时间。

paras.en: They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose, and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace.
paras.zh: 他们断言，虽然做一些工作也许有必要，但意义、目标和社会价值存在于工作场所之外建立和维系的社群与人际关系之中。

paras.en: Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.
paras.zh: 因此，生活本身就应该被看作目的。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What do we learn about American workers from the passage?
paras.zh: 第十二题：从这篇短文中我们可以了解到美国劳动者的什么情况？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the passage say long working hours contribute to?
paras.zh: 第十三题：短文说工作时间长会导致什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What does automation do, according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第十四题：根据短文，自动化会带来什么影响？

paras.en: Question 15: What do post-work theorists advocate?
paras.zh: 第十五题：“后工作”理论家提倡什么？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes independent of IQ.
paras.zh: 最近的研究表明，自制力和毅力能提高学业成绩，而且与智商无关。

paras.en: Even our personal beliefs about effort can affect academic outcomes.
paras.zh: 甚至我们个人对努力的看法，也会影响学业成绩。

paras.en: Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait.
paras.zh: 认为努力就能有所成就的孩子，表现要好于那些认为能力是固定不变的孩子。

paras.en: Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about effort are particularly important in childhood.
paras.zh: 既然毅力与学业成功之间有联系，那么在童年时期，要不要付出努力的决定就尤其重要。

paras.en: Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what’s worth the effort.
paras.zh: 然而，探讨幼儿如何知道什么事值得付出努力的研究相对较少。

paras.en: We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they’re not just idly watching.
paras.zh: 我们都知道婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者，但他们并不只是闲着看看而已。

w.m: adv. 无所事事地；闲散地

paras.en: They are tiny learning machines.
paras.zh: 他们是小小的学习机器。

paras.en: They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples.
paras.zh: 他们只需要几个例子，就能归纳出因果关系、社会角色这样的抽象概念。

paras.en: Even a 15 months old infant can outperform a high-level computer in such tasks.
paras.zh: 在这类任务中，甚至一个15个月大的婴儿都能胜过高级计算机。

paras.en: Could infants also make broad, generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort?
paras.zh: 在努力这件事上，婴儿是否也能从几个例子中做出广泛的、可以推而广之的推断呢？

w.m: adj. 可推广的；可概括的

paras.en: If so, then maybe persistence isn’t simply a character trait.
paras.zh: 如果是这样，那么毅力也许不只是一种性格特质。

paras.en: Maybe it’s flexible and adaptable, based on social context.
paras.zh: 也许它是灵活的、可以根据社会环境调整的。

w.m: adj. 能适应的；可调整的

paras.en: To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things: an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal.
paras.zh: 为了探究这个问题，我们给15个月大的婴儿看两种情景之一：一个实验人员费了很大劲才实现两个不同的目标，或者一个实验人员毫不费力地实现了每个目标。

paras.en: Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top.
paras.zh: 然后我们给婴儿介绍一个新奇的音乐玩具，看起来按一下顶上的大按钮就能让它响起来。

paras.en: The button could be pressed down, but didn’t actually activate anything.
paras.zh: 这个按钮能按下去，但实际上什么也启动不了。

paras.en: Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button, so that they heard the toy making music.
paras.zh: 我们趁婴儿看不见，用一个隐藏的按钮打开了音乐玩具，让他们听到玩具在放音乐。

paras.en: We gave the babies the music toy and left the room.
paras.zh: 我们把音乐玩具交给婴儿，然后离开了房间。

paras.en: Then analysts who didn’t know which condition each baby was in watched videotapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
paras.zh: 然后，由不知道每个婴儿属于哪种实验条件的分析人员观看实验录像，数出婴儿为了启动玩具按了多少次按钮。

paras.en: Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed pushed the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed.
paras.zh: 在一项研究和一次预先登记的重复实验中，看过大人坚持并最终成功的婴儿，按按钮的次数大约是看过大人毫不费力就成功的婴儿的两倍。

paras.en: In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding.
paras.zh: 也就是说，婴儿只看了两个大人努力并获得成功的例子，就懂得了努力是有价值的。

paras.en: Part of what’s exciting about this finding is that the babies didn’t just imitate the adults’ actions.
paras.zh: 这个发现让人兴奋的部分原因在于，婴儿不只是模仿了大人的动作。

paras.en: Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task.
paras.zh: 相反，他们把努力的价值推广到了一个新的任务上。

paras.en: The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music.
paras.zh: 实验人员从来没有示范过按按钮或者设法让玩具放音乐。

paras.en: Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions, that the new toy probably also required persistence.
paras.zh: 相反，婴儿从几个不同的努力行动的例子中领会到，这个新玩具很可能也需要坚持。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say even our personal beliefs about effort can do?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人说，甚至我们个人对努力的看法会产生什么作用？

paras.en: Question 17: How did the researchers turn on the music toy in their experiment?
paras.zh: 第十七题：研究人员在实验中是怎样打开音乐玩具的？

paras.en: Question 18: What could the infants do in the experiment, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第十八题：根据说话人的介绍，婴儿在实验中能做什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it’s likely that you’re losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more.
paras.zh: 如果长期迟到已经主宰了你的生活，变成了你身上的典型特征，那你很可能正在错过工作机会、娱乐机会、友谊，以及其他更多东西。

w.m: adj. 最典型的；决定性的

paras.en: If you’re showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
paras.zh: 如果你在自己的生活里总是迟到，那就要把生活安排得有条理，把守时放在首位，并解决背后的原因。

paras.en: When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to, if you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do.
paras.zh: 当你得去某个地方时，尽量比要求的时间早15到30分钟到；如果你总是迟到，那就说明你一定是有某件每次都做的事没算进去。

paras.en: Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive.
paras.zh: 要预料到这一点，给自己留出额外的时间赶路。

paras.en: Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early.
paras.zh: 记录下你到底有没有真的早到。

paras.en: You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.
paras.zh: 你可能会发现，提早出门正好让你准时到达。

paras.en: Set two alarms.
paras.zh: 定两个闹钟。

paras.en: Set one alarm that lets you know it’s time to drop what you’re doing, and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door.
paras.zh: 一个闹钟提醒你该放下手头的事了，第二个闹钟则意味着你得出门了。

paras.en: Obey the alarms.
paras.zh: 要听闹钟的。

paras.en: As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you’re doing.
paras.zh: 第一个闹钟一响，就停下手头的事。

paras.en: If it’s something you’ll be coming back to like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off.
paras.zh: 如果是你之后还要接着做的事，比如一项工作任务，那就记一笔，提醒自己做到了哪里。

paras.en: Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you’re going.
paras.zh: 带上你需要的所有东西，并确保你知道怎么去要去的地方。

paras.en: Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings.
paras.zh: 争取在第二个闹钟响之前出门上路。

paras.en: This will only work if you take the alarms seriously.
paras.zh: 只有你认真对待闹钟，这个办法才管用。

paras.en: So make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
paras.zh: 所以一听到闹钟响，一定要马上行动。

paras.en: Prepare for the day ahead.
paras.zh: 为第二天做好准备。

paras.en: Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event, so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it’s the actual day.
paras.zh: 每次活动前，都要提前把笔记和材料整理好，这样到了当天，你只需要拿上就走。

w.m: adj. 有条理的；整理好的

paras.en: If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before.
paras.zh: 如果早上起床对你来说很困难，那就尽量在前一天晚上多做些准备。

paras.en: Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
paras.zh: 睡觉前，把衣服摆好，把第二天要用的包收拾好。

paras.en: Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings.
paras.zh: 要学会在任务和会议之间留出时间。

paras.en: It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between.
paras.zh: 在一个会议和另一个会议之间连轴转、中间不留空隙，很快就会让人受不了。

paras.en: If you overschedule yourself, however, you’ll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump.
paras.zh: 不过，如果你把日程排得太满，一遇到点小麻烦就会迟到。

paras.en: As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time.
paras.zh: 这段时间除了给你留出空隙，还能充当活动之间的缓冲，万一你在上一个会议里被耽搁了，就可以挪用这段时间，让你仍然能准时赶到下一个会议。

paras.en: Calculate transit time between activities, and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.
paras.zh: 计算好各项活动之间路上要花的时间，然后再加上10到30分钟，以防意外延误。

w.m: adj. 意想不到的；出乎意料的

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What is the speaker’s purpose of giving this talk?
paras.zh: 第十九题：说话人做这次讲话的目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What should you do if mornings are a struggle for you?
paras.zh: 第二十题：如果早上起床对你来说很困难，你应该怎么做？

paras.en: Question 21: According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：根据说话人的说法，我们可以怎样应对意外延误？

w.m: adj. 意想不到的；出乎意料的

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat?
paras.zh: 你觉得波士顿人热情好客吗？

paras.en: Do you find other cities to be more or less polite?
paras.zh: 你觉得其他城市更礼貌还是更不礼貌？

w.m: 或多或少；（此处）更……或更不……

paras.en: Different cities have different feels for visitors.
paras.zh: 不同的城市给游客的感觉不同。

paras.en: Some are friendly and open.
paras.zh: 有的城市友好开放。

paras.en: Some are formal and distant.
paras.zh: 有的城市拘谨冷淡。

paras.en: Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude.
paras.zh: 波士顿往往给人一种匆匆忙忙的感觉，有时还有点粗鲁。

paras.en: That’s what some tourists have said.
paras.zh: 有些游客就是这么说的。

paras.en: One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities, take a close look next time you’re in Boston, and here are some of the things you’ll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn, and occasionally cursing at each other.
paras.zh: 有一项研究发现，与美国其他城市的居民相比，这里的人不太愿意主动帮助陌生人。下次你到波士顿时仔细看看，你很可能会看到这些情形：尽管一再提醒不要在地铁站吸烟，还是有人在那里抽烟；行人不顾人行横道的信号灯显示不许通行，照样过马路，对来往车辆视而不见；司机超速行驶，猛按喇叭，偶尔还互相咒骂。

paras.en: Drivers who can’t be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
paras.zh: 还有的司机懒得找地方停车，干脆打开转向灯，把车停在马路中间。

paras.en: Sometimes Bostonians seem like they’re just too busy to be polite.
paras.zh: 有时候，波士顿人似乎就是太忙了，顾不上讲礼貌。

paras.en: Why is their city like that?
paras.zh: 他们的城市为什么会是这样呢？

paras.en: Former U.S. Representative Chester Atkins says it’s because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered and had little time for courtesy.
paras.zh: 前美国众议员切斯特·阿特金斯说，这是因为最早定居在这里的清教徒先辈们本身就没有耐心、脾气暴躁，根本不讲究礼貌。

paras.en: That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes.
paras.zh: 他认为，这种文化一直延续到了今天。

paras.en: Boston College professor Thomas O’Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston’s history as a city, where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion.
paras.zh: 波士顿学院的托马斯·奥康纳教授认为，原因之一是波士顿作为一座城市的历史：每一批新移民来到这里，都受到怀疑和排斥。

paras.en: That’s given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve.
paras.zh: 这让波士顿形成了一种排外和拘谨的风气。

paras.en: He thinks the idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture.
paras.zh: 他认为，陌生人之间互相打招呼，根本就不是当地文化的一部分。

paras.en: He says, “People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger.”
paras.zh: 他说：“人们会跟认识的人聊天，但不会跟陌生人聊。”

paras.en: Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it’s because Boston’s upper class used manners to make class distinctions.
paras.zh: 马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的新闻学教授拉尔夫·怀特黑德认为，这是因为波士顿的上流社会用礼节来划分阶层。

paras.en: By being snobbish about manners, proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.
paras.zh: 他说，正统的波士顿人在礼节上自命不凡，结果让其他人对礼貌嗤之以鼻。

w.m: adj. 势利的；自命不凡的

paras.en: Some say that’s just the way Boston is, and that the city will never change.
paras.zh: 有人说，波士顿就是这个样子，这座城市永远不会改变。

paras.en: Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images.
paras.zh: 不过，其他一些以更加粗鲁出名的城市正在努力改变自己的形象。

paras.en: Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly.
paras.zh: 巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人正在努力变得友好。

paras.en: New York City is another.
paras.zh: 纽约市是另一个例子。

paras.en: There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate.
paras.zh: 在那里，市政府正努力劝说地铁乘客多为别人着想。

w.m: adj. 体贴的；考虑周到的

paras.en: If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.
paras.zh: 既然那些城市都能做出努力，也许波士顿也应该这么做。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do visitors find about the cities they’ve been to?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：游客们觉得自己去过的城市怎么样？

paras.en: Question 23: What did one study find about Bostonians compared with residents of other U.S. cities?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：一项研究发现，与美国其他城市的居民相比，波士顿人有什么特点？

paras.en: Question 24: What does Thomas O’Connor say about the idea of strangers greeting one another?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：关于陌生人之间互相打招呼，托马斯·奥康纳是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker think Boston should do?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人认为波士顿应该怎么做？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，两位面试官在两名候选人雷切尔和彼得之间犹豫不决，比较了两人的学业和面试表现，意见不一时打算交给约翰决定。第二段长对话里，主持人采访时装设计师克莱门汀·奥尔特加，她介绍了新系列的风格、那件斗篷的灵感来源和混搭不同风格的做法。第一篇短文介绍一项研究：没受过训练的流浪狗也能看懂人的手势，善待流浪狗可以减少冲突。第二篇短文讲冰箱里各处温度不同，并说明不同的食物该放在冰箱的哪个位置。第一段录音里，一位研究者介绍她关于压力、抑郁与老年人髋部骨折的研究，以及这项研究让她兴奋的地方。第二段录音介绍厨师的“mise en place”（就位）工作法，以及它对生活的启发。第三段录音讲人们为什么不再给自己定目标，建议衡量自己走了多远，而不是离目标还差多少。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six Part Two, Listening Comprehension.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解。

paras.en: Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: We are down to two candidates for one position, and we need to decide by the end of the day in order to finalize this whole procedure.
paras.zh: 一个职位还剩两名候选人，我们得在今天下班前做出决定，把整个招聘流程定下来。

w.h: by the end of the day

paras.en: Yes, but it isn’t an easy choice to make.
paras.zh: 是啊，可这个选择不好做。

paras.en: Both applicants are quite strong.
paras.zh: 两位应聘者都相当优秀。

paras.en: Let’s get to it then.
paras.zh: 那我们就开始吧。

paras.en: Both of them went to good universities, and both of them studied business-related subjects, so academically, I’d say they’re pretty much the same.
paras.zh: 他们俩都上了好大学，都学的是商科相关的专业，所以论学业，我觉得他们差不多。

paras.en: What do you think?
paras.zh: 你怎么看？

paras.en: I would agree.
paras.zh: 我同意。

paras.en: Yes, the only difference worth noting, perhaps, is that it looks like Rachel scored moderately stronger grades throughout high school and university, but as I said, only a tiny bit higher than Peter.
paras.zh: 是的，唯一值得一提的区别也许是，雷切尔整个高中和大学的成绩看起来稍微好一些，不过就像我说的，只比彼得高那么一点点。

paras.en: That’s true and worth noting.
paras.zh: 没错，这一点值得一提。

paras.en: Thank you.
paras.zh: 谢谢。

paras.en: In addition, Rachel interviewed very well.
paras.zh: 另外，雷切尔面试表现很好。

paras.en: I thought she came across as bright and alert.
paras.zh: 我觉得她给人的印象是聪明、反应快。

paras.en: Yes, she asked some very good questions about the position and the company, which made me think she is very keen about the job.
paras.zh: 是的，她就这个职位和公司问了几个很好的问题，让我觉得她非常想要这份工作。

paras.en: I thought so too.
paras.zh: 我也这么觉得。

paras.en: Now let’s look at Peter’s interview performance.
paras.zh: 现在来看看彼得的面试表现。

paras.en: I thought he also did very well.
paras.zh: 我觉得他表现得也很好。

paras.en: He came across as respectful and professional, wouldn’t you say?
paras.zh: 他给人的印象是彬彬有礼、很专业，你说是不是？

w.m: adj. 有礼貌的；尊重人的

paras.en: Calm and poised, very mature for his age.
paras.zh: 沉着镇定，以他的年龄来说非常成熟。

paras.en: Exactly.
paras.zh: 正是。

paras.en: In my notes, I wrote that he seemed composed and in control of his emotions.
paras.zh: 我在笔记里写的是，他看起来很镇静，能控制住自己的情绪。

paras.en: I think he definitely looked more mature than Rachel.
paras.zh: 我觉得他确实比雷切尔显得更成熟。

paras.en: Interesting.
paras.zh: 有意思。

paras.en: So we agree that Rachel appeared inexperienced and less mature than Peter, even though both candidates are the same age and have practically no work experience.
paras.zh: 这么说，我们都认为雷切尔比彼得显得没经验、不够成熟，尽管两位候选人年龄一样，而且都几乎没有工作经验。

paras.en: When comparing them side by side, yes, Peter seemed more self-assured somehow.
paras.zh: 把他们放在一起比较的话，是的，不知为什么，彼得好像更自信一些。

w.m: adv. 不知为什么；不知怎么地

paras.en: Maybe it was something about their body language.
paras.zh: 也许跟他们的肢体语言有关。

paras.en: Sure, maybe he was simply less nervous.
paras.zh: 没错，也许他只是没那么紧张。

paras.en: Maybe, who knows?
paras.zh: 也许吧，谁知道呢？

paras.en: To be honest, I think I like Rachel better.
paras.zh: 说实话，我觉得我更喜欢雷切尔。

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

paras.en: Really?
paras.zh: 真的吗？

paras.en: I think I like Peter.
paras.zh: 我觉得我更喜欢彼得。

paras.en: Ah, well.
paras.zh: 啊，好吧。

paras.en: If there’s a tie and we can’t come to an agreement, then we’ll take it to John and let him cast the deciding vote.
paras.zh: 要是我们意见各半，谈不拢，那就交给约翰，让他投决定票。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard, Question one: Why does the man think it is difficult to make the decision?
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。第一题：男士为什么认为这个决定很难做？

paras.en: Question two: What do the speakers say may be worth noting?
paras.zh: 第二题：说话人说什么可能值得一提？

paras.en: Question three: According to the man, what might account for Peter appearing somewhat more self-assured than Rachel?
paras.zh: 第三题：根据男士的说法，彼得为什么显得比雷切尔自信一些？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man say they will do if they can’t reach an agreement?
paras.zh: 第四题：男士说，如果他们达不成一致，会怎么做？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: We’re here with Clementine Ortega, head designer of the private fashion label L’Orange, to discuss her latest collection.
paras.zh: 今天我们请到了私人时装品牌L’Orange的首席设计师克莱门汀·奥尔特加，和她聊聊她的最新系列。

paras.en: Ms. Ortega, how would you describe this season’s look?
paras.zh: 奥尔特加女士，您会怎样描述这一季的造型？

paras.en: To be honest, my preferred style has always been on the ambiguous side, and I think this collection is even more so.
paras.zh: 说实话，我偏爱的风格一向偏向模棱两可，我觉得这个系列更是如此。

w.m: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊的

paras.en: I try not to adhere to social norms and expectations.
paras.zh: 我尽量不去遵从社会规范和期待。

paras.en: Rather, I always try to incorporate something slightly absurd into my aesthetic.
paras.zh: 相反，我总是设法在自己的审美里融入一些有点荒诞的东西。

paras.en: The assortment of accessories in this collection have had quite the impact on critics.
paras.zh: 这个系列里的各种配饰给评论家留下了很深的印象。

paras.en: The dazzling cape deployed at the end of the show, for example, bewildered many in the audience.
paras.zh: 比如，秀场最后亮相的那件耀眼的斗篷，让很多观众看得一头雾水。

w.m: adj. 耀眼的；令人眼花缭乱的

paras.en: What was your inspiration for this piece?
paras.zh: 这件作品的灵感来自哪里？

paras.en: Over the summer, I traveled through rural mountain villages throughout Asia in search of handicrafts to decorate my new studio with.
paras.zh: 夏天的时候，我走遍了亚洲各地的乡村山区，想找些手工艺品来装饰我的新工作室。

paras.en: The embroidery done by the women in a particular village was so exquisite I couldn’t stop thinking about it.
paras.zh: 某个村子里的妇女做的刺绣太精美了，我一直忘不了。

paras.en: Trying to recreate their designs would have been futile, so instead I applied my own eccentric approach.
paras.zh: 想要重现她们的图案，是不可能做到的，所以我就用了自己独特的方法。

w.m: adj. 古怪的；与众不同的

paras.en: Using glitter, I drew similar intricate patterns onto the velvet cape.
paras.zh: 我用亮片在天鹅绒斗篷上画出了类似的复杂图案。

paras.en: This ended up in the glamorous, luminous look that concluded the show.
paras.zh: 最后就成了压轴登场的那套光彩夺目的造型。

w.m: adj. 富有魅力的；迷人的

paras.en: It was indeed majestic, and yet, dare I say, masculine at the same time.
paras.zh: 那确实很有气势，不过恕我直言，同时也带点男性化的味道。

w.m: adj. 男性化的；有男子气概的

paras.en: Well, yes, that was intentional.
paras.zh: 嗯，是的，那是有意为之的。

paras.en: I like to merge styles that are often at opposite ends of the fashion spectrum.
paras.zh: 我喜欢把时尚界里常常截然相反的风格融合在一起。

paras.en: Hence, the sparkling cape was paired with a traditional power suit you would typically see in a business setting.
paras.zh: 所以，那件闪闪发光的斗篷搭配的是一套你在商务场合常见的传统职业套装。

paras.en: It was sensational, if I do say so myself.
paras.zh: 不是我自夸，效果真的很轰动。

w.h: if I do say so myself

paras.en: Spectacular for sure, a stunning show all around.
paras.zh: 绝对精彩，整场秀都非常出色。

w.m: adj. 极好的；令人惊叹的

paras.en: Going against stereotypes, the incorporation of indigenous aspects, along with your underlying signature touch, made this collection a statement of the season.
paras.zh: 打破刻板印象，融入本土元素，再加上您骨子里的个人标志风格，让这个系列成了本季的代表之作。

w.m: n. 宣言；（引人注目的）代表作

paras.en: You have proven yourself a formidable young designer, and we can’t wait to see what creations you come up with next.
paras.zh: 您已经证明自己是一位实力非凡的年轻设计师，我们迫不及待地想看看您接下来会创作出什么作品。

w.m: adj. 实力强大的；令人敬畏的

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
paras.zh: 第五题：说话人主要在谈论什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the woman say she always tries to incorporate into her aesthetic?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士说她总是设法在自己的审美里融入什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the woman say she likes to do?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士说她喜欢做什么？

paras.en: Question eight: What is the man looking forward to?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士期待的是什么？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: Pet dogs can often readily understand a wide range of their owner’s commands and gestures, but are these abilities inborn or are they exclusively learned through training?
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。宠物狗往往能轻松听懂主人的各种指令和手势，但这些能力是天生的，还是完全靠训练学来的呢？

w.m: adv. 容易地；轻而易举地
adj. 天生的；与生俱来的

paras.en: To find out, a new study examined whether stray dogs could understand human gestures, the study revealed that 80 percent of participating dogs successfully followed pointing gestures to a specific location, despite having never received prior training.
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚这一点，一项新研究考察了流浪狗能否看懂人的手势。研究发现，80%参与实验的狗虽然从没受过训练，却能顺着人指的手势成功找到特定的位置。

paras.en: The results suggest that dogs can understand complex gestures by simply watching humans.
paras.zh: 研究结果表明，狗只要观察人类，就能理解复杂的手势。

paras.en: This could have implications in reducing conflict between stray dogs and humans.
paras.zh: 这对于减少流浪狗与人之间的冲突可能有重要意义。

paras.en: Dogs were domesticated 10,000 to 15,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 狗是在一万到一万五千年前被驯化的。

paras.en: This means they are probably the oldest domesticated animals on the planet.
paras.zh: 也就是说，它们很可能是地球上最早被驯化的动物。

paras.en: Humans then bred dogs with the most desirable and useful traits, so that they could function as companions and workers.
paras.zh: 后来，人类培育出具有最理想、最有用特性的狗，让它们可以当伙伴、做帮手。

w.m: v. 培育；繁殖（breed的过去式）
adj. 理想的；令人满意的

paras.en: This resulted in domesticated dogs that are highly responsive to human commands and gestures.
paras.zh: 结果就有了对人类指令和手势反应非常灵敏的家犬。

paras.en: However, it was not clear whether dogs understand us through training alone, or whether this was an inherent ability.
paras.zh: 不过，人们一直不清楚，狗能听懂我们，究竟只是靠训练，还是一种天生的能力。

paras.en: Why does this matter?
paras.zh: 这一点为什么重要呢？

paras.en: Stray dogs are a common feature in cities around the world.
paras.zh: 流浪狗在世界各地的城市里都很常见。

paras.en: They may observe and occasionally interact with people, but such dogs have never been trained and are behaviorally wild.
paras.zh: 它们可能会观察人，偶尔也跟人有些接触，但这样的狗从来没有受过训练，在行为上是野性的。

paras.en: Conflicts between stray dogs and humans are a problem.
paras.zh: 流浪狗与人之间的冲突是个问题。

paras.en: Understanding how humans shape stray dogs’ behavior may help alleviate this problem.
paras.zh: 了解人类如何影响流浪狗的行为，也许有助于缓解这个问题。

paras.en: According to the researchers of the new study, stray dogs are intelligent creatures.
paras.zh: 据这项新研究的研究人员说，流浪狗是聪明的动物。

paras.en: They closely observe humans and use their understanding of us to make a decision.
paras.zh: 它们会仔细观察人，并根据对我们的了解来做决定。

paras.en: Treating stray dogs with sensitivity and respect, and giving them space, the researchers assert, can reduce much conflict.
paras.zh: 研究人员断言，体贴、尊重地对待流浪狗，给它们留出空间，可以大大减少冲突。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does the passage say about 80% of participating dogs in the new study?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于80%参与实验的狗，短文是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 10: What may help alleviate the problem caused by stray dogs?
paras.zh: 第十题：什么也许有助于缓解流浪狗造成的问题？

paras.en: Question 11: What do the researchers suggest we do to reduce conflicts between stray dogs and humans?
paras.zh: 第十一题：研究人员建议我们怎样做来减少流浪狗与人之间的冲突？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Think your refrigerator is just one big box of evenly cold air?
paras.zh: 你以为冰箱只是一个装满均匀冷气的大箱子吗？

paras.en: Not so.
paras.zh: 不是这样的。

paras.en: The temperature inside the average fridge actually varies from front to back, bottom to top, and everywhere in between.
paras.zh: 一般冰箱里的温度其实前后不同、上下不同，中间各处也都不一样。

paras.en: Because of this, food product placement within the appliance is far more important than you probably realize.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，食物在冰箱里放在什么位置，比你可能意识到的重要得多。

paras.en: The whole purpose of the modern refrigerator is to slow the growth of bacteria, which thrive in temperatures from 4.4 to 60 degrees Celsius.
paras.zh: 现代冰箱的全部用处就是减缓细菌的生长，而细菌在4.4到60摄氏度的温度下会大量繁殖。

paras.en: As a result, refrigerators are typically set at or below that low end to protect foods against bacteria.
paras.zh: 因此，冰箱通常设定在这个范围的下限或者更低，以防止食物滋生细菌。

paras.en: Although it might seem like time spent organizing the fridge will spoil your day, doing so will actually make it more user-friendly, easier to clean, and food safety-conscious.
paras.zh: 虽然花时间整理冰箱可能看起来会耽误你一天的工夫，但这样做其实会让冰箱更好用、更容易清洁，也更有利于食品安全。

paras.en: Those little bins on the inside of refrigerator doors are convenient, but they don’t maintain a consistent temperature.
paras.zh: 冰箱门内侧的那些小格子很方便，但温度保持不稳定。

paras.en: So definitely refrain from putting perishable foods in there.
paras.zh: 所以千万不要把容易变质的食物放在那里。

w.m: adj. 易腐烂的；易变质的

paras.en: The top area is not as cold as the bottom of the fridge, so save it for the foods that don’t need extra chilly temperatures.
paras.zh: 冰箱上层没有下层那么冷，所以留给那些不需要特别低温的食物。

paras.en: Store foods that are ready to eat or already cooked on the top shelf.
paras.zh: 即食食品或者已经做熟的食物放在最上层的架子上。

paras.en: The middle shelf is the most temperature-controlled part of the fridge, so place eggs here.
paras.zh: 中层架子是冰箱里温度控制得最好的地方，所以把鸡蛋放在这里。

paras.en: Drinks and prepared foods can also live on the middle shelf if you run out of room up top.
paras.zh: 如果上层放不下了，饮料和做好的食物也可以放在中层架子上。

paras.en: The back of the bottom shelf is the coldest spot in the fridge, so store perishable dairy products here to keep them edible longer.
paras.zh: 下层架子的靠里处是冰箱里最冷的地方，所以把容易变质的奶制品放在这里，让它们保存得更久。

w.m: adj. 易腐烂的；易变质的
adj. 可以吃的；可食用的

paras.en: Never store foods with high water content here, because the water within them can and will freeze effectively.
paras.zh: 千万不要把含水量高的食物放在这里，因为它们里面的水分可能会、也一定会结冰。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: Why is food product placement within the fridge very important?
paras.zh: 第十二题：为什么食物在冰箱里放在什么位置非常重要？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the passage say is the whole purpose of the modern refrigerator?
paras.zh: 第十三题：短文说现代冰箱的全部用处是什么？

paras.en: Question 14: Where in the fridge should we store foods already cooked?
paras.zh: 第十四题：已经做熟的食物应该放在冰箱的什么地方？

paras.en: Question 15: Why should we never store foods with high water content at the back of the bottom shelf?
paras.zh: 第十五题：为什么千万不要把含水量高的食物放在下层架子的靠里处？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: My current research is mainly looking at factors like stress and how it affects our immune system.
paras.zh: 我目前的研究主要关注压力这类因素，以及它们如何影响我们的免疫系统。

paras.en: So the current projects that I’m quite excited about are looking at older people and factors that are important to them.
paras.zh: 所以我目前特别感兴趣的几个项目，研究的都是老年人以及对他们来说很重要的因素。

paras.en: In one project, we are looking at hip fracture in older people, which is a common event, and we’re trying to understand the impact of depression.
paras.zh: 在其中一个项目里，我们研究的是老年人的髋部骨折，这种情况很常见，我们想弄清楚抑郁会带来什么影响。

paras.en: Often, people in hospital with a hip fracture develop depression, and these are the people that then go on to become feeble a lot more quickly than others.
paras.zh: 因髋部骨折住院的人常常会患上抑郁症，而这些人随后身体衰弱的速度要比其他人快得多。

paras.en: They get infections.
paras.zh: 他们会受到感染。

paras.en: Often, these infections lead to death.
paras.zh: 这些感染常常导致死亡。

paras.en: So we’re trying to slow down that progression to feebleness.
paras.zh: 所以我们在设法减缓他们走向衰弱的进程。

paras.en: So if we can better understand how these factors interact, then we can actually start doing something about it.
paras.zh: 所以如果我们能更好地了解这些因素是怎样相互作用的，就能真正着手解决这个问题了。

paras.en: The impact that my research will have in Birmingham, first of all, is obviously for older people, because these are the people that are having hip fractures and developing depression, and we’re trying to improve their health and their quality of life.
paras.zh: 我的研究在伯明翰会产生的影响，首先显然是对老年人的，因为正是这些人在发生髋部骨折、患上抑郁症，而我们在努力改善他们的健康和生活质量。

paras.en: But this isn’t just a problem in Birmingham or even in the UK.
paras.zh: 但这不只是伯明翰的问题，甚至也不只是英国的问题。

paras.en: This is a problem globally.
paras.zh: 这是一个全球性的问题。

paras.en: People are aging.
paras.zh: 人们正在变老。

paras.en: There’s a lot more people in the older generation who are living for longer, but not necessarily staying healthy for a large part of their lives.
paras.zh: 老一辈里有越来越多的人活得更久了，但不一定在人生的大部分时间里都保持健康。

paras.en: So the last part of their life can often be full of ill health, and we’re trying to understand factors that can contribute to the quality of life later on.
paras.zh: 所以，人生的最后一段时间常常疾病缠身，我们正努力弄清楚哪些因素会影响晚年的生活质量。

paras.en: I think the thing that excites me most about my research is that it feels real and relevant.
paras.zh: 我觉得我的研究最让我兴奋的地方是，它让人觉得真实，而且跟现实息息相关。

paras.en: Lots of academics are probably very excited about their research, but it might not be that relevant to those around them, whereas I feel that the work I do is relevant to everyone because everyone is aging.
paras.zh: 很多学者可能都对自己的研究很感兴趣，但他们的研究可能跟身边的人没多大关系；而我觉得我做的工作跟每个人都有关系，因为每个人都在变老。

paras.en: Health is an issue for everyone, regardless of their age, and what I’m trying to do is understand the factors that affect health, and how we can improve the quality of life in people.
paras.zh: 无论年龄大小，健康都是每个人都要面对的问题，我想做的就是了解影响健康的因素，以及我们怎样才能提高人们的生活质量。

paras.en: So that’s one of the things that really excites me about it.
paras.zh: 这就是它真正让我兴奋的地方之一。

paras.en: One of the other things is rather than just taking one perspective, so rather than looking at aging and health just from the perspective of the psychologist, we are now bringing together a lot of different techniques and a lot of different viewpoints to actually look at the sort of different factors affecting health.
paras.zh: 另一点是，我们不只从一个角度出发，也就是说，不只从心理学家的角度来看待衰老和健康，而是把很多不同的技术和观点结合起来，真正去研究影响健康的各种不同因素。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say is quite common among older people?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人说什么在老年人中相当常见？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the speaker think excites her most about her research?
paras.zh: 第十七题：说话人认为她的研究最让她兴奋的是什么？

paras.en: Question 18: How does the speaker approach her research project?
paras.zh: 第十八题：说话人是怎样开展她的研究项目的？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Americans are obsessed with celebrity chefs.
paras.zh: 美国人对明星厨师着了迷。

paras.en: We talk about them and try to eat like them, but could we learn something more from them than recipes and techniques?
paras.zh: 我们谈论他们，想学他们那样吃，可除了菜谱和厨艺，我们能不能从他们身上学到更多东西呢？

paras.en: According to Marketdata Enterprises, Americans spend nearly $10 billion a year on self-help and personal organization products.
paras.zh: 据市场研究公司 Marketdata Enterprises 统计，美国人每年在自助类和个人整理类产品上花费将近100亿美元。

paras.en: The market is huge, partly because most colleges and graduate schools don’t teach basic organization, but cooking schools and professional kitchens do.
paras.zh: 这个市场很大，部分原因是大多数大学和研究生院都不教基本的整理方法，而烹饪学校和专业厨房会教。

paras.en: Perhaps the principles of cooking organization can be extended to help even those of us who aren’t top chefs.
paras.zh: 也许烹饪中的整理原则可以推而广之，让我们这些不是顶级厨师的人也能受益。

paras.en: The system that makes kitchens function is called mise en place, or literally put in place.
paras.zh: 让厨房运转起来的这套体系叫作“mise en place”，字面意思就是“就位”。

w.m: adv. 字面上；照字面意思

paras.en: It’s a French phrase that means to gather and arrange the ingredients and tools needed for cooking.
paras.zh: 这是一个法语短语，意思是把烹饪所需的食材和工具收集起来、摆放好。

paras.en: But for many professional cooks, the phrase means something deeper.
paras.zh: 但对很多专业厨师来说，这个短语有更深的含义。

paras.en: Some cooks call it their religion.
paras.zh: 有些厨师把它称作自己的信仰。

paras.en: It helps them coordinate vast amounts of labor and material, and transforms the lives of its practitioners through focus and self-discipline.
paras.zh: 它帮助他们协调大量的人力和原料，并通过专注和自律改变践行者的生活。

paras.en: Students at the Culinary Institute of America view it as a way of life.
paras.zh: 美国烹饪学院的学生把它看作一种生活方式。

paras.en: It’s a way of concentrating their mind to only focus on the aspects that they need to be working on at the moment, to kind of rid themselves of distractions.
paras.zh: 这是一种集中注意力的方法，让自己只关注当下需要处理的那些方面，算是摆脱干扰。

w.m: n. 分散注意力的事物；干扰

paras.en: And it’s a habit that some students carry with them, even when they’re not in the kitchen.
paras.zh: 而且这是一些学生会带在身上的习惯，即使不在厨房里也一样。

paras.en: They mise en place their life.
paras.zh: 他们把自己的生活也“就位”了。

paras.en: They set up their books for class.
paras.zh: 他们会把上课用的书准备好。

paras.en: They set up their chef whites.
paras.zh: 他们会把厨师白衣准备好。

paras.en: They shine their shoes.
paras.zh: 他们会把鞋擦得锃亮。

paras.en: They know everything that they need every step of the day.
paras.zh: 一天里的每一步，他们都清楚自己需要什么。

paras.en: Then, how does one attain this level of organization?
paras.zh: 那么，一个人怎样才能达到这样的条理水平呢？

paras.en: The key to high-level organization is the mindset.
paras.zh: 做到高度有条理，关键在于心态。

paras.en: Cooks can easily do six hours of preparation for a three-hour dinner shift.
paras.zh: 厨师为了一个三小时的晚餐班次，很容易就要准备六个小时。

paras.en: Mise en place forces cooks to account for every minute of their time and every movement.
paras.zh: “就位”法逼着厨师把每一分钟、每一个动作都考虑在内。

paras.en: Every component of one single dish is in one single corner, so their hand literally moves inches.
paras.zh: 一道菜的每样配料都放在同一个角落里，所以他们的手实际上只需移动几英寸。

paras.en: Explains Duane Limpuma, an instructor at the Culinary Institute of America.
paras.zh: 美国烹饪学院的讲师杜安·林普马解释道。

paras.en: Once students set up their station, I should be able to cover up their eyes, and they should know that their knives are always here, their oil is always right here, their salt and pepper is always right here.
paras.zh: 学生们把自己的操作台布置好之后，我就算蒙上他们的眼睛，他们也应该知道刀永远在这儿，油永远就在这儿，盐和胡椒永远就在这儿。

paras.en: But practiced at its highest level, mise en place says that time is precious, resources are precious, space is precious.
paras.zh: 不过，如果做到最高境界，“就位”法告诉我们，时间是宝贵的，资源是宝贵的，空间也是宝贵的。

paras.en: Your self-respect and the respect of others are precious.
paras.zh: 你的自尊和别人对你的尊重都是宝贵的。

paras.en: Use them wisely.
paras.zh: 要明智地利用它们。

paras.en: Isn’t that a philosophy for our time?
paras.zh: 这难道不是适合我们这个时代的人生哲学吗？

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about most colleges and graduate schools in America?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于美国的大多数大学和研究生院，说话人是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question 20: How do students at the Culinary Institute of America view mise en place, or put in place?
paras.zh: 第二十题：美国烹饪学院的学生怎样看待“mise en place”，也就是“就位”？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：讲话结束时，说话人建议我们做什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Why do we stop making goals for ourselves and stop progressing in life?
paras.zh: 我们为什么不再给自己定目标，人生也不再进步了呢？

paras.en: One reason is the belief that we should accept who we are and not constantly strive to improve ourselves.
paras.zh: 原因之一是有一种观念，认为我们应该接受自己本来的样子，不要总是拼命改进自己。

paras.en: The mistake we make with this is that whilst self-acceptance is imperative, it should actually be used as the basis for growth.
paras.zh: 我们在这一点上犯的错误是：虽然接纳自己是必不可少的，但它其实应该作为成长的基础。

w.m: adj. 必要的；必不可少的

paras.en: When we’re not growing, learning, and seeking improvements in our lives, we tend to stagnate, accepting what is and stop believing we can be better.
paras.zh: 当我们在生活中不再成长、不再学习、不再追求进步时，我们往往就会停滞不前，满足于现状，不再相信自己可以变得更好。

paras.en: A key tool for creating goals and progressing is using our imagination.
paras.zh: 制定目标、取得进步的一个关键工具就是发挥我们的想象力。

paras.en: Yet, as is so often the case, by the time we’ve reached midlife, we’ve stopped dreaming about what we want to achieve and feel quite negatively about goal setting.
paras.zh: 然而，常常是这样：到了中年，我们就不再梦想自己想要实现什么，对定目标这件事也相当消极。

w.h: as is so often the case

paras.en: Instead of feeling confidence, happiness, and satisfaction from achieving our goals, we feel we are always falling short.
paras.zh: 我们没有因为实现了目标而感到自信、快乐和满足，反而觉得自己总是差那么一点。

paras.en: That leads to disappointment, and we stop dreaming.
paras.zh: 这会让人失望，于是我们就不再梦想了。

paras.en: We stop imagining the life we’d like to have or the person we’d like to be.
paras.zh: 我们不再想象自己想要的生活，也不再想象自己想成为的那个人。

paras.en: Quickly finding ourselves shattered by the pain of our reality.
paras.zh: 很快就发现自己被现实的痛苦击得粉碎。

paras.en: Up until now, unless we work in the creative industry, we’ve found the idea of using play a bit childish.
paras.zh: 直到现在，除非我们从事创意行业，否则我们都会觉得用玩的方式有点幼稚。

paras.en: In the West, we are mostly operating from our heads, the rational mind, but it’s beginning to be better understood because using our imagination is actually one of the most powerful things we could ever do.
paras.zh: 在西方，我们大多是靠头脑、靠理性思维在做事，不过人们开始更好地理解这一点了，因为发挥想象力其实是我们能做的最有力量的事情之一。

paras.en: The problem with finding ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal is because the goal always changes, and we’re always adapting, whether we realize it or not.
paras.zh: 我们之所以因为没实现目标而恼火，问题在于目标总是在变，而我们也一直在调整，不管自己有没有意识到。

paras.en: What happens, therefore, is that we end up feeling like we are never going to reach our goals, and herein lies one of the biggest misconceptions and reasons for failure: dissatisfaction and unhappiness.
paras.zh: 因此，结果就是我们总觉得自己永远也达不到目标，而这正是最大的误解之一，也是失败的最大原因之一：不满和不快乐。

paras.en: We measure against the goal rather than where we’ve come from, Dan Sullivan calls this the gap and the gain.
paras.zh: 我们拿目标来衡量自己，而不是拿自己的起点来衡量，丹·沙利文把这称为“差距与收获”。

paras.en: We measure always against the goal, which we never feel we’re reaching, rather than the gain, that is where we’ve come from.
paras.zh: 我们总是拿那个似乎永远也达不到的目标来衡量自己，而不是拿收获，也就是我们已经走了多远来衡量。

paras.en: In measuring where we’ve come from rather than where we’re trying to get to, we see results.
paras.zh: 当我们衡量自己已经走了多远，而不是还要走多远时，就能看到成果。

paras.en: We see things we’ve taken for granted or not noticed.
paras.zh: 我们会看到那些自己一直视为理所当然、或者没有注意到的东西。

paras.en: It’s a simple yet profound change in perception, and what I love about it is the power it has to instantly shift us up a gear.
paras.zh: 这是认知上一个简单而深刻的转变，我喜欢它的地方在于，它能立刻让我们提升一个档次。

w.m: adj. 深刻的；意义深远的
使……提升一个档次；加把劲

paras.en: It’s so so simple yet has an immediate positive impact on our thinking.
paras.zh: 它非常非常简单，却能立刻对我们的思维产生积极影响。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What should self-acceptance be used as, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：根据说话人的说法，自我接纳应该被用作什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What do people tend to do when they have reached midlife?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：人们到了中年往往会怎么样？

paras.en: Question 24: Why do we find ourselves irritated for not achieving the goal?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：我们为什么会因为没有实现目标而恼火？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker say has an immediate positive impact on our thinking?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人说什么能立刻对我们的思维产生积极影响？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2025年12月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2025年12月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，职业外交官布莱克韦尔勋爵谈到温诺皮亚的政局，又讲了自己怎样走上外交之路，以及外交官需要哪些能力。第二段长对话里，两位同事加班修改一份合同，男士想收工回家，并担心董事会会拖延项目，女士则比较乐观。第一篇短文讲作者处理员工纠纷的经验：真相不明时，不妨往好处想，然后翻篇。第二篇短文讲喜欢做饭的美国人越来越少，在外吃饭花的钱却更多。第一段录音讲托运行李为什么会丢、丢了以后怎么处理。第二段录音介绍一项研究：面对面交谈时只顾看手机，会让对方感到被排斥。第三段录音介绍民宿的兴起，以及开民宿前要考虑的房产、家庭生活方式和收入三个因素。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Today’s special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country’s most experienced and distinguished career diplomats.
paras.zh: 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克韦尔勋爵，他是我国经验最丰富、最杰出的职业外交官之一。

paras.en: Welcome.
paras.zh: 欢迎您。

paras.en: It’s my pleasure.
paras.zh: 很荣幸。

paras.en: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service.
paras.zh: 我们的听众一定特别想了解外交这一行。

paras.en: However, before we talk about that, I’d like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia.
paras.zh: 不过，在谈这个之前，我想先问问您今天上了新闻的温诺皮亚共和国的最新动态。

paras.en: What can you tell us?
paras.zh: 您能给我们讲讲吗？

paras.en: I’m afraid I don’t know much beyond what we’ve all seen on the news.
paras.zh: 恐怕我知道的也不比大家在新闻里看到的多。

paras.en: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on.
paras.zh: 看起来温诺皮亚政府似乎正陷入某种合法性危机，在就国家元首人选达成一致之前，已经成立了一个过渡性的临时政府。

paras.en: But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I’ve never been involved with Winopian relations.
paras.zh: 不过我的工作主要集中在欧洲和美洲这两大洲，所以从来没参与过跟温诺皮亚有关的外交事务。

paras.en: It’s for this reason that I don’t know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，这件事除了报纸上大家都能看到的那些，别的我一概不知。

paras.en: Oh, I see.
paras.zh: 哦，我明白了。

paras.en: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our export envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation, and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
paras.zh: 不过请放心，我们驻那里领事馆的专家使节会密切关注局势，我预计我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。

w.m: n. 出口；（此处疑为 expert，专家）

paras.en: So, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
paras.zh: 那么，怎样才能从事外交工作呢？

paras.en: There are many different paths one can take.
paras.zh: 可以走的路有很多。

paras.en: All diplomats have their own story, but in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering, followed by six years’ service in the air force.
paras.zh: 每个外交官都有自己的故事，就拿我来说，我先拿了电气工程学位，之后在空军服役了六年。

paras.en: Then I went to law school, and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps, where I’ve been for 22 years.
paras.zh: 然后我去读了法学院，拿到国际法学位以后，就进了外交使团，到现在已经二十二年了。

paras.en: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
paras.zh: 您认为干这一行最需要哪些关键能力？

paras.en: There are so many.
paras.zh: 太多了。

paras.en: Being a hard worker and good student is important.
paras.zh: 勤奋、好学很重要。

paras.en: You never stop learning.
paras.zh: 学习是永无止境的。

paras.en: In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric.
paras.zh: 另外，外交官说话、措辞一定要清楚得体、有说服力。

w.m: adj. 善于表达的；表达清晰的

paras.en: Whether it is diffusing tension or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
paras.zh: 无论是缓和紧张局势，还是推行政策，跟人打交道的能力和沟通能力都至关重要。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
paras.zh: 第一题：从对话中我们可以了解到这位男士的什么情况？

paras.en: Question two: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?
paras.zh: 第二题：男士说温诺皮亚政府可能正在经历什么？

paras.en: Question three: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
paras.zh: 第三题：根据男士所说，怎样才能从事外交工作？

paras.en: Question four: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?
paras.zh: 第四题：对话快结束时，两人主要在讨论什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: It’s getting late, and we’re both displaying signs of weariness, I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
paras.zh: 天不早了，我们俩都累了，我看今天就到这儿吧，明天早上再接着干。

paras.en: Oh, come on, Jeff.
paras.zh: 哎呀，别这样嘛，杰夫。

paras.en: We are so close.
paras.zh: 我们就差一点了。

paras.en: Don’t you think we are almost done?
paras.zh: 你不觉得我们快做完了吗？

paras.en: Let’s do two more hours, please.
paras.zh: 再干两个小时吧，拜托了。

paras.en: One hour, then I’m going home.
paras.zh: 一个小时，干完我就回家。

paras.en: Okay, fine.
paras.zh: 好吧，行。

paras.en: I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments, we will be all done.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们进展很顺利，再改几处，就能全部完成了。

paras.en: I’m sure looking forward to it.
paras.zh: 我真盼着那一刻呢。

paras.en: I’m so tired of this project.
paras.zh: 这个项目我真是受够了。

paras.en: Don’t get me wrong; it’s a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company.
paras.zh: 别误会，这对我来说是个很好的职业机会，对公司来说也是一个里程碑。

paras.en: But it’s just been so long.
paras.zh: 只是拖得实在太久了。

paras.en: Yeah, two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough.
paras.zh: 是啊，两个月来除了这一份合同什么都没干，是有点累人。

paras.en: Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we’ll be done by next week.
paras.zh: 不过，我觉得运气好的话，下周就能完成。

paras.en: You must be delusional.
paras.zh: 你这是在做梦吧。

w.m: adj. 妄想的；不切实际的

paras.en: You don’t think so?
paras.zh: 你不这么觉得吗？

paras.en: No chance.
paras.zh: 不可能。

paras.en: Sections four, five, eight, and nine still have to be aligned to the new framework.
paras.zh: 第四、五、八、九部分还得按新框架调整一致。

paras.en: Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight.
paras.zh: 然后我们还得把整份校对一遍，确保所有卖点都无懈可击。

w.m: adj. 无懈可击的；严密的

paras.en: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
paras.zh: 不过这些最多也就花几天时间。

paras.en: I wasn’t finished.
paras.zh: 我还没说完呢。

paras.en: When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
paras.zh: 等我们弄完、交到上面以后，你觉得会怎么样？

paras.en: What, they’ll argue about it for like a month?
paras.zh: 他们会为这事争上差不多一个月？

paras.en: There’s always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made.
paras.zh: 总会有那么个把董事插手，要求做些修改。

paras.en: They might think they’re being helpful, but in reality, they’re being obstructive and hampering progress.
paras.zh: 他们可能觉得自己是在帮忙，但实际上是在添乱，拖慢进度。

paras.en: Oh, Jeff, you’re too preoccupied and cynical.
paras.zh: 哎呀，杰夫，你顾虑太多，也太悲观了。

w.m: adj. 心事重重的；想得太多的
adj. 愤世嫉俗的；凡事往坏处想的

paras.en: It won’t be anywhere as bad as that.
paras.zh: 根本不会有那么糟。

w.m: adv. （用于否定）远远（不）；一点也（不）

paras.en: You’ll see.
paras.zh: 等着瞧吧。

paras.en: The entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible, and the board too is virtually unanimous in its support.
paras.zh: 整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快落实，董事会也几乎一致支持。

paras.en: Go on, then.
paras.zh: 那好吧。

paras.en: Let’s stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow.
paras.zh: 我们就到这儿，明天同一时间再碰头。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?
paras.zh: 第五题：男士为什么提议今天就到此为止？

paras.en: Question six: What does the woman say is a little tough?
paras.zh: 第六题：女士说什么事有点累人？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they’ll finish by next week?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士认为下周就能完成，男士说她这么想一定是怎么了？

paras.en: Question eight: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第八题：根据女士的说法，整个管理层希望看到什么？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: One thing I’ve learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right or wrong solutions to employee disputes.
paras.zh: 我做了二十五年管理工作，学到的一点是：人的行为中存在大量灰色地带，员工之间的纠纷也不一定总有明确的对错之分。

w.m: 二十五年；四分之一世纪

paras.en: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
paras.zh: 两个人对同一件事说法不一的时候，你很难知道该信谁。

paras.en: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
paras.zh: 有一件这样的事，我总会想起来。

paras.en: It happened years ago, and it’s a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
paras.zh: 那是多年前的事了，这场冲突有多容易被忘掉，从这一点就能看出来：我连当时为什么争都不记得了，但怎么解决的，我记得清清楚楚。

paras.en: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we’d never get to the truth.
paras.zh: 两位很有才干的年轻主管，其中一位归我管，他们对同一件事的说法大相径庭，看来我们很可能永远也弄不清真相。

paras.en: We reached a deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, “Here’s something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.”
paras.zh: 我们陷入了僵局，另一位员工的经理说：“我从以前跟过的一位优秀经理那里学到了一句话。”

paras.en: He used to say, “When in doubt, assume positive intent,” and just like that, we had a path forward.
paras.zh: 那位经理常说：“拿不准的时候，就假定对方是出于好意。”就这样，我们一下子找到了出路。

paras.en: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
paras.zh: 我和那位经理都认为，事情的真相我们可能永远也弄不清了。

w.m: n. 职位相当的人；对应的人

paras.en: Quite likely, there were elements of truth in both employees’ stories.
paras.zh: 很可能两位员工的说法都有一部分是真的。

paras.en: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
paras.zh: 我们商定，今后会留意他们的言行和关系，但不再进一步干预。

paras.en: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
paras.zh: 我们把两个人都往好处想，然后就翻篇了。

paras.en: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
paras.zh: 结果，我们把这场冲突抛在了脑后。

paras.en: In fact, their problems didn’t recur.
paras.zh: 事实上，他们的问题再也没有出现过。

paras.en: Over the years, this general approach has proved useful.
paras.zh: 这些年来，这种通用的做法证明很管用。

paras.en: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
paras.zh: 每当真相不明时，往好处想、商定翻篇，可能是一个有建设性的决定。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: When can it be hard to know whom to believe?
paras.zh: 第九题：什么时候很难知道该相信谁？

paras.en: Question 10: What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example?
paras.zh: 第十题：说话人对作为例子提到的那次纠纷，确切记得的是什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event?
paras.zh: 第十一题：两名员工对同一件事说法不一时，说话人和那位经理做了什么？

w.m: n. 职位相当的人；对应的人

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat planned and budgeted for.
paras.zh: 对有些美国人来说，出去吃顿饭是一种早有计划、事先做好预算的享受。

paras.en: For others, it’s just a daily occurrence, and that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
paras.zh: 对另一些人来说，这只是家常便饭，而且随着喜欢做饭的美国人越来越少，后一种人正在成为多数。

paras.en: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans’ attitudes to cooking.
paras.zh: 二十一世纪初，研究人员埃迪·尹做了一项调查，想弄清美国人对做饭的态度。

paras.en: The survey found that 15 percent of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook, and 35% reported mixed feelings.
paras.zh: 调查发现，15%的美国人喜欢做饭，50%说讨厌做饭，35%表示心情复杂。

paras.en: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it, and 45% had mixed feelings.
paras.zh: 十五年后尹又做了同样的调查，只有10%的受访者说喜欢做饭，45%说讨厌，45%心情复杂。

paras.en: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
paras.zh: 尹认为，做饭和缝纫是一个道理。

paras.en: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
paras.zh: 就在二十世纪初，很多美国人还是自己缝衣服穿。

paras.en: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing.
paras.zh: 如今，绝大多数美国人都买衣服穿。

paras.en: Only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby.
paras.zh: 只有极少数人还自己缝，而且主要是当作一种爱好。

paras.en: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
paras.zh: 尹认为，在家做饭的人也会这样越来越少。

paras.en: Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out.
paras.zh: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上要花三千多美元。

paras.en: However, what people save in convenience they lose in cash.
paras.zh: 然而，人们省了事，却费了钱。

paras.en: Take buying lunch on work days, for example.
paras.zh: 就拿上班日买午饭来说吧。

paras.en: People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
paras.zh: 买午饭的话，人们平均每顿要花10美元。

paras.en: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
paras.zh: 而自己带午饭，花的钱会少一些。

paras.en: One survey found people only spend, on average, $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
paras.zh: 一项调查发现，从家里带午饭，人们平均只花6.30美元。

paras.en: Americans’ growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
paras.zh: 美国人越来越不愿意花时间待在厨房里，这意味着食品杂货业将面临一系列挑战。

paras.en: It’s likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
paras.zh: 这很可能也会给家庭财务带来不利影响。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What do an increasing number of Americans do, according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第十二题：根据短文，越来越多的美国人在做什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What does Eddie Yoon think cooking is akin to?
paras.zh: 第十三题：埃迪·尹认为做饭和什么类似？
