paras.en: Question 14: What will Americans be able to do by making their own lunch?
paras.zh: 第十四题：美国人自己做午饭，能做到什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the passage say signifies a host of challenges for America’s grocery industry?
paras.zh: 第十五题：短文说什么意味着美国的食品杂货业将面临一系列挑战？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Every year of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing, and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
paras.zh: 全世界每年托运上飞机的行李有二十五亿多件，其中两千六百万件会丢失，而这两千六百万件里，有一百万件再也回不到原来的主人手里。

paras.en: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
paras.zh: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，还有一些人干脆忘了取走自己的某件行李，都是其中的原因。

paras.en: But the number one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don’t know to whom it belongs.
paras.zh: 但行李丢失的头号原因是没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它是谁的。

paras.en: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
paras.zh: 把行李从值机处送到登机口，再到到达口，再到行李提取处，是个很讲究时机的精细活儿。

w.m: adj. 微妙的；需要小心处理的

paras.en: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won’t make connecting flights.
paras.zh: 如果系统运转太慢，行李就赶不上转机航班。

paras.en: If it’s too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
paras.zh: 如果太快，行李可能赶上了转机，乘客却可能误了航班。

paras.en: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
paras.zh: 每个机场都有自己的办法，来分配行李中转需要多长时间。

paras.en: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
paras.zh: 有些机场有先进的自动化系统，包括能读取行李标签的扫描仪、不用停车就能装卸行李的目的地编码运输车，以及能把行李送到相应登机口的分拣机。

paras.en: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
paras.zh: 即便如此，这些技术也未必能保证你的行李标签不会在传送带上被扯掉，那样你就成了一件无名行李的主人。

paras.en: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared mishandled by the carrier.
paras.zh: 一旦行李丢失、乘客提出索赔，承运人就会宣布这件行李为“处理不当”。

paras.en: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen, or damaged.
paras.zh: “处理不当”指的是延误、丢失、被盗或损坏的行李。

paras.en: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
paras.zh: 大多数延误的行李只比主人晚一个航班，二十四小时内就能送到。

paras.en: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination, if the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
paras.zh: 其他行李由航空公司员工检查，寻找能说明归属和目的地的线索，如果谜团解开了，这些行李会在四五天内还给主人。

paras.en: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
paras.zh: 没有目的地代码或身份标签的行李会被运到一个中央仓库，在接下来的九十天里经过一整套全面的行李追踪流程。

paras.en: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners’ descriptions.
paras.zh: 航空公司会把这些处理不当的行李登记造册，很多公司还用数据库，把行李里的东西和失主的描述对上号。

paras.en: It takes about three months to go from missing in action to irretrievably lost.
paras.zh: 从“下落不明”到彻底找不回来，大约要三个月。

w.m: （原指士兵）作战中失踪；下落不明

paras.en: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public, so never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage, and make sure your name is on the bag along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
paras.zh: 一旦到了那一步，这些行李就会被捐给慈善机构、拿去拍卖，或者被一家公司买下再卖给公众；所以千万别在托运行李里放真正贵重的东西，还要确保行李上写着你的名字和电话号码，这样工作人员才能联系到你。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What is the number one reason a bag ends up lost, according to this talk?
paras.zh: 第十六题：根据这段讲话，行李丢失的头号原因是什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems?
paras.zh: 第十七题：即使有先进的自动化系统，你的行李还可能遇到什么情况？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
paras.zh: 第十八题：讲话结束时，说话人建议我们怎么做？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: You’ve probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone, and you’ve probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
paras.zh: 你可能遇到过这样的情况：跟某个人在一起，他却只顾摆弄手机，把你晾在一边；你自己可能也这么干过。

paras.en: In a recent survey, nine out of 10 respondents said they’d used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
paras.zh: 在最近一项调查中，十分之九的受访者说，他们在最近一次社交活动中用过手机。

paras.en: There’s also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
paras.zh: 也有证据表明，这种行为对社交有害。

paras.en: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
paras.zh: 它会让人们对面对面的交流不那么满意，还会引发怨恨和嫉妒。

paras.en: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
paras.zh: 现在，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨产生这些影响的原因。

paras.en: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
paras.zh: 这项研究共有128名参与者，大多是女学生。

paras.en: The participants watched a three-minute animation, in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
paras.zh: 参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画，里面两个卡通人物在互动、交谈。

paras.en: The conversation couldn’t be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
paras.zh: 对话听不到，但可以通过嘴部动作看出来。

paras.en: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video, and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
paras.zh: 参与者要把自己想象成视频里离得最近的那个人物，然后对这些对话以及自己对谈话对象的感受作出判断。

paras.en: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participant’s conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
paras.zh: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的谈话对象把手机放在桌上，整个谈话过程中一直没用。

paras.en: In another version, their partner’s attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
paras.zh: 在另一个版本中，谈话对象的注意力很快被手机上的什么东西吸引过去，剩下的时间都在摆弄手机。

paras.en: A third version involved the participants’ partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
paras.zh: 第三个版本是，参与者的谈话对象一会儿摆弄手机，一会儿又把手机晾在一边。

paras.en: If you’ve experienced a similar situation, you probably won’t be surprised by the results of the experiments.
paras.zh: 如果你有过类似的经历，大概不会对实验结果感到意外。

paras.en: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
paras.zh: 参与者对社交时使用手机持负面看法。

paras.en: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
paras.zh: 手机出现得越多，他们对互动质量和关系质量的评价就越差。

paras.en: The researchers believed that focusing on one’s phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it’s seen as a form of social exclusion, they assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，之所以会有这种影响，是因为只顾看手机、不理身边的人，会被看作一种社交排斥；他们断言，这种行为就好比一个人不得不在学校食堂独自吃饭。

paras.en: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
paras.zh: 反常之处在于，这种排斥恰恰发生在双方面对面、正在交谈的时候。

w.m: n. 意外转折；反常之处

paras.en: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants’ sense of belonging, need for meaning, and self-esteem.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊心都有不利影响。

paras.en: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
paras.zh: 这些负面影响和传统形式的社交排斥造成的影响类似。

paras.en: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience, this common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment, even as we try to connect with others.
paras.zh: 这些新发现很重要，因为它们让我们更深入地了解了日常生活里一个不起眼却很常见的现象：这种常见的行为会造成恶性循环，让人越来越疏远，即便我们正努力跟别人交流。

w.m: adj. 微妙的；不易察觉的

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about using one’s smartphone during a face-to-face conversation?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于面对面交谈时用手机，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions?
paras.zh: 第二十题：在这项新研究中，参与者对社交时使用手机有什么反应？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说，面对面交谈时使用手机这种常见行为会导致什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons, many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business.
paras.zh: 出于各种原因，越来越多的人外出旅行，很多人是游客，但也有很多人是因私事或公事出门。

paras.en: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
paras.zh: 不管出于什么原因出行，旅行者的一个普遍抱怨是住的地方千篇一律、没有人情味。

w.m: adj. 没有人情味的；冷冰冰的

paras.en: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food, and service are concerned.
paras.zh: 在五家差不多的酒店连住五晚之后，商务旅客可能很难记得每天发生了什么，甚至记不清去过哪些城镇；游客则可能误以为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装修、饮食和服务方面是这样。

paras.en: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or bed and breakfast arrangements, B and B’s, I mean bed and breakfast arrangements, are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting.
paras.zh: 为了摆脱这种千篇一律、没有人情味的感觉，旅行者开始选择住进当地人家里，也就是住民宿；民宿，我是说提供住宿和早餐的家庭旅馆，就是私人住宅，在非常个性化、温馨友好的环境里为客人提供住宿和早餐。

w.m: adj. 没有人情味的；冷冰冰的
住宿加早餐（的旅馆）；民宿

paras.en: For decades, B and B’s have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles, and in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
paras.zh: 几十年来，民宿一直是游览欧洲、尤其是不列颠群岛的经典方式；其实在美国，这也不算什么新鲜主意。

paras.en: The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
paras.zh: 这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期，那时客栈很少，疲惫的旅人只能指望陌生人好心给一顿饭、一张床。

paras.en: But the revival of B and B’s as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
paras.zh: 但民宿作为一种受欢迎的住处重新兴起，是近些年才有的现象。

w.m: adj. 令人向往的；理想的

paras.en: If the idea of operating a B and B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
paras.zh: 如果你对经营民宿感兴趣，那么在投身这一行之前，有几个因素需要考虑。

paras.en: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself but the location.
paras.zh: 首先要考虑的是你的房产，不只是房子本身，还有地段。

paras.en: If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination such as New York City or Washington D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B and B.
paras.zh: 如果你住在著名历史遗址附近，或者住在纽约市、华盛顿特区这样的热门目的地，那么你的房子就算相当简单，开民宿照样能经营得不错。

paras.en: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath, or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
paras.zh: 另一方面，如果你的房子建筑风格独特，或者有方便旅客的设施，比如独立入口、独立浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意跑上一段路来找你。

paras.en: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
paras.zh: 另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。

paras.en: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry, and bookkeeping involved.
paras.zh: 你必须考虑：家里所有人是不是真的喜欢有客人来，愿不愿意一遍遍地介绍当地景点和活动，有没有时间和精力应付随之而来的额外做饭、打扫、洗衣和记账。

paras.en: The final consideration is a financial one.
paras.zh: 最后要考虑的是钱的问题。

paras.en: Potential B and B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
paras.zh: 想开民宿的人必须对能赚多少钱有现实的预期。

paras.en: While B and B’s usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B and B.
paras.zh: 虽然民宿的初期成本通常很低，但专家估计，房东至少要有五间房经常租出去，才能靠民宿维持生计。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：说话人说旅行者通常抱怨什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What is said about bed and breakfast arrangements?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于住宿加早餐式的民宿，文中说了什么？

w.m: 住宿加早餐（的旅馆）；民宿

paras.en: Question 24: What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B and B business?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：如果你想做民宿生意，首先要考虑的是什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What does the speaker say potential B and B hosts must be realistic about?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：说话人说想开民宿的人必须对什么有现实的预期？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2025年12月大学英语六级 第2套
passages.name: 2025年12月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，两人聊学校食堂：女士嫌饭菜一般、价格离谱，男士觉得价格合理，两人都夸食堂出餐快、环境好。第二段长对话讲管理者怎样和年轻员工相处：年轻人看重工作与生活的平衡，按工作质量衡量效率，想在价值观一致的公司做有意义的事。第一篇短文介绍一项研究：菜单上单设素食区、推荐素菜，反而可能让常吃素的人少点素菜。第二篇短文介绍用冷冻法清除空气污染物的新方法，有望用来改造空调、净化室内空气。第一段录音讲一种鱼通过了镜子测试，由此引出鱼有没有自我意识、镜子测试是否可靠的问题。第二段录音介绍一项研究：幼儿读电子书比读纸质书更投入、学到的新词更多，但附加功能要服务于教育内容。第三段录音劝人不要为过去的决定后悔，而要从教训中学习、继续往前走。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: I must say, I love our canteen.
paras.zh: 说真的，我太喜欢我们的食堂了。

paras.en: It’s such a great meeting point.
paras.zh: 这里真是个碰面的好地方。

paras.en: Yeah, it really is, both for students and teachers.
paras.zh: 是啊，确实是，学生和老师都爱来。

paras.en: Shame about the food.
paras.zh: 就是饭菜不怎么样，可惜了。

paras.en: What do you mean?
paras.zh: 你这话什么意思？

paras.en: I think the food is fine.
paras.zh: 我觉得饭菜挺好的呀。

paras.en: I would say the food is just okay, but the prices are absurd.
paras.zh: 要我说，饭菜也就一般，可价格贵得离谱。

paras.en: Don’t you agree?
paras.zh: 你不这么觉得吗？

paras.en: I don’t actually.
paras.zh: 其实我不这么觉得。

paras.en: I personally think they’re perfectly appropriate.
paras.zh: 我个人觉得价格完全合理。

paras.en: If it’s overpriced, why does it get so frantically busy at lunch times?
paras.zh: 要是真的定价太高，为什么一到午饭时间就挤得不得了？

w.m: adv. 疯狂地；手忙脚乱地

paras.en: Hmm.
paras.zh: 嗯。

w.m: int. 嗯（表示犹豫或思考）

paras.en: You make a good point.
paras.zh: 你说得有道理。

paras.en: I guess a lot of it is good value, maybe even most of it.
paras.zh: 我想很多东西确实物有所值，说不定大部分都是。

paras.en: However, don’t you think six bucks for a slice of apple crumble is beyond most students’ budgets?
paras.zh: 不过，一块苹果酥要六美元，你不觉得大多数学生都负担不起吗？

paras.en: Ah, yes.
paras.zh: 啊，对。

paras.en: Desserts are overpriced.
paras.zh: 甜点是贵了点。

paras.en: I’ll give you that.
paras.zh: 这点我承认。

paras.en: To be honest, I’ve forgotten about those as I never eat them.
paras.zh: 说实话，我都把甜点忘了，因为我从来不吃。

paras.en: I never really crave sweet things or any fancy delicacies.
paras.zh: 我从来不怎么馋甜食，也不馋什么花哨的精致点心。

paras.en: What I always go for is their scrambled eggs.
paras.zh: 我每次都点他们的炒鸡蛋。

paras.en: They have such a great variety.
paras.zh: 花样可多了。

paras.en: Yeah, those are good.
paras.zh: 对，那个确实好吃。

paras.en: They also come out really fast.
paras.zh: 而且出餐特别快。

paras.en: Actually, that’s one of the best things about the canteen: the speed.
paras.zh: 说真的，这正是食堂最大的优点之一：快。

paras.en: If I fancy something more substantial than a sandwich, but I don’t have much time for lunch, the university canteen is always a good option.
paras.zh: 要是我想吃点比三明治顶饱的东西，可午饭时间又不多，学校食堂永远是个好选择。

paras.en: The kitchen staff work at such a brisk pace; they really deserve to be complimented for it.
paras.zh: 后厨员工手脚那么麻利，真该好好夸夸他们。

paras.en: Totally, and it’s such a great environment too.
paras.zh: 完全同意，而且环境也特别好。

paras.en: Like the entire building is beautiful.
paras.zh: 就是说，整栋楼都很漂亮。

paras.en: It is very nice.
paras.zh: 确实很好看。

w.m: adj. 好看的；令人愉快的

paras.en: The massive glass windows make all the difference.
paras.zh: 那几扇超大的玻璃窗一下子让整个地方都不一样了。

paras.en: I think they’re so cool.
paras.zh: 我觉得特别酷。

paras.en: Apparently, they did a massive renovation a few years ago.
paras.zh: 听说他们几年前大规模翻修过一次。

paras.en: It cost them a pretty penny.
paras.zh: 花了他们一大笔钱。

paras.en: I’m not surprised.
paras.zh: 我一点也不意外。

paras.en: It’s a very versatile space, suitable both for eating and relaxing, and for working.
paras.zh: 这里用途特别多，吃饭、休息都合适，还能工作。

w.m: adj. 多用途的；多功能的

paras.en: You’re right, working too.
paras.zh: 没错，还能工作。

paras.en: I’ve used my laptop there once or twice, and there’s always a group project or meeting going on at the far end.
paras.zh: 我在那儿用笔记本电脑干过一两回活，最里头总有人在做小组作业或者开会。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What does the woman say about the food at the canteen?
paras.zh: 第一题：关于食堂的饭菜，女士是怎么说的？

paras.en: Question two: How does the woman feel about the canteen’s sweet things or fancy delicacies?
paras.zh: 第二题：女士对食堂的甜食和花哨的精致点心有什么看法？

paras.en: Question three: What does the man say is one of the best things about the canteen?
paras.zh: 第三题：男士说食堂最大的优点之一是什么？

paras.en: Question four: What did the canteen undergo a few years ago?
paras.zh: 第四题：几年前食堂经历了什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hi Tony.
paras.zh: 你好，托尼。

paras.en: Today we’re talking about how managers can get along better with young people at work.
paras.zh: 今天我们来聊聊，管理者怎样才能在工作中跟年轻人相处得更好。

paras.en: We often hear young people today have a poor work ethic.
paras.zh: 我们常听人说，现在的年轻人缺乏职业道德。

paras.en: That’s not really justified, though, is it?
paras.zh: 不过这种说法其实站不住脚，对吧？

paras.en: Not really.
paras.zh: 确实站不住脚。

paras.en: In reality, young people of this age group are as varied and multifaceted as any other generation.
paras.zh: 实际上，这个年龄段的年轻人和其他任何一代人一样，千差万别，各有各的样子。

w.m: adj. 各不相同的；多样的

paras.en: Yeah, but if you are struggling to work with young people in your workspace, what can you do?
paras.zh: 是，可要是你在单位里跟年轻人怎么也合作不好，该怎么办呢？

paras.en: Well, it’s essential to connect with them to learn about their values.
paras.zh: 嗯，关键是要跟他们多沟通，了解他们看重什么。

w.m: adj. 极其重要的；必不可少的

paras.en: It’s also really important to recognize the way young people want to balance their work life with their personal life.
paras.zh: 还有一点很重要：要认识到年轻人希望在工作和个人生活之间保持平衡。

paras.en: So they generally don’t want to defer happiness in return for career advancement.
paras.zh: 所以他们一般不愿意为了升职而推迟享受幸福。

paras.en: Absolutely, they are not willing to sacrifice their personal lives for their work lives, and this leads people to equate that with an unwillingness to work hard.
paras.zh: 完全正确，他们不愿意为了工作牺牲个人生活，于是有人就把这一点等同于不肯努力工作。

paras.en: Right, but that couldn’t be further from the truth, could it?
paras.zh: 对，可这跟事实完全相反，不是吗？

w.h: could not be further from the truth

paras.en: Young people will work extremely hard during their defined work hours, but they expect to have their time off, like weekends and nights, free from work.
paras.zh: 在规定的工作时间里，年轻人会非常卖力，但他们希望休息时间，比如周末和晚上，不被工作打扰。

paras.en: So, how should managers go about assessing young people’s productivity?
paras.zh: 那么，管理者应该怎样去评估年轻人的工作效率呢？

w.m: n. 生产效率；工作效率

paras.en: Generally, young people believe their productivity should not be measured by the number of hours they work, since someone can work for eight hours and accomplish next to nothing of significance for the company.
paras.zh: 一般来说，年轻人认为工作效率不该按工作了多少小时来衡量，因为一个人可能干了八个小时，却几乎没为公司做成什么要紧的事。

w.m: n. 生产效率；工作效率

paras.en: Instead, young people measure their productivity levels by the quality of the work they perform.
paras.zh: 他们看的是自己完成的工作质量，用它来衡量工作效率。

w.m: n. 生产效率；工作效率

paras.en: But we often hear that young people want to feel more than just being a part of a big machine.
paras.zh: 可我们也常听说，年轻人不想觉得自己只是大机器上的一个零件。

paras.en: Such a perspective can be hard to discredit, can’t it?
paras.zh: 这种看法很难反驳，对吧？

paras.en: It’s important to legitimize their work.
paras.zh: 要让他们的工作得到认可，这很重要。

w.m: v. 使合法化；认可……的价值

paras.en: Young workers want to work on projects that matter to themselves, the company, or the world at large.
paras.zh: 年轻员工想做的项目，要对自己、对公司或者对整个世界有意义。

paras.en: They must feel the need to stay working at a company whose values align with their own.
paras.zh: 他们一定会觉得，要待就待在价值观跟自己一致的公司。

paras.en: Thanks for your advice.
paras.zh: 谢谢你的建议。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: According to the woman, what view about today’s young people is not really justified?
paras.zh: 第五题：据女士所说，关于现在的年轻人，哪种看法其实站不住脚？

paras.en: Question six: What does the man say is important for managers to get along better with young workers?
paras.zh: 第六题：男士说，管理者要想和年轻员工相处得更好，什么很重要？

paras.en: Question seven: How do young people measure their productivity levels according to the man?
paras.zh: 第七题：据男士所说，年轻人怎样衡量自己的工作效率？

w.m: n. 生产效率；工作效率

paras.en: Question eight: What companies does the man think would appeal to young workers?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士认为什么样的公司会吸引年轻员工？

paras.en: Section B, Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: Many restaurants are trying to persuade customers to eat more sustainably, moving away from environmentally unfriendly meat towards greener dishes.
paras.zh: 许多餐馆正在设法劝顾客吃得更环保，少吃不利于环境的肉类，多吃更绿色的菜。

paras.en: Although it sounds counterintuitive, restaurants which include specific vegetarian sections on their menus may be unintentionally encouraging customers to eat meat, a new study suggests.
paras.zh: 一项新研究表明，虽然听起来有违常理，但在菜单上专门设素食区的餐馆，可能在无意中鼓励顾客吃肉。

w.m: adj. 违反直觉的；有违常理的

paras.en: Behavioral scientist Linda Bacon, one of the study’s authors, said, “Restaurants can have a positive impact on the environment by encouraging their customers to choose more plant-based food and less meat.”
paras.zh: 该研究的作者之一、行为科学家琳达·培根说：“餐馆可以鼓励顾客多选植物性食物、少吃肉，从而对环境产生积极影响。”

w.m: adj. 以植物为主的；植物性的

paras.en: However, our findings suggest that while certain restaurant menu designs can encourage some consumers to make pro-environmental food choices, they can have the opposite effect on others.
paras.zh: 不过，我们的研究结果表明，某些餐馆菜单设计虽然能促使一部分顾客选择更环保的食物，但对另一些人却会适得其反。

paras.en: The study involved 750 people, half of whom frequently ate vegetarian food and half of whom rarely ate it.
paras.zh: 这项研究有750人参加，其中一半人经常吃素食，另一半人很少吃。

paras.en: No vegetarians were included.
paras.zh: 参与者中没有素食者。

paras.en: They were given different menus and asked to choose a meal as if they were eating out with friends.
paras.zh: 研究人员给他们发了不同的菜单，让他们就当是在和朋友下馆子，点一份餐。

paras.en: Placing vegetarian dishes in a separate section did not have a significant effect on the choices made by infrequent vegetarian food eaters, but it did have a notable effect on the frequent eaters, lowering their chance of picking a vegetarian option by 65 percent.
paras.zh: 把素菜单独放在一个区，对不常吃素的人点什么没有明显影响，但对常吃素的人影响却很明显：他们选素菜的可能性降低了65%。

w.m: adj. 不常发生的；稀少的
adj. 显著的；值得注意的

paras.en: The researchers also discovered that presenting a vegetarian dish as the chef’s recommendation, or including a more appealing description of a non-meat meal, leads to a greater proportion of infrequent vegetarian eaters choosing a vegetarian option, but again, these altered menu designs backfired with those who ate vegetarian food more frequently, leading them to be less likely to choose a vegetarian dish.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，把一道素菜作为主厨推荐，或者把无肉餐点描述得更诱人，会让更多不常吃素的人选择素菜；但同样，这些改过的菜单设计在常吃素的人身上又起了反作用，让他们更不愿意选素菜。

w.m: v. 适得其反；起反作用

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What does a new study suggest about restaurants including vegetarian sections on their menus?
paras.zh: 第九题：关于在菜单上设素食区的餐馆，一项新研究有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 10: How was the study carried out on 750 participants?
paras.zh: 第十题：这项有750名参与者的研究是怎样进行的？

paras.en: Question 11: How do altered menu designs affect frequent eaters of vegetarian food?
paras.zh: 第十一题：改过的菜单设计对常吃素的人有什么影响？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences have been trying to find a way to prevent deadly outdoor air pollution from penetrating indoors.
paras.zh: 诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院一直在想办法，不让致命的室外空气污染渗进室内。

paras.en: They found that if pollution is frozen to around minus 18 degrees Celsius in a condensing tube, the particles gather together and fall to the bottom, allowing fresh, clean air to pass through.
paras.zh: 他们发现，在冷凝管里把污染物冷冻到零下18摄氏度左右，颗粒物就会聚到一起、落到管底，干净的新鲜空气就能通过。

paras.en: Their method was able to remove 99% of pollutants.
paras.zh: 他们的方法能清除99%的污染物。

paras.en: It is hoped that the work could pave the way for simple modification of air conditioning units, so that they can also clean polluted indoor air.
paras.zh: 人们希望，这项研究能为简单改造空调机组铺平道路，让空调也能净化被污染的室内空气。

paras.en: Outdoor air pollution in cities is a global problem, whether it be haze plaguing Kolkata or poor air impacting the health of children in London schools.
paras.zh: 城市室外空气污染是个全球性问题，不管是困扰加尔各答的雾霾，还是影响伦敦学校孩子健康的糟糕空气。

paras.en: While there are some existing technologies to purify indoor air, they can be inefficient, expensive, or produce harmful by-products.
paras.zh: 虽然现在已有一些净化室内空气的技术，但它们可能效率低、价格贵，或者会产生有害的副产品。

paras.en: When outdoor air quality is poor, people tend to spend even more time indoors, but outdoor pollution also leads to indoor pollution, and people still suffer.
paras.zh: 室外空气质量差的时候人们往往会在室内待更长时间，可室外污染也会造成室内污染，人们还是要受害。

paras.en: It is estimated that pollution is linked to over 40,000 early deaths in Britain each year.
paras.zh: 据估计，英国每年有4万多人的过早死亡与污染有关。

paras.en: Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences said, “We have shown in our experiments that simply by circulating polluted air through a small freezing chamber, we can remove most of the fine particles and gas pollutants.
paras.zh: 中国科学院的潘刚教授说：“我们在实验中证明，只要让被污染的空气在一个小冷冻室里循环流过，就能除掉大部分细颗粒物和气态污染物。

paras.en: Our study makes it possible to add an air cleaner option to household appliances in areas which might experience extremely poor air conditions.
paras.zh: 有了我们的研究，在空气状况可能极差的地区，家用电器就可以加装空气净化功能。

paras.en: By controlling indoor air pollution and improving air quality in this way, this work could be greatly beneficial to public health.
paras.zh: 用这种方法控制室内空气污染、改善空气质量，这项研究可能会大大有益于公众健康。”

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the passage say about Nottingham Trent University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences?
paras.zh: 第十二题：关于诺丁汉特伦特大学和中国科学院，短文说了什么？

paras.en: Question 13: What do we learn from the passage about existing technologies to purify indoor air?
paras.zh: 第十三题：关于现有的室内空气净化技术，我们从短文中了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What do people tend to do when outdoor air quality is poor?
paras.zh: 第十四题：室外空气质量差的时候，人们往往会怎么做？

paras.en: Question 15: What did Professor Gang Pan of the Chinese Academy of Sciences say about their study?
paras.zh: 第十五题：中国科学院的潘刚教授对他们的研究有什么说法？

paras.en: Section C, directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Research recently carried out by my team suggests that fish may be self-aware.
paras.zh: 我的团队最近做的一项研究表明，鱼可能有自我意识。

paras.en: A certain species of fish recently passed the well-known mirror test.
paras.zh: 最近，有一种鱼通过了著名的镜子测试。

paras.en: This is a test that demonstrates self-recognition in animals.
paras.zh: 这项测试用来证明动物能认出自己。

paras.en: Only a few animals, such as humans, apes, dolphins, and some birds can recognize themselves in a mirror, and only these animals capable of self-recognition will attempt to remove marks placed on their skin after noticing them in the reflection.
paras.zh: 只有少数动物，比如人类、类人猿、海豚和某些鸟类，能在镜子里认出自己；也只有这些能自我识别的动物，在镜中看到自己皮肤上被做的记号后，才会试着把它去掉。

paras.en: This ability suggests a level of higher intelligence and awareness.
paras.zh: 这种能力意味着更高水平的智力和意识。

paras.en: This is not shown by children until around 18 months.
paras.zh: 孩子要到18个月左右才会表现出这种能力。

paras.en: Until now, no fish has demonstrated the ability, but our experiments show the fish in question will scrape up against hard surfaces to remove marks placed on its body by our researchers after viewing itself in a mirror.
paras.zh: 在此之前，还没有哪种鱼表现出这种能力；但我们的实验显示，研究人员在这种鱼身上做了记号后，它在镜子里看到自己，就会在坚硬的物体表面上蹭，想把记号去掉。

paras.en: The behaviors we observe leave little doubt that this fish behaviorally fulfills all criteria of the mirror test as originally laid out.
paras.zh: 从我们观察到的行为看，几乎可以肯定，这种鱼在行为上满足了镜子测试最初设定的全部标准。

paras.en: The fish in our study never attempted to remove the marks when no mirror was present, or when the marks were just placed on the mirror.
paras.zh: 在我们的研究中，没有镜子的时候，或者记号只是做在镜子上的时候，鱼从来没有试图去除记号。

paras.en: Unmarked fish also did not attempt to remove marks from themselves when interacting with a marked fish on the other side of a window.
paras.zh: 身上没有记号的鱼，隔着一扇窗和有记号的鱼互动时，也不会试图去掉自己身上的记号。

paras.en: These results show either that fish are self-aware, or that the mirror test, which is considered to be the gold standard test used to denote higher intelligence, may be flawed.
paras.zh: 这些结果说明，要么鱼有自我意识，要么镜子测试本身有缺陷，而这项测试一直被看作判断高等智力的黄金标准。

paras.en: What is less clear is whether these behaviours should be considered as evidence that fish are self-aware, even though in the past these same behaviours have been interpreted as self-awareness in so many other animals.
paras.zh: 不那么清楚的是，这些行为该不该被当作鱼有自我意识的证据，尽管过去在许多其他动物身上，同样的行为都被解读为有自我意识。

paras.en: Depending on your position, you might reject the interpretation that these behaviours in a fish satisfy passing the test at all, but on what objective basis can you do this when the behaviours they show are so functionally similar to those of other species that have passed the test?
paras.zh: 你也许会因为自己的立场，根本不接受“鱼的这些行为就算通过了测试”这种解读；可是，鱼表现出的行为和那些已经通过测试的物种在功能上这么相似，你又凭什么客观依据去否定呢？

paras.en: Results from our research raise more questions than answers.
paras.zh: 我们的研究结果带来的问题比答案还多。

paras.en: What if self-awareness develops like an onion, building layer upon layer, rather than appearing all at once.
paras.zh: 要是自我意识就像洋葱一样，是一层一层长出来的，而不是一下子出现的呢？

paras.en: Perhaps, in order to explore self-awareness further, we should stop looking at responses to the mirror as a decisive test.
paras.zh: 也许，为了进一步探究自我意识，我们不该再把对镜子的反应当成决定性的测试。

paras.en: Only with a richer theory of the self and a larger test battery will we be able to determine all of the various levels of self-awareness, including where exactly fish fit in.
paras.zh: 只有关于自我的理论更丰富、成套的测试更多，我们才能确定自我意识的各个层次，包括鱼究竟处在哪个位置。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What do we learn about the well-known mirror test?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于著名的镜子测试，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What does the study by the speaker’s team show about the fish they experimented with?
paras.zh: 第十七题：说话人团队的研究，对他们用来做实验的鱼有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 18: What does the speaker say about the results of their research?
paras.zh: 第十八题：说话人对他们的研究结果是怎么说的？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: Reading with a young child is important, but does it matter whether you read from an electronic book or traditional print?
paras.zh: 陪小孩子读书很重要，可读电子书还是读传统的纸质书，有没有区别呢？

w.m: n. 印刷品；纸质出版物

paras.en: As any parent knows, small children are generally keen on screens, so the finding from a new study that very young children enjoy electronic books more than printed picture books may not come as a huge surprise.
paras.zh: 当父母的都知道，小孩子一般都爱看屏幕，所以一项新研究发现，很小的孩子喜欢电子书胜过纸质图画书，这也许并不让人太意外。

paras.en: But the following additional findings might: both parents and children behave differently when reading electronic versus printed picture books, and the children who read the electronic books learned more.
paras.zh: 但接下来这些新发现可能会让人意外：读电子图画书和读纸质图画书时，父母和孩子的表现都不一样，而且读电子书的孩子学到的更多。

paras.en: Previous studies of young children have suggested that electronic books, which incorporate extra features such as dictionaries and images that depict story events, may have advantages over print.
paras.zh: 以往针对幼儿的研究表明，电子书加入了词典、描绘故事情节的图片等额外功能，可能比纸质书更有优势。

paras.en: In fact, multiple studies have found that electronic books support story comprehension and vocabulary gains beyond what is provided by printed books.
paras.zh: 事实上，多项研究发现，电子书对理解故事和积累词汇的帮助，超过了纸质书。

paras.en: But there’s also work suggesting that children sometimes invest less mental effort in learning from electronic books, and that parents talk less about content when sharing such books.
paras.zh: 但也有研究认为，孩子读电子书时，有时在学习上花的心思更少，而父母和孩子一起看这类书时，谈论内容也更少。

paras.en: The study we’re looking at today aims to give us a better understanding of how good electronic books are for young children.
paras.zh: 我们今天要看的这项研究，目的是让我们更清楚地了解电子书对幼儿到底有多大好处。

paras.en: For this study, researchers videoed children aged 17 to 26 months reading with one of their parents.
paras.zh: 为了这项研究，研究人员拍下了17到26个月大的孩子和父母中的一方一起读书的视频。

paras.en: Each parent and child pair was randomly assigned to read either two educational electronic books or two printed books with the same content.
paras.zh: 每一对父母和孩子被随机分配，要么读两本教育类电子书，要么读两本内容相同的纸质书。

paras.en: While the parent read the words in the printed books aloud, the electronic books had audio of voice actors reading the text.
paras.zh: 纸质书由父母把文字大声读出来，电子书则配有配音演员朗读文字的音频。

paras.en: The researchers found that parents who read the printed books pointed more frequently to pages than parents who read the electronic books, but the opposite was true for the children.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，和读电子书的父母相比，读纸质书的父母更常用手指着书页；可孩子的情况正好相反。

paras.en: Children who read the electronic books also commented more on the content and learned more new words than the children who read printed books.
paras.zh: 和读纸质书的孩子相比，读电子书的孩子对内容发表的看法也更多，学到的新词也更多。

paras.en: This greater learning is ascribed to greater engagement with the electronic books.
paras.zh: 孩子们学得更多，是因为他们读电子书时更投入。

paras.en: It’s important to note that the electronic books in the study were simple, while they included background music, animation, and sound effects.
paras.zh: 需要注意的是，研究里用的电子书很简单，虽然配了背景音乐、动画和音效。

paras.en: There were no other extra features.
paras.zh: 但没有其他附加功能。

paras.en: It’s also important to note that there’s research on older children finding that electronic books don’t always bolster learning.
paras.zh: 还要注意的是，有针对大一点孩子的研究发现，电子书并不总能促进学习。

paras.en: Parents and educators need to beware.
paras.zh: 家长和教育工作者需要当心。

paras.en: Extra features in electronic books may increase children’s participation with them.
paras.zh: 电子书里的附加功能也许能让孩子更积极地参与其中。

paras.en: However, if these features don’t draw attention to the educational content, they may not serve as a supportive feature.
paras.zh: 但是，如果这些功能不能把注意力引到教育内容上，它们就起不到辅助作用。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What finding from the new study might come as a huge surprise?
paras.zh: 第十九题：这项新研究的哪个发现可能会让人大吃一惊？

paras.en: Question 20: What do we learn about previous studies of young children reading electronic books?
paras.zh: 第二十题：关于以往对幼儿读电子书的研究，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 21: What extra features should be included in electronic books to bolster children’s learning?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：电子书里应该加入什么附加功能，才能促进孩子的学习？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Let me be honest with you.
paras.zh: 跟大家说句实话吧。

paras.en: If you are living your life full of regrets, you’re wasting your time.
paras.zh: 如果你的生活里满是后悔，那你就是在浪费时间。

paras.en: Why would you go through life regretting the very decisions that made you who you are today?
paras.zh: 正是那些决定造就了今天的你，你为什么要一辈子为它们后悔呢？

paras.en: There are plenty of unfavorable decisions we’ve made, but does that mean we should regret them?
paras.zh: 我们做过很多不好的决定，可这就意味着我们该后悔吗？

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不是的。

paras.en: I’ve had many moments where I sit and think about all the things I wish I could have done differently.
paras.zh: 我有很多时候会坐着想：那些事我当初要是换个做法就好了。

paras.en: However, just because things could be different, it doesn’t necessarily mean they would be better.
paras.zh: 可是，事情本可以不一样，并不一定意味着就会更好。

paras.en: You don’t have to continually be thinking of all your past decisions and whether or not you made the right one, you can’t go back and change anything.
paras.zh: 你没必要一直去想过去做的所有决定、想自己当时选得对不对，反正你也回不去，什么都改变不了。

paras.en: So what’s the point in worrying about it?
paras.zh: 那为它发愁又有什么意义呢？

paras.en: Every single decision you’ve ever made, positive or negative, has made you the person you are today.
paras.zh: 你做过的每一个决定，不管是好是坏，都成就了今天的你。

w.m: adj. 单个的（强调每一个）

paras.en: We want to go back and change parts of our past, but what would be the benefit of that, we would have lost the valuable knowledge from the lessons we learned.
paras.zh: 我们想回到过去，改掉其中一些部分，可那样做有什么好处呢？我们会失去从教训中学到的宝贵认识。

paras.en: There are reasons you make the choices you do, and that tells us about who you are.
paras.zh: 你做出那样的选择总有原因，而这也说明了你是什么样的人。

paras.en: So when it comes to any decision in life, be unapologetically yourself, because at the end of the day, it was you who made that decision.
paras.zh: 所以，面对人生中的任何决定，都要理直气壮地做自己，因为说到底，做决定的是你自己。

w.m: adv. 毫无歉意地；理直气壮地

w.h: at the end of the day

paras.en: With less time spent focused on regrets, you’ll finally have time to focus on the more essential things in life.
paras.zh: 少花点时间纠结后悔的事，你终于就有时间去关注人生中更重要的事了。

paras.en: In any situation, you grow more as a person with every decision you make.
paras.zh: 不管在什么情况下，每做一个决定，你都会成长一些。

paras.en: Life is full of lessons to learn, so we can’t let regret stop us from moving forward.
paras.zh: 人生有太多要学的功课，所以我们不能让后悔挡住前进的脚步。

paras.en: We don’t know if we’ve made the right or wrong choice until after it’s already been made, so it can be easy to start regretting your decision.
paras.zh: 选择要等做出来以后，我们才知道它是对是错，所以人很容易就开始后悔自己的决定。

paras.en: But if the decision has already been made, what’s the purpose of dwelling on it?
paras.zh: 可既然决定已经做了，再反复纠结又有什么用呢？

paras.en: There isn’t one.
paras.zh: 一点用都没有。

w.m: pron. （指代前面提到的事物）一个

paras.en: All you can do is move forward.
paras.zh: 你能做的只有往前走。

paras.en: You can’t let yourself sit there and worry about every past choice.
paras.zh: 你不能让自己坐在那儿，为过去的每个选择发愁。

paras.en: We aren’t all perfect.
paras.zh: 我们谁都不是完美的。

paras.en: Whenever you make a decision, there will always be a possibility for regret later.
paras.zh: 每次做决定，事后总有可能后悔。

paras.en: But that’s how life is supposed to be.
paras.zh: 可人生本来就该是这样。

paras.en: You will make poor decisions in life.
paras.zh: 人生中你一定会做出一些糟糕的决定。

paras.en: We all do.
paras.zh: 我们都会。

paras.en: But it’s what you do with the lessons learned that matters.
paras.zh: 但真正要紧的，是你怎样对待学到的教训。

paras.en: Think about every decision you’ve ever made.
paras.zh: 想一想你做过的每一个决定。

paras.en: Were they always the best?
paras.zh: 它们都是最好的吗？

paras.en: Of course not.
paras.zh: 当然不是。

paras.en: But look at how far you’ve come since then.
paras.zh: 可你看看，从那时到现在，你已经走了多远。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What should we do with the unfavorable decisions we’ve made?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：对于我们做过的不好的决定，我们该怎么办？

paras.en: Question 23: What does the speaker say about every single decision?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于每一个决定，说话人是怎么说的？

w.m: adj. 单个的（强调每一个）

paras.en: Question 24: What is life full of, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：据说话人所说，人生充满了什么？

paras.en: Question 25: What is said to be of real importance when we make poor decisions in life?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：我们在人生中做了糟糕的决定时，什么才是真正重要的？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。

passages.paper: 2026年6月大学英语六级 第1套
passages.name: 2026年6月大学英语六级 第1套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，职业发展顾问露西·威廉斯谈怎样在职场上出人头地：多和同事沟通，不要一味加班，重质不重量，乐于助人但别自以为是。第二段长对话里，两位同学商量怎样分工做课题展示，男士抱怨自己干得最多，最后两人轮流讲各个部分。第一篇短文介绍一项研究：化妆会改变别人对你的看法，男性觉得化妆的女性更有威望，女性却觉得她们更强势、更有威胁。第二篇短文讲意志力：它不是咬牙硬扛，而是用心中的“动力”来控制自己的行为。第一段录音讲美国食品药品监督管理局更新了孕妇吃海鲜的建议，但批评者认为新建议仍让人困惑。第二段录音讲休假：每次休七到十一天最放松，一年里最好均匀地多休几次。第三段录音介绍瑞典正在研发的自动驾驶汽车，能在司机疲劳或情绪激动时接管驾驶。

paras.en: Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Welcome to Business Matters.
paras.zh: 欢迎收听《商业要闻》。

paras.en: Today we have invited career development consultant Lucy Williams to talk about how to get ahead at work.
paras.zh: 今天我们请来了职业发展顾问露西·威廉斯，跟我们聊聊怎样在工作中出人头地。

paras.en: Hi, Lucy.
paras.zh: 你好，露西。

paras.en: Many of us never seem to get promoted.
paras.zh: 我们很多人好像怎么也升不了职。

paras.en: Why is that, and what can we do about it?
paras.zh: 这是为什么，我们又能做些什么呢？

paras.en: One mistake people make is to limit communication only to their bosses.
paras.zh: 人们常犯的一个错误，是只跟自己的上司沟通。

paras.en: It’s important to expand your network and include your coworkers.
paras.zh: 重要的是扩大人脉，把同事也纳入进来。

paras.en: But some of our coworkers are less senior to us.
paras.zh: 可有些同事的职位比我们低。

paras.en: Is it really necessary to connect with them?
paras.zh: 真的有必要跟他们打交道吗？

paras.en: It’s important not to underestimate your colleagues.
paras.zh: 千万不要小看你的同事。

paras.en: Sometimes a job title might not clearly demonstrate the influence they may have.
paras.zh: 有时候，从职位名称上不一定看得出他们可能有多大的影响力。

paras.en: Now many of us think that working hard creates a good impression, but this isn’t always true, is it?
paras.zh: 我们很多人觉得努力工作能给人留下好印象，可事实并不总是这样，对吧？

paras.en: That’s right.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: We should avoid trying to take on too much work and constantly staying late just to show that you are committed.
paras.zh: 我们应该避免揽太多活，也别总是加班到很晚，就为了表现自己很投入。

w.m: adj. 投入的；尽心尽力的

paras.en: I see.
paras.zh: 我明白了。

paras.en: So setting expectations too high at the beginning can make us look bad if we don’t maintain them.
paras.zh: 所以说，一开始就把别人的期望定得太高，以后要是保持不住，反而会显得我们很差劲。

paras.en: Yeah, it’s better to make sure you are putting in quality time instead of just a large quantity of time, and these efforts can easily be demonstrated by the results we achieve.
paras.zh: 对，最好确保你投入的是有质量的时间，而不只是大量的时间，这些努力很容易通过我们取得的成果体现出来。

paras.en: What about helping others at work?
paras.zh: 那在工作中帮助别人呢？

paras.en: Should you try and go beyond your normal responsibilities and offer to help people with their projects?
paras.zh: 应不应该做些分外的事，主动帮别人做他们的项目？

paras.en: Extend your assistance to those who need it, but only as long as your own work will not go unattended.
paras.zh: 谁需要帮忙就帮一把，但前提是你自己的工作不能没人管。

w.m: adj. 无人照看的；没人管的

paras.en: If someone can benefit from your assistance or advice, help them out to gain their respect and trust.
paras.zh: 如果有人能从你的帮助或建议中受益，就帮帮他们，这样能赢得他们的尊重和信任。

paras.en: But it goes without saying that you shouldn’t act like a know-it-all; otherwise, you’ll appear arrogant.
paras.zh: 不过不用说，你可别摆出一副什么都懂的样子，不然就会显得很傲慢。

w.m: n. 自以为无所不知的人

paras.en: Absolutely, be humble, and you’ll get a lot of time later on to show your genius.
paras.zh: 完全同意，要谦虚，以后有的是时间展示你的才华。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What are the speakers mainly talking about?
paras.zh: 第一题：说话人主要在谈论什么？

paras.en: Question two: What does the woman say is one mistake people make?
paras.zh: 第二题：女士说人们常犯的一个错误是什么？

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman advise people to do in their work?
paras.zh: 第三题：女士建议人们在工作中怎么做？

paras.en: Question four: Why does the man say one should not act like a know-it-all?
paras.zh: 第四题：男士为什么说不应该摆出一副什么都懂的样子？

w.m: n. 自以为无所不知的人

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: I think we first need to decide how to divide up the presentation responsibilities.
paras.zh: 我觉得我们首先得决定怎样分配展示的任务。

paras.en: From what I recall, the presentation consists of five parts, not including the introduction and conclusion.
paras.zh: 我记得展示一共分五个部分，不算开头和结尾。

paras.en: That would mean altogether we need to allocate seven parts between the two of us.
paras.zh: 也就是说，我们两个人一共要分七个部分。

paras.en: So we have the abstract, background research, the project design, the results, and the discussion portions.
paras.zh: 所以有摘要、背景研究、项目设计、结果和讨论这几部分。

paras.en: As the abstract section only applies to the article, we needn’t include it in the presentation.
paras.zh: 摘要部分只用在论文里，展示时就不用讲了。

paras.en: How would you suggest we dole out the rest?
paras.zh: 你说剩下的怎么分？

paras.en: How do you feel about handling the background bit?
paras.zh: 背景部分你来讲怎么样？

paras.en: In this way, we can both discuss the part of the project that we devoted most of our time to.
paras.zh: 这样，我们俩都能讲自己在项目里花时间最多的那部分。

paras.en: Hold on a minute.
paras.zh: 等一下。

paras.en: You want me, the one who did the bulk of the task, to also do the majority of the presentation.
paras.zh: 活大部分是我干的，你还要我把展示的大头也包了？

paras.en: The background research, which was so meticulous, took more than a month.
paras.zh: 背景研究做得那么细，花了一个多月。

w.m: adj. 一丝不苟的；细致的

paras.en: Okay, okay, I get it.
paras.zh: 好了，好了，我明白了。

paras.en: Quit your moaning.
paras.zh: 别再发牢骚了。

paras.en: I appreciate the rigorous work ethic you applied to the research, but not the sarcasm that comes up every time I mention it.
paras.zh: 你做研究时那种严谨的工作态度我很欣赏，可我一提起这件事你就冷嘲热讽，这我可不欣赏。

paras.en: What do you think would be a fair arrangement?
paras.zh: 你觉得怎么分才公平？

paras.en: I think the best arrangement would be to split the research into two parts: before 1980 and afterward.
paras.zh: 我觉得最好的办法是把研究分成两部分：1980年以前和1980年以后。

paras.en: I will take the before portion, and you would be assigned the after 1980, leaving the project and results.
paras.zh: 我讲1980年以前的部分，1980年以后的分给你，剩下项目和结果两部分。

paras.en: I volunteered to describe the project, but as I struggled a bit with the statistics in the results section, how about you handling that?
paras.zh: 我主动要讲项目，可结果部分的统计数据我有点吃力，那部分你来讲怎么样？

paras.en: That’s agreeable to me.
paras.zh: 我同意。

w.m: adj. 可以接受的；同意的

paras.en: I propose we both handle the discussion section in parts, along with the question and answer afterward, leaving only the introduction and conclusion.
paras.zh: 我提议，讨论部分我们俩一人讲一段，之后的问答环节也一样，这样就只剩开头和结尾了。

paras.en: I will take responsibility for the conclusion and put you in charge of the introduction.
paras.zh: 结尾我来负责，开头交给你。

paras.en: This will make it so that we alternate presenting, so as to avoid sounding monotonous to the audience.
paras.zh: 这样我们就能轮流讲，免得观众听着觉得单调。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What does the woman say they first need to do?
paras.zh: 第五题：女士说他们首先需要做什么？

paras.en: Question six: Why does the man refuse to handle the background part?
paras.zh: 第六题：男士为什么拒绝负责背景部分？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the woman urge the man to stop doing?
paras.zh: 第七题：女士催促男士不要再做什么？

paras.en: Question eight: Why does the man suggest he present the conclusion and the woman do the introduction?
paras.zh: 第八题：男士为什么提议由他讲结尾、女士讲开头？

paras.en: Section B: Directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one: Makeup can do more than just change your appearance; it can also alter others’ perceptions of you, for better or for worse.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文：化妆不只能改变你的外表，还能改变别人对你的看法，可能变好，也可能变坏。

paras.en: According to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland, although both men and women perceive women who wear makeup as being of a higher status, men associate makeup with prestigious positive qualities, while women view other women wearing makeup as being dominant and a potential threat.
paras.zh: 苏格兰斯特灵大学的一项新研究发现，虽然男性和女性都认为化妆的女性地位更高，但男性把化妆和有威望这类积极特质联系在一起，女性则觉得化了妆的其他女性很强势，是潜在的威胁。

w.m: adj. 有威望的；有声望的
adj. 强势的；占支配地位的

paras.en: The research showed that men and women both rated the faces with cosmetics as being more attractive, but only women rated made-up faces as being more dominant, while only men rated made-up faces as being higher in prestige.
paras.zh: 研究显示，男性和女性都认为化了妆的面孔更有吸引力，但只有女性认为化了妆的面孔更强势，也只有男性认为化了妆的面孔更有威望。

w.m: adj. 强势的；占支配地位的

paras.en: A follow-up study investigated the root cause behind these differences in perception, and found that female-on-female jealousy seemed to be the main cause for the differences in perception.
paras.zh: 一项后续研究调查了这些看法差异背后的根本原因，发现女性对女性的嫉妒似乎是造成看法差异的主要原因。

paras.en: Women rating women with makeup said they would be more jealous of them and thought they would be more attractive to men than their non-makeup-wearing counterparts.
paras.zh: 给化妆女性打分的女性说，她们会更嫉妒这些女性，并且认为比起不化妆的女性，她们对男性更有吸引力。

paras.en: Cosmetic products are good for more than just giving you a pretty face, it can be particularly useful for women to understand how wearing makeup alters others’ perceptions of them in situations where they are trying to gain others’ trust and admiration.
paras.zh: 化妆品的用处不只是让你变漂亮；在想要赢得别人的信任和钦佩的场合，女性了解化妆会怎样改变别人对自己的看法，会特别有用。

paras.en: At a job interview, knowing whether the hiring committee will consist of men or women might influence a female candidate’s decision about wearing makeup.
paras.zh: 在求职面试中，知道招聘委员会由男性还是女性组成，可能会影响女性求职者化不化妆的决定。

paras.en: Whether the interviewers will view her as attractive, dominant, and prestigious can affect the interviewer’s actions and perhaps the outcome of the interview itself.
paras.zh: 面试官会不会觉得她有吸引力、强势、有威望，会影响面试官的做法，或许还会影响面试本身的结果。

w.m: adj. 强势的；占支配地位的
adj. 有威望的；有声望的

paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What can makeup do according to new research from the University of Stirling in Scotland?
paras.zh: 第九题：根据苏格兰斯特灵大学的新研究，化妆能起到什么作用？

paras.en: Question 10: How did both men and women rate the faces with cosmetics in the new research?
paras.zh: 第十题：在这项新研究中，男性和女性都怎样评价化了妆的面孔？

paras.zh: 第十一题：女性求职者为什么需要知道招聘委员会成员的性别？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: You may have seen advertisements trumpeting methods of changing a habit that require absolutely no willpower whatsoever.
paras.zh: 你可能见过一些广告，大肆宣扬改掉习惯的方法，说完全不需要任何意志力。

paras.en: But can you really change a bad habit or create a good one without willpower?
paras.zh: 可不靠意志力，你真的能改掉坏习惯、养成好习惯吗？

paras.en: To answer this question, we first have to ask, what is willpower?
paras.zh: 要回答这个问题，我们首先得问：什么是意志力？

paras.en: Most people, sadly, think of it only as the ability to clench their teeth and resist attractive temptations.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，大多数人只把它看作咬紧牙关、抵挡诱惑的能力。

paras.en: In this view, willpower means self-denial and no fun.
paras.zh: 照这种看法，意志力就意味着克制自己、毫无乐趣。

paras.en: No wonder people hope to make changes without it.
paras.zh: 难怪人们希望不靠它就能做出改变。

paras.en: I define willpower as using only the thought of your motivators to control your actions.
paras.zh: 我对意志力的定义是：只用想着自己的动力，来控制自己的行为。

paras.en: Let’s say your motivators are prevent diabetes and reach a healthy weight.
paras.zh: 比方说，你的动力是预防糖尿病、减到健康体重。

paras.en: So, if you are at the all-you-can-eat buffet, you think about your motivator, avoid diabetes through weight loss, and you take small portions and avoid the dessert table.
paras.zh: 那么，如果你在吃自助餐，你就想想自己的动力：通过减肥来避免得糖尿病，于是你每样只拿一点，也不去甜点台。

paras.en: So, amazingly enough, willpower begins with a thought, a bright idea, some way to improve your life or contribute to others.
paras.zh: 所以，说来也奇妙，意志力是从一个念头开始的：一个好主意，一种改善自己生活或者为别人做贡献的办法。

paras.en: This bright idea is your motivator.
paras.zh: 这个好主意就是你的动力。

paras.en: Dr. Walter Mitchell, an expert on willpower skills, uses the expressive term, a burning goal.
paras.zh: 意志力技巧专家沃尔特·米切尔博士用了一个很有表现力的说法：燃烧的目标。

w.m: adj. 有表现力的；富于表情的

paras.en: Whether you call it a motivator, a burning goal, or a bright idea, this idea is the force behind your willpower.
paras.zh: 不管你叫它动力、燃烧的目标还是好主意，这个想法都是你意志力背后的力量。

paras.en: What sort of bright ideas motivators make for effective willpower?
paras.zh: 什么样的好主意，也就是动力，才能造就有效的意志力呢？

paras.en: In fact, any goal that you value strongly counts.
paras.zh: 其实，任何你非常看重的目标都算。

paras.en: The list may include good health, self-respect, a better future for your family, personal mission, and being a role model for your child.
paras.zh: 这份清单可以包括身体健康、自尊、家人更好的未来、个人使命，以及给孩子做个好榜样。

paras.en: All these can certainly drive a positive change.
paras.zh: 这些都肯定能推动积极的改变。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What methods do some advertisements trumpet about changing a habit?
paras.zh: 第十二题：一些广告在改掉习惯这方面大肆宣扬什么方法？

paras.en: Question 13: What does the speaker define willpower as?
paras.zh: 第十三题：说话人把意志力定义为什么？

paras.en: Question 14: What may sound amazing enough as regards willpower?
paras.zh: 第十四题：关于意志力，什么听起来可能挺奇妙的？

paras.en: Question 15: What does the speaker say may make for effective willpower?
paras.zh: 第十五题：说话人说什么能造就有效的意志力？

paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: For many pregnant women, understanding what seafood is safe and healthy, and what should be avoided because of mercury concerns comes with a lot of worrying.
paras.zh: 对许多孕妇来说，弄清楚哪些海鲜安全又健康、哪些因为担心汞含量而不该吃，是件很让人操心的事。

paras.en: In part, that’s because the federal government’s advice on the matter, first issued in 2004, has long been criticized as vague.
paras.zh: 部分原因是，联邦政府在这方面的建议2004年首次发布，一直被批评含糊不清。

paras.en: That guidance has included advice on how much seafood to eat, and which species pregnant and breastfeeding women should avoid over concerns about mercury contamination.
paras.zh: 这份指导意见包括了该吃多少海鲜，以及孕妇和哺乳期妇女因为担心汞污染应该避开哪些种类。

paras.en: But critics say the government advisory has done more harm than good, scaring many pregnant and breastfeeding women away from eating seafood altogether.
paras.zh: 但批评者说，政府的这份建议弊大于利，把许多孕妇和哺乳期妇女吓得干脆不吃海鲜了。

paras.en: The problem is real, according to a spokesman for the Food and Drug Administration, or FDA for short.
paras.zh: 据美国食品药品监督管理局（简称FDA）的一位发言人说，这个问题确实存在。

paras.en: The agency analyzed fish consumption data from more than 1,000 pregnant women in the U.S. and found that 21% of them ate no fish whatsoever in the previous month, and those who did eat fish consumed far less than recommended by the dietary guidelines.
paras.zh: 该机构分析了美国1000多名孕妇吃鱼的数据，发现其中21%的人上个月一条鱼都没吃，而吃了鱼的人吃得也远少于膳食指南推荐的量。

paras.en: Some 50% ate less than two ounces a week, and 75% ate less than four ounces.
paras.zh: 大约50%的人每周吃不到2盎司，75%的人吃不到4盎司。

paras.en: This week, the FDA issued an update to the advice, listing more than 60 species in a chart that ranks fish as a best choice, good choice, and choices to avoid.
paras.zh: 本周，FDA发布了更新后的建议，在一张图表中列出了60多种鱼，把鱼分为最佳选择、良好选择和应避免的选择三类。

paras.en: The goal is to make it easier for mothers to be to feel confident about the type of seafood they include in their diets.
paras.zh: 目的是让准妈妈们对自己吃的海鲜种类更放心。

paras.en: The new advice recommends consumers choose a variety of fish to eat, and it comes with an easy-to-understand illustration of what an appropriate portion size should be: four ounces for an adult, and two ounces for children aged four to seven.
paras.zh: 新建议提倡消费者吃多种多样的鱼，还附了一张简单易懂的示意图，说明一份的合适分量：成人4盎司，4到7岁的儿童2盎司。

paras.en: And while expectant mothers have long been warned to stay away from shark and four other particular types of fish from the Gulf of Mexico, now there are three new species on the list of what to avoid, but not everyone is thrilled with the new advice.
paras.zh: 一直以来，准妈妈们都被警告不要吃鲨鱼和另外四种来自墨西哥湾的特定鱼类；而现在，应避免的鱼类名单上又多了三种，但并不是所有人都对新建议感到满意。

w.m: adj. 非常高兴的；兴奋的

paras.en: Critics say the new advice doesn’t always agree with the agency’s own scientific findings.
paras.zh: 批评者说，新建议和该机构自己的科学研究结果并不总是一致的。

paras.en: While mercury is of great concern when people are talking about pregnant women and seafood, it’s not the only factor contributing to anxiety.
paras.zh: 虽然人们谈起孕妇和海鲜时最担心的是汞，但它并不是引起焦虑的唯一因素。

paras.en: The FDA maintains that its final consumption recommendations were based on thorough scientific analysis.
paras.zh: FDA坚称，它最终的食用建议是基于全面的科学分析。

paras.en: Agency spokesman Cassell says the FDA believes the recommendations will increase confidence, not uncertainty.
paras.zh: 该机构发言人卡斯尔说，FDA相信这些建议会增强大家的信心，而不是带来更多不确定。

paras.en: But critics disagree.
paras.zh: 但批评者并不认同。

paras.en: They think the FDA’s advice is not based on the evidence in its own detailed report, and so it confuses everyone.
paras.zh: 他们认为，FDA的建议并不是基于它自己那份详细报告里的证据，所以让每个人都很困惑。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say about the federal government’s advice on seafood safety?
paras.zh: 第十六题：关于联邦政府在海鲜安全方面的建议，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 17: What did the Food and Drug Administration do this week?
paras.zh: 第十七题：美国食品药品监督管理局本周做了什么？

paras.en: Question 18: According to the speaker, what are people concerned about regarding pregnant women and seafood?
paras.zh: 第十八题：据说话人所说，谈到孕妇和海鲜，人们担心什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: know you’re busy with work, but you also need to take some time off to recharge those batteries.
paras.zh: 我知道你工作忙，但你也得抽时间休个假，好好充充电。

paras.en: So, should you plan one big vacation for the year, or should you take multiple short vacations throughout?
paras.zh: 那么，一年里是该计划一次长假，还是全年分几次短假呢？

paras.en: Quantity can sometimes beat quality.
paras.zh: 有时候数量能胜过质量。

paras.en: First and foremost, regardless of how you use your vacation days, you need to be using them and soon.
paras.zh: 首先，也是最重要的，不管你怎么用自己的假期，你都得用起来，而且要尽快。

paras.en: The longer you put off your time off, the worse you’re making things for yourself.
paras.zh: 休假拖得越久，你就把自己的处境弄得越糟。

paras.en: One 9-year-long study published in Psychosomatic Medicine suggests not taking at least one vacation a year may increase your risk of mortality due to heart disease.
paras.zh: 一项发表在《身心医学》上、为期9年的研究表明，一年连一次假都不休，可能会增加死于心脏病的风险。

paras.en: So, not only are you killing your joy, you’re possibly killing yourself.
paras.zh: 所以，你不光是在扼杀自己的快乐，还可能是在要自己的命。

paras.en: Give yourself a break, folks.
paras.zh: 伙计们，给自己放个假吧。

w.m: 给自己放个假；休息一下

paras.en: When you should take those breaks, however, depends on a few factors: how many days you have available to use, what activities bring you joy, whether you have a family or not, and other variables come into play.
paras.zh: 不过，什么时候休假，要看几个因素：你有多少天假可以用，什么活动能让你开心，你有没有家庭，还有其他一些变量也会起作用。

paras.en: Because of that, there’s no perfect formula that works for everyone, but there are still a few things everyone can try to shoot for.
paras.zh: 正因为这样，没有一个对每个人都适用的完美公式，但还是有几件事是每个人都可以努力争取的。

paras.en: We know that in terms of maximizing relaxation, you should aim for vacations that range somewhere between seven and 11 days long.
paras.zh: 我们知道，要想最大限度地放松，每次休假最好在七到十一天之间。

paras.en: That gives you enough time to let go of your stress at work, completely loosen up, and achieve full-on calm.
paras.zh: 这样你才有足够的时间放下工作压力，彻底放松，达到完全平静的状态。

paras.en: That above-mentioned study also recommends you space out your vacations evenly instead of using up all of your days at once.
paras.zh: 上面提到的那项研究还建议，要把假期均匀地分开，而不是一次把假全用完。

paras.en: Eight days might sound like a lot for someone who only gets 10 days of vacation a year, but if you frame them with weekends, you can manage two evenly spaced 8-day vacations a year.
paras.zh: 对一年只有10天假的人来说，8天听起来好像很多，但如果你把周末连上，一年就能休两次间隔均匀的8天假。

w.m: v. 给……加框；把……衔接在两头

paras.en: If you have 14 days of paid leave, that’s almost three separate 8-day vacations you can use to split your year into thirds.
paras.zh: 如果你有14天带薪假，差不多就能休三次各8天的假，把一年分成三段。

paras.en: As tempting as it might be to use all your days to take one long summer break, your overall goal should be to achieve the perfect balance between length plus joy and frequency.
paras.zh: 虽然把所有假期都用来休一个长长的暑假很诱人，但你的总体目标应该是在时长加乐趣和休假频率之间找到完美的平衡。

paras.en: Vacation frequency is important because planning multiple breaks throughout the year means you always have something to look forward to planning things and the anticipation that comes with it tends to make us happier.
paras.zh: 休假频率很重要，因为全年安排多次休假，意味着你总有盼头；而计划的过程和随之而来的期待，往往会让我们更开心。

paras.en: If you only take one long vacation every year, the excitement builds much more slowly and seems so far off that it can actually lead to feelings of despair.
paras.zh: 如果你每年只休一次长假，兴奋感积累得要慢得多，假期又显得那么遥远，结果可能真的会让人感到绝望。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What does the speaker say about people not taking any vacation?
paras.zh: 第十九题：对于根本不休假的人，说话人说了什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What does the 9-year study recommend people do when planning vacations?
paras.zh: 第二十题：那项为期9年的研究建议人们在计划休假时怎么做？

paras.en: Question 21: Why is vacation frequency important, according to the speaker?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：据说话人所说，休假频率为什么很重要？

paras.en: Recording 3.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Autonomous cars that can take over from drivers if they are tired or caught in the heat of an argument are being developed in Sweden.
paras.zh: 瑞典正在研发一种自动驾驶汽车，司机疲劳或者跟人吵得正凶时，它能替司机接管驾驶。

paras.en: Researchers working as part of the European Union’s 77 billion euro research program are developing sensor-based systems that monitor whether a driver is distracted, anxious, or tired.
paras.zh: 参与欧盟770亿欧元研究计划的研究人员，正在开发基于传感器的系统，监测司机是不是分心、焦虑或疲劳。

paras.en: If a driver is not in a fit state to be on the road, the car automatically takes control of the wheel to prevent accidents.
paras.zh: 如果司机的状态不适合上路，汽车就会自动接过方向盘，防止发生事故。

paras.en: Dr. Anna Anund from the Swedish National Road and Transport Research Institute, who is leading the project, said a driver’s state can be measured using a number of sensors, including heart rate monitors and eye sensors, which track where a driver’s gaze is.
paras.zh: 负责这个项目的是瑞典国家道路与交通研究所的安娜·阿努德博士，她说，司机的状态可以用许多传感器来测量，包括心率监测器和追踪司机视线的眼部传感器。

paras.en: She said the aim was to really make sure that the transition from the driver to the vehicle is done in a safe way, so we can take into consideration the driver’s state, and so we do not give control to a driver who is under pressure of fatigue, stress, anxiety, and so on.
paras.zh: 她说，目标是确保从司机到车辆的交接安全完成，这样我们就能考虑到司机的状态，不会把控制权交给一个正承受疲劳、压力、焦虑等负担的司机。

paras.en: According to data from the European Commission, Sweden has the safest roads in the EU, with the UK a close second.
paras.zh: 欧盟委员会的数据显示，瑞典的道路是欧盟最安全的，英国紧随其后。

paras.en: However, the number of road accidents in both has largely leveled out since 2010.
paras.zh: 不过，自2010年以来，这两个国家的道路交通事故数量基本持平。

paras.en: Driver fatigue is thought to be responsible for as many as a fifth of road crashes across the EU, although there are certain times of the day when more accidents happen.
paras.zh: 在整个欧盟，多达五分之一的交通事故被认为是司机疲劳造成的，不过一天中有些时段事故会更多。

paras.en: At 6 a.m., for example, drivers are said to be 20 times more likely to have an accident than at 10 a.m. While most experts agree driverless technology should help bring down accident numbers in the long term, some have questioned whether it is safe.
paras.zh: 比如，据说早上6点司机出事故的可能性是上午10点的20倍。虽然大多数专家都认为，从长远来看，无人驾驶技术应该有助于减少事故数量，但也有人质疑它是否安全。

paras.en: The researchers have said the technology they are developing is seeking to bridge the gap between level three on the autonomy scale, in which drivers have to be ready to take control of the car at any point, and level four, in which driving is automated.
paras.zh: 研究人员说，他们正在研发的技术，要在自动化等级的第三级和第四级之间架起桥梁：第三级要求司机随时准备接管汽车，第四级则是完全自动驾驶。

paras.en: Daniel Ruiz, the chief executive of the UK’s connected and autonomous vehicle program Meridian, said, “There is a strong debate going on about how it is possible to make a level three car completely safe.”.
paras.zh: 英国网联与自动驾驶汽车项目“子午线”的首席执行官丹尼尔·鲁伊斯说：“关于怎样才能让一辆三级汽车做到绝对安全，人们正在激烈地争论。”

paras.en: Despite advances in technology, we still have some way to go in shifting public sentiment.
paras.zh: 尽管技术进步了，但要扭转公众的看法，我们还有一段路要走。

paras.en: With an increase in attention-grabbing accidents recently, drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to.
paras.zh: 由于最近引人注目的事故越来越多，司机们现在觉得自动驾驶汽车没有以前安全了。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What are researchers doing in Sweden?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：研究人员正在瑞典做什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What did the researchers’ project aim to do, according to Dr. Anna Anund?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：据安娜·阿努德博士所说，研究人员的项目目的是什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What is thought to be responsible for a fifth of road accidents across the European Union?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：在整个欧盟，五分之一的交通事故被认为是什么造成的？

paras.en: Question 25: Why do drivers now view self-driving cars as less safe than they used to?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：司机们现在为什么觉得自动驾驶汽车没有以前安全了？

paras.en: That’s the end of listening comprehension.
paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
