passages.name: 2026年6月大学英语六级 第2套 Part II Listening
passages.title: 听力原文精读
passages.genre: 长对话 · 短文 · 讲座
passages.summary: 第一段长对话里，弗兰克想趁结婚十周年订一趟巴塞罗那之旅，却找不到合适又不贵的住处，同事建议他先住两晚高档酒店、再去海边便宜的地方。第二段长对话里，两位药剂师聊起日常工作：苏珊娜帮一位病人避开了药物相互作用，保罗在做一个面向慢性病患者的用药管理项目。第一篇短文介绍斯坦福大学的研究：热情对成绩的推动作用在个人主义文化中更明显，在集体主义文化中则较弱。第二篇短文解释自然界为什么会出现图案，并以窗上冰晶为例说明分子层面的过程如何形成大尺度图案。第一段录音讲怎样养成新习惯：制订具体计划，并且一次只专注于一件事。第二段录音介绍一项研究：冥王星大气中的雾霾散射阳光，可能是它大气温度低的原因。第三段录音讲八到十岁是父母影响孩子音乐品味的关键时期，以及父母该怎样引导。

paras.en: College English Test Band Six, Part Two, Listening Comprehension, Section A, Directions.
paras.zh: 大学英语六级考试，第二部分，听力理解，A节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two long conversations.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。

paras.en: At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions.
paras.zh: 每段对话结束时，你会听到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 对话和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Conversation one.
paras.zh: 第一段对话。

paras.en: Hi Frank, are you working through your lunch hour again?
paras.zh: 嗨，弗兰克，你又不吃午饭在干活啊？

paras.en: No, not at all.
paras.zh: 没有，根本不是。

paras.en: It’s my tenth wedding anniversary next week, and I promised Jane that I would book a city break for us, as I have annual leave to take, and it would be nice to celebrate somewhere warm.
paras.zh: 下周是我们结婚十周年纪念日，我答应了简，要订一趟城市短途游，因为我有年假要休，找个暖和的地方庆祝一下也挺好的。

paras.en: So I’m trying to book something in Barcelona.
paras.zh: 所以我正想在巴塞罗那订个地方。

paras.en: That sounds so romantic.
paras.zh: 听起来真浪漫。

paras.en: I adore Barcelona.
paras.zh: 我特别喜欢巴塞罗那。

paras.en: It’s such a fabulous cosmopolitan city.
paras.zh: 那可真是一座很棒的国际化都市。

w.m: adj. 国际化的；世界性的

paras.en: There’s so much to do there.
paras.zh: 那儿能玩的东西太多了。

paras.en: Excellent food and that cathedral that they are still building after about 150 years.
paras.zh: 吃的特别好，还有那座盖了大约150年还没完工的大教堂。

paras.en: Very cool.
paras.zh: 特别酷。

paras.en: I know, but the anniversary is looming, and I’m still scrambling to find accommodation.
paras.zh: 我知道，可纪念日马上就到了，我还在手忙脚乱地找住处。

paras.en: Everything is either wildly expensive or already fully booked.
paras.zh: 要么贵得离谱，要么早就订满了。

paras.en: I’m starting to feel a bit frantic.
paras.zh: 我开始有点急了。

w.m: adj. 心急如焚的；慌乱的

paras.en: Well, if you are going for a whole week, why don’t you do a couple of nights in somewhere really glamorous, and then do the rest of the week a bit further up the coast, where the accommodation is cheaper, and that will offset the cost of the expensive place.
paras.zh: 嗯，要是你们去一整个星期，为什么不在特别高档的地方住上两晚，剩下几天就沿着海岸往北走远一点，那边住宿便宜，正好能把贵的那家的开销抵掉。

w.m: adj. 富有魅力的；奢华的

paras.en: That might be a good plan.
paras.zh: 这个办法可能不错。

paras.en: It’s not too expensive to rent a car, so we could still drive into the city.
paras.zh: 租车也不算太贵，所以我们还是可以开车进城。

paras.en: Yes, there are lots of places outside the city that have pools and are all inclusive, so we wouldn’t even need to pay for food or drinks.
paras.zh: 对，城外有很多地方都带泳池，而且全包，我们连吃的喝的都不用另外付钱。

paras.en: I’ll send a query now about the dates we’re interested in.
paras.zh: 我现在就去问问我们想去的那几天。

paras.en: That sounds perfect.
paras.zh: 听起来很完美。

paras.en: I’m sure that Jane will be absolutely thrilled to bits.
paras.zh: 我敢肯定简一定会乐开花的。

paras.en: I really do recommend visiting that cathedral.
paras.zh: 我真心推荐你们去看看那座大教堂。

paras.en: You can go all the way up to the top of it, but you need to go up a really steep spiral staircase to get there.
paras.zh: 可以一直爬到顶上，不过得爬一段特别陡的旋转楼梯才能上去。

paras.en: Considering Jane is terrified of heights, I think if I tried to make her do that, I would come back divorced.
paras.zh: 简可是恐高的，我要是硬让她爬，回来恐怕就得离婚了。

paras.en: Thanks for the help, though it was turning into a logistical nightmare.
paras.zh: 谢谢你帮忙，这事都快成安排上的噩梦了。

paras.en: Questions one to four are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第一到第四题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question one: What is the man planning to do?
paras.zh: 第一题：这位男士打算做什么？

paras.en: Question two: Why is the man starting to feel a bit frantic?
paras.zh: 第二题：这位男士为什么开始有点急了？

w.m: adj. 心急如焚的；慌乱的

paras.en: Question three: What does the woman suggest the man do?
paras.zh: 第三题：女士建议男士做什么？

paras.en: Question four: What does the man say about his wife, Jane?
paras.zh: 第四题：关于他的妻子简，男士说了什么？

paras.en: Conversation two.
paras.zh: 第二段对话。

paras.en: Hey there, Paul.
paras.zh: 嘿，保罗。

paras.en: How’s it going?
paras.zh: 最近怎么样？

paras.en: Hi, Suzanne.
paras.zh: 嗨，苏珊娜。

paras.en: Just keeping busy with the usual stuff: filling prescriptions, talking to patients about their medications, that kind of thing.
paras.zh: 还是忙那些老一套：按处方配药，跟病人讲讲他们吃的药，就这些事。

paras.en: How about you?
paras.zh: 你呢？

paras.en: Same here.
paras.zh: 我也一样。

paras.en: Although I did have an interesting case come in this morning.
paras.zh: 不过今天上午倒是来了个挺有意思的病例。

paras.en: A patient came in inquiring about a medication that had a potential interaction with another medication she was already taking.
paras.zh: 有位病人来问一种药，这种药跟她正在吃的另一种药可能会相互作用。

paras.en: Oh, that’s always tricky.
paras.zh: 哦，这种情况总是挺棘手的。

paras.en: What did you do?
paras.zh: 你是怎么处理的？

paras.en: I explained the issue to her as best I could, and recommended she double check with her doctor.
paras.zh: 我尽量把问题给她讲清楚，然后建议她再跟医生确认一下。

paras.en: And you know what?
paras.zh: 你猜怎么着？

paras.en: She actually followed my advice, and the doctor ended up switching the patient’s medication.
paras.zh: 她还真听了我的建议，后来医生就给她换了药。

paras.en: Ah, that’s great!
paras.zh: 啊，太好了！

paras.en: You must feel quite accomplished.
paras.zh: 你一定很有成就感吧。

w.m: adj. 有成就感的；有造诣的

paras.en: Totally, these moments are the highlights of my routine work, employing my pharmaceutical expertise to the benefit of people’s health and well-being.
paras.zh: 那当然，这样的时刻就是我日常工作里最高光的部分，用我的药学专业知识来造福大家的健康和幸福。

paras.en: I fully agree.
paras.zh: 我完全同意。

paras.en: Unfortunately, the opposite is true when the patient is too stubborn and they refuse to listen to us.
paras.zh: 可惜要是病人特别固执、不肯听我们的话，情况就正好相反了。

paras.en: So true.
paras.zh: 太对了。

paras.en: In other developments, we’ve had a lot of people coming in to get their flu shots, which is always good to see.
paras.zh: 还有一件事，最近有很多人来打流感疫苗，这总是让人高兴的。

paras.en: Good, good.
paras.zh: 好，好。

paras.en: I’ve been working on a new medication therapy management program for our patients with chronic conditions.
paras.zh: 我一直在给我们的慢性病患者做一个新的药物治疗管理项目。

paras.en: It helps patients manage their medications more effectively.
paras.zh: 它能帮病人更有效地管理用药。

paras.en: That sounds interesting.
paras.zh: 听起来很有意思。

paras.en: We review all of their medications and make sure that they’re taking them as prescribed.
paras.zh: 我们会把他们吃的药全部检查一遍，确保他们按医嘱服药。

paras.en: We also look for any potential drug interactions or side effects.
paras.zh: 我们还会排查有没有潜在的药物相互作用或副作用。

paras.en: Patient response has so far been very positive.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，病人的反响非常好。

paras.en: Some have reported seeing improvements in their health, which is really rewarding to see.
paras.zh: 有些病人说身体有了好转，看到这个真的很欣慰。

w.m: adj. 值得的；令人满足的

paras.en: That’s great to hear.
paras.zh: 听到这个真好。

paras.en: Do you use text message reminders?
paras.zh: 你们用短信提醒吗？

paras.en: Yes, absolutely.
paras.zh: 用，当然用。

paras.en: It’s a great idea.
paras.zh: 这主意很好。

paras.en: Medication non-adherence is a big problem, especially for older patients.
paras.zh: 不按医嘱服药是个大问题，尤其是老年病人。

w.m: n. 不遵从；（此处）不按医嘱服药

paras.en: We’re still in the early stages of the program, but I’m hopeful that it will make a real difference for our patients.
paras.zh: 我们这个项目还在起步阶段，但我很希望它能给病人带来实实在在的改变。

paras.en: Questions five to eight are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第五到第八题根据你刚才听到的对话提问。

paras.en: Question five: What do we learn about the speakers?
paras.zh: 第五题：关于这两位说话人，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question six: What does the woman say about an interesting case she had?
paras.zh: 第六题：关于她遇到的一个有意思的病例，女士说了什么？

paras.en: Question seven: What does the man say he has been working on?
paras.zh: 第七题：男士说他一直在忙什么？

paras.en: Question eight: What is a big problem, especially for older patients, according to the woman?
paras.zh: 第八题：据女士说，什么是一个大问题，尤其是对老年病人来说？

paras.en: Section B, directions.
paras.zh: B节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear two passages.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到两篇短文。

paras.en: At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions.
paras.zh: 每篇短文结束时，你会听到三到四个问题。

paras.en: Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once.
paras.zh: 短文和问题都只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Passage one.
paras.zh: 第一篇短文。

paras.en: In America, at least, passion is a word that often comes up on job descriptions and in interviews.
paras.zh: 至少在美国，“热情”是个常在招聘启事和面试中出现的词。

paras.en: On the whole, passionate people are thought of in a positive light and considered likely to achieve their goals, but when it comes to predicting achievement, has the importance of passion been overstated?
paras.zh: 总的来说，有热情的人给人的印象是正面的，被认为容易实现目标，可说到预测一个人能否有所成就，热情的重要性是不是被夸大了呢？

w.m: adj. 有热情的；热情洋溢的

paras.en: According to a new study from Stanford University, passion may be less important in certain cultures, and the fact that passion is often seen as a key to achievement may reflect a distinctly Western model of motivation.
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学的一项新研究表明，在某些文化中，热情可能没那么重要；而热情常被看作成功的关键，这可能反映出的是一种典型的西方动机模式。

paras.en: The chief factor explored in the study was how individualistic a society was.
paras.zh: 这项研究考察的主要因素，是一个社会的个人主义程度有多高。

paras.en: In individualistic cultures, the researchers assert, people are more motivated by pursuing paths related to their passions, but those in collectivistic cultures are more likely to see themselves as part of a network.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，在个人主义文化中，人们更多是因为追求与自己热情所在相关的道路而受到激励；但在集体主义文化中，人们更可能把自己看作某个关系网中的一员。

paras.en: They often place fulfilling obligations to others above focusing on their own interests.
paras.zh: 他们往往把履行对他人的义务看得比关注自身兴趣更重要。

paras.en: The researchers looked at data from nearly 60 countries.
paras.zh: 研究人员分析了将近60个国家的数据。

paras.en: They found that in science subjects, passion was positively correlated with academic achievements.
paras.zh: 他们发现，在理科科目中，热情与学业成绩呈正相关。

paras.en: Higher levels of enjoyment and interest also bolstered test scores, but the strength of this correlation wasn’t the same across cultures.
paras.zh: 更高的乐趣和兴趣也提高了考试成绩，但这种相关性的强弱在各个文化中并不一样。

paras.en: Those in individualistic societies such as the U.S., Australia, and the U.K. showed a stronger link between passion and achievement, the effect of passion on performance was more subtle for those in more collectivistic societies such as Colombia or Thailand.
paras.zh: 在美国、澳大利亚、英国这样的个人主义社会里，热情与成绩之间的联系更强；而在哥伦比亚、泰国这样集体主义色彩更浓的社会里，热情对成绩的影响就不那么明显。

paras.en: These findings were mirrored in achievement in both mathematics and reading.
paras.zh: 在数学和阅读成绩上，也得出了同样的结果。

paras.en: It’s clear from the findings that passion isn’t the only thing that motivates people to achieve their goals.
paras.zh: 从这些结果可以清楚地看出，热情并不是激励人们实现目标的唯一因素。

paras.en: Questions nine to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第九到第十一题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question nine: What are passionate people considered likely to do in America?
paras.zh: 第九题：在美国，有热情的人被认为可能会做到什么？

paras.en: Question 10: What does a new study from Stanford show about the importance of passion in predicting achievement?
paras.zh: 第十题：关于热情在预测成就方面的重要性，斯坦福大学的一项新研究说明了什么？

paras.en: Question 11: What did the researchers find about the effect of passion on academic achievement for those in more collectivistic societies?
paras.zh: 第十一题：对集体主义色彩更浓的社会里的人，研究人员发现热情对学业成绩有什么影响？

paras.en: Passage two.
paras.zh: 第二篇短文。

paras.en: Why does nature create patterns?
paras.zh: 大自然为什么会形成图案？

paras.en: The reason patterns often appear in nature is simple: the same basic physical or chemical processes occur in many patterned substances and organisms as they form.
paras.zh: 自然界常出现图案的原因很简单：许多带图案的物质和生物在形成时，都会经历同样的基本物理或化学过程。

paras.en: Whether in plants and animals or rocks, foams, and ice crystals, the intricate patterns that happen in nature come down to what’s happening at the level of atoms and molecules.
paras.zh: 无论是动植物，还是岩石、泡沫和冰晶，自然界中错综复杂的图案，归根结底都取决于原子和分子层面发生的事。

paras.en: A pattern in nature is any regularly repeated arrangement of shapes or colors.
paras.zh: 自然界中的图案，就是形状或颜色有规律地重复排列。

paras.en: Some of the most striking examples include the six-sided arrays of rocks at Giant’s Causeway in the United Kingdom, and the colorful stripes and spots on tropical fish.
paras.zh: 最引人注目的例子包括英国巨人之路上六边形排列的岩石，还有热带鱼身上色彩鲜艳的条纹和斑点。

w.m: adj. 引人注目的；显著的
巨人之路（英国北爱尔兰景点）

paras.en: Patterns like these begin to form at a small scale when materials undergo processes like drying, freezing, wrinkling, diffusing, and reacting.
paras.zh: 当材料经历干燥、冻结、起皱、扩散和反应这样的过程时，这类图案就开始在微小尺度上形成。

paras.en: Those changes then give rise to complex patterns at a larger scale that people can see.
paras.zh: 这些变化接着会在更大的尺度上形成人们看得见的复杂图案。

paras.en: Imagine delicate frozen crystals on a window during winter.
paras.zh: 想象一下冬天窗户上精致的冰晶。

paras.en: What creates that pattern?
paras.zh: 这种图案是怎么形成的？

paras.en: When water freezes, its molecules begin clustering together.
paras.zh: 水结冰时，水分子会开始聚集在一起。

paras.en: Water molecules have a particular bent shape that causes them to stack into clusters as they freeze.
paras.zh: 水分子有一种特别的弯曲形状，所以结冰时会层层堆叠成团。

paras.en: As the cluster grows, many outside factors, including humidity and temperature, begin to affect its overall shape.
paras.zh: 随着冰团变大，湿度、温度等许多外部因素就开始影响它的整体形状。

paras.en: If the water is freezing on a window, for example, random imperfections on the glass surface affect the stacking and create the larger pattern.
paras.zh: 比如说，如果水是在窗户上结冰，玻璃表面随机分布的瑕疵就会影响冰的堆叠，形成更大的图案。

paras.en: But scientists do not always know the purpose of a pattern, or even if there is one.
paras.zh: 不过科学家们并不总是知道一个图案有什么用，甚至不知道它到底有没有用。

paras.en: The molecular processes involved are simple enough that they might generate a pattern by coincidence.
paras.zh: 其中涉及的分子过程非常简单，可能只是巧合之下就形成了图案。

paras.en: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十二到第十五题根据你刚才听到的短文提问。

paras.en: Question 12: What does the passage say is a pattern in nature?
paras.zh: 第十二题：根据短文，什么是自然界中的图案？

paras.en: Question 13: What gives rise to complex patterns at a larger scale?
paras.zh: 第十三题：是什么在更大的尺度上形成了复杂的图案？

paras.en: Question 14: What does the example of frozen crystals on a window show?
paras.zh: 第十四题：窗户上冰晶的例子说明了什么？

paras.en: Question 15: What might molecular processes produce according to the passage?
paras.zh: 第十五题：根据短文，分子过程可能会产生什么？

paras.en: Section C, Directions.
paras.zh: C节，说明。

paras.en: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks, followed by three or four questions.
paras.zh: 在本节中，你将听到三段讲座或讲话的录音，每段后面有三到四个问题。

paras.en: The recordings will be played only once.
paras.zh: 录音只播放一遍。

paras.en: After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C, and D.
paras.zh: 听到问题后，你必须从标有A、B、C、D的四个选项中选出最佳答案。

paras.en: Then, mark the corresponding letter on answer sheet one with a single line through the center.
paras.zh: 然后在答题卡一上找到相应的字母，在它中间划一条横线。

paras.en: Recording one.
paras.zh: 第一段录音。

paras.en: Many people, myself included, have multiple areas of life they would like to improve.
paras.zh: 很多人，包括我自己，生活中都有好几个方面想要改进。

paras.en: For example, I would like to reach more people with my writing, to lift heavier weights at the gym, and to start practicing mindfulness more consistently.
paras.zh: 比如说，我想让更多人读到我写的东西，想在健身房举起更重的重量，还想更坚持不懈地练习正念。

paras.en: Those are just a few of the goals I find desirable, and you probably have a long list yourself.
paras.zh: 这些只是我想实现的几个目标，你自己可能也有一长串。

w.m: adj. 值得拥有的；令人向往的

paras.en: The problem is, even if we are committed to working hard on our goals, our natural tendency is to return to our old habits at some point.
paras.zh: 问题是，即使我们下定决心为目标努力，人的天性总会让我们在某个时候回到老习惯上去。

paras.en: Making a permanent lifestyle change is really difficult.
paras.zh: 要永久地改变生活方式真的很难。

paras.en: Recently, I’ve come across a few studies that will make these difficult lifestyle changes a bit easier.
paras.zh: 最近我看到了几项研究，能让这些难以做到的生活方式改变变得稍微容易一点。

paras.en: As you’ll see, however, the approach to mastering many areas of life is somewhat counterintuitive.
paras.zh: 不过你会看到，掌握生活中多个方面的方法有点违反直觉。

paras.en: Research has shown that you are two to three times more likely to stick with your habits if you make a specific plan for when, where, and how you will perform the behavior.
paras.zh: 研究表明，如果你为何时、何地、如何去做某个行为制订具体计划，坚持习惯的可能性会高出两到三倍。

paras.en: For example, in one study, scientists asked people to fill out a sentence to specify during the next week they would do at least 20 minutes of vigorous exercise on which day, at what time of day, and at or in what place.
paras.zh: 比如，在一项研究中，科学家让人们填一个句子，具体写明下周哪一天、几点、在什么地方，至少做20分钟剧烈运动。

w.m: v. 明确说明；具体指定
adj. 剧烈的；充满活力的

paras.en: Researchers found that people who filled out this sentence were two to three times more likely to actually exercise compared to a control group who did not make plans for their future behavior.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，和没有为今后的行为制订计划的对照组相比，填了这个句子的人真正去锻炼的可能性要高两到三倍。

paras.en: Psychologists call these specific plans implementation intentions because they state when, where, and how you intend to implement a particular behavior.
paras.zh: 心理学家把这种具体计划称为“执行意图”，因为它们说明了你打算何时、何地、如何执行某个特定行为。

paras.en: However, follow-up research has discovered implementation intentions only work when you focus on one thing at a time.
paras.zh: 不过，后续研究发现，执行意图只有在你一次专注于一件事时才有效。

paras.en: In fact, researchers found that people who tried to accomplish multiple goals were less committed and less likely to succeed than those who focused on a single goal.
paras.zh: 事实上，研究人员发现，比起专注于一个目标的人，那些想同时实现多个目标的人决心更弱，也更不容易成功。

w.m: adj. 坚定的；尽心尽力的

paras.en: Another science-based reason to focus on one thing at a time is that when you begin practicing a new habit, it requires a lot of conscious effort to remember to do it.
paras.zh: 一次只专注于一件事，还有一个科学依据：当你开始培养一个新习惯时，要记得去做它，需要花很多有意识的努力。

paras.en: After a while, however, the pattern of behavior becomes easier.
paras.zh: 不过过了一段时间，这种行为模式就变得容易了。

w.m: 过了一会儿；一段时间后

paras.en: Eventually, your new habit becomes a normal routine, and the process is more or less mindless and automatic.
paras.zh: 最终，你的新习惯会变成平常的例行公事，整个过程或多或少就不用动脑、自动完成了。

paras.en: The most important thing to note is that there is some tipping point at which new habits become more or less automatic.
paras.zh: 最需要注意的一点是，存在某个临界点，过了这个点，新习惯就差不多变成自动的了。

paras.en: The time it takes to build a habit depends on many factors, including how difficult the habit is, your genetics, and more.
paras.zh: 养成一个习惯需要多长时间，取决于很多因素，包括这个习惯有多难、你的基因等等。

paras.en: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十六到第十八题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 16: What does the speaker say is really difficult?
paras.zh: 第十六题：说话人说什么事真的很难？

paras.en: Question 17: What did researchers find about people with implementation intentions?
paras.zh: 第十七题：对有执行意图的人，研究人员有什么发现？

paras.en: Question 18: According to the speaker, what is required of you when you begin practicing a new habit?
paras.zh: 第十八题：据说话人说，当你开始培养一个新习惯时，需要你做到什么？

paras.en: Recording two.
paras.zh: 第二段录音。

paras.en: It was a lazy, hazy, crazy day on the dwarf planet Pluto when New Horizons, a spacecraft from Earth, flew by at a speed of 31,000 miles per hour two years ago.
paras.zh: 两年前，地球发射的“新视野号”探测器以每小时31,000英里的速度飞掠矮行星冥王星，那天的冥王星慵懒、朦胧，又有点疯狂。

paras.en: The spacecraft took a bunch of photos, made some quick measurements of Pluto’s atmosphere, and sent them all back here, giving planetary scientists their first up close look of the distant dwarf planet.
paras.zh: 探测器拍了一大堆照片，对冥王星的大气层做了一些快速测量，然后把这些全都传回地球，让行星科学家第一次近距离看到了这颗遥远的矮行星。

paras.en: One of the more bizarre things they found was that the haze in Pluto’s atmosphere was much thicker than previously thought.
paras.zh: 他们发现的比较奇怪的现象之一，是冥王星大气中的雾霾比以前想象的要厚得多。

paras.en: The planet also had an atmosphere much cooler than earlier estimates, topping out at minus 333.4 degrees Fahrenheit.
paras.zh: 这颗行星的大气也比之前估计的冷得多，最高只有零下333.4华氏度。

paras.en: Now, a study published in Nature links those two atmospheric observations.
paras.zh: 现在，《自然》杂志上发表的一项研究把这两项大气观测结果联系了起来。

paras.en: A computer model developed by planetary scientist Xi Zhang and colleagues shows the haze of tiny droplets in the upper atmosphere is likely scattering light from the sun, preventing heat from reaching the planet below.
paras.zh: 行星科学家张曦和同事开发的一个计算机模型显示，高层大气中由微小液滴组成的雾霾很可能在散射太阳光，使热量无法到达下面的星球表面。

paras.en: We see hazy skies on Earth too, from time to time, whenever solid particles get suspended in the air, from water-based fogs to ash from fires to the toxic droplets that make up a thick smog, but on Earth the overall temperature of the planet is dominated by the distribution of gases in our atmosphere.
paras.zh: 地球上也时不时会出现雾蒙蒙的天空，只要有固体颗粒悬浮在空气中就会这样，从水汽形成的雾，到火灾产生的灰烬，再到组成浓重烟雾的有毒液滴，都是如此；但在地球上，整个星球的总体温度主要是由大气中气体的分布决定的。

paras.en: On Pluto, the authors suggest haze might be more influential.
paras.zh: 作者们认为，在冥王星上，雾霾的影响可能更大。

paras.en: Particles can reflect light from the sun here on Earth.
paras.zh: 在地球上，颗粒物也能反射太阳光。

paras.en: It happens after volcanoes erupt, emitting clouds of particles that reflect the sun’s rays into the atmosphere.
paras.zh: 火山喷发后就会出现这种情况，火山喷出的颗粒云会把太阳光反射到大气中。

paras.en: Some people even propose imitating this phenomenon to alleviate the effects of climate change.
paras.zh: 甚至有人提议模仿这种现象来缓解气候变化的影响。

paras.en: But our planet isn’t dominated by that process, or at least it hasn’t been for a few billion years.
paras.zh: 但我们的星球并不受这一过程主导，至少过去几十亿年来都没有受它主导。

paras.en: If Pluto’s atmosphere is very different from ours and from that of other nearby planets, it could help scientists expand their understanding of planetary atmospheres.
paras.zh: 如果冥王星的大气与我们的大气、与附近其他行星的大气都大不相同，那它就能帮助科学家拓展对行星大气的认识。

paras.en: But right now, this is just a good guess based on data from New Horizons and a sophisticated computer model, not direct observations of the haze’s composition.
paras.zh: 但现在，这还只是根据“新视野号”的数据和一个复杂的计算机模型做出的合理推测，并不是对雾霾成分的直接观测。

paras.en: There are other theories floating around to explain Pluto’s cool temperatures, including blaming the cold air on gases in the atmosphere.
paras.zh: 解释冥王星低温的理论还有好几种，其中一种把冷空气归因于大气中的气体。

paras.en: Luckily, the authors will get a chance to test their notions when the James Webb Space telescope launches later.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，等詹姆斯·韦布太空望远镜晚些时候发射以后，作者们就有机会检验自己的想法了。

paras.en: That observatory can detect different spectrums of light, which the hazy plutonian atmosphere would be positively glowing with as it scattered sunlight.
paras.zh: 这台天文台能探测到不同光谱的光，而冥王星雾蒙蒙的大气在散射太阳光时，正好会发出这种光。

paras.en: The researchers just have to wait and see if the light from the telescope validates their bright idea.
paras.zh: 研究人员只需要等着看望远镜接收到的光能不能证实他们这个绝妙的想法。

paras.en: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第十九到第二十一题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 19: What was one of the more bizarre findings about Pluto’s atmosphere?
paras.zh: 第十九题：关于冥王星的大气，比较奇怪的发现之一是什么？

paras.en: Question 20: What is said to determine the overall temperature on Earth?
paras.zh: 第二十题：据说是什么决定了地球的总体温度？

paras.en: Question 21: What does the speaker say the researchers have to wait and see?
paras.zh: 第二十一题：说话人说研究人员要等着看什么？

paras.en: Recording three.
paras.zh: 第三段录音。

paras.en: Parents have a small window where they can influence their eight to 10-year-old children’s music taste.
paras.zh: 父母影响孩子音乐品味的时间窗口很短，就在孩子八到十岁之间。

paras.en: Researchers have concluded, the 24-month time frame comes at an age when youngsters are old enough to appreciate poetic lyrics and snappy tunes, but have not yet started to be embarrassed by their mother and father’s preferences.
paras.zh: 研究人员得出结论，这24个月正好处在这样一个年龄段：孩子已经大到能欣赏有诗意的歌词和轻快的曲调，却还没开始觉得父母的喜好让人难为情。

paras.en: Dr. Hauke Egermann, a lecturer in music at the University of York, carried out a literature review into more than a dozen studies looking at parental musical influence.
paras.zh: 约克大学的音乐讲师豪克·埃格曼博士对十几项研究父母音乐影响的研究做了文献综述。

paras.en: Children have an openness to new music, and this means parents have an important role to play in developing the musical preferences of their kids,” he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“孩子对新音乐很开放，这就意味着父母在培养孩子的音乐喜好方面能起重要作用。”

paras.en: However, time is of the essence, as parental influence is most likely to be effective during the critical time period before age 10.
paras.zh: 不过，时间非常关键，因为父母的影响最可能在十岁以前这个关键时期起作用。

paras.en: During adolescence, children tend to gravitate away from their parents’ choices and are more influenced by their peers.
paras.zh: 到了青春期，孩子往往会疏远父母的选择，更多地受同龄人影响。

paras.en: A separate survey of 2,000 British parents by music streaming service Deezer also found that nearly four fifths of parents agreed that their children were far more receptive to their musical suggestions before the age of 10.
paras.zh: 音乐流媒体服务商Deezer对2,000名英国家长另做的一项调查也发现，近五分之四的家长认为，孩子在十岁以前对他们推荐的音乐接受度高得多。

paras.en: In contrast, just 10% of parents reported positive reactions from their teenage children when they shared their favourite music.
paras.zh: 相比之下，只有10%的家长说，他们和十几岁的孩子分享自己喜欢的音乐时，孩子反应积极。

w.m: adj. 十几岁的；青少年的

paras.en: Some 79% of fathers said they had tried to influence their children’s music, but just 69% of mothers.
paras.zh: 约79%的父亲说曾试着影响孩子的音乐喜好，而母亲只有69%。

paras.en: However, mothers were more effective, with 38% reporting that their kids loved the tunes they shared, compared to 30% of dads who, in some cases, said their children cried or even fell asleep.
paras.zh: 不过，母亲们更有效果，38%的母亲说孩子喜欢她们分享的歌曲，相比之下爸爸只有30%，有些爸爸还说孩子听哭了，甚至听睡着了。

paras.en: Dr. Egermann claims introducing children to a variety of musical styles is the key to fostering good taste in later life.
paras.zh: 埃格曼博士称，让孩子接触各种音乐风格，是培养他们日后良好品味的关键。

paras.en: By playing children a variety of genres before this critical period, research on familiarization suggests they will enjoy lots of different types of music as adults.
paras.zh: 关于熟悉化的研究表明，在这个关键时期之前给孩子播放各种类型的音乐，他们长大后就会喜欢很多不同类型的音乐。

paras.en: He added, the benefits of having a wider taste in music include the ability to manage their emotions more effectively, socialize and bond with others more easily, and to have a better understanding of other cultures as well.
paras.zh: 他还说，音乐品味更广的好处包括：能更有效地管理情绪，更容易与人交往、建立感情，还能更好地了解其他文化。

paras.en: Dr. Egermann advises parents not to push their favourite music too hard on their children, but instead play it as background music while a child is playing.
paras.zh: 埃格曼博士建议父母不要太强硬地把自己喜欢的音乐推给孩子，而是在孩子玩的时候把它当背景音乐放。

paras.en: They can also help create positive memories about artists and bands by going to concerts and live music events together.
paras.zh: 他们还可以一起去听音乐会和现场演出，帮孩子对艺人和乐队留下美好的回忆。

paras.en: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.
paras.zh: 第二十二到第二十五题根据你刚才听到的录音提问。

paras.en: Question 22: What do we learn from researchers’ conclusion at the beginning of the talk?
paras.zh: 第二十二题：从讲话开头研究人员的结论中，我们了解到什么？

paras.en: Question 23: What does Dr. Hauke Egermann say about adolescence?
paras.zh: 第二十三题：关于青春期，豪克·埃格曼博士说了什么？

paras.en: Question 24: What is the key to fostering good taste in later life, according to Dr. Hauke Egermann?
paras.zh: 第二十四题：据豪克·埃格曼博士说，培养日后良好品味的关键是什么？

paras.en: Question 25: How can parents help children create positive memories about artists and bands?
paras.zh: 第二十五题：父母怎样帮孩子对艺人和乐队留下美好的回忆？

paras.zh: 听力理解部分到此结束。
